children.text:
mīmāṃsāślokavārttikaṃ
sucaritamiśrapraṇītayā
kāśikākhyayā ṭīkayā sametam /
(tṛtīyo bhāga')
children.translated_text:
<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s>,
accompanied by the commentary called <s>Kāśikā</s>
composed by <s>Sucaritamiśra</s>.
(Third Part)
Because of the non-deviation of perception, and because that which has such characteristics
as well as <s>anumāna</s> (inference) and the rest, which are well-established, are also not to be examined from this point onwards.

children.text:
atra bhāṣyakāreṇa vijñānavādānte"ato na vyabhicarati pratyakṣam"iti pratyakṣāvyabhicāritvamupasaṃhṛtya 'anumānaṃ jñātasambandhasye' tyādinānumānalakṣaṇaṃ praṇītam /
tasya tātparya darśayati-pratyakṣeti /
ayamartha' /
vṛttikāragranthe hi 'tena vyabhicarati pratyakṣam /
tatpūrvavakatvāccānumānādyapi' iti pratyakṣavyabhicārapūrvakamanumānādīnāmapi vyabhicārāta parīkṣyatvamuktam /
tatra pratyakṣāvyabhicāritve pratipādite vyabhicārikaraṇaprabhavatvena tāvad vyabhicāraśaṅkā prayuktā /
yadi paraṃ svarūpāśrayo vyabhicāra' sambhavati /
so 'pi vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇakeṣu nāśaṅkanīya eva /
na hi pratibuddhadṛśa' pratibandhakasaṃvidviditavyabhicāra' /
sakalavyavahārocchedaprasaṅgāt /
evamitareṣvapi yathāsvamavasare vakṣyāma' /
tasmādanumānādyapi lokaprasiddhaṃ na parīkṣitavyamiti||
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator), at the end of the discussion on the doctrine of consciousness (<s>vijñānavāda</s>), having concluded the non-deviation of perception with the statement "therefore perception does not deviate," formulated the definition of <s>anumāna</s> (inference) beginning with "of that whose connection is known." He shows the purport of this — with the word "perception" etc. The meaning is as follows: In the text of the <s>Vṛttikāra</s> (glossator), it is stated "therefore perception deviates; and because <s>anumāna</s> etc. are preceded by that, <s>anumāna</s> etc. are also to be examined due to their deviation preceded by the deviation of perception." Therein, when the non-deviation of perception has been established, the suspicion of deviation is raised on the ground that it originates from an instrument that deviates. If, however, deviation based on one's own nature were possible, even that should not be suspected in those that have the characteristics to be described. For one whose vision is awakened, one whose knowledge of the invariable concomitance is known, does not deviate — since there would follow the consequence of the destruction of all worldly transactions. Thus we shall explain in regard to the others as well, each in its proper occasion. Therefore <s>anumāna</s> etc., being well-established in the world, are not to be examined.

children.text:
iyaṃ ca sarvavakṣyamāṇapramāṇalakṣaṇabhāṣyatātparyavyākhyā sādhāraṇī vārtikakāreṇa kṛtā /
sarvavakṣyamāṇapramāṇaprapañcasya hīdameva sādhāraṇaṃ sthānam /
anena ca ślokena samarthitārambhāvasara' prapañco viśeṣato vyākhyāsyata iti /
tadetaduktaṃ bhavati /
nātra naiyāyikādivadalokikaṃ pramāṇānāṃ svarūpamupadarśayituṃ lakṣaṇāni praṇītāni /
lokaprasiddhapramā(ṇā) vyabhicāritvānmīmāṃsakānām /
kintu śaṅkitavyabhicārāpāditaparīkṣāpratyākhyāvanārthaṃ lokaprasiddhameva svarūpamupadarśyate /
ato napramāṇalakṣaṇe saṅgati' pratyakṣādilakṣaṇasyāśaṅkitavyeti ||1 || idānīṃ lakṣaṇabhāṣyavyākhyānāvasare prāthamyādanumānalakṣaṇamanusandhāsyati /
tatra ca 'jñātasambandhasye'tyucyate /
tatra na vidma' ko jñātasambandhasamāsārtha iti /
na tāvata puruṣa' sambandhī samudāyo vā /
anupādānāt /

nanu buddhisambandhopasthāpita' puruṣa' samudāyidvayākṣipta' samudāyo vā viśeṣyate /
buddhirhi svaśabdādavagatā tadvantamantareṇātmānamalabhamānopasthāpayati svāśrayamiti nānupādānadoṣa' /

gamyamānasyāviśeṣāt /
na khalu dhūmaśabdārthāvinābhāvādavagato 'gnirjvalatīti viśeṣyate /
vakṣyati ca-
gamyamānasya cārthasya naiva dṛṣṭaṃ viśeṣaṇam /
iti /
syānmatam /
satyam /
anupāttaṃ na viśeṣyate /
upātta eva tviha sambandhī /
tathāhi ayamatra padānvaya' /
anumānamekadeśadarśanādekadeśāntare buddhiriti /
ata' kasyaigadeśasyetyākāṅkṣāyāṃ sa evaikadeśo jñātasambandhasyeti viśeṣyate /
nanu darśanopasarjanatvādekadeśo na viśeṣaṇamarhati /
na hyupasarjanaṃ padaṃ padāntareṇa sambadhyate /
na hi bhavati puruṣaṃ pratyupasarjanībhutasya rājña' ṛddhasya rājapuraṣa iti viśeṣaṇam /
ucyate /
kanopasarjanatvadasambandha' /
ka ākāṅkṣitaṃ hi pūraṇasamarthamupasarjanenāpi sambadhyata eva /
atraikadeśadarśanādityukte 'sti kasyaikadeśasyetyākāṅkṣā /
arthasambandhe 'pyākāṅkṣaiva hetu' /
upasarjanasaṃjñā tu"upasarjanaṃ pūrvam(2-2-30) iti /
pūrveprayogasiddhyarthaiva /
ata eva hi kasya gurukulamiti vyavahāropapatti' /
tatra hi kulopasarjanasyaiva guro' kasyeti viśeṣaṇam /
api ca darśanakriyākarmaṇo dṛśyasyaikadeśasya prādhānyamaprādhanasya sāpekṣasyāpi padāntareṇa sambandho dṛṣṭa', yathā rājapuruṣa'śobhana iti /
ata upapannaṃ jñātasambandhasyaikadeśadarśanāditi /
nopapannam /
uktaṃ hi guruṇaiva-"nopasarjanaṃ padaṃ padāntareṇa samabadhyate ṛddhasya rājapuruṣa itivat"iti /
na ca parihṛtam upasarjana /
children.translated_text: And this general explanation of the purport of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the definitions of all the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) to be discussed has been composed by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> (the author of the Vārttika). For this is the common ground for the entire elaboration of all the <s>pramāṇas</s> to be discussed. And by this verse, the occasion for elaboration, whose commencement has been justified, will be specifically explained. Thus what is stated amounts to this: Here, unlike the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others, the definitions have not been formulated to display some non-worldly nature of the <s>pramāṇas</s>, since for the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> the well-established means of valid knowledge are non-deviating. Rather, the well-established nature itself is displayed for the purpose of refuting the examination imposed by suspected deviation. Therefore, there is no need for apprehension regarding the relevance of defining <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and the rest. Now, at the occasion of explaining the definitions in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, he will investigate the definition of <s>anumāna</s> first, due to its priority. And therein it is said "of that whose connection is known" (<s>jñātasambandhasya</s>). Here we do not know what is the meaning of the compound <s>jñātasambandha</s>. It is not the person who is the relatum, nor the aggregate — because they are not employed (in the compound). For a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound does not take a meaning of another word that is not employed. "But surely, the person presented by the connection with cognition, or the aggregate implied by the two relata, is qualified" — for cognition, understood from its own word, unable to obtain itself without one possessing it, presents its own substratum — so there is no fault of non-employment. This is not so, because of the lack of specification of what is understood. Surely, fire understood from the invariable concomitance with the meaning of the word "smoke" is not specified as "burning." And he will state: "For that which is understood, specification has never been observed." The view may be correct. True — what is not employed is not specified. But here, the relatum is actually employed. For here the syntactic connection of the words is as follows: <s>anumāna</s> is cognition of one part from the perception of another part. Therefore, when the question arises "of which one part?" — that very one part is specified as "of that whose connection is known." But since the one part is subordinate to perception, it does not deserve to be a qualifier. For a subordinate word is not connected with another word. For it is not the case that a specification of the king, who has become subordinate to the person, as "rich" becomes "the king's person" — (the qualification of the king). It is said: By whom is the non-connection due to subordination established? For what is capable of completing what is desired is connected even with a subordinate. Here, when "from the perception of one part" is stated, there is the expectation "of which one part?" In semantic connection too, expectation alone is the cause. The technical term <s>upasarjana</s> (subordinate), however, as in "the subordinate comes first" (Pāṇini 2.2.30), is only for the purpose of establishing the prior position in usage. This is precisely why the usage "whose teacher's family" is appropriate. For therein, the specification is "whose" for the teacher, whose family is subordinate. Moreover, the primacy of the one part — the object of the action of seeing — is seen, and even of the non-primary when it requires something else, connection with another word is observed, as in "the king's man is handsome." Therefore, "from the perception of one part of that whose connection is known" is well-established. It is not well-established. For the teacher himself has stated: "A subordinate word is not connected with another word, just as 'the king's man' with 'rich.'" And the subordinate has not been answered.
The knower is called <s>jñātasambandha</s> (one whose connection is known), or the one part is thus designated;
or, on the view of a <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional) compound, the relatumship is of the one part.

children.text:

siddhānte hi gamyamānāyā eva vyaktergāvau gāva' śuklo gauriti ca vibhaktyā śabdāntareṇa ca viśeṣaṇaṃ bhaviṣyati /
mañcā' krośantīti ca /
āha ca-
jāterastitvanāstitve na hi kaścida vivakṣati /
nityatvāllakṣyamāṇāyā vyakteste hi viśeṣaṇe||
children.translated_text: For in a qualifier, "rich" would qualify the king. But what was stated — that "expectation is the cause of connection" — is unjustified. Even one possessing expectation has been declared to be incapable. If it be said that this fault arises in a single sentence — "<s>anumāna</s> is cognition in another part from the perception of one part" — and therefore, when the sentence is completed, in the expectation "of which one part?" the word "one part" occurring in the sentence is specified by "whose connection is known" — that is not so, because the sentence in which the expectation arises is not heard. This is the same fault of non-employment of another word-meaning. But where there is employment, incapacity due to subordination has been stated. Moreover, the very fault here is the splitting of the sentence. And what was said — that perception has the object of seeing as primary — is also unjustified, because in a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound the meaning of the latter word is primary. And connection with another word based on real primary-subordinate status has not been observed — as is evident in "the king's man" (where the king, though primary in reality, is grammatically subordinate). "But the primacy of the one part is understood from the word itself" — for this is a sixth case (genitive) in the sense of object, through the rule governing <s>kṛt</s> formations. No, because it is not heard. For in a compound, the sixth case is not heard. And what is not heard does not express its own meaning. Rather, as in "the chief of the <s>Niṣādas</s>," its meaning is understood through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). But by the heard form, perception as delimited by the seen object is understood as primary. The rule that "the meaning of the latter word is primary" also follows from this very fact — that it is so understood from the compound. And real primacy of the subordinate is not the cause of connection with another word, nor in a compound requiring something else. Because the word <s>guru</s> (teacher) in "whose teacher's family" always requires something else, the incapacity is not a fault — for the meaning of <s>guru</s> is not understood without its correlate being included, since it is a relational word. Therefore, it enters the compound only when the required meaning is present — so there is no fault. But the word <s>ekadeśa</s> (one part) is not like this — hence the dissimilarity. Therefore, the meaning of the compound <s>jñātasambandha</s> is difficult to ascertain. Hence he says — "the knower" etc. The purport is: True, the one part is not another word-meaning. But the very knower, presented by the connection with cognition, is designated as <s>jñātasambandha</s>. And even what is understood, when presented by an unfailing mark, is indeed specified. For the non-employment of another word-meaning in "obeisance to the one who holds the <s>Pināka</s> (trident)" is not a fault. Moreover, how does the meaning of the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound in the <s>devatā-taddhita</s> formation apply to the <s>Soma</s> juice, which is not employed, when "he takes the <s>Aindravāyava</s> (offering to Indra and Vāyu)"? If it be said that the <s>Soma</s> juice is another word-meaning understood from context — "he buys <s>Soma</s>," "he presses it," "he purifies it," "he receives it in a stream" — then here too, the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> meaning of the knower, understood from the inseparability of cognition, is not unjustified. What was stated by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> in the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) — that "what is understood is not specified" — some have boasted of that as though they had obtained something rare. It should simply be disregarded. For in the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion), specification of what is understood — namely, the individual — will occur through case-endings and other words, as in "two cows, cows, a white cow," and "the platforms are crying out" (<s>mañcāḥ krośanti</s>). And he states: "No one denies the existence or non-existence of the universal. For the individual, which is perceived, is the qualifier, being eternal."

children.translated_text: Thus (he explains). "This smoke is burning" does not occur — because it is not expressed. For the world should not be censured for this. But one who, out of mischief, designates fire by the word "smoke" through secondary signification and wishes to use it thus — we do not prevent him. Now, if the knower is <s>jñātasambandha</s>, then the one part is not specified, and it would follow that the cognition of the pervader from seeing the pervader is <s>anumāna</s> — but this is not desired. For <s>anumāna</s> is the knowledge of the pervader from the pervaded. In the connection "of the one part whose connection is known" (<s>jñātasambandhasya ekadeśasya</s>), there might be the obtaining of a specified one part. For therein, by the genitive in "of the one part whose connection is known," the pervaded itself is indicated as the relatum. For the genitive is always seen to indicate the pervaded. It is said: We have stated that nothing non-worldly about the nature of the <s>pramāṇas</s> is being described here. Rather, the well-established nature is reiterated for the purpose of demonstrating non-examination. For in the world, it is well-known that <s>anumāna</s> is the knowledge of the determining one part from the perception of the determined one part. For even without a qualifier, a specified one part is obtained. Moreover, he says "the meaning that is not proximate." And the memory of the pervaded from mere association with the pervader is not one whose object is not proximate — because memory does not have as its object something not contained in the scope of a prior <s>pramāṇa</s>. But from the pervaded alone, due to the previously experienced regularity, the mountain etc. qualified by the pervader is apprehended. Therefore, the obtaining of a specified one part is well-established. As for what was said — that in "of the one part whose connection is known" the genitive indicates specification — that is unjustified, because the genitive can arise even from the pervader. For the usage occurs: "Being produced is the <s>hetu</s> (reason) of impermanence." And impermanence is the pervader of being produced. Therefore, even when employed without specification, the specification of a particular one part is not unjustified through interpretation of the particular connection. For it is well said: "Specification is understood from interpretation, not from doubt — that is not a fault of definition." This is the meaning of "the knower is <s>jñātasambandha</s>."
Or, the pair that is mutually known in connection — that is <s>jñātasambandha</s>;
by the words 'one part' and 'of that,' the two members of the aggregate are denoted.

children.text:
vyākhyānāntaramāha- ekadeśīti /
ekadeśau hi naikadeśinamantareṇa syātāmiti ākṣiptasyaikadeśino yuktamanyapadārthatvam /
nanvevaṃ jñātasambandhasyaikadeśino ya ekadeśastasyaikaddeśasya darśanādityucyamāne sa eva darśanopasarjanatvādekadeśasyaikadeśina' sambandha' sambandhiviśeṣāpekṣasya vā samāsadoṣa' prasajyate /
bhavedetadevam /
yadyekatadapi paramparayā vājapeyasya yūpa itivadekadeśino bhavatyeva /
ka' punaratraikakadeśī jñātasambandha' pakṣa' sapakṣo vā /
na tāvat pakṣa' jñāyamānasambandhasakṛddarśananirgrāhyā /
bhūyobhistu darśanai' pūrvapūrvāvagatasakaladeśakālaviviktadhūmavanmātrasyāgnimattayā vyāptivadhāritā /
na punaratrāyāmidānīṃ vā dhūmavānagnimāniti /
ata' pakṣaikadeśino 'pi sāmānyato dhūmavattaupādhikasambandho jñāta iti sa eva jñātasaṃbandha' /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even for the part of the <s>pakṣa</s>, the relation qualified by the general property of possessing smoke is known — hence that alone is what has its relation known.

Even when [the relation] is grasped in general, the place and such [constitute] the part; and the two parts [i.e., the inferential mark and the probandum] are considered as the substrate and the superstratum.
But
They should not be viewed as the whole and the part. (1)

He states another explanation — 'ekadeśī' (a part). For [two] parts cannot exist without a possessor of parts — hence it is proper that the possessor of parts, being implied, is the meaning of another word. If it be objected: 'When for one whose relation is known, from the perception of one part of that one part [the inference follows]' — being so stated, since the part is subordinate to perception, a fault of compound arises — either the relation of the part to the possessor of parts, or [a compound] requiring specification of the relatum. Let it be so. Even if [taken] as one, indirectly it becomes a possessor of parts, like [the expression] 'the sacrificial post of the <s>Vājapeya</s>.' But then, who here is the possessor of parts whose relation is known — the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus) or the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue)? Not the <s>pakṣa</s> first, for the relation being known is not ascertainable from a single perception. Rather, through repeated perceptions, the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is ascertained — that what merely possesses smoke, distinguished from all place and time previously apprehended, possesses fire. But not [the specific claim] 'this one here and now possesses smoke and therefore fire.'

children.text:
karmadhārayasamāso vāyamityāha- karmadhārayeti /
ayamartha'- jñātaścāsau saṃbandhaśceti karmadhārayo 'yam /
atra ca pakṣe saṃbandhini gamye gamake caikadeśatā /
kathaṃ sambandhyādhārasya sambandhasya sambandhināvekadeśau /
na hi bhūdharādhārasya dhūmasyaikadeśo
giri' /

children.translated_text: Rather, smoke is the superstratum, and is considered a part of it [the ground] by virtue of being a part of that.
It is said:
The use of the term 'part' is justified even with reference to the substrate-aspect.
Just as with parts in relation to [their] whole-substrates, and with collectivities — thus it should be stated. (2)

He says [the compound] could also be a <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional compound) — 'karmadhāraya.' The meaning is this: 'known' and 'relation' — this is a <s>karmadhāraya</s>. And here, the 'part-hood' resides in the <s>pakṣa</s>, the relatum, the inferable, and the indicator. How [can it be that] the parts of the relation are the relation's substrate and the relatum? For the hill is not a 'part' of smoke whose substrate is the ground-bearer.

children.text:
dvayaṃ vānyapadārtha ityāha- dvayaṃ veti /
sambandhagrahaṇakāle parasparasambandhamupalabdhaṃ vyāpyavyāpakadvayaṃ jñātasambandhamucyate, tasya ca samudāyināvekadeśau /
yathā caitadevaṃ tathā pragevoktamiti /
kiṃ puna' karmadhārayapakṣe dvayānyapadārthve vā prameyam /
na tāvat sambandhasamudāyāveva /
tayo' pūrvamevāvagatatvāt /
adhunā ca dharmadharmivibhāgenānavagamāt /
na cānya ekadeśī /
tasyānupādānāt /
na caikadeśābhyāmākṣepa' /
sambandhasamudāyanirākāṅkṣatvāt /
na ca svatantraikadeśadarśanāt svatantraikadeśāntare jñānamanumānaṃ, siddhatvāt /
vakṣyati hi na dharmamātraṃ, siddhatvāditi /
atrābhidhīyate- ayamatrārtho jñātasya sambandhasya jñātasambandhasya vā dvayasya kvacidekadeśadarśanāt tatraivaikadeśāntare buddhiranumānamiti /
kuta etat /
asannikṛṣṭagrahaṇāt /
na hi svatantraikadeśo 'sannikṛṣṭa' /
kvacideva parvatādāvekadeśo 'sannikṛṣṭo bhavati /
tatrānavagatapūrvatvāditi kimanupapannamiti /
ka' punaratra sambandho 'numānāṅgamiṣyate /

children.translated_text: Invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>), based on essential identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) or origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>) — so say some.
For thus it has been stated by them:
'From the relation of effect and cause, or from essential nature as the determinant,
The rule of invariable concomitance [is established] from non-observation [in the counter-instance], not from observation [in the homologue].'

children.text:
iti /
na hi vipakṣasapakṣayoradarśanād darśanādvāvinābhāvasiddhi' /
tenāniyatasyāpi tatra vṛtte' sambhavāt /
kiñcidavipakṣavyāvṛttyā ca sarvavipakṣavyāvṛttyāsiddhe' /
sarvavipakṣāṇāṃ ca yugapad grahītumaśakte' /
kintu agnyādau sati dhūmāderbhāvādasati cābhāvāt tadāyattasvabhāvo dhūmādiriti vidite tadavinābhāva' siddhyati /
tatkāryasya tamantareṇātmalābhābhāvāt /
tadatrāgnau darśanamitaratrādarśanaṃ tadutpattau hetu' /
tato 'vinābhāvasiddhi' /
tādātmye 'pi tatsiddhi' taṃ vinā bhavatastādātmyānupapatte' /
nanvevaṃvidhānvayavirahiṇo gandhanna rūparasādayo 'numīyeran /
na ca khalu tasya rūpamātmā /
na ca kāraṇamiti kathaṃ tatastatsiddhi' /
śrūyatāṃ yathā siddhyati /
rasādeva hi svahetāvagnāviva dhūmādanumīyamāne samasāmagrīkendhanavikāravadrūpāvagatiriti nānupapatti' /
children.translated_text: For invariable concomitance is not established from non-observation or observation in the counter-instance and homologue respectively, since even an undetermined [property] could occur there. Moreover, non-deviation from all counter-instances is not established by non-deviation from some; and all counter-instances cannot be grasped simultaneously. But when it is known that smoke and such, being present when fire and such are present and absent when they are absent, have their nature dependent on that [fire] — then invariable concomitance is established, because of the impossibility of the effect obtaining its own existence without that [cause]. Thus, observation [of smoke] in fire and non-observation elsewhere are the basis for [establishing] its origination [from fire], and thence invariable concomitance is established. In the case of essential identity too, it is established, because <s>tādātmya</s> (essential identity) cannot hold for that which exists without that [universal nature]. If it be objected: 'Then color, taste, etc., which lack such positive and negative concomitance with smell, would not be inferred [to be present in earth]' — for neither is color the essence of [smell], nor its cause — then how is it established from that? Listen to how it is established: For when smell is inferred from its own cause, fire and such, like smoke [is inferred from fuel], the apprehension of color is [established] like the modification of fuel sharing the same aggregate of causes — hence there is no impossibility.
As they say:
'The ascertainment of color and such from taste [follows] because of dependence on the same aggregate of causes,
Through inference of a property of the cause, like the modification of fuel [producing] smoke.'

children.text:
iti /
nanu yuktendhanavikāre tasya dhūmasya caikāgnikāraṇātvādavagati' /
na tu rūparasāvekakāraṇakau /
kāraṇarasā hi kārye rasamārambhantekāraṇarūpāṇi ca kārye rūpam /
tat kuta' samānakāraṇatā /
naikakāraṇatayaikasāmagryadhīnatvam /
kintu rasād rasaheturanumīyamāna' pravṛttirūpajananaśkatirūpopādānakāraṇasahakṛto 'numīyate /
tathāvidhasyaiva kāraṇatvāt pravṛttiśaktinā ca kāraṇena rūpaṃ janyata iti rūpasiddhi' /
tadidamanupapannam yat tāvat kāryaṃ kāraṇena vinā na bhavatīti tatastajjñānamuktam /
tadayuktam /
kathaṃ hi kāraṇena vinā kāryameva na bhavati ityetadevāvaseyam /
tadvinā bhavato nityaṃ sattvasattvaṃ vā syāt /
tataśca kāryataiva hīyeta /
children.translated_text: If it be objected: 'In the case of fuel-modification, the apprehension of that smoke [follows] because it has a single cause, fire. But color and taste do not have a single cause. For the tastes of the cause produce taste in the effect, and the colors of the cause produce color in the effect. So whence comes the identity of cause?' [The reply:] The dependence on a single aggregate of causes is not due to having a single cause. Rather, when the cause of taste is inferred from taste, it is inferred as assisted by the color-material-cause possessing the capacity to generate color along with activity. For only such [a complete cause] is [truly] a cause. And by a cause possessing the capacity for activity, color is produced — hence color is established. This is untenable. First, regarding what was said — that an effect does not exist without a cause, and hence from that, knowledge of the cause [follows]: that is improper. For how is it to be ascertained that the effect simply does not exist without the cause? Without that [cause], it would be either eternally existent or eternally non-existent, and thus its very nature as an effect would be lost.
For they have said:
'Eternal existence or non-existence [would follow] from the cause's non-dependence on another;
For it is from dependence that the occasional occurrence of things is possible.'

children.text:
iti /
apekṣāta' kādācitkatvamanapekṣaṃ tu sadasadvā syāt /
gaganaśaśaviṣāṇavaditi cet /
yadyevamanyo 'yaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvāt svabhāvaniyama' yadanapekṣaṃ tannityaṃ sadasadvā bhavatīti /
yacca rasādrūpāvagatirekasāmagryadhīnatvādityuktam /
tadapyuktam /
yadyapi pravṛttiśaktirūpopādānakāraṇasahakṛto rasaheturavagata' svakāryād, rūpaṃ tu kuto 'vagamyate /
pravṛttisāmarthyāt kāraṇāditi cet /
nanu nādo rūpasya kāryaṃ nātmeti kathaṃ tadagame hetu' /
pravṛttiśakte' kāraṇasya kāryāvyabhicāraditi cet /
na /
tarhi kāryatadātmanorevāvinābhāva' kāraṇe 'pi (bhāvād ? bhavet ) bhavatviti cet /
na /
agnerapi dhūmānumānaprasaṅgāt /
astviti cet /
atantraṃ tarhi kāryatvamanumāne syānmatam /
na pravṛttisāmarthyāt kāraṇād rūpānumānam /
api tarhi rūpavadrūpakāraṇasahakāriṇā rasakāraṇena raso janyate /
sahakārikāraṇamapi saviśeṣaṇaṃ kāraṇameveti rasāditaretarānugṛhītaṃ
kāraṇacakramanumāsyata iti /
tanna /
kāryakāraṇayorayaugapadyādrūpakāraṇasya tadvatānupapatti' /
pāriśeṣyād (dūṣyād?) rūpameva sahakārīti vācyam /
tatra ca vṛthā tatkāraṇānumānapariśrama' /
children.translated_text: From dependence comes occasional occurrence; but what is independent would be either existent or non-existent. Like the horn of a sky-hare, [one might say]? If so, then this rule of essential nature is something other than the relation of cause and effect — namely, that what is independent is either eternally existent or non-existent. And as for what was said — that the apprehension of color from taste [follows] from dependence on the same aggregate of causes — that too has been addressed. Even if the cause of taste, assisted by the material-cause of color possessing the capacity for activity, is ascertained from its own effect, how is color thereby ascertained? From the cause possessing the capacity for activity, [one might say]? But taste is neither the effect of color nor its essence — so how is it a basis for ascertaining that [color]? Because the cause possessing the capacity for activity does not deviate from the effect, [one might say]? No. Then let there be invariable concomitance of the effect and its essential nature in the cause itself — let that suffice! No — because then the inference of smoke from fire would follow [which is absurd]. Let it be so, [one might say]? Then effect-hood would be irrelevant to inference — that would be the [absurd] conclusion. Color is not inferred from the cause possessing the capacity for activity. Moreover, just as color [requires a cause having] a subsidiary cause possessing color, so taste is produced by a cause of taste having a subsidiary cause possessing taste. A subsidiary cause, even with qualification, is still a cause; hence a mutually supporting causal circle of taste and the others would have to be inferred — but that is wrong, because cause and effect cannot be simultaneous, so the cause of color cannot possess that [color]. By elimination, color alone should be called the subsidiary cause. But then the effort of inferring its cause is futile.
Even [the claim that] 'color is a subsidiary cause' —
One cannot experience this without first establishing the invariable concomitance of color and taste.

children.text: prāgeva tu tannirṇaye vṛthā rūpataddhetvo' sahakāritvakalpanā /
children.translated_text: But in establishing that very [concomitance], the postulation of the subsidiary-cause relationship of color and its cause is futile.
The relation that is the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of the <s>liṅga</s>-property by the <s>liṅgin</s> (the property-bearer) is desired here. (3)

He says the pair [taken together] is the meaning of another word — 'dvayam va' (or the pair). The pair of pervaded and pervader, whose mutual relation was apprehended at the time of grasping the relation, is called 'that whose relation is known,' and the two parts [of the pair] are its parts. That this is so has been stated previously. But what is the object of valid cognition — in the <s>karmadhāraya</s> interpretation or in the pair-as-another-meaning interpretation? Not the relation and the aggregate themselves, for they were already known before. And they are not now cognized in the form of the distinction between property and property-bearer. Nor is there another possessor of parts, since it is not mentioned. Nor is there implication from the [two] parts, since the relation-aggregate is self-sufficient. And from the perception of one independent part, the cognition of another independent part is not inference, because [the latter] is already established. For he will say: 'Not the property alone, because it is already established.' Here the meaning is explained: the meaning here is that from the perception of one part of the pair whose relation is known, or of the pair that has its relation known, the cognition of the other part in that very [locus] is inference. Why is this? Because of the apprehension of what is not in proximity. For an independent part is not 'not in proximity.' Only somewhere, as on a mountain and such, is a part not in proximity. And there, since it was not previously ascertained, what is untenable? But what relation is here accepted as a component of inference?

children.text:
api cānubhavaviruddhamevedam /
na khalu rasamupalabhya taddhetvanumānamukhena rūpāvagatirlaukikānām /
api tarhi rūparasayo' sāhityaniyamāt sahasaiva rasād rūpamanumīyate /
api ca kāryakāraṇabhūtayoreva bahulamanumānavyavahāro dṛśyate ityanādṛtyaṃ kāryatvamavyabhacāre /
tādātmyamapi meyābhāvaprasaṅgāddheyameva /
kiṃ hi vṛkṣātmani śiṃśapātve vidite meyamavaśiṣyate /
nirbhāgaṃ vastu, bhāgāvagrahāṇāṃ deśādibhede 'pyabādhitānāṃ samyaktvāt /
kālpanikabhedāśrayatvāccanumānasya vāstavamaikātmyamanaṅgam /
vṛkṣavyavahāro 'numīyata iti ced kathamanātmavyavahāra'śiṃśapātvādanumīyate /
tādātmye vṛkṣavadananumānaprasaṅgāt /
vyavahārayogyatāyāmapyevameviti yat kiñcidetat /
evameva vaiśiṣikādisamayasiddhā api kāryakāraṇabhāvādaya' sambandhaprakārā' prayuktā veditavyā' /
te 'pi hyaniyatānanumānotpattikāraṇam /
astu tarhi niyamo vānumānāṅgam /
na /
pramāṇābhāvādanavagate' /
na tāvadāpātajaṃ pratyakṣamasyāvadhāraṇakṣamam /
īkṣate khalvayaṃ visphāritākṣa' sahasā mahānase dhūmamagninā sahitam /
na tu jānāti niyato 'yamaneneti /
duradhigamo hi sarvabhāvānāṃ svabhāvaniyama' /
na tamunnetumutsahante jhaṭiti mahānto 'pi /
na hi nirvikalpakāgocare vikalpa' pramāṇam /
tatpura' saratvāt tasya /
syādetat /
deśādibhedeṣvavyabhicārāt svabhāvaniyamo 'vadhāryata iti /
kenāvadhāryate sarvadarśanānāmanvayamātre vyāpārāt /
atha pūrvapūrvajñānajanitabhāvanāsacivamantimamanenāyaṃ niyata iti bhavatyālocanājñānam /
tato vikalpā' pravartiṣyanta iti /
naitadevam /
indriyavyāpārasāpekṣaṃ hi pratyakṣam /
na ca sahabhāvadarśanādanyatra bahiridandriyavyāpāra' /
na ca bahirviṣayavedane tannirapekṣamanta'karaṇaṃ pravartate /
api ca nirūpitarūpā api bhāvā deśādibhedeṣvanyathābhavanto 'nūbhūyanta iti na svabhāvaniyamaṃ pratyāśrayitumucitaṃ prāmāṇikānām /

children.translated_text: Hence they say:
'Due to the difference in the forms of place, time, and such, when the capacities are different,
The establishment of things through inference is exceedingly difficult.'

Moreover, this is contradicted by experience. Certainly, ordinary people do not, upon perceiving taste, apprehend color through the inferential route of inferring its cause. Rather, because of the rule of co-occurrence of color and taste, color is inferred directly from taste simultaneously. Furthermore, the transaction of inference is predominantly seen only between things standing in the relation of cause and effect — hence, effect-hood is to be disregarded regarding non-deviation. Essential identity too must be abandoned, since otherwise the object of valid cognition would be absent. For when the <s>śiṃśapā</s>-hood [being a particular species of tree] is known in the essence of a tree, what remains as the object to be known? The object is without parts [i.e., undivided], since the partial apprehensions, even with difference of place and so forth, are uncontradicted and hence valid. And since inference depends on fictitious divisions, real oneness is not a component [of inference]. If it be said that 'tree-ness as a usage is inferred' — then how is the usage of 'self' [i.e., essential nature] not inferred from <s>śiṃśapā</s>-hood? Because in essential identity, there would be the unwanted consequence of non-inference, as with 'tree.' The same applies to fitness for practical usage — hence all this is pointless. Similarly, the types of relations established in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> and other systems — cause-effect relations and the like — when employed, should be understood [as follows]: they too, being undetermined, are not causes for the production of inference. Let determination, then, be a component of inference. No — because, in the absence of a means of valid cognition, it cannot be ascertained. First, perception that arises casually is not capable of ascertaining this. For one observes with wide-open eyes, suddenly, smoke in the kitchen together with fire — but does not know 'this is invariably determined by that.' For the determination of the essential nature of all things is difficult to grasp; even great ones cannot readily extract it. For in the domain of the non-conceptual [perception], conceptual construction is not a valid means — because the former is prior [to the latter]. One might say: 'From non-deviation across differences of place and such, the determination of essential nature is ascertained.' But by whom is it ascertained, when the operation of all perceptions is confined to mere co-occurrence? If it be said: 'The final [perception], assisted by the impression generated by preceding cognitions, gives rise to the reflective cognition that "this is invariably determined by that"' — and thence conceptual constructions proceed — that is not so. For perception depends on the operation of the sense organs, and there is no operation of the external sense organs beyond the perception of co-existence. And the internal organ does not operate in apprehending external objects without dependence on that [external sense]. Moreover, even things whose nature has been ascertained are experienced as behaving otherwise across differences of place and such — hence it is not proper for those who respect valid means of cognition to rely on the determination of essential nature.

children.text: vyāpyasya gamakatvaṃ ca vyāpakaṃ gamyamiṣyate // Msv_5,4.4 //
children.translated_text: The pervaded is held to be the indicator, and the pervader is held to be the indicated. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.4)

children.text: yo yasya deśakālābhyāṃ samonyūno 'pi vā bhavet /
children.translated_text: That which, in terms of place and time, is equal to another, or even less [in extent],
That is the pervaded; and its pervader is the equal or the greater [in extent]. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.5)
Therefore, when the pervaded object is grasped, the pervader of that is grasped;

children.text: na hyanyathā bhavatyeṣā vyāpyavyāpakatā tayo' // Msv_5,4.6 //
children.translated_text: For this relation of pervaded and pervader between those two does not hold otherwise. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.6)

children.text:
iti tasmād vaktavyo 'numānāṅgabhūta' sambandha' /
ata āha-sambandhaiti /
vyāptirhi sāhityaniyamamapadiśati /
taddarśino hmekadeśaderśanādekadeśāntare buddhirutpadyate, ata' sāmānyavacano 'pi sambandhaśabda uparitanasamabhivyāhārādatrānumānalakṣaṇagranthe
children.translated_text: Of one who perceives that [co-occurrence], from the perception of one part, a cognition of the other part arises; hence, even though the word 'relation' is of general import, in this text defining inference, by virtue of its syntactic connection with the above,
It bears a specific meaning.
And the means of valid cognition for ascertaining this [vyāpti] will be stated further on. (3)
Therefore, the relation that is a component of inference must be stated. Hence he says — 'sambandha' (relation). For <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) denotes the rule of co-occurrence.

children.text: yadi jñātasambandhasyānumānaṃ sa tarhi sambandho sambanadhe dvyāśraya ityubhayānu māne liṅgaṃ syādata āha-vyāpyeti ||4||
children.translated_text: If inference belongs to one whose relation is known, then that relation [itself requires knowledge of] a relation — [leading to] mutual dependence — and both inferences would have the inferential mark [as their basis]. Hence he says — 'vyāpya' (the pervaded). (4)

children.text:
atra kāraṇamāha-yo yasyeti dvayena /
sa'- samanyūnadeśakālo hi vyāpyo bhavati /
purvaṃ tāvad yatrobhayorapi dharmayorvyāpyavyāpakatvam /
yathā parastādudāhariṣyate /
uttarastu yathā dhūmādi', sa hi prāyeṇāgnideśakālavartī bhavati /
sakalatadīyadeśakālāvyāpte' /
vyāpakastu samādhikadeśakāla' /
atrāpi pūrvokta eva pūrva' /
uttarastu yathāgnireva dhūmasya /
sa hi tasya deśakālau tāvad vyāpnotyeva /
asatyapi dhūme bhavan deśakālābhyāmadhiko 'pyabhidhīyate /
yataścānayorīdṛśaṃ svarūpaṃ nānyathā vyāpyavyāpakatātmakatā,tena kāraṇena vyāpya eva gṛhīte vyāpakasya grahaṇaṃ bhavati yadasau taṃ vināpi na bhavatyeva /
na hyasāvagniriva dhūmasyāgnerdeśakālāvatikramyāpi bhavati /
yena taṃ vināpi bhavastaṃ na gamayet /
agnistvavaṃvidha iti nāsau dhūmasya gamako bhavati /
nanu cāyaṃ viśeṣojñātasambandhaśabdānnāvagamyate /
children.translated_text: Here he states the reason with the two [verses] beginning with 'yo yasya.' The <s>vyāpya</s> (pervaded) is that which occupies a space and time equal to or less [than the pervader]. First, where both properties have the relationship of pervaded and pervader — as will be illustrated below. The latter [case is] like smoke and such; for it generally exists in the space and time of fire, not pervading the entire space and time of fire. The <s>vyāpaka</s> (pervader), however, occupies a space and time equal to or greater. Here too the former [case] is as previously stated. The latter [case is] like fire itself with respect to smoke; for it pervades the space and time of smoke at least. Even in the absence of smoke, fire is said to exceed in space and time. And since such is the nature of these two — namely, being of the nature of pervaded and pervader, and not otherwise — for this reason, when only the <s>vyāpya</s> is apprehended, the apprehension of the <s>vyāpaka</s> follows, since the former never exists without the latter. For the <s>vyāpya</s> does not exist beyond the space and time of the <s>vyāpaka</s>, as fire exceeds smoke's space and time. Therefore, existing without the pervader, it would not lead to knowledge of it. But fire, being of such nature [that it exceeds smoke], does not serve as an indicator of smoke. Objection: But this distinction is not understood from the word 'known relation' [in the <s>bhāṣya</s>].
Even though the <s>vyāpya</s> is in reality apprehended through the <s>vyāpaka</s>,
because of non-contradiction even in its being of greater extent, the <s>vyāpaka</s> would not establish the <s>vyāpya</s>. // Msv_5,4.7 //
And this is clearly seen in the case of 'cow' and 'having horns' in inference:

children.text: vyāpyatvād gamikā gāvo vyāpikā na viṣāṇitā // Msv_5,4.8 //
children.translated_text: because of being <s>vyāpya</s> (pervaded), cows are indicative; 'having horns,' being the <s>vyāpaka</s> (pervader), is not indicative. // Msv_5,4.8 //

children.text: sa hi sambandhajñānamātramaṅgatayā darśayati, na vyāpyatāmiti kuto viśeṣalābha' /
children.translated_text: For he [the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>] shows 'knowledge of relation' merely as an ancillary, not <s>vyāpyatā</s> (the state of being pervaded) — so where is the gain of distinction?
It has been said that this <s>bhāṣya</s> is a paraphrase of common definitions, intended to convey the matter without critical examination.

children.text: loke ca vyāpyaikadeśadarśina eva vyāpakajñānamanumānamiti siddham /
children.translated_text: And in common usage, only one who sees a part of the <s>vyāpya</s> has knowledge of the <s>vyāpaka</s> — this is established as <s>anumāna</s> (inference).

children.text: nahyanyatheti cāpakṛṣya pūrveṇa yojayitvā teneti tadupajīvanena vyākhyeyamiti ||6||
children.translated_text: The phrase 'na hyanyathā' (for not otherwise) should be construed by drawing it back to connect with the preceding, and then explained as depending on it. // 6 //

children.text:
nanu vyāpakādapi vyāpasaṃvittirdṛṣṭā /
anityatvādiva kṛtakatvasya /
bhavati hi bhāvānāmānatyatvāt kṛtakatvānumānam /
vyāpakaṃ cānityatvaṃ kṛtakatvasya /
ato vyāpakaṃ gamyaṃ vyāpyaṃ gamakamityavyāpakamata āha-vyāpakatveti /
ayayamabhiprāya' /
satyaṃ vyāpakasya gamakatvam /
na tu vyāpakatvagṛhītasya /
tena hi rūpeṇa gṛhīto 'sau vyāpād deśakālādhikye 'pi na virūdhyate /

children.translated_text: Objection: But it also has <s>vyāpyatā</s> (the state of being pervaded).

children.text: astu nāmavastutatastattu rūpaṃ na gṛhītamiti kathaṃ gamakatvam /
children.translated_text: Let it be so in reality; but that form has not been apprehended — so how can it serve as an indicator?

children.text: avagate tu tādrūpye tenaivagamakatvaṃ na vyāpakatayā /
children.translated_text: When that form is understood, then by that very form it serves as indicator, not by virtue of being <s>vyāpaka</s>.
Therefore, <s>vyāpyatā</s> alone is the ancillary of inference, not <s>vyāpakatā</s> — thus it is well said. // 7 //

Objection: Cognition of the <s>vyāpya</s> is also seen from the <s>vyāpaka</s>. Just as 'being produced' is [inferred] from 'impermanence.' For there is an inference of 'being produced' from the impermanence of things. And impermanence is the <s>vyāpaka</s> of 'being produced.' Therefore the <s>vyāpaka</s> is what is to be known and the <s>vyāpya</s> is the indicator — this objection is addressed by 'vyāpakatva' etc. The intention is as follows: True, the <s>vyāpaka</s> can serve as an indicator. But not one that is apprehended qua its being a <s>vyāpaka</s>. For when apprehended in that form, it is not contradicted by being of greater extent in space and time than the <s>vyāpya</s>.
Just as the <s>vyāpya</s> is the indicator and the <s>vyāpaka</s> is what is to be indicated.
For of 'cow-ness' and 'having horns,' the latter is indeed the <s>vyāpaka</s>.
'Mitau' means: in inference.
The meaning is: this distinction between what is to be indicated and the indicator is seen in the case of 'cow-ness' and 'having horns.' // 8 //
He demonstrates with an unambiguous example that <s>vyāpyatva</s> (being pervaded) is the ancillary, not <s>vyāpakatva</s>, beginning with 'upalakṣitam.'
Therefore, even where both properties are accepted as <s>vyāpya</s> and <s>vyāpaka</s>,

children.text: tatrāpi vyāpyataiva syādaṅgaṃ na vyāpitā mite' // Msv_5,4.9 //
children.translated_text: even there, <s>vyāpyatā</s> alone would be the ancillary in inference, not <s>vyāpakatā</s>. // Msv_5,4.9 //
Therefore, in other substrata, of whichever [property], by whichever [other property], of whatever kind,

children.text: deśe yāvati kāle vā vyāpatā prāṅanirūpitā // Msv_5,4.10 //
children.translated_text: in whatever extent of space or time the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) was previously ascertained— // Msv_5,4.10 //

children.text: evamasaṅkare gamyakagamakavivekād yatrāpi vyāptisaṅkaro bhavati tatrāpi vyāpyatvameva gamakatve kāraṇamiti niṣkṛṣyata ityāha- teneti ||9||
children.translated_text: Thus, from the discrimination of what is to be indicated and the indicator in the unambiguous case, even where there is confusion of <s>vyāpti</s>, <s>vyāpyatva</s> alone is extracted as the cause of being an indicator — he states this with 'tena.' // 9 //

children.text:
nanu vyāptiranumānāṅgamityuktam /
kasya punariyaṃ saṃyogina' samavāyina' sambandhisambandhino vā /
na hyatra vyavasthāmupalabhāmahe /
sarveṣāmapyanumāpakatvāt /
tad yadi saṃyogī vyāpya' /
rasādrūpānumānaṃ na syāt /
atha samavāyī dhūmādagnyanumānam, sambandhisambandhinaśca pitrorbrāhmaṇatvāt putrasya brāhmaṇatvānumānamityādi darśayitavyam /
api ca vyāptirityanvayo 'bhidhīyate /
upaśleṣa iti yāvat /
na cāsau bhūmau pratiṣṭhitenāgnināgaganagatasya dhūmāgrasya sambhavati /
naca bhūmiṣṭhāṃ śaṅkucchāyāṃ divi vartamāna' ṛkṣodayo 'veti /
vyāptiśca kasyacit kenacid bhavantī deśato vā syāt kālato vā /
pūrvasmin kalpe bhāvi' saviturudayasyādyatanārkasyaivodayāt aṣṭau yāmānatikramyānumānaṃ na syāt /
parasmin dhūmādagnyanumānamityādi paryanuyoktavyam /
ata āha-teneti dvayena /
yena kāraṇena yasyaiva saṃyogādīnāmanyatamasya, yenaiva-teṣāmanyatamena, yādṛśī-upaśliṣṭenetareṇa vā vyāpyatā prāgavagatā, saivānumāne kāraṇaṃ bhavati /
nahyuśleṣo vyāpti' /
uktaṃ hi-"sambandhaniyamo 'sāv" iti /
sa cānupaśliṣṭenāpi bhavati /
yo hi yasmin sati bhavati, asati ca na bhavati, tena niyamyata ityucyate /
kimatropaśleṣeṇa /
na cātra deśādīnāmanyatamavivakṣā /
yāvati hi deśe kāle vā vartamānasya yasya vāpyatā nirūpitapūrvā, yāvaddeśakālabhāvinā vyāpakena tasya vyāpakāṃśasya tāvatyeva deśādau vartamānasya sa vyāpyāṃśastādṛgeva, gaganādivartidharmyantare dṛṣṭāntadhadharmyapekṣayā sādhyadharmiṇi dṛṣṭa' san pratipādako bhavati /
children.translated_text: Objection: It has been said that <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is an ancillary of inference. But of what kind is this — of conjunction, of inherence, or of a relation of the relata? For we do not find a definite answer here, since all kinds serve as inferential indicators. If the <s>vyāpya</s> is one connected by conjunction, then the inference of color from taste would not be possible. If by inherence, then the inference of fire from smoke would need to be shown, as would the inference of a son's <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-hood from his parents' <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-hood as a case of relation-of-the-related. Moreover, <s>vyāpti</s> means <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) — i.e., contact. But this is not possible between fire standing on the ground and the tip of smoke in the sky. Nor does the rising of a constellation in the sky accompany the shadow of the gnomon on the ground. And <s>vyāpti</s>, being the relation of something with something, may be spatial or temporal. In the former case, the inference of sunrise from a past sunrise would not work, since the sunrise of the past epoch does not exceed eight watches without being identical to today's sunrise. In the latter case, the inference of fire from smoke and similar cases should be examined. Therefore he says with the two [verses] beginning with 'tena': By whatever cause, of whichever one among conjunction and others, by whichever one among them, of whatever kind — whether the <s>vyāpyatā</s> (state of being pervaded) was previously ascertained with contact or without it — that very thing becomes the cause in inference. For contact is not <s>vyāpti</s>. As it was said: 'That is the invariable concomitance of the relation.' And that occurs even without contact. For whatever exists when something exists, and does not exist when that something does not exist, is said to be invariably concomitant with it. What use is contact here? Nor is there an intention to specify any particular one of space and so forth. For of whatever [property] present in whatever extent of space or time the <s>vyāpyatā</s> was previously ascertained, that <s>vyāpya</s>-aspect, being present in just that much of space and so forth, with its <s>vyāpaka</s>-aspect being present in just that much space and time — when seen in another substrate such as the sky, in relation to the example-substrate and the subject-substrate, becomes a probative factor.

children.text: tasya tāvati tādṛk sa dṛṣṭo dharmyantare puna' /
children.translated_text: That [<s>vyāpya</s>]-aspect, of that kind, of that extent, seen in another substrate,
is the probative factor of the <s>vyāpaka</s>-aspect in exactly the same way. // Msv_5,4.11 //
And <s>vyāpti</s> is apprehended through repeated observation, in the case of general properties;
and in some cases, even of particular properties, through the elimination of differences. // Msv_5,4.12 //

children.text:
niyamo hyanumānāṅgam /
sa ca sarveṣāmaviśiṣṭa eva kimavāntaravibhāgena /
deśe yāvatītyanatidūramadhirūḍhasya dhūmāderdūrataravartino 'pi nadīpūrasya vyāptiṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: With 'in whatever extent of space,' he shows the <s>vyāpti</s> of smoke and such that has risen not too far, with a river-flood that exists further away.
And of the gnomon-shadow with the rising of a constellation that exists very far away.
'In whatever extent of time'—
shows <s>vyāpti</s> even in the inference of sunrise and such that are yet to come. // 11 //
For invariable concomitance is the ancillary of inference. And it is non-different for all — what use is an internal subdivision?

children.text:
nanvasyāṃ vyāptau na kiñcit pramāṇamastītyuktamata āha-bhūyodarśaneti /
kathaṃ punarbhūyodarśanagamyā vyāpti' /
kiṃ hi tatra
pratyekameva bhūyāṃsi darśanāni pramāṇamāhosvid darśanaprabhavam /
tatra na tāvat pratyekasandarśanasamadhigamyā vyāptirityavasitameva /
no khalvasya sahasāgnadhūmāvagniśaraṇe vilokayamānasyāgninā vyāpto dhūma iti matirāvirasti /
na cānanubhūtamavikalpakena savikalpakenāpi viṣayīkriyate /
na cānekarśanārabdho darśanasamudāya' kaścidasti, tasya darśanātirekeṇābhāvāt /
niruddhānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ cāsaṃhanyamānatvāt /
purastanānekadarśanāhitasaṃskārasahāyamantimaṃ tu darśanaṃ katarat pramāṇamiti cintanīyam /
na tāvat pratyakṣam /
taddhi dvedhā vibhaktam /
ālocanājñānaṃ tatprabhavaṃ ca vikalpasambhinnam /
na tāvat pūrvaṃ vyāpteravadhāraṇe samartham apratisandhānāt /
vyāpteścāyamanena pratibaddha iti pratisandhānātmakatvāt /
naca tadanapekṣamuttaramātmānaṃ labhate /
yañcedaṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ sācinyam, idamapi na caturaśram /
saṃskārā' khalu yadvasturūpopalambhasambhāvitātmāno bhavanti, tatraiva smṛtimātramādadhati /
na punararthāntaragrahaṇāya kalpante /
pratyakṣe ca vyāptipramāṇe kathamataphalebhya' puṃviśeṣeṣu vaidikakarmānumānam /
na ca tattatkarmaniyamastasya tasya paśvāde' phalasyāparokṣamīkṣyate atīndriyatvāt /
yañcedamadhvarevitate vaidikādaṅgāt pradhānāñcāpūrvānumānam, tadapi na syāt /
vyāptyavadhāraṇe pramāṇābhāvāt /
meghābhāvācca vṛṣṭyabhāvānumānamityādi darśayitavyam /
ato na tāvat pratyakṣā vyāpti' /
na cānumānikī /
pramāṇābhāvādeva tadadhīnātmalābhasya tasyānupapatte' /
śabdastvanāgatotpādyabhāvaviṣayo na siddhavyāptikḷptaye prabhavati /
upamānamapi pramāṇāntaraprasiddhavastusādṛśyamātraviṣayaṃ na vastuna' satāṃ pramiṇoti /
arthāpattirapyanyathānupapadyamānārthaviṣayā darśanaprabhavā /
na ca sahitāvadhāritayorasatyāṃ vyāptau kiñcidanupapannaṃ nāma||
children.translated_text: Objection: There is no <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) for this <s>vyāpti</s>. Therefore he says 'bhūyodarśana' etc. But how is <s>vyāpti</s> apprehended through repeated observation? Is each individual observation a <s>pramāṇa</s>, or is it something born from observation? Now, it is already settled that <s>vyāpti</s> is not comprehended from each individual observation. For surely, when someone suddenly sees fire and smoke together in a fireplace, the thought 'smoke is pervaded by fire' does not arise. Nor is what has not been experienced through non-conceptual [cognition] objectified even by conceptual [cognition]. Nor is there any aggregate of observations commenced by many observations, since it does not exist apart from the individual observations, and because past, future, and present [observations] cannot be combined. It is the final observation, aided by the impressions deposited by many previous observations, that should be considered as the <s>pramāṇa</s>. But it is not perception. For that is divided into two: apprehensive cognition (<s>ālocanajñāna</s>) and the conceptual cognition born from it. Now, the former is not capable of ascertaining <s>vyāpti</s>, because it lacks recognition. And since <s>vyāpti</s> is of the nature of recognition — 'this is invariably concomitant with that' — and the latter cannot obtain itself without the former [being capable], and this accumulation of <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions) is not quite right either. For <s>saṃskāras</s>, whose nature is constituted by the apprehension of the form of a given object, only produce memory regarding that very object. They are not capable of apprehending something else. And if perception were the <s>pramāṇa</s> for <s>vyāpti</s>, how could there be inference of Vedic rituals with regard to particular persons where the results have not materialized? For the invariable connection between specific rituals and their fruits such as animals is not directly perceived, being beyond the senses. And the inference of <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit) from the principal and subsidiary Vedic rites for one who performs the sacrifice would also not be possible, due to the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> for ascertaining <s>vyāpti</s>. The inference of the absence of rain from the absence of clouds, and similar cases, should be demonstrated. Therefore <s>vyāpti</s> is not first of all perceptual. Nor is it inferential, because, due to the very absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s>, that [inference] whose self-attainment depends on it is not established. Verbal testimony, having as its object things that are not yet produced or that are absent, is not capable of establishing an already-established <s>vyāpti</s>. Analogy too, having as its object merely the similarity of an object known through another <s>pramāṇa</s>, does not measure the reality of existing things. <s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) too, having as its object a meaning that is otherwise inexplicable, is born from observation. And when <s>vyāpti</s> has not been ascertained for two things observed together, nothing is indeed inexplicable.

children.text:
nanu kāryatā nopapadyate /
kathaṃ hi kāryamasati kāraṇe bhavati /
bhūyodarśanasamadhigamyaṃ ca kāryatvamiti bhūyodarśanaprasūtakāryatvāvagamānyathānupapattipramāṇikā kāraṇavyāptisiddhi' /
kathamidānīmakāryakāraṇabhūteṣu vyāpti' setsyati /
bhūyāṃsi darśanānyevāsatyāṃ vyāptau nopapadyanta iti cet, kiṃ hi teṣāṃ vyāptimantareṇa na sambhavati svarūpaṃ, tāvacca kāraṇasāmagrīkaṃ hi va' siddham /
svagocaraprakāśanamapi svata eva viṣasyāpi svapramāṇaparicchannasya na kiñcidanapapannaṃ paśyāma' /
na cāsau pramāṇāntareṇa pratihanyate /
yannopapadyeta /
na ca bhāvasvarūpā vyāptirabhāvena pramīyata iti sāmpratam /
tatrāsāvabhāvapramāṇikā na syādeva||
children.translated_text: Objection: But the relation of effect is not established [without <s>vyāpti</s>]. For how can an effect exist in the absence of its cause? And since 'being an effect' is comprehended through repeated observation, the establishment of causal <s>vyāpti</s> is warranted by <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), from the otherwise inexplicability of the comprehension of 'being an effect' born from repeated observation. How then will <s>vyāpti</s> be established in cases where there is no cause-effect relation? If [you say] that many observations are themselves not possible without <s>vyāpti</s> — what is it about them that is not possible without <s>vyāpti</s>? Their own nature? But that is established as having the full complement of causes. And the illumination of their own object, being self-established, even for poison comprehended by its own <s>pramāṇa</s> — we see nothing inexplicable. Nor is it contradicted by another <s>pramāṇa</s> — which would make it inexplicable. Nor is <s>vyāpti</s>, which is of the nature of a positive entity, measured by absence — thus this is proper. In that case, that [<s>vyāpti</s>] established through the <s>pramāṇa</s> of absence would not exist at all.

svābhāvikatve ca na vyabhicārāśaṅkopapattimatī /
kimidānimanaṅgabhūtameva bhūyodarśanam /
nānaṅgam /
