vahnirhi dhūmena saṃyukta' saṃvedito 'pi kadācidvidhūmo dṛśyate /
tatrārdrendhanādirūpādhiranupraviśati /
na tu svābhāviko 'gnerdhūmena saṃbandha iti niścīyate /
taddarśanācca dhūme 'pi
bhavati śaṅkā /
kadācidaupādhika' pāvakenāsyāpi saṃbandha iti /
sā bhūyodarśanena nivartyate /
bahuśo 'pi dṛśyamānasya dhūmasya nāgnisaṃbandhe kaścidupādhirūpalabhyate /
prayatnenāpi cānviṣṭo na dṛṣṭa upādhirnāstīti niścīyate /
tadevaṃ dhūmamātrānubandhagniriti siddhaṃ bhavati /
tataścānaupādhikasya na vyabhicārāśaṅketi /
sa vaktavya' kimidānīṃ sāhityamātramanumānāṅgaṃ tanniyamo vā /
yadi sāhityamātraṃ tattarhi prathamadarśana eva samadhigatamiti punardhūmadarśino 'viditavyāpterapyanumānaṃ syāt /
atha tanniyama' tasyaivedaṃ pramāṇamanusriyate kuta' sidhyatīti /
na hi prathamadarśino 'yamanena niyata iti matirāvirbhavantī dṛśyate /
anavacchinnadeśakālatayāvagata' saṃbandha' svābhāviko bhavati, tato niyama iti cet /
sa tarhi tathāvidha' prathamamevāvagata iti bhūyodarśanaṃ nāpekṣeta /
tathā dṛṣṭasyāpyagnerdhūmasaṃbandho vyabhicarati /
taddarśanāñca dhūme 'pi vyabhicārāśaṅkā jāyate /
tannirākaraṇāyāsakṛddarśanāpekṣeti cet, yadyanavacchinnasyāpi deśata' kālato vā kadācit kasyacit kasyacid viyogo dṛśyate /
kastarhi itaratrāpi samāśvāsa' /
nanviyamāśaṅkā bhūyodarśanena nirākriyata ityuktam /
kathaṃ nirākriyate /
yadā śataśo 'pi dhūmavānagriravagato vidhūmo dṛśyate /
na cātra pratiniyama' iyadabhirdarśanairavyabhicāra' sidhyati iti /
nanu dhūmasyāpyagnisabandhe na kaścidupādhirupalabhyate agneriva dhūmasaṃbandhe /
ata' kathamasau satyapi dhūme na bhaviṣyati /
na /
deśāderevopādhitvena śaṅkyamānatvāt /
agnau dhūmasaṃbandhavyabhicāramupalabhyāśaṅkate- kadācid dhūmasyāpyagnisambandhe deśakālādyupādhi' syāditi /
dṛṣṭaṃ hi kvacid deśe kharjūrāṇāṃ piṇḍakharjūraphalatvam /
vṛścakadaṃśanasya ca maraṇakāraṇatvam /
taddeśāntare na bhavati /
tadvat dhūmo 'pi jātu jāyetāntareṇāpi hutāśanaṃ kvaciditi śaṅkamānā na tasya niyamamagninādhyavasyanti śatāṃśenāpi /
vipakṣād vyāvṛtti'śaṅkamānā anumānodayaṃ pratibandhātīti katarañcedaṃ pramāṇam, anaupādhiko 'gnirdhūmamātrānubandhīti /
na tāvat pratyakṣam /
sāhityamātropakṣīṇatvāt /
nānumānam /
tasyāsatyāṃ vyāptāvasambhavāt /
vyāptisiddhyartaṃ cāparāparānumānakalpanāyāmanavasthāpātāt /
pramāṇāntarāṇi nirākṛtapūrvāṇyeva /
ato vyākhyeyamunumānāṅgasambandhāvadhāraṇe pramāṇam, tad vyākhyāyate /
idaṃ tāvat pramāṇābhāvavādī vaktavya' /
kiṃ khalu vyāptigocaraṃ jñānaṃ na jāyata eva, sandigdhaṃ vā jāyate, viparyeti vā /
tredhā hi parīkṣakairaprāmāṇyaṃ vibhaktam /
prakārāntarāsambhavāt /
na tāvadādya' pakṣa' /
saṃvidavyavahāravirodhāt /
dṛśyate hi bahulaṃ dhūmamagnāvupalamāno 'yamanena niyata ityavadhāraṇapura' saraṃ tato 'gnimanumāya tadanurūpaṃ vyavaharamāṇa' /
tannāsatyāṃ vyāptisaṃvittāvupapadyeta /
vyavahāradarśanādeva saṃśayaviparyayau nirākāryau /
tābhyāmevaṃvidhavyavahārāsambhavāt /
ato na tāvadaprāmāṇyam /
prāmāṇyaṃ tu ṣoḍhā vibhajyate /
tad yathāyogyaṃ kasyacit kasyāñcit vyāptasaṃvittau vyavasthāpayāma' /
yathaiva tāvad dhūmasyāgninā vyāptau pratyakṣasya /
na hīha pramāṇāntarāṇi sambhavantīti varṇitameva /
nanu prathamadarśane 'navagamātpratyakṣāsambhavo 'pyukta eva /
ata eva bhūyodarśanāvagamyatvam /
nanu tānyapi vikalpya dūṣitāni pratyekasāhityayorasambhavāt /
satyam /
na pratyekaṃ vyāptiravagamyate /
na ca darśanāni saṃhanyante /
prācīnānekadarśanajanitasaṃskārasahāye carame darśane cetasi cakāsti dhūmasya vahniniyatasvabhāvatvaṃ, ratnavattvamiva parīkṣamāṇasya, śabdatattvamiva vyākaraṇasmṛtisaṃskṛtasya, brāhmaṇatvamiva mātāpitṛsambandhasmaraṇasahakṛtasya, tailād viviktamiva vilīnājyaṃ rasagandhasahakṛtendriyasya /
na hyetat sarvamāpātānna pratibhātamiti parastādapi bhāsamānamanyathā bhavati /
na ca pramāṇāntaratvamāpādayati /
nanūktaṃ na smṛteranyatra saṃskārā vyāpriyanta iti /
kena vā saṃskārāṇāṃ smṛteranyatra vyāpāra upeyate /
smārayanta eva tu te pūrvapūrvāvagatamagnisambandhaṃ dhūmasya vyāptisaṃvidaṃ janayitumabhipravṛttacasyendriyasya sahāyībhavanti /
āntarālikasmṛtivyavahitamapi cendriyasambandhānusāri pratyakṣamiti varṇitam /
indriyasambandhaphalāparokṣāvabhāsānusārāt /
na ca yat sahasā na pratibhāti tatpaścādapi pratibhāsamānaṃ pratyakṣatāṃ jahāti /
yathodāhṛtyeṣveva brāhmaṇam /
nanu na tāvadāpātajaṃ pratyakṣaṃ vyāptau pramāṇamiti bhaṇitam /
tatapūrvakaṃ ca savikalpakamiti kathaṃ tasyāpi prāmāṇyam /
asti vā brāhmaṇādipratyakṣe nirvikalpakāvasthāyāṃ vṛddhādāviv narāntaraviviktākārapratibhāsa' /
yena parastāt savikalpakaṃ
pravartate /
yathā tu tatra piṇḍamātradarśina' smṛtayonisambandhasya brāhmaṇo 'yamiti pratyakṣaṃ jāyate, evamihāpi bahuśo 'gnidhūmadarśino 'ntime darśane nirvikalpavṛttadhūmasvalakṣaṇasyāgninā niyato 'yamiti dhūsvabhāvagocaraṃ pratyakṣam, etāvadeva svavikalpasya nirvikalpakapūrvatvam, yattajjanmapūrvikā pravṛtti', saṃjñādismaraṇārthaṃ hi tat prathamamarthyate /
tacceha vyaktidarśana eva pūrvasaṃskārodabodhāt siddhamiti nāvaśyamanayo' samānaviṣayatā /
ata eva tailaviviktavilīnājyabodhe tailamidamiti viparyasyato
gandhasahakṛtendriyasya (sa)vikalpapratyakṣatvasiddhi' /
na hi tatrāsaṅkīrṇā ghṛtākārā saṃvidāsīt /
tailamidamiti viparyayāt /
ata' parastādeva sahakārivaśāt nirvikalpakopadarśitavyaktiviṣayaṃ ghṛtamidamiti savikalpakaṃ pratyakṣamīvirasti /
evamihāpīti na doṣa' /
kiṃ punariha savikalpakena viṣayīkriyate /
niyato 'yamaneneti niyama' /
asya hi bahulaṃ dhūmamagnāvupalabhamānasyānagnau ca vyatirekamante bhavati vimarśa'- api syād vyāpto 'yamaneneti /
kathamaparathā jāṅgalādibhedabhinnānekadeśaparityāgena sāyamādibhedabhinnānekakālaparihāreṇa ca tṛmadārugomayendhanādisamavadhānaviśeṣaṃ pratyanādṛto 'gnimevānudhāvatyanagnau ca na bhavati /
tata' paraṃ ca yathāgniradhūmabhāsvaratvādiparityāgenāpi (du?ku) kūlālātādau vartamānoṣṇatvamajahat tanniyato bhavati /
evamagninā dhūma ityaparokṣaniścayo jāyate /
yattu deśāntarādau vyabhicāra iti, tanna tāvad dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ nāpi śrutamiti nāśaṅkāmadhirohati /
evamapi tu śaṅkamānasya sarvapramāṇeṣvanāśvāsa' kvacid vyabhicāradarśanāt /
yattvavadhārito 'pi svabhāvaniyamo deśāntarādāvanyathā bhavati vṛścikāderiti /
tanna avāntarajātibhedāt /
na hi yad yena niyatamavagatamabādhitaṃ ca tadanyathā bhavati /
avāntarajātibhedāttu śaktisadasadbhāvakṛtā kāryavyavastheti na kvacid vyabhicāra' /
nanu anumānameva kiṃ neṣyate /
yadaupādhikaṃ tad vyabhicarati /
agniriva dhūmam /
na ca tathā dhūmo 'gnimityanaupādhika iti /
bhavatvevam /
avyavasthā tūpasthitā /
arthāpattistarhi bhavatu /
idamev cāgnau darśanamanagnau cādarśanamanupapadyamānamagninā niyamaṃ pratipādayati /
kimatra nopapadyate /
darśanaṃ tāvat tatra bhavatītyetāvataivopapannam, na hi yadekatra bhavati tenānyatra na bhavitavyam /
anyatra bhavato 'daraśanamanupapannamiti cet /
na /
viprakṛṣṭānāmanyeṣāmapyasannikarṣādadaraśanopapatte' /
sannihiteṣvanagniṣvadarśanamanupapannamiti ced abhāvādupapatte' /
teṣu hyasau nāstyev, kathamupala(bhyate?bhyeta) /
tatra satāpyanyatrāpi na bhavitavyameveti kimatra pramāṇam /
ato darśanādarśanasahakṛtendriyasyaiva vastusvabhāvāvadhāraṇamaparokṣaṃ jāyata ityevaṃ samarthanīyam /
nanvetadeva na vidma' /
kīdṛśo 'sau vastuna' svabhāvo 'vadhāryata iti /
uktamasakṛd dhūmo 'gninā niyata iti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- yadā yatra dhūmastadā tatrāgniriti /
nanu sannihitavartamānadeśakālamātrasambandho 'stu pratyakṣa' /
anāgatādisambandhastu katham, atiprasaṅgo hi tathā (sati) syāt /
na /
sannihitarūpamātropalambhāt /
rūpameva tu tādṛśaṃ dhūmādīnāṃ yadevamunnīyate, sthiramiva rūpaṃ kuḍyādīnām /
asti hi teṣu vidyudādivilakṣaṇakālāntarasthāyirūpaprakāśa' /
sannihitāvāntarasambandho na pratyakṣa iti tadrūpamapratyakṣaṃ bhavati /
apratyakṣe hi tasmin nedaṃ rajatamiti sūrvānubhūtarajatabādho na syād, bhinnaviṣayatvāt /
svakāle hi pūrvavijñānena rajataṃ viṣayīkṛtaṃ na bhaviṣyadvādhakajñānakṣaṇa iti kathaṃ tatrāprasaktaṃ bādhyate /
kālāntarasambdho 'pi tena rūpeṇa pūrvajñānāvadhāritaṃ bhaviṣyajjñānakālamapi vyāptotīti bhavati samānaviṣayatāmāsādya bādha' /
nanu yad vastuno rūpaṃ tatparānapekṣamavagamyate, agnerivoṣṇatvam /
na ca dhūmasyāgṛhītapratisambandhinā tadrūpamavagamyata iti kathaṃ vasturūpatvam /
maivam /
sambandho hyasau, kathamanavagate pratisambdhinyavasīyate /
yathāha-
'niyamo nāma sambandha' svamatenocyate 'dhunā'
iti /
ato yadetadagninā dhūmasya niyatvaṃ bhāvātmakamidaṃ tatpratyakṣeṇāvagamyata iti kimanupapannam /
yathā cānagninivṛttirna niyama' tathā varṇitameva /
vipakṣavyāvṛttyā tu vidhirūpa eva niyama' parīkṣakairvyākhyāya parebhya' pratipādyate /
children.translated_text: One might hold the view: what is this <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of smoke by fire other than the non-occurrence [of smoke] in the absence of fire? And since that [non-occurrence] has the nature of absence, it is cognized through absence [as a means of knowledge]—this is quite reasonable. No, that is not so, because it has the nature of a positive entity. For the nature of smoke and the like is a positive entity, determined by something; it is excluded from the other. 'But this [smoke] is also excluded from the absence of a hare's horn, so it would be determined even by a hare's horn.' How can it be determined by something non-existent?—if this be asked: what is the fault? For determination is exclusion, and that [exclusion] exists—what does it matter whether the hare's horn is existent or non-existent? If it is held that the counter-positive (<s>vipakṣa</s>) is that which obstructs what is excluded from the counter-positive—and smoke is pervaded by the absence of a hare's horn, since smoke that has ceased due to the absence of that [hare's horn] is like non-fire—then that absence too is a counter-positive indeed. Moreover, since not all counter-positives are fit for apprehension, the cessation [of the <s>hetu</s>] from them cannot be understood through absence. For it will be stated that the absence of a valid means of knowledge fit [for apprehending] is the means of knowing absence. Therefore there is no means of knowledge at all for <s>vyāpti</s>. If [you say] it is mental [perception]—no, because the mind is not independent with respect to external [objects]. Here one might argue: although the external sense-organs are incapable of grasping the <s>vyāpti</s> with past, future, and other varieties of entities, the mind, whose capacity is specifically connected with the determination of all past and other objects, [operates] somewhere—and through perception arising dependent on that [mind], <s>vyāpti</s> will be grasped. But this is not so, because the mind is not independent with respect to external [objects]. It has been explained that the mind is not at all independent in the cognition of external objects. For it is stated: 'the mind along with that [external sense].' If the mind were held to be independent with respect to external [objects], everyone would perceive everything. If [you say] the arrangement is due to impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>)—no, because they are causes only of memory. Here one might argue: although the mind is entirely non-independent in ascertaining external objects, still, supported by impressions generated by successive prior experiences, it will operate even externally, like the operation of the eye aided [by light] with respect to form and the like. Therefore there is no disorder. But this is not so, because [impressions] are causes only of memory. For impressions empowered by prior experience are unable to provide assistance to the mind in the external apprehension; they cause memory alone. For there would follow the apprehension even of objects that are [merely] objects of memory. For there too exists an impression that causes memory. If that [impression] becomes an aid to the mind somewhere in apprehension, then why should it not also apprehend objects that are [merely] objects of memory?—all this amounts to nothing. But he who says: the co-presence of fire and smoke is a relation; and that is known at the very first moment of cognition; and the relation of fire and smoke appears as unlimited by place and time—for one does not have the cognition 'their relation is here and now [only].' Rather, of both that are appearing as present and proximate, place and time are qualifiers, and [one cognizes] 'these two are related'—not 'the relation is here and now.' Thus, a relation of unlimited form, being natural, is established. And when it is natural, there is no occasion for suspecting deviation. What then of repeated observation—is it not a necessary component? It is not unnecessary; but it is a component through the removal of the suspicion of adventitious conditions (<s>upādhis</s>). For fire, even when cognized as conjoined with smoke, is sometimes seen without smoke. There, an adventitious condition such as wet fuel enters. But it is not ascertained that the relation of fire with smoke is natural. And from seeing that, there arises doubt regarding smoke too: perhaps its relation with fire is also sometimes adventitious. That [doubt] is removed by repeated observation. Even when seen many times, no adventitious condition is found in the relation of smoke with fire. And even when sought with effort, no adventitious condition is found—thus it is ascertained that none exists. Thus it is established that fire invariably accompanies smoke alone. And therefore there is no suspicion of deviation for what is non-adventitious. He should be asked: now, is mere co-presence the component of inference, or is the invariable rule [of co-presence] the component? If mere co-presence, then since that is known at the very first observation, even one who sees smoke subsequently without knowing the <s>vyāpti</s> would make an inference. But if it is the invariable rule, then by what means of knowledge is this very [rule] that is being pursued established? For one does not see a cognition arising in the first observer [to the effect] that 'this is invariably connected with that.' If [you say] the relation, being known as unlimited by place and time, is natural, and therefore invariable—then that, being known as such from the very first [observation], should not require repeated observation. Furthermore, even the relation of fire with smoke, as observed, deviates [sometimes]. And from seeing that, doubt about deviation arises regarding smoke too. If [you say] repeated observation is required to remove that—when, even of what is unlimited, separation from some [entity] at some place or time is seen, what then is the confidence regarding other [cases]? But this doubt, it was said, is removed by repeated observation. How is it removed? When fire, known with smoke even a hundred times, is seen without smoke! And there is no invariable rule here that 'with so many observations, non-deviation is established.' But is it not the case that no adventitious condition is found in the relation of smoke with fire, just as none [is found] in fire's relation with smoke? Therefore, how could that [fire] not exist even when smoke exists? No, because place and the like themselves are suspected as adventitious conditions. Having observed the deviation of fire's connection with smoke, one suspects: perhaps there might be an adventitious condition of place, time, and the like in the connection of smoke with fire too. For it is seen that in some places, date palms bear the fruit of pressed dates; and the bite of a scorpion causes death. That does not occur in other places. Similarly, those who suspect that smoke too might sometimes arise even without fire somewhere do not ascertain its invariable connection with fire even to a hundredth degree. Those who suspect exclusion from the counter-positive obstruct the arising of inference—so which is the means of knowledge [that establishes] 'fire is invariably concomitant with smoke alone, and this is non-adventitious'? It is not perception, to begin with, because it is exhausted by mere co-presence. Nor is it inference, because that is impossible when <s>vyāpti</s> has not been established. And if one postulates successive further inferences to establish <s>vyāpti</s>, there would be an infinite regress. Other means of knowledge have already been refuted. Therefore, the means of knowledge for ascertaining the relation that is a component of inference must be explained; [and so] it is explained [as follows]. First, the proponent of the absence of a means of knowledge should be asked: does the cognition directed at <s>vyāpti</s> not arise at all, or does it arise as doubtful, or does it err? For non-validity has been divided threefold by the examiners, since no other mode is possible. The first option is not [tenable], because it contradicts cognition and practical activity. For one is abundantly seen apprehending smoke in fire, preceding the determination 'this is invariably connected with that,' then inferring fire and engaging in practical activity accordingly. That would not be possible if there were no cognition of <s>vyāpti</s>. From the very observation of practical activity, doubt and error must be rejected, since such practical activity is impossible from those two. Therefore, non-validity is not [the case] to begin with. Validity, however, is divided sixfold. We shall establish that as appropriate for someone's [cognition] regarding some <s>vyāpti</s>-cognition. First, just as perception [is the means] for the <s>vyāpti</s> of smoke with fire—for it has been explained that no other means of knowledge is possible here. But it was also stated that perception is impossible at the first observation because of non-apprehension. Precisely for that reason, it is to be known through repeated observation. But those [objections] too were individually considered and refuted, on the ground that neither individual co-presence nor [mere aggregation] is possible. True. <s>Vyāpti</s> is not apprehended from each individual [observation]. Nor do the observations combine [mechanically]. But in the final observation, in the mind assisted by impressions generated by numerous prior observations, there shines the nature of smoke as invariably determined by fire—just as the gem-nature [shines] for one examining [gems], or the true meaning of words for one whose mind is refined by grammar and memory, or Brahminhood for one assisted by the memory of the relation with mother and father, or clarified butter dissolved [in oil and] distinguished from oil for one whose sense is aided by taste and smell. For all this does not appear at the first glance, yet its appearing subsequently is not otherwise [i.e., not illusory]. Nor does it become a different means of knowledge. But it was objected that impressions do not function anywhere other than in memory. By what [evidence] is the function of impressions accepted as operating elsewhere than in memory? They do indeed cause remembering; but they assist the sense that is engaged in producing the <s>vyāpti</s>-cognition, by bringing to mind the previously known connection of smoke with fire. And it has been explained that perception, even when interspersed with intervening memory, follows the connection with the sense-organ, because it follows the non-mediated appearance that is the result of sense-contact. And what does not appear suddenly does not lose its character as perception even when it appears subsequently—as in the very examples cited, [the cognition] 'this is a Brahmin.' But it was stated that perception arising at the first glance is not a means of knowledge for <s>vyāpti</s>. And the determinate perception that follows is preceded by that [indeterminate perception]; so how can it too be valid? Or is there, in the perception of a Brahmin and the like, at the indeterminate stage, an appearance of a form distinct from other persons, as in an elder and so on, by which the subsequent determinate [perception] operates? But just as there, for one who sees merely the physical form, the perception 'this is a Brahmin' arises through the relation with the memory of lineage—so here too, for one who has seen fire and smoke many times, at the final observation, with respect to the particular of smoke apprehended in the indeterminate mode, [there arises] the perception directed at the nature of smoke: 'this is invariably connected with fire.' This alone constitutes the precedence of the indeterminate to the determinate: that the operation preceding the latter's arising is for the purpose of remembering names and such; that is what is first required. And here, that is established by the very observation of the particular instance, since the awakening of prior impressions [occurs then]; so the two need not necessarily have the same object. For precisely this reason, in the cognition of dissolved clarified butter distinguished from oil, the validity as determinate perception is established for the sense aided by smell, even when it erroneously [cognizes] 'this is oil.' For there, there was no unmixed cognition of the form of clarified butter—since there was the error 'this is oil.' Therefore, it is only subsequently, through the force of the auxiliary [condition], that the determinate perception 'this is clarified butter' arises, directed at the particular shown by the indeterminate [perception]. So here too, there is no fault. What then is made the object by the determinate perception here? The invariable rule: 'this is invariably connected with that.' For this one, who has abundantly apprehended smoke in fire and also the negative correlation in the absence of fire, at the end has the reflection: 'perhaps this is pervaded by that.' How otherwise [could one explain that] without regard for the abandonment of numerous places differing in being jungle-land and so on, and without regard for the setting aside of numerous times differing as evening and so on, and without attending to the special co-presence of fuel such as grass, wood, cow-dung, and the like, [smoke] follows fire alone and does not exist in the absence of fire? And furthermore, just as fire, while present in a potter's kiln and such, abandons smokelessness, luminosity, and the like, yet without abandoning heat, is invariably connected with that [heat]—so too [the cognition] 'smoke is invariably connected with fire' arises as a direct and certain cognition. As for what was said about deviation in other places and the like—that has never been seen before, nor heard; so the doubt does not mount. But even for one who doubts thus, there would be lack of confidence in all means of knowledge, since deviation is seen somewhere [for every one of them]. As for the objection that even an ascertained natural invariable connection may turn out otherwise in another place and so on, like the scorpion and the like—that is not so, because of the difference in sub-species. For what has been known as invariably connected with something, and has not been sublated, does not turn out otherwise. Due to the difference in sub-species, the arrangement of effects is caused by the existence and non-existence of capacities; so there is no deviation anywhere. But why is inference itself not simply accepted? Whatever is adventitious deviates, like fire from smoke. But smoke [in relation to fire] is not like that—[it is] non-adventitious. Let it be so. But an infinite regress is at hand. Then let it be <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). This very seeing [of smoke] in fire and non-seeing in the absence of fire, being otherwise inexplicable, establishes the invariable rule with fire. What is inexplicable here? The seeing [of smoke] occurs there [in fire]—that much alone is explained. For it is not the case that what exists in one place must not exist elsewhere. If [you say] the non-seeing of what exists elsewhere is inexplicable—no, because non-seeing is explained by the non-proximity even of other distant [things]. If [you say] the non-seeing in proximate non-fires is inexplicable—[that is explained] by absence. For in those [non-fires], it simply does not exist; how could it be apprehended? [If you say] 'that which exists there should not exist elsewhere either'—what is the means of knowledge for that? Therefore, it should be maintained thus: the ascertainment of the real nature of the thing arises directly for the sense assisted by observation and non-observation. But this is precisely what we do not understand: what kind of nature of the thing is being ascertained? It has been said repeatedly: 'smoke is invariably connected with fire.' This amounts to saying: 'whenever and wherever there is smoke, there and then there is fire.' But let the relation with the proximate present place and time alone be perceptual. How [is the relation with] the future and the like [established]? For if so, there would be over-extension. No, because only the form as proximate is apprehended. But the form of smoke and the like is such that it is thus inferred—like the stable form of walls and the like. For in those, there is a manifestation of form enduring into another time, distinct from lightning and the like. If the proximate subordinate relation is not perceptual, then that form too would be non-perceptual. For if that were non-perceptual, the sublation 'this is not silver' of previously experienced silver would not occur, because the objects would be different. For at its own time, silver was made the object by the prior cognition, and [the silver] will not exist at the moment of the sublating cognition; so how is what is inapplicable there sublated? [It is because] the relation with another time too—the object ascertained by the prior cognition is pervaded even up to the time of the future cognition through that very form—and thus, attaining a common object-hood, sublation occurs. But the form of a thing is known independently of anything else, like the heat of fire. And the form of smoke is not known when the correlate has not been grasped—so how can it be the nature of the thing? Not so. For that [invariable connection] is indeed a relation; how can it be ascertained when the correlate has not been cognized? As it is stated: 'The invariable connection, being a relation, is now stated according to our view.' Therefore, what objection is there to the claim that this invariable connection of smoke with fire, being a positive entity, is apprehended by perception? And that non-occurrence in the absence of fire is not the invariable connection—that has already been explained. But by exclusion from the counter-positive, the invariable connection, being of the nature of a positive entity, is explained by the examiners and communicated to others.
Just as the proximity of <s>Rohiṇī</s> is established by observing the rise of <s>Kṛttikā</s>,

children.text:
nanu niyamyatvamapi karmakārakatvaṃ tacca śaktirūpaṃ kathaṃ pratyakṣam /
na /
kārakāntarapratyakṣavadupapatte' /
kārakāntaraśaktayo 'pi hi na pratyakṣā', ato 'satyeva śaktipratyakṣatve kārakaṃ pratyakṣameṣitavyam /
evamihāpi niyamya' pratyakṣo bhaviṣyatīti
kimanupapannam /
ata' siddhaṃ tāvat pratyakṣatvam /
āgamikeṣu cārtheṣu tasya tasya phalasya tena tena vedavedyen karmaṇā samanvayāt, karmāntarānvayasya cānavagamād anenaiva karmaṇedaṃ phalaṃ vyāptamiti śāstrādadagamyate /
niyatasādhyatvāvagamāt /
meghābhāvavṛṣṭyabhāvayośca svatantrābhāvapratīkāśamākāśasya vapu' saṃlakṣyate /
vṛṣṭyabhāva iti ca pṛthivyā eva
nibiḍakaṭhorapāṇḍurādibhāva' /
tacca rūpamubhayasyāpi pratyakṣasamadhigamyameveti tadeva tatra vyāptipramāṇam /
evamanyatrāpi darśayitavyamiti /
bhavatu tāvadanyad vyākhyāsyāma iti samadhigataṃ tāvad vyāpte' svarūpaṃ pramāṇaṃ ca /
idaṃ tu cintanīyam /
kasya kena vyāptiriti /
na hyekatra viditāvagnidhūmaviśeṣau pradeśāntare dṛśyete /
yat tayorakasyaikenānvayavyatirekasamadhigamyā vyāptirbhavet, ato vācyaṃ vyāpteradhikaraṇam /
ata āha- sāmānyeti /
satyaṃ na viśeṣayorvyāpti', sāmānyātmanoreva dhūmākṛtiragnayākṛtyā niyateti /
children.translated_text: True — there is no <s>vyāpti</s> of the particulars; rather, the smoke-form as universal is invariably connected with the fire-form as universal.
Therefore there is no fault.

children.text: idaṃ tu prāyikam, sthāyinostu viśeṣayorapi kvacid
children.translated_text: But this is the general case. For permanent particulars, however, in some cases
<s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) does exist — so he says: "in some cases."

"But is not the status of being determined — which is the status of being the object of an action — also a form of capacity (<s>śakti</s>)? How then is it perceptible?" No — because it is justified just as the perceptibility of other <s>kārakas</s> (factors of action) is. For the capacities of other <s>kārakas</s> are also not perceptible. Therefore, even when the capacity is not itself perceptible, the <s>kāraka</s> should be accepted as perceptible. Likewise here too, the determined entity will be perceptible — so what is unjustified? Therefore, perceptibility is established for now. And in matters governed by scripture, from the <s>Vedic</s> texts, the invariable connection (<s>vyāpti</s>) of a given result with a given ritual act is ascertained, since the connection with any other act is not apprehended — hence it is understood from scripture that this result is pervaded only by this act. This is due to the ascertainment of the determined means-end relation. And of the absence of clouds and the absence of rain, the form of the sky that appears like the absence of an independent entity is observed. "Absence of rain" here refers to the compact, hard, pale, etc. state of the earth itself. And the form of both is ascertained by perception itself — hence that alone is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) for the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) there. Thus it should be shown in other cases as well. Let that be — we shall explain other matters. So far, the nature and <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>vyāpti</s> have been understood. But this is to be investigated: whose <s>vyāpti</s> with what? For the particular fire and particular smoke observed in one place are not seen in another place. That the <s>vyāpti</s> of one of them with the other, ascertainable through co-presence and co-absence (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), exists — therefore, the locus of <s>vyāpti</s> must be stated. Hence he says — "of the universal" etc.

children.text:
atraivodāharaṇamāha-kṛttikodayamiti /
yatra hi kṛttikodayaṃ dṛṣṭvā rohiṇyāsatti' kathyate- anantaramudeṣyati rohiṇīti, tasminnanumāne viśeṣasyaiva viśeṣeṇa vyāpti' /
na hi tayo' sāmānyamasti /
vyaktibhede pramāṇābhāvāt /
pratyabhijñāyate hi saiveyaṃ kṛttikā, saiveyaṃ rohiṇīti /
kathamanyā bhaviṣyati /
ata' siddhaṃ viśeṣayorevātra vyāptiriti /
yadi tarhi vyāptiranumānām, asti khalvasau hiṃsātvasyādharmatvena bāhyahiṃsāsvityata' kratāvapi hiṃsātvādadharmatvamanumīyate /
tatra ca
children.translated_text: He gives an example of this very point — "the rise of <s>Kṛttikā</s>" etc. For where one, having seen the rise of <s>Kṛttikā</s>, states the proximity of <s>Rohiṇī</s> — "<s>Rohiṇī</s> will rise next" — in that inference, <s>vyāpti</s> is precisely of a particular with a particular. For there is no universal of those two, since there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for difference of individuals. For it is recognized: "this is that very <s>Kṛttikā</s>, this is that very <s>Rohiṇī</s>." How could there be another? Therefore, it is established that <s>vyāpti</s> here is indeed of particulars. If then <s>vyāpti</s> is <s>anumāna</s> (inference), surely it exists between the property of being violent (<s>hiṃsātva</s>) and the property of being <s>adharma</s> (unrighteous) in cases of external violence — and therefore, <s>adharma</s> is inferred in ritual acts too on account of their being violent. With regard to that —

children.text: vyāpteśca dṛśyamānāyā' kaścid dharma' prayojaka' // Msv_5,4.13 //
children.translated_text: And of the <s>vyāpti</s> that is observed, some property is the actual cause;
it is determined through the capacity that 'when this exists, this other must exist';
others depend on <s>vyāptis</s> (pervasions) employed by others.
Even when those are observed, they do not desire the determination of the pervader-aspect;

children.text: ye tu tānapi visrabdhaṃ sādhyasiddhai prayuñjate // Msv_5,4.15 //
children.translated_text: but those who confidently use even such (non-probative reasons) for establishing the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) —

children.text:
daikṣapaśuhiṃsādīnāmadharmatvaṃ prasajyetetyata āha-vyāpteśceti dvayena /
ayamabhiprāya'--- satyāmāpātād bhavati bhrama', yathā kila hiṃsātvamātrānubandhyadharmatvamiti /
natvetadevam /
nirjñātena hyadharmatvena hiṃsātvaṃ vyāpyate /
na ca śāstrādṛte tajjñānopāya' sambhavati /
naca hiṃsātvamātramanarthasādhanamiti śāstramasti /
viśeṣahiṃsāyā vihitatvāt /
vidhyavarūddhaviṣaye ca pratiṣedhānavakāśāt /
pratiṣedhamantareṇa cānarthasādhanatvajñānopāyābhāvāt /
ata' parihṛtyāpavādaviṣayamutsargau'bhiniviśata iti hiṃsāntarāṇi 'na hiṃsyādi'ti pratiṣedho 'valambate /
evaṃ ca yadyapi bāhyahiṃsāsu hiṃsātvādharmatvayo' sāhityamavagataṃ, tathāpi na hiṃsātvamadharmatvaprayojakam /
kintu niṣiddhatvam /
asatyapi hiṃsātve niṣiddhatvamātreṇa surāpānādāvadharmatvasiddhe' /
ato ya evāsmin satyevāsya bhavituṃ śaktirasti ityanena rūpeṇa nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, that which is determined through the capacity 'when this property is present, this other is capable of existing' — in this form,
is understood as the pervaded — that is the meaning.
That very property is called the cause (<s>prayojaka</s>).

children.text: paraprayuktavyāptyujīvinastu hiṃsātvādaya', na tairadharmatvādivyāpakakāṃśo 'vadhārayituṃ kvacidvihitānāṃ daikṣapaśvādihiṃsānāmadharmatvamiti ||14||
children.translated_text: But properties like being violent, which depend on <s>vyāptis</s> employed by others, do not determine the pervader-aspect — namely, that the violence in <s>dīkṣā</s> sacrificial animals and the like, which are enjoined in certain contexts, is <s>adharma</s>.

It would follow that the violence in <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) sacrificial animal-killing and the like is <s>adharma</s> (unrighteous) — hence he says with two verses beginning with "of the <s>vyāpti</s>." The purport is this: When the connection appears prima facie, confusion arises, such as "surely <s>adharma</s> always accompanies the mere property of being violent." But this is not so. For <s>adharma</s> pervades the property of being violent only when it is ascertained. And the means of such knowledge is not possible without scripture. And there is no scripture stating that the mere property of being violent produces undesirable results — because specific acts of violence are enjoined. And in the domain governed by an injunction, there is no scope for a prohibition. And without a prohibition, there is no means of knowing that something produces undesirable results. Therefore, setting aside the domain of exceptions (<s>apavāda</s>), one adheres to the general rule (<s>utsarga</s>) — and so the prohibitions like "one shall not kill" apply to other acts of violence. And thus, although the co-occurrence of being violent and being <s>adharma</s> is observed in external acts of violence, still, the property of being violent is not the cause of being <s>adharma</s>. Rather, being prohibited is the cause. For even in the absence of the property of being violent, <s>adharma</s> is established merely from being prohibited, as in drinking liquor and the like.

children.text:
ye tvevañjātīyakānapyaprayojakān hetūn prayuñjate, te sulabhai' pratihetvādidauṣauściraṃ bhrāmyanti /
śakyate hi pratiheturdarśayituṃ, daikṣapaśuhiṃsādharma' vihitatvādagnihautrādivaditi /
prayojake hi hetāvevañjātīyakā doṣā nāspadaṃ labhante /

children.translated_text: But in a non-probative one, they are easily available.
This is what he states — "but those who" etc.
"Confidently" is a qualifier of the action;

children.text: yathā viśvāso bhavati tathā prayuñjata ityartha' ||15||
children.translated_text: the meaning is: they employ them in such a way that there is trust.

But those who employ such non-probative reasons (<s>hetus</s>) of this kind wander for a long time through faults such as counter-reasons easily available. For a counter-reason can be shown: the violence in <s>dīkṣā</s> sacrificial animals is <s>dharma</s> (righteous), because it is enjoined, like the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like. For in a truly probative reason, faults of this kind find no foothold.
They wander for a long time through faults such as counter-reasons easily available.
In those cases, there is contradiction with scripture, and self-defeat of one's own position.
And non-worldly disputes — those should be avoided by logicians. Therefore,
the <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) of violent acts is argued from their being prohibited.
In the absence of that (prohibition), that (<s>adharma</s>) is not established, since the property of being violent is not the cause.
And when falsity is argued by a pair of reasons for all cognitions —
that which proves the property of being a cognition, or the property of being produced, etc.,
is not the (actual) cause.
And the heaven-producing nature of sacrifices etc. is argued as being restricted to the three <s>varṇas</s> (castes).
It was stated that "they wander through faults such as counter-reasons" — now he presents those very faults: "in those cases" etc.
The counter-reason has already been stated by us.
Contradiction with scripture (<s>āgama</s>) also befalls those who argue thus, since scripture is the sole <s>pramāṇa</s> for <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
In some cases there is self-defeat; in others, non-worldly disputes.
He now gives an example of contradiction with scripture — "by being prohibited" etc.
And this has already been explained by us earlier, by the principle of anticipating future considerations.

children.text:
iṣṭavirodhodāharaṇamāha-hetudvayeti /
bādhakāraṇadoṣādhīnaṃ hi sarvatra mithyābuddhīnāṃ mithyātvam, na ca jñānatvenotpattittvena vā
prayujyate, satyamithyātvasādhāraṇatvādanayo' /
jñānatvādeva tanmithyātvaṃ sādhayato bauddhasyeṣṭavighātakārī hetu', dharmadharmisvarūpasvaviśeṣayorapi pratikṣepāt /
sarvalokaprasiddhapṛthivyādyapalāpāccālokikavivādo 'pyatraiva darśayitavya', na hi sarvavijñānāni mithyetyevaṃvidhaṃ vivādaṃ lokikā' sahante /
sahasaiva hyevaṃvidhavivādaśrāviṇāmudvego jāyate /

children.translated_text: Just as in the statement "the moon is without the moon" (<s>acandraḥ śaśī</s>) and the like.
Therefore, this is a non-worldly dispute.
And thus it has been stated:
"And due to universal consensus, you certainly have a <s>pakṣabādha</s> (thesis-defeat) here."

He gives an example of self-defeat — "by a pair of reasons" etc. For the falsity of all false cognitions depends on the fault of a sublating cognition, and it is not argued on the basis of being a cognition or being produced — since these are common to both true and false cognitions. For the Buddhist who seeks to prove the falsity of all cognitions from the mere fact of being a cognition, the reason (<s>hetu</s>) defeats his own thesis — since it would negate the very nature of both <s>dharma</s> and <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer), and their specific forms. And a non-worldly dispute is also to be shown in this very case, due to the denial of well-known things like earth etc. recognized by all people — for worldly people do not tolerate such a dispute as "all cognitions are false." For upon merely hearing such a dispute, agitation immediately arises in the listeners.

children.text:
aparamapyāgamavirodhasyodāharaṇaṃ darśayati-traivarṇaketi /
santi khalu svargakāmo yajetetyevaṃ vihitāni somādīni karmāṇi /
teṣu kiṃ
children.translated_text: He shows yet another example of contradiction with scripture — "of the three <s>varṇas</s>" etc. There are indeed rituals such as <s>Soma</s> sacrifices enjoined by statements like "one who desires heaven should sacrifice." In those, is the qualification
not argued merely by the property of being human, present also in a <s>Śūdra</s>?
And destructibility, argued through the property of being produced, having parts, etc., is
not argued by reasons similar to cognition immediately following effort.

children.text:
caturṇāṃ varṇānāmadhikāra', utāpaśūdrāṇāṃ trayāṇāmiti saṃśaye caturṇāmiti prāptam, catvāro 'pi hi varṇā' svargaṃ kāmayantara iti svargakāmapadenābhidhīyante /
svargakāmaścātrādhikāritayā jñāyata iti prāpte uktam-- apaśūdrāṇāmadhikāra iti /
vidyāgnisādhyā hi te kratava' /
anagniravidvāṃścāntimo varṇa' /
kathamasau vaitānike karmaṇyadhikriyate /
nanu śrutyarthāvagatādhikārasāmarthyādeva śūdrasyāgnividyayorakṣepo bhaviṣyati /
na /
avidhānāt /
traivarṇakasyaiva 'aṣṭavarṣaṃ brāhmaṇamavupanayīta' 'vasante brāhmaṇo 'gnīnādadhīta' ityevamādibhiragnividye vihite /
na cāniyamenaiva te śūdrasyāpi bhaviṣyata' iti śakyate vaktum /
ko hi pratilabdhavidyāgnisambandhastraivarṇikādhikārasampāditāsu kāmaśrutiṣu niyatakālayovasthamupanayanamādhānaṃ vā jaghanyavarṇasyopakalpayitumutsahate /
atastraivarṇikatvaprayuktameva yāgādīnāṃ svargahetutvam /
na manuṣyatvamātreṇa śūdramavāyinā prayujyate /
tad yadi kaścadanumānakuśala' prayuṅkte śūdrakṛto yāga' svargahetu' manuṣyakṛtatvāt traivarṇikācaritayāgavaditi /
tasyāgamavirodha' /
nanvāgamavirodha udāhṛta eva, kiṃ punastadudāharaṇena /

children.translated_text: It is said:

children.text: pūrvamadharmatvānumānasya vaidikahiṃsāviṣayasya sākṣādāgamavirodho varṇita', vyaktameva daikṣapaśuhiṃsā vidhīyamānatvād arthasādhanamityetadavagamyate, kathamasāvadharmo bhaviṣyatīti, codanālakṣaṇasyārthasya dharmatvāt /
children.translated_text: Previously, the direct contradiction with scripture was described for the inference of <s>adharma</s> concerning <s>Vedic</s> violence — for it is clearly understood that the violence in <s>dīkṣā</s> sacrificial animals, being enjoined, produces desired results; how then could it be <s>adharma</s>? — since what is characterized by injunction (<s>codanā</s>) has the nature of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: iha tu śūdrakṛtasya yāgāde' svargahetutā na sākṣādāgamena pratikṣipyate /
children.translated_text: But here, the heaven-producing nature of a sacrifice performed by a <s>Śūdra</s> is not directly rejected by scripture.
Rather, from the establishment of the three-<s>varṇa</s> qualification, the rest is excluded by implication — that is the distinction.

When there is doubt whether the qualification for the four <s>varṇas</s> exists, or for the three excluding the <s>Śūdra</s>, the prima facie view is that all four are qualified — for all four <s>varṇas</s> do desire heaven, and are thus denoted by the term "one who desires heaven." And when the prima facie view holds that the one who desires heaven is known to be the qualified person — the established conclusion states: the qualification is for the three, excluding the <s>Śūdra</s>. For those rituals require fire and learning (<s>vidyā</s>). And the lowest <s>varṇa</s> is without fire and without learning. How then can he be qualified for solemn (<s>vaitānika</s>) ritual? But might not the exclusion of fire and learning for the <s>Śūdra</s> follow from the very capacity of qualification understood from the meaning of scripture? No — because there is no injunction (for it). Fire and learning are enjoined only for the three <s>varṇas</s> through texts like "one should initiate a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> at eight years" and "a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish the sacrificial fires in spring." And one cannot say that by the absence of restriction these will also apply to the <s>Śūdra</s>. For who would venture to assign to the lowest <s>varṇa</s> the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation) and <s>ādhāna</s> (fire-establishment) — which are fixed as to time and age — in the <s>kāmaśrutis</s> (desire-based injunctions) that are accomplished through the qualification of the three <s>varṇas</s> who have already obtained connection with learning and fire? Therefore, the heaven-producing nature of sacrifices etc. is restricted to the three <s>varṇas</s>. It is not argued merely by the property of being human, which includes the <s>Śūdra</s>. Now, if someone skilled in inference argues: "A sacrifice performed by a <s>Śūdra</s> produces heaven, because it is performed by a human, just like a sacrifice performed by the three <s>varṇas</s>" — his argument contradicts scripture. "But contradiction with scripture has already been exemplified — what is the need for yet another example?"

children.text:
aprayojakodāharaṇacchalenedānīṃ paropālambhānārthamudāharaṇāntarāṇi darśayati---kṛtetidvayena /
prayatnānantarajñānasadṛśā' pratyayānavasthānādayo 'bhimatā' tai' śabdagocaraistasya vināśitā na prayujyate /
kṛtakatvādiprayuktā hyasau /
na ca kṛtakatvameva prayatnānantaradarśanena sādhayituṃ śakyam /
ākāśādibhirvyabhicārāt /
yadi tarhi sāvayavatvaprayuktā vināśitā,
children.translated_text: Now, under the pretext of exemplifying non-probative reasons, for the purpose of refuting the opponent's position, he shows further examples — with two verses beginning with "produced" etc. The cognitions immediately following effort, the non-abiding nature of mental impressions, etc. — accepted by those opponents and within the domain of the word (śabda) — are refuted by these. For that (destructibility) is argued from the property of being produced and the like. And the property of being produced cannot be established merely by the perception of something following effort — because of deviation in cases like <s>ākāśa</s> (space) etc. If then destructibility is argued from having parts —
the property of having a universal (<s>jāti</s>), the property of being an object of sense, etc. — these depend merely on the existence of a real entity.

children.text: śabdānityatvasiddhyarthaṃ ko vaded yo na tārkika' /
children.translated_text: To prove the impermanence of sound — who other than a logician would argue thus?

children.text: tasmād ya eva yasyārtho dṛṣṭa' sādhanaśaktita' // Msv_5,4.22 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever property of a given thing has been seen to have the capacity to prove —

children.text: sa eva gamakastasya na prasaṅgānvito 'pi ya' /
children.translated_text: that alone is its indicator, not what is merely connected by implication.
And the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) too, taken up by the two words 'one part,' is one possessing a part.

children.text:
kimidānīṃ naśvarāṇi bhuvanāni bhuvanasanniveśāśca mahīmahīdharodadhiprabhṛtaya' /
satyam /
sarvameva sāvayavaṃ vināśadharmakam, mahīmahīdharādayo 'pi samāsāditasvāvayavasaṃyogāvibhāgāviśeṣā bhāgaśo naśyantyeva /
niranvayaṃ tu vināśaṃ na kasyacidabhyupagacchāma' /
evaṃ mahābhūmerapyāvāpodvāpabhedānnāśo darśayitavya' /
tathā yadapi vaiśeṣikairjātimattvādaindriyakatvācca śabdānityatvamanumitaṃ, tadapyayuktam /
etaddhi jātimattvādi vastusanmātranibandhanameva nityānityasādhāraṇam, nānenānityatā sādhyate /
children.translated_text: For this property of possessing a universal etc. depends merely on the existence of a real entity, and is common to both permanent and impermanent things — impermanence is not thereby proved.
What does "depending merely on the existence of a real entity" mean? It means: depending on what is ultimately real.
Only ultimately real things — like a pot, space, the self —

children.text: indriyaviṣayā jātimantaśca, na bhrāntisaṃviditā' śaśaviṣāṇādaya iveti ||21||
children.translated_text: are objects of the senses and possess universals, not things cognized through error, like the horn of a hare.

"What then — are the worlds perishable, and the arrangements of worlds such as earth, mountains, oceans, etc.?" True — everything that has parts is subject to destruction. Earth, mountains, etc. too, having attained no distinction from the conjunction and disjunction of their own parts, do perish part by part. However, we do not accept the destruction of anything without residue. Thus, the destruction of even the great earth is to be shown through the distinction of accretion and removal. Similarly, what was inferred by the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> — that sound is impermanent because it possesses a universal and because it is an object of sense — that too is unjustified.

children.text: ayamartha'--- ya eva niṣiddhatvādirartho yasyādharmatvade' sādhanaśaktiyuktatvenāvagata' /
children.translated_text: This is the meaning: The very meaning of being prohibited, etc., whose capacity as a means (<s>sādhanaśakti</s>) has been ascertained as being endowed with the property of being <s>adharma</s> (demerit),

children.text: asmin satyamunā bhavitavyamitīdṛśyā śaktyāvadhāryata iti yāvat /
children.translated_text: is determined through such a capacity, namely, 'when this [prohibition] is present, that [demerit] must exist.'

children.text: niyamyaśaktireva hi sādhanaśaktirityākhyāyate, niyatāvagato hi niyāmakaṃ śankoti (gamayituṃ) nānya iti, (sa) niyamya eva gamako na prasaṅgānvito hiṃsātvādi' /
children.translated_text: For the capacity of the determined entity is itself called the proving capacity (<s>sādhanaśakti</s>); for what is known in a determined manner can indicate the determinant and nothing else. That determinant alone is the indicator, not what is accompanied by [mere] occasion (<s>prasaṅga</s>) — such as the property of being an act of killing.

children.text: niṣiddhatvenānvetumabhipravṛttenādharmatvena prasaṅgāddhi hiṃsātvamapyanvitamiti prasaṅgānvitaṃ hiṃsātvaṃ nādharmatvasya gamakaṃ bhavatīti ||22||
children.translated_text: For when the property of being <s>adharma</s>, which has been adopted as something to be connected with the meaning of prohibition, is also connected with the property of being killing through mere occasion — therefore the property of being killing, being merely associated by occasion, does not serve as an indicator of <s>adharma</s>. // 22 //
Having thus stated the non-probative nature of a non-causing (reason), he concludes — "therefore" etc.

children.text:
evaṃ tāvat sarvaprakāro 'numānāṅgabhūta' sambandhapadārtho vyākhyāta' /
idānīmekadeśadarśanādekadeśāntare buddhiriti vyākhyeyam /
tatra caitadeva tāvad vaktavyam /
svatantraikadeśadarśanāttathāvaidhekadeśāntare jñānamanumānamityāpadyeti /
taccayuktam /
smaraṇaṃ hi tat, kathamanumānaṃ bhavet /
athaika
children.translated_text: Thus far, the meaning of the term 'connection' (<s>sambandha</s>), which is a component of inference, has been explained in all respects. Now, 'the cognition of one part from the perception of another part' is to be explained. And first, this itself must be stated: From the perception of one independently posited part, the knowledge of the other part in the same manner is arrived at as <s>anumāna</s> (inference). But this is not correct, for that is remembrance — how could it be inference? Therefore —
For the forms of smoke and such do not constitute the one-partness with respect to another object;

children.text: sa eva cobhayātmāyaṃ gamyo gamaka eva vā // Msv_5,4.24 //
children.translated_text: and this very [one-part-possessor] is the object to be inferred, being of a dual nature — or is the indicator itself. // Msv_5,4.24 //
because it has not been taken up [in the definition].
For here the one-part-possessor is not taken up by any word.
Therefore, anticipating the objection that the definition is deficient because the one-part-possessor is not taken up, he says — 'taken up' [is to be understood].

children.text: yadyapi svaśabdena naikadeśyupāttastathāpyekadeśaśabdābhyāmevārthādākṣipyata iti na nyūnatvadoṣa iti ||23||
children.translated_text: Although the one-part-possessor is not taken up by its own specific word, nevertheless it is implicitly indicated by the two words 'one part' alone — hence there is no defect of deficiency. // 23 //
If the object of inference is held to be a one-part-possessor (<s>ekadeśin</s>) qualified by one part as distinguished from another part — that is not so,

children.text:
arthākṣepe kāraṇamāha---aparārthaiti /
na hi dhūmādisvarūpamātraparārthībhūtamekadeśapadāspadaṃ bhavati /
na ca parasparāpekṣayaikadeśavācoyuktirupapadyate /
na hyagnyaikadeśo dhūma iti kasyacit pratipattirasti /
children.translated_text: For no one has the cognition that 'smoke is a part of fire.'
Nor can smoke be understood as a part of fire when fire itself has not been apprehended.
And when fire has been apprehended, there is no object left to be inferred.

children.text: ata ekadeśatvānupapattyaiva tadāśraya' kaścidekadeśyavagamyata iti siddhamiti ||23||
children.translated_text: Therefore, precisely because of the impossibility of partness, some one-part-possessor that is its basis is understood — this is established. // 23 //

He states the reason for the implicit indication — 'with respect to another object.' For the mere form of smoke and such, serving another's purpose, is not the basis for the word 'part.' Nor is the usage of 'one part' with respect to mutual reference tenable.

children.text:
nanvākṣipyatāmekadeśaśabdābhyāmekadeśī /
tadekatvaṃ tu kuto 'vagamyate /
ata' kvacidev dhūmaṃ dṛṣṭvā kvacidekadeśyantare 'numānaṃ na syāt /
aikādhikaraṇyaṃ tvekadeśayorna sidhyati, anupādānādityata āha--sa eveti /
pūrvaprakṛtamekadeśavāniti vivakṣitaikasaṅkhyamekadeśinaṃ pratyavamṛśati sa eveti /
sa khalveka evaikadeśī gamyagamakarūpa' ubhayātmakatvāt /
tasya hi tau nāma vakṣyamāṇātmānau sta', yaddvirūpatvamarhati /
nanvekatvaṃ naikadeśinau'nupāttaṃ labhyata ityuktam /
na /
jñātasambandhasyetyekavacanenaivopādānāt /
ekadeśini hyanyapadār(thaikasyair?the e) katvamekavacanenopāttaṃ , pramātṛpakṣe 'pi pabrathamoccaritenaikadeśaśabdena svāśraya ekadeśinyākṣipte dvitīyāpekṣākṣaṇe 'pi sa eva buddhau viparivartamānastadāśrayatvenāvagamyate nānya' /

children.translated_text: Because there is no reason for abandoning that, and because such is the observed manner of usage.

children.text: yathā devadattasyaikakatra kare kaṅkaṇamaṅgulīyakaṃ karāntara iti na bhinna' karāśrahayo 'vagamyate /
children.translated_text: Just as 'a bracelet on one hand and a ring on the other hand of <s>Devadatta</s>' — a different basis for the hands is not understood.
Is then <s>Devadatta</s> one and the same?
Therefore, it is established that there is one and the same one-part-possessor of the dual nature of the inferable and the indicator. // 24 //

Let the one-part-possessor be implicitly indicated by the words 'one part'; but whence is its identity [with the locus] known? Therefore, having perceived smoke somewhere, inference of another one-part-possessor elsewhere would not be possible. But the co-location of the two parts is not established, due to non-employment. Hence he says — 'that very one.' He reflects upon the one-part-possessor with the intended singular number from the previously mentioned one-part-possessor — 'that very one.' That one single one-part-possessor, being of dual nature as both the object to be inferred and the indicator — for its two aspects are those to be described, which deserve the dual nature. But [objection:] the oneness of the one-part-possessor is obtained from non-employment — this has been said. No, because it is already taken up by the singular number in 'of that whose connection is known' (<s>jñātasambandhasya</s>). For in the one-part-possessor, the oneness with the meaning of another word is taken up by the singular number. Even in the cognizer's case, when the one-part-possessor is implicitly indicated by the first uttered word 'one part,' at the moment of the requirement of the second [word], that very same one revolving in the mind is understood as the basis of that — not another.
With the unestablished one part, the inferable; with the established one, the indicator;

children.text: ātta' pṛthagabhinno vā prayoktṝṇāṃ vivakṣayā // Msv_5,4.25 //
children.translated_text: taken separately or as undifferentiated, according to the intention of the users. // Msv_5,4.25 //
'Impermanent because it is produced'; 'possessing smoke, possessing fire' —
the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>) taken as undifferentiated is [one reading]; 'difference here is fire' — such is [the other]. // Msv_5,4.26 //

children.text:
ubhayātmā san gamyagamaka ityuktam /
tāvevobhayātmānau darśayati--asiddheneti /
yadi hyasāvekadeśyasiddha eva syāta siddho
vā, tadā na dvirūpatāṃ labhate /
sa tu dhūmavadādinā rūpeṇa pratyakṣasiddho 'gnimadādinā cāsiddha iti dvyātmakatvādubhayopapattiriti /
āha--- astvarthādupātta ekadeśī /
sa caiko gamyo gamaka iti /
sa tu kathaṃ pramātṛbhirūpādātavya iti /
na ca tadupādānaprakāra' kaścidbhāṣyakāreṇopātta' /
ata' punarapi nyūnatvamityata āha--- ātta iti /

children.translated_text: Where the specification is intended, the taking up of the specification is resorted to.
But here, no specification is intended.
Let it be taken up by the two words 'one part' as either separate or undifferentiated, according to the intention regarding the one-part-possessor and the cognizer.
Because both modes of inferential usage are observed. // 25 //

It was said that being of dual nature, it is both the inferable and the indicator. He shows these two aspects — 'with the unestablished.' For if that one-part-possessor were only unestablished or only established, it would not obtain the dual nature. But it is established by perception through the form of 'possessing smoke' and unestablished through the form of 'possessing fire' — hence, due to its dual nature, both are tenable. He says: Let the one-part-possessor be implicitly indicated; and let it be the single inferable and indicator. But how is it to be taken up by the cognizers? And no manner of taking it up has been provided by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>. Therefore, there is again deficiency — hence he says 'taken.'
He shows that very dual usage — 'impermanent.'
The text is explained by mere recitation. // 26 //

children.text:
ekadeśī gamyo gamako bhedābhedābhyāmupātto iti darśitam /
kiyati punaranumānasya vyāpāra iti bhavati saṃśaya' /
bhavati hi viśiṣṭārthapratītāvapi viśeṣaṇamātraparyavasāyi pramāṇam /
yathā śabda' /
sa khalvākṛtiviśiṣṭāyāṃ vyaktau dhiyamādadhāti, atha cānvayavyatirekābhyāmākṛtimātraparyavasāyīti niścīyate /
tadihāpi yadi tadvadeva viśeṣaṇamātraparyavasāyi pramāṇamiṣyate, tata' siddhasādhyatvam /
siddhaṃ hi sambandhajñānakāle 'gnimātram /
kiṃ tadanumānena /
yadi tu dvikhaṇḍadaṇḍyādiśabdavadviśiṣṭamevānumānaṃ gocarayatītīṣyate /
tatra sambandhagrahaṇābhāvāda(na)numeyatvam /
na hyagnimadviśeṣeṇa parvādinānvito dhūmo dṛṣṭa' /
na ca samastāgnimatsādhāraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: It has been shown that the one-part-possessor, the inferable and indicator, is taken up through both difference and non-difference. Now there arises the question: How far does the operation of inference extend? For even in the cognition of a qualified object, the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) may terminate in the qualifier alone — as in the case of verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>). For it produces cognition with respect to the individual qualified by the universal, and yet it is determined through co-presence and co-absence to terminate in the universal alone. So here too, if the <s>pramāṇa</s> is held to terminate in the qualifier alone, as in that case, there follows the defect of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>). For at the time of apprehending the invariable concomitance, fire alone is already established — what need is there for inference? But if inference is held to have as its object the qualified entity, as in the case of words like <s>daṇḍya</s> ('the punishable') with its two components — then there is no apprehension of the connection, and hence no inferability. For smoke has not been seen connected with a particular fire-possessing location like a mountain. Nor is there any universal connection common to all fire-possessing [locations].
It is the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>) qualified by one part that is inferred here;
for without its dependence [on the substratum], inferability is not possible. // Msv_5,4.27 //

children.text: na dharmamātraṃ siddhatvāt tathā dharmī tathobhayam /
children.translated_text: It is not the property alone that is inferred, since it is already established; likewise the substratum, or both;

children.text: vyastaṃ vāpi samastaṃ vā svātantryeṇānumīyate // Msv_5,4.28 //
children.translated_text: neither separately nor collectively is it inferred independently. // Msv_5,4.28 //
If one part were the mark (<s>liṅga</s>), its invariable concomitance with the provable,

children.text: dvayaṃ ca na syādiṣṭaṃ sat pakṣeṣveṣu yathākramam // Msv_5,4.29 //
children.translated_text: and both, would not hold — as desired in these alternatives, respectively. // Msv_5,4.29 //

children.text:
sāmānyaṃ kiñcitsamasti /
tabhdāve 'pi punarapi siddhasādhyataiva /
ata evāhu'-
"anumāmaṅgapaṅke 'smin nimagnā vādidantina' /
viśeṣe 'nugamābhāva' sāmānye siddhasādhyatā"||
children.translated_text: There is some general feature in common. Even in its absence, there is again the defect of proving what is already established. Hence they say: 'In this mire of the components of inference, the disputant-elephants are sunk — in the particular, there is no invariable concomitance; in the general, there is the defect of proving what is already established.'

children.text:
ityata āha--ekadeśeti /
ayamabhiprāya'--- daṇḍyadiśabdavad viśiṣṭaviṣayamevānumānam /
na ca sambandhagrahaṇābhāva' /

children.translated_text: Because, by abandoning all limiting conditions, the connection of what merely possesses smoke with what possesses fire is understood — this has been stated by us.

children.text: asatyapi sāmānye kenacidekenopādhinānantānāmapi bhāvānāṃ sambandho gṛhyata eva /
children.translated_text: Even without a universal, through some single limiting condition, the connection of innumerable entities is indeed apprehended.

Although 'what possesses smoke possesses fire' is understood in a general way, nevertheless through the re-cognition 'this is that' in the form of a particular, the being an object of a <s>pramāṇa</s> is also established — this has already been stated.

children.text: kasmāt punarviśeṣaṇamātraparyavasāyyeva pramāṇaṃ neṣyate, ata āha--- nahīti ||27||
children.translated_text: Why then is the <s>pramāṇa</s> not accepted as terminating in the qualifier alone? Hence he says — 'for without' [its dependence]. // 27 //

Therefore he says — 'qualified by one part.' The purport is: Like the word <s>daṇḍya</s> ('the punishable'), inference has only the qualified entity as its object. Nor is there absence of apprehension of the connection.
He shows the impossibility itself — 'not the property.'
For 'the property alone is already established at the time of apprehending the connection' — this has been stated by you yourself.

children.text: evameva dharmimātrānumāne svatantrobhayānumāne vā siddhasādhyatā darśayitavyetyāha--- tatheti ||28||
children.translated_text: Similarly, the defect of proving what is already established must be shown for inference of the substratum alone or inference of both independently — hence he says — 'likewise.' // 28 //
He states further defects in the alternatives of the property, substratum, and both as the inferables, in order — 'of one part.' // 29 //
Properties such as impermanence are not [accompanied by] properties such as being-produced;
there is no invariable concomitance of these with sound, nor of both with both. // Msv_5,4.30 //
Nor is the connection, by name or by the sixth case [genitive], taken up in the formulation;
nor is the invariable concomitance of the mark exemplified here. // Msv_5,4.31 //

children.text:
etadeva vivṛṇoti---anityatvādayaiti /
pakṣaikadeśo hi liṅgaṃ bhavati /
na cānityatvākhyasya dharmasya svatantrapakṣīkṛtasya kṛtakatvaṃ dharma iti kathamapakṣadharmo liṅgaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: And when the property called impermanence is independently made the thesis, being-produced is not a property of it — so how will a non-property-of-the-thesis serve as a mark?

children.text: evaṃ dhvanimātre 'pi svatantre kṛtakatvaṃ tatra tatra dhvaniriti niyama' sambhavati /
children.translated_text: Similarly, even when sound alone is independently [the thesis], the invariable concomitance 'wherever being-produced, there is sound' is possible.

children.text: tathobhayasya dhvanyanitayatvātmakasyobhayena pakṣadharmatvānugamātmakena na sambandha ityanāgataṃ sambandhaśabdaṃ pūrvāparābhyāṃ sambandhya tantreṇa vyākhyā kartavyeti /
children.translated_text: Likewise, when both — constituted by sound and impermanence together — [are the thesis], with both — constituted by thesis-property-ness and invariable concomitance — there is no connection. Thus, connecting the word 'connection' (<s>sambandha</s>), which has not yet appeared, with both the preceding and following [words], the explanation is to be given as an integrated reading.

children.text: samadhigataṃ tāvad dharmadharmyubhayeṣāṃ vyastasamastānāṃ na sādhyatvamiti ||30||
children.translated_text: Thus it has been understood that neither the property, nor the substratum, nor both — whether separately or collectively — are the object to be proved. // 30 //
He elaborates on this — 'impermanence and such.' For one part of the thesis is the mark (<s>liṅga</s>).

children.text:
atha kasmād dharmadharmisambandha eva sādhyo na bhavatītyata āha--sambandhaiti /
mitāvati sādhanavākyamapadiśati /
na
khalu parīkṣaka' sādhanavākye samnabdhavācinā kenacinnāmnā ṣaṣṭhyā vā sambandha upādīyate /
na hyevaṃ prayujyate, agniparvatayorasti sambandha' dhūmavattvāditi /
nāpi parvatasyāgniriti /
deśameva tvagnyādinā viśiṣṭamanumimānā dṛśyante /
yadevaṃ prayañjate, agnimān parvata iti /
sambandho 'pi nānumīyata ityatītena sambandha iti /
na paraṃ pratijñāyāṃ nopādīyate, udāharaṇe 'pi na tenānugamo liṅgasya nirdiśyate /
nahi bhavati darśanaṃ, yatra yatra dhūmastatra tatrāgnisambandha iti /
children.translated_text: For the statement 'wherever there is smoke, there is a connection with fire' does not occur.

children.text: bhavati tu yo yo dhūmavān sa so 'gnimāniti deśa eva nidarśanaṃ, tadetadāha---na cāpīti /
children.translated_text: Rather, 'wherever there is smoke-possessor, there is a fire-possessor' — thus the illustration concerns the locus alone. This is what he says — 'nor is ... here.'
'Here' refers back to the formulation.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati-- na sādhanavākye sambandha' sādhyatayopādīyate nāpi dṛṣṭāntatayā dirdiśyate na cāyathāpratibhāsaṃ parīkṣakāṇāṃ vaktumucitamiti ||31||
children.translated_text: What is stated amounts to this: The connection is neither taken up as the object to be proved in the proving statement, nor pointed out as the illustration, and examiners should not speak contrary to how things appear. // 31 //

Now, why is the connection of property and substratum itself not what is to be proved? Hence he says — 'connection.' He indicates the proving statement in the formulation. Surely an examiner does not take up the connection in the proving statement by any name or genitive denoting connection. For the formulation does not run: 'There is a connection between fire and the mountain, because of possessing smoke.' Nor 'fire belongs to the mountain.' Rather, they are seen to infer the locus itself as qualified by fire and such. For this is how they formulate: 'The mountain possesses fire.' The connection too is not inferred — this is [the meaning] of 'connection' in the past [verse]. Not only is it not taken up in the thesis, but even in the example, the invariable concomitance of the mark is not shown through it.
Nor should the two forms of that [one-part-possessor] be what constitutes the provable and the proving;
therefore, since the meaning of the possessive suffix is what is grasped through the meaning [of the words], its cognizability // Msv_5,4.32 //
should not be considered independently, as from words like <s>daṇḍya</s> ('the punishable');
in the cognition of the qualified object, the connection would be a necessary concomitant. // Msv_5,4.33 //

children.text:
api cāyaṃ sambandha' sādhyamāna' sanmātratayā vā sādhyate, kenacid vā dharmeṇa viśiṣṭa' /
na tāvad vastusattāmātramanumānasya viṣaya' /
na ca parvatādivatsiddhasādhyarūpamākāradvayaṃ sambandho vahati, yenānumānasya viṣayo bhavet /
tasmānna kathañcit sambandha' sādhya ityāha---naceti /
kananvasati sambandhe viśiṣṭa eva sādhayituṃ na śakyate /
nāsti nāma sa prakāra', yadasambandhyamāna evāgninā parvatastadviśiṣṭo bhavatītyata āha---- tasmāditi vyāntena /
na(nu) satyamasati sambandhe viśiṣṭo na bhavati, na tvetāvatā sambandhasādhyatā sidhyati, viśiṣṭasādhyatvānyathānupapattyaiva tvarthagṛhītā matubarthasya sambandhasya sādhyatā na puna' svatantrasyeti /
atraiva dṛṣṭāntamāha---yatheti /
daṇḍyādiśabdā hi daṇḍādiviśiṣṭamevābhidadhānā' sambandhamapyarthādupādadate, natvabhidadhati /
tadvadihāpi parvato 'gnimāniti sādhyamāner'thagṛhīto 'gnisambandha', na puna' sa eva sādhyate /
yathā daṇḍyādiśabdato viśiṣṭārthapratītau satyāṃ sambandho nāntarīyako bhavati, evamatrāpi viśiṣṭe sādhyamāne 'nuniṣpādī bhavatītyartha' /
idaṃ tu cintanīyam /
kathaṃ daṇḍyādiśabdā viśiṣṭavacanā iti /
matvarthīyapratyayāntā hite /
sa cāsyāsminnastīti sambandhe smaryate, ata' sambandha evātra pratyayārtha' /
sa ca pradhāna' /
'prakṛtipratyayau pratyayārthaṃ saha brūta' prādhānyena' iti smṛte' /
idaṃ hi bhedenaivobhayarabhidhāne prādhānyapratipādanārthaṃ vacanam /
pradhānaṃ ca śabdārtha' /
ata' sambandhavacanā eva daṇḍyādiśabdā iti yuktam /
