children.translated_text: Moreover, is this relation, when being proved, proved merely as existent, or as qualified by some property? Now, mere material existence is not the object of inference. And the relation does not carry two forms — one established and one to be established — like a mountain and such, by virtue of which it could be the object of inference. Therefore, the relation is not in any way what is to be proved — hence he says 'na ca' (and not). For when the relation does not exist, it simply cannot be proved as qualified. There is indeed no mode [of proof] such that the mountain, even without being related to fire, becomes qualified by it — hence he says 'tasmāt' (therefore), completing the argument. But granted that when the relation does not exist, the qualified [entity] does not come into being; yet this alone does not establish that the relation is what is to be proved. Rather, the provability of the relation — having the meaning of a possessive suffix — is grasped implicitly from the otherwise inexplicability of the provability of the qualified [entity]; it is not [proved] independently. He gives an illustration of this very point — 'yathā' (just as). For words like '<s>daṇḍin</s>' (staff-bearer) and such, denoting specifically that which is qualified by a staff and the like, also include the relation implicitly, but do not denote [the relation itself]. Similarly here too, when 'the mountain possesses fire' is being proved, the relation with fire is grasped implicitly, but it is not itself what is being proved. Just as, when from words like '<s>daṇḍin</s>' the meaning of the qualified [person] is understood, the relation becomes inevitable — similarly here too, when the qualified is being proved, it comes to be produced [as understood] — this is the meaning. But this should be considered: How are words like '<s>daṇḍin</s>' said to denote the qualified? They end in a possessive suffix. And that [suffix] is traditionally glossed as 'that (belongs) to this, (exists) in this' — hence the relation alone is the meaning of the suffix there. And that [relation] is primary. Because the tradition states: 'The stem and suffix together express the meaning of the suffix as primary.' For this statement is meant to teach the primacy when both are denoted separately. And what is primary is the word-meaning. Therefore, it is proper that words like '<s>daṇḍin</s>' denote the relation. Moreover, since 'a cognition of the qualified does not arise without the qualifier being apprehended,' when one intends to denote the qualified, the denotation of the qualifier necessarily comes first — and from that alone the apprehension of the qualified is accomplished; hence one cannot posit that as the denotative power of the word [extending that far]. For this very reason, the denotation of the individual qualified by the universal will be refuted in the <s>Ākṛtyadhikaraṇa</s>. Furthermore, the tradition states: 'In <s>kṛt</s>-formations, <s>taddhita</s>-formations, and compounds, the relation is denoted by <s>tva</s> and <s>tal</s> [abstract suffixes].' And how would the relation be denoted by those two in <s>taddhita</s> formations, if it were not the denotation of the <s>taddhita</s> [suffix itself]? For the tradition [about <s>tva</s> and <s>tal</s>] is for the purpose of extracting the denotation: 'By virtue of whichever quality's existence the word is applied to a substance, that denotation [is extracted] by <s>tva</s> and <s>tal</s>.' So, if the relation of the staff with the person is the denotation of the word '<s>daṇḍin</s>,' then in extracting that denotation, the teaching of <s>tva</s> and <s>tal</s> as in '<s>daṇḍitva</s>,' '<s>daṇḍitā</s>' is justified — just as the universal denoted by the word 'cow' is extracted as 'cow-ness' by the <s>tva</s>-suffix. Therefore, since the relation is the very denotation of words like '<s>daṇḍin</s>,' how can it be said now that the relation is merely 'entailed' [rather than directly denoted]? Here it is replied: First, the denotation-of-relation cannot be determined merely by following the tradition. For [the tradition] is merely a grammatical teaching — 'that (belongs) to this, (exists) in this' (Pāṇini 5.2.94) — not a semantic teaching. Moreover, in the derived form versus the paraphrase, the primary-secondary relationship of [the components] is seen to differ. For instance, in '<s>citragu</s>' (one with variegated cows), in the derived form, <s>Devadatta</s> and such, qualified by variegated cows, is understood as primary. But in the paraphrase 'citrā gāvo yasya' (whose cows are variegated), the cows are primary, and <s>Devadatta</s> and such serve as the qualifier in a subordinate capacity. And those [cows] are primary. In the <s>Veda</s> too: '<s>rathantarasāmā somaḥ</s>' (the <s>Soma</s> with the <s>Rathantara sāman</s>). So even though the tradition-maker, in the paraphrase 'that of this,' designates the relation as primary by means of the genitive case, still in the derived <s>taddhita</s> form like '<s>gomat</s>' (possessing cows), it is the possessor [of the quality] that is primary, since that is how it is understood. For the word '<s>gomat</s>' appears as having the person as primary, not the relation as primary. Even the revered <s>Pāṇini</s> intended to teach the denotation of the qualified through the medium of denoting the relation. In a derived form being analyzed, the use of the genitive is unavoidable. And from just that [genitive], the misconception arises that its meaning is being designated as primary in terms of denotation. Hence, first of all, the denotation-of-relation is not [established] merely by following the tradition. As for the [objection] that the qualifier is denoted first — true. But here the relation is not the qualifier. The staff is the qualifier of the staff-bearer, not the relation. And that [staff] is denoted first by the stem itself. Therefore, there is no fault of postulating multiple denotative powers. For in the case of undivided words like 'cow' and such, even when the qualified is understood, it is proper [to say] that only the qualifier is denoted — for there, the fault of postulating both denotative powers for one and the same [word] would arise. But words like '<s>daṇḍin</s>' have parts [stem and suffix].
These two — having obtained the status of qualifier and qualified — through the two separate [parts, namely] stem and suffix,
Are to be understood [as the inferential object]; but the relation of principal and subordinate is accepted by some as optional. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.34)
In every case, the property of the property-bearer is understood through the property,
But in terms of the qualifier-qualified [relationship], no distinction is ascertained. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.35)

children.text:
viśeṣyāvabhidhīyate iti kimanupapannam /
ata' prakṛtyabhihitaprathamatarāvagatadaṇḍaviśiṣṭa' puruṣo daṇḍiśabdenābhidhīyate /
nanvasati sambandhe daṇḍoviśeṣṭumeva naraṃ na śaknoti /
satyam /
na tvetāvatā sambandho vācyo bhavati /
na hi pṛthivyāmanavasthitā gāvo na tadvantaṃ viśiṣantīti pṛthivyapyabhidhīyata iti yuktamabhidhātum /
yata eva tvasati sambandhe viśiṣṭāvagatiranapapannā, ata eva sambandho 'pyarthādantarbhāvyate /
na tvabhidhīyate /
yattu sambandhābhidhāne tvataloranuśāsanamasati sambandhavācyatve 'nupapannamiti, tadayuktam /
na hyabhidheyaniṣkarṣe gomadādiṣu bhāvapratyayānuśāsanam, api tarhi abhidheyaniṣkarṣe hi 'yasya guṇasya hi bhāvādi'ti tvabhidheyāniṣkarṣārthameva smaraṇam /
itarathā tvanenaiva gatārthatvāt kṛttaddhitasamāseṣvatyavacanīyamāpadyeta /
ata' prāk pratīte ekanimittasambandhiviśiṣṭe 'parasmin sambandhinyabhihiter'thagṛhīta' sambandho nābhidheyapakṣe nikṣipyate /
sarvayaugikānāmapi caiṣaiva dig darśayitavyā /
āha ca--
sarvatra yaugikai' śabdairdravyamevābhidhīyate /
na hi sambandhavācyatvaṃ sambhavatyatigauravāt||
children.translated_text: The qualified is being denoted — what is untenable in this? Therefore, the person — already apprehended first through the stem as qualified by the staff — is denoted by the word '<s>daṇḍin</s>.' Objection: Without the relation existing, the staff simply cannot qualify the person. True. But this alone does not make the relation a denotatum. For it is not proper to say: 'Because cows standing on the earth do not qualify that possessor [without the earth], therefore the earth too is denoted.' Rather, precisely because the apprehension of the qualified is impossible without the relation, the relation too is included implicitly — but it is not denoted. As for [the objection that] the teaching of <s>tva</s> and <s>tal</s> for denoting the relation is untenable without the relation being the denotatum — that is improper. For the teaching of bhāva-suffixes in words like '<s>gomat</s>' is not for the extraction of the denotatum; rather, the tradition 'by virtue of whichever quality's existence...' [concerning <s>tva</s> and <s>tal</s>] is precisely for the purpose of extracting the non-denotatum [i.e., making it expressible]. Otherwise, since the meaning would already be achieved by the [previous] rule alone, the rule 'in <s>kṛt</s>-formations, <s>taddhita</s>-formations and compounds' would become unnecessary. Therefore, when the qualified entity — qualified by the other relatum — is first apprehended through its single cause [the stem], and the other relatum is [then] denoted [by the suffix], the relation grasped implicitly is not to be placed in the category of denotatum. And the same direction should be shown for all etymological [words]. He also says: 'In all cases, with etymological words, it is the substance alone that is denoted. For denotation of the relation is not possible, due to excessive cumbersomeness.'
Thus.

Therefore, since there is no possibility of another object of inference, the property and property-bearer — which stand in the relation of qualifier and qualified — are the two things to be comprehended through inference. (32-33)

children.text:
upasaṃharati---- viśeṣaṇeti gamyāvityantena /
sa cāyamaṅgāṅgibhāva' kaiścid vikalpenāśrita' /
evaṃ hi manyante /
sarvathā hi dharmamātre dharmaṇi vā svatantre pramīyamāṇe siddhasādhyatādidoṣo bhavati kana viśiṣṭapramāyām /
viśiṣṭatā tu kadācit kasyacid yathābhiprāyaṃ bhavatu nāma, na kiñcid duṣyati /
sarvathā tāvat dharmiṇa eva parvatāderagnyādidharmastaddharmeṇaiva dhūmādināvagantavya' /
sa tu dharmo viśeṣaṇabhūto viśeṣyabhūto
children.translated_text: He concludes — from 'viśeṣaṇa' to the end 'gamyāv.' And this relation of principal and subordinate is accepted by some as optional. For they hold thus: In every case, when either the property alone or the property-bearer alone is independently cognized, the fault of proving what is already established and such arises, but not in the cognition of the qualified [complex]. But the qualified-nature may sometimes, for someone, be according to their intention — that is not harmful. In every case, at any rate, the property of the property-bearer such as the mountain — namely fire and such — is to be understood through that very property [i.e., the inferential mark] such as smoke. And that property, whether treated as the qualifier or as the qualified —
Others state a reply here: If the property-bearer is [taken as] the qualifier,
The relation of the probans-property with it is unclear, due to its being subordinate. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.36)
Since the property is primary, the relation [of the probans] with the property would arise from the sentence;

children.text: tatrāsambhavata' paścāt kalpyo 'sau dharmiṇā saha // Msv_5,4.37 //
children.translated_text: Where that [direct sentential connection] is not possible, thereafter [the relation] is to be constructed with the property-bearer. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.37)
— or [as the qualified] — is to be understood, and there is no distinction.
Since in either case there is no independent inference [of just one], he says — 'aṅga' (component), to be completed by the end-word [of the verse]. (34-35)

children.text:
atra dūṣaṇamāha---atreti /
ayamabhiprāya'--- laukikāni hi pramāṇāni lakṣaṇakārairapi yathālokamevānugantavyāni /
na tu viparītam /
nahyagni' parvataviśiṣṭa iti loko budhyate /
api tu parvato 'gnimāniti /
tathā svayamanumānena pratipannimarthaṃ tenaiva paraṃ pratipādayanto laukikā dharmaṇā viśiṣṭameva hetuṃ prayuñjānā dṛśyante, yathāgnayanumāni eva dhūmavattvādagnimāniti /
taccedamagnau deśena viśiṣṭe 'numīyamāne nopapadyate /
viśeṣaṇatayā hi parvataviśiṣṭo 'gniriti dharmiṇyupātte dhūmavattvāditi hetudharmeṇa tasya sambandho na sphuṭaṃ prakāśate /
dharmadharmitayāvagatasya hetutvam /
na ca guṇabhāvopātto dharmī hetudharmasambandhamarhati,
guṇānāṃ parasparāsambanadhāt /
ato 'smāt parārthahetuprayogaviśeṣādeva laukikānāmīdṛśī pratipattirunnīyate /
yat svayamapi dharmaviśiṣṭameva dharmiṇaṃ budhyate na viparītamiti ||36 || yadi tarhi dharmiṇo hetudharmeṇa sambandho na sphuṭa' kena tarhi prasajyata ityata āha--pradhānatvaditi /
dhvaniviśiṣṭamanityatvaṃ kṛtakatvādityucyamāne 'nityatvākhyena dharmeṇaiva sādhyatayā pradhānabhūtena kṛtakatvādihetu' sambadhyeta na dhvaninā guṇabhūtena /
sarvasya hyekavākyagatasya pradhānānvaya eva yukta' /
pradhānasambandhe ca hetorapakṣadharmatvam /
nahi kṛtakatvama
children.translated_text: He states the objection here — 'atra' (here). The intention is as follows: For even the definers of valid means of cognition must follow the valid means of cognition as they operate in ordinary life, not the reverse. For ordinary people do not think 'fire is qualified by the mountain'; rather, [they think] 'the mountain possesses fire.' Likewise, when communicating to others the object they have themselves ascertained through inference, ordinary people are seen to employ the probans qualified by the property — for instance, in inferring fire, [they say] 'from possessing smoke, [the mountain] possesses fire.' But when fire, qualified by a location, is what is being inferred, this does not work. For when the property-bearer is taken as the qualifier and 'fire qualified by the mountain' [is the formulation], the relation of the probans-property 'possessing smoke' with that [fire qualified by mountain] is not clearly manifest. For what is known in the relation of property and property-bearer is what serves as the probans. And the property-bearer, taken as subordinate, does not merit a relation with the probans-property, since subordinate elements are not mutually related. Therefore, from this very distinguishing feature in the formulation of the probans for the sake of others, the ordinary understanding is inferred: that one understands the property-bearer as qualified by the property, not the reverse. (36) If, then, the relation of the probans-property with the property-bearer is not clear, by what [relation] does it hold? Hence he says — 'pradhānatvāt' (because of being primary). When one says 'sound, qualified by being of the nature of a pot, is impermanent because of being produced,' the probans 'being produced' is related to the property 'impermanence' alone — which is primary as the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) — not to 'sound,' which is subordinate. For the concomitance of everything within one sentence with the principal [element] alone is proper. And when the probans is related to the principal, it fails to be a property of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus). For 'being produced' is not a property of impermanence —
— but of sound. Otherwise it should be stated that in the case of non-concomitance,

children.text: bhedopāttasya dharmasya guṇabhāvo na duṣyati // Msv_5,4.38 //
children.translated_text: The subordinate status of the property taken up separately [by the expression] is not a fault. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.38)

children.text:
nityatvasya dharma', kiṃ tarhi dhvane' /
ato dharmyeva dharmaviśiṣṭa' svayaṃ pramātṛbhiravagamyate /
tathaiva parasmai pratipādyata iti yuktamiti /
yadi tūcyate, satyaṃ pradhānatayā dharmeṇa heto' sambandho vākyādavagamyate, liṅgabalīyastvena tu vākyaṃ bādhitvā dharmiṇaiva sambandha' kalpayiṣyate /
hetudharmasya hi dharmiṇaiva sambandhayogyatā na dharmeṇa, ato dharmasambandhābhāvād dharmiṇaiva sambandho bhaviṣyatītyata āha--- tatreti /

children.translated_text: The intention is: True, the relation with the property is indeed established in this way.
But this very difficulty — namely the disruption of the natural flow of the sentence —
Hence he says — 'kalpyo 'sau' (it is to be constructed).
To construct otherwise what was understood in one way is itself the fault — such is the purport. (37)

Impermanence is a property — of what? Not of sound. Rather, the property-bearer itself, qualified by the property, is understood by the cognizers themselves, and is communicated to others in the same way — this is proper. But if it be said: True, the relation of the probans with the property arises from the sentence as primary, but by the force of the inferential mark, overriding the sentence, the relation will be constructed with the property-bearer. For the probans-property is fit to be related to the property-bearer alone, not to the property; hence, from the absence of a relation with the property, the relation will be with the property-bearer alone — hence he says 'tatra' (there).

children.text:
dhvane' kṛtakatvāditi vā punardharmyupādānena heturviśeṣaṇīya', na caivaṃ prayoktāra' prayuñjānā dṛśyanta ityabhiprāyeṇāha---dhvaneriti /
yastu vadati dharmiṇyapi viśeṣṭe sādhye 'nvayopadarśanavelāyāṃ yatra yatra kṛtakatvamityukte dhvanireva pradhānatayā sambadhyeta nānityatvaṃ guṇabhūtatvādititaṃ pratyāha---anvayasyeti /
anvayopadarśanakāle hi bhedenaiva dharmamupādadate /
yatra yatra kṛtakatvaṃ tatra tatrānityatvamiti na tatra pradhānasambandhāśaṅkā /
ata' pratijñāvasthāyāṃ dharmaviśiṣṭe dharmiṇi sādhyamāne yoguṇabhāva āsīt nāsau dṛṣṭāntavākye duṣyati /
hetustvaviśiṣṭa eva tārkikai' prayujyata ityuktam /
tatrāviśeṣita eva prayukte bhavati pradhānabhūtadharmasambandhāśaṅketi /
yastu vadati ṣaṣṭhyantena dhvaninānityatvaṃ viśeṣyate dhvaneranityatvamiti /
evaṃ ca kṛtakatvādityasyāvipariṇatavibhaktikena dhvaninaiva sambandha' sphuṭo bhavati /
dharmasambandha eva yathāvad vibhaktivipariṇāmena syāt /
sa cānyāyya iti sa vaktavya' /
nirākṛto 'yaṃ pakṣo vārtikakṛtaiva---
"sambandho 'pyanupādānānnāmnā ṣaṣṭhyapi vā mitau"
iti /
ṣaṣṭhīnirdeśe hi sambandha eva sādhyo bhavet /
tasya ca sādhyatā nirākṛtaiva /
viśiṣṭasādhyapakṣa eva sthitvā dharmiviśiṣṭatā dharmasyedānīṃ
children.translated_text: Or else, [from the formulation] 'of sound, because of being produced,' the <s>hetu</s> (logical reason) is to be qualified by the mention of the <s>dharmin</s> (subject). But proponents are not seen employing it in this way — this is the intention behind the statement 'dhvaneḥ' etc. But he who says that when the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) is also qualified by the <s>dharmin</s>, at the time of showing positive concomitance, when one says 'wherever there is being-produced,' it is sound alone that would be primarily connected, not impermanence, because impermanence is subordinate — to this he replies with 'anvayasya' etc. For at the time of demonstrating positive concomitance, one takes up the property as distinct: 'wherever there is being-produced, there is impermanence' — hence no suspicion of primary connection arises. Therefore, in the stage of the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>), when the <s>dharmin</s> qualified by the <s>dharma</s> is being proved, the subordinate status [of impermanence] obtained; but that is not vitiated in the illustrative statement. The <s>hetu</s> is employed by logicians without qualification — thus it has been said. When it is so employed without qualification, there arises the suspicion of connection with the primary property. But he who says that impermanence is qualified by sound through the genitive case ending — 'the impermanence of sound' — and thus the connection of 'because of being produced' with sound, whose case-ending has not been transformed, becomes clear; the connection with the property would only be through proper case-ending transformation; and that is improper — so he should say. This position has been refuted by the author of the <s>Vārttika</s> himself: 'Even the relation, through non-mention of the name or even with the genitive, in inference.' For in the genitive indication, the relation itself would become what is to be proved. And the provability of that has already been refuted. Standing in the position that the <s>sādhya</s> is qualified, the qualification of the <s>dharma</s> by the <s>dharmin</s> is now [to be examined]—
If the spatial qualification of fire [is what is to be proved], this is not the definition of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis);
its qualification by space would be of such a kind. // Msv_5,4.39 //

children.text: yo 'gni' so 'sti kvaciddeśe yo dṛṣṭo yatra tatra vā /
children.translated_text: Whichever fire exists in some place, or whichever was seen wherever,

children.text: agni' pūrvānubhūto vā deśamātreṇa saṅgata' // Msv_5,4.40 //
children.translated_text: or fire previously experienced, connected merely by space— // Msv_5,4.40 //

children.text: yo 'gni' so 'nena yukto vā yo dṛṣṭo 'nena so 'thavā /
children.translated_text: whichever fire is connected with this [space], or whichever was seen, that one, or

children.text: yo 'yaṃ sa deśamātreṇa yukta' pūrveṇa vāpyayam // Msv_5,4.41 //
children.translated_text: this one here, connected merely by space, or this very one with the previous [space]— // Msv_5,4.41 //
or 'this fire which is qualified by this space' — in this matter, however,

children.text: pūrvayo' siddhasādhyatvaṃ pareṣu syād viruddhatā // Msv_5,4.42 //
children.translated_text: in the first two, there is the fault of proving what is already established; in the others, there would be contradiction. // Msv_5,4.42 //
<s>Vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of all fires with this space is not possible,

children.text: nāpi pūrvasya nāpyeṣa vahni' sarvairviśeṣyate // Msv_5,4.43 //
children.translated_text: nor is this fire qualified by all [spaces], nor [is there pervasion] of the previous [fire]. // Msv_5,4.43 //
This is refuted.
Why is the provability of the relation being raised again here?
Enough of this childish talk! // 38 //
Moreover, if the spatial qualification of fire is what is to be proved, the impossibility of all the forthcoming types of thesis is also [to be shown] — thus he says 'agneḥ' etc.
The particle 'ca' is for accumulating further objections.
'Etad' refers back to the characteristics about to be stated.
He briefly proposes to state those very types of thesis. // 38 //

children.text:
idānīṃ vibhajya tāneva darśayati---yo 'gniritītītyantena /
nigadavyākhyāto grantha' /
vivekastu pakṣāṇāṃ praṇihitairavagamyata iti /

children.translated_text: Here, in the first two theses, the fault is that of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>).

children.text: siddho hi kvacidagni', dṛṣṭapūrvo 'pi pūrvadeśādhikaraṇa' siddha eva kiṃ tat pra(sā)dhānena /
children.translated_text: For fire existing somewhere is already established; even previously seen fire, having a prior location as its locus, is already established — what is the point of proving it?

children.text: pareṣu tu pañcasu pakṣeṣu pramāṇāntaravirodha ityāha--- iha tviti /
children.translated_text: In the remaining five theses, there is contradiction with other <s>pramāṇas</s> — thus he says 'iha tu' etc.
The fault of proving what is already established is quite obvious. // 40-42 //
He now shows those separately, with the passage beginning 'yo 'gniḥ' etc. The text is explained by recitation. The discrimination of the theses is to be understood by the attentive.
He elaborates the contradiction — 'vyāptiḥ ita' etc.

children.text: yattāvat yo 'gni' so 'nena yukta ityuktaṃ tadayuktam /
children.translated_text: What was said — 'whichever fire is connected with this' — that is improper.

children.text: nahyanena deśena sarvāgnayo vyāpyante deśasyāvaibhavāt sarvāgnīnāṃ cātrāsannidhānāt, tadbhāvo hyatrābhāvena virudhyata iti ||42||
children.translated_text: For all fires are not pervaded by this space, since the space is not omnipresent and all fires are not present here; being such here is contradicted by absence there. // 42 //

children.text: deśai' pūrveṇa vāpyasya na deśena viśeṣyatā /
children.translated_text: Neither by other spaces nor by the previous one can this [fire] be qualified by space;
'This, qualified by this space' — how can this be said? // Msv_5,4.44 //
When fire is ascertained independently of space as 'not this,'

children.text: agne' pūrvataraṃ cātra deśa evāvadhāryate // Msv_5,4.45 //
children.translated_text: and prior to fire, space alone is ascertained here— // Msv_5,4.45 //
the space cognized at the time of that knowledge would not be a qualifier;
of space — such as a mountain — in its own nature, apart from fire— // Msv_5,4.46 //

children.text:
yo dṛṣṭo 'nena so 'thaveti yaduktaṃ dūṣayati---nāpi pūrvasyeti /
dṛṣṭasyāpyagneranena deśena vyāptirna vidyata ityartha' /
yo 'yaṃsa deśamātreṇetyatra dūṣaṇamāha---nāpīti deśairantena /
na hyeṣa pura'sthito vahni' sarvairdeśairviśeṣyate sarvatra tasyābhāvāditi /
children.translated_text: For this fire standing before us is not qualified by all spaces, since it is absent everywhere [else].
For 'or this very one with the previous' — he states the contradiction with 'pūrveṇa' etc.

children.text: pūrveṇa deśenāsyāgnerviśeṣyatā nāstyeva, pūrvadeśasyātrābhāvāt, asya ca tatra /
children.translated_text: There is simply no qualification of this fire by the previous space, since the previous space is absent here, and this [fire] is absent there.

children.text: pūrvānubhūtasya tvagnerdeśamātreṇa sambandha' pura'sthitavahne' sarvadeśasambandhanirākaraṇenaiva tulyanyāyatayā nirākṛta iti na pṛthagupanyasya dūṣita iti ||43||
children.translated_text: And the connection of previously experienced fire with space alone has been refuted by the same reasoning as the refutation of the connection of the fire standing before us with all spaces — hence it is not separately stated and refuted. // 43 //

What was said 'whichever was seen, that one, or' — he refutes this with 'nāpi pūrvasya' etc. The meaning is: even of previously seen fire, there is no <s>vyāpti</s> with this space. For 'this one here, connected merely by space' — he states the objection with 'nāpi' through 'deśaiḥ' etc.

children.text:
evaṃ saptasu pakṣeṣu nirākṛteṣvaṣṭama' pakṣo 'vaśiṣyate etaddeśaviśiṣṭo vā yo 'yamagniriti tannirākaroti--- etaditi /
ayaṃ pura'sthito 'gniranena deśena viśiṣṭa' sādhyata iti sa vaktavya' /
svadeśakālavartyeva smaraṇena viṣayīkṛta' kathamasāvanena deśena viśeṣṭuṃ śakya' /

children.translated_text: By one who speaks thus, even 'nor of the previous' has not been considered.

children.text: anavacchinnasmṛtāvapi ca dharmo dharmiṇo viśeṣaṇamiti nedaṃ yuktisādhyam /
children.translated_text: And that a property is a qualifier of the <s>dharmin</s> even in an undetermined memory is not to be established by mere reasoning.
Because properties are always apprehended precisely as qualifiers of the <s>dharmin</s> — enough of this!

children.text: deśa eva tu pūrvāvagato viśeṣyatāmarhatītyabhiprāyeṇāha--- agneriti ||44-45||
children.translated_text: Space alone, previously apprehended, deserves to be the subject of qualification — with this intention he says 'agneḥ' etc. // 44-45 //

When seven theses have thus been refuted, the eighth thesis remains: 'or this fire which is qualified by this space' — he refutes this with 'etad' etc. This fire standing before us is to be proved as qualified by this space — so it must be said. But it exists only in its own space and time, and is objectified by memory — how then can it be qualified by this [other] space?

children.text:
yadi cāgnirviśeṣyo bhavet tatastasyaivāyamādyo jñānakālo bhavet, prasiddhasyāprasiddhena viśeṣaṇāt /
iha tvādau parvata eva jñāyate /
kathamasau paścāt pratyeṣyamāṇasyāgnerviśeṣaṇaṃ bhavatītyāha---tajjñāneti /
tadavṛttenāgniṃ nirdiśati /
agnerjñānakāle hi sa eva deśo buddha',nāgni', ata' kasya
children.translated_text: And if fire were the subject to be qualified, then this would be the first moment of its cognition, since what is established is qualified by what is unestablished. But here, first the mountain alone is cognized. How then can it be a qualifier of fire which is to be cognized later? — thus he says 'tajjñāna' etc. He designates fire by its non-occurrence [at that stage]. For at the time of the cognition of fire, that very space is [already] cognized, not fire; hence, of what [is it a qualifier]?
When fire has been grasped, the subsequent cognition of [space] qualified by fire is not faulty;

children.text: tasmāt dharmaviśiṣṭasya dharmiṇa' syāt prameyatā // Msv_5,4.47 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) qualified by the <s>dharma</s> (property) should be the object of valid cognition. // Msv_5,4.47 //
That [object of valid cognition] has been conceived by others as the space qualified by fire, or smoke,

children.text: nanu śabdavadeva syāt liṅgagamyaṃ viśeṣaṇam // Msv_5,4.48 //
children.translated_text: but surely, just as with words, the qualifier should be what is to be known through the inferential mark. // Msv_5,4.48 //
Not so; for here there is no postulation of multiple capacities of the inferential mark,
nor is it the object to be inferred; and the qualified [subject] has already been ascertained. // Msv_5,4.49 //

children.text:
deśo viśeṣaṇaṃ bhavati /
pramitaṃ hi vastvapramitena dharmeṇa pramitsitaṃ bhavati kakīdṛgdharmo 'yamiti /
tathā cadeśa iti sa eva pramitsyate, pramīyate ca, na punaragniriti /
children.translated_text: And thus space is what is both sought to be cognized and cognized — not fire.

children.text: nanu deśo 'pi pratyakṣāvagata eveti kakathamasāvanumānasyaviṣayo bhaviṣyatītyata āha--- deśasyeti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But space too is cognized by perception — so how can it be the object of inference? Therefore he says 'deśasya' etc.

children.text: svarūpamātrameva hi deśasya pratyakṣeṇāvagatam, anumānena tu pāvakādiviśiṣṭatā tasyānumīyata iti na gṛhītagrāhitvamiti /
children.translated_text: For the mere own-nature of space is cognized by perception, but by inference its qualification by fire and such is inferred — so this is not apprehending what is already apprehended.

children.text: ato dharmyeva dharmaviśiṣṭa' prameya' na dharmo dharmiviśiṣṭa ityāha---tasmāditi ||46-47||
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) itself, qualified by the <s>dharma</s> (property), is the object of valid cognition — not the <s>dharma</s> qualified by the <s>dharmin</s> — thus he says 'tasmāt' etc. // 46-47 //
Space is the qualifier. For a thing already cognized becomes the object of further cognition through an uncognized property — 'what kind of property does this have?'

children.text:
evaṃ ca deśa evāgniviśiṣṭa' prameyo 'vatiṣṭhate /
sa hi dharmī, tadāśrayatvādagne' /
na tvagni', atadāśrayatvād
deśasyetyāha---sā deśasyeti /
anye tu pūrvāvagatadhūmamapyagniviśiṣṭamanumānasya prameyaṃ manyante /
tadapi sādhvevetyabhiprāyeṇāha---dhūmasyānyaiśca kalpiteti /
sā prameyateti sambandha' /

children.translated_text: Here he raises an objection — 'nanu' etc.
It has been said that what is qualified is the object of inference.
By the principle of the unapprehended qualifier, the inferential mark too, like words, should appropriately result in [apprehending] only the qualifier.

children.text: śabdo hi viśeṣaṇamātra eva vartata ityākṛtyadhikaraṇe vakṣyata iti ||48||
children.translated_text: For words function only with respect to the qualifier — this will be stated in the <s>Ākṛtyadhikaraṇa</s>. // 48 //

And thus space itself, qualified by fire, remains as the object of valid cognition. For it is the <s>dharmin</s>, since fire depends on it. But fire is not [the <s>dharmin</s>], since space does not depend on it — thus he says 'sā deśasya' etc. Others, however, consider that even previously apprehended smoke, qualified by fire, is the object of inference. This too is quite right — with this intention he says 'dhūmasyānyaiśca kalpitā' etc. 'That provability' is the connection.

children.text:
pariharati---naivamiti /
kāraṇamāha---nahīti /
anekaśaktikalpanābhayena hi śabdasya viśeṣaṇamātraparyavasānamiṣṭam /
liṅgaṃ tu pūrvāvagatapratibandhavalena pratibandhakadhiyamupakalpayati /
tad yāvataiva pratibaddhamavagataṃ dhūmavattvaṃ pratibaddhamavagatamityagnimattvamevānumāpayatīti na kaścit doṣa iti /
na ca viśeṣaṇamātramanumeyaṃ siddhasādhyatvādityuktamityābhiprāyeṇāha---
children.translated_text: He answers — 'naivam' etc. He states the reason — 'na hi' etc. For it is out of the fear of postulating multiple capacities that the termination of words in the qualifier alone is accepted. But the inferential mark, by the force of previously apprehended invariable concomitance, produces the cognition of invariable concomitance. As much as smoke-possession is apprehended as invariably concomitant, so it indicates fire-possession — hence there is no fault. Nor is the qualifier alone the object of inference, because of proving what is already proved — this has been said — with this intention he says—
And because it is unknown in its qualified form, the inferability belongs to that alone.
Objection: But if smoke is what is qualified, then the <s>hetu</s> would be a part of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis). // Msv_5,4.50 //
This is not so; for when the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) is a particular, with a general <s>hetu</s>,
in the smoke, its knowledge, the relation, and the memory — in establishing their authority— // Msv_5,4.51 //
the unity of object with the result, from the operation of those, has been stated earlier;

children.text: prameyadhī' pramāṇaṃ hi bhāṣyakārastu manyate // Msv_5,4.52 //
children.translated_text: the cognition of what is to be measured is the <s>pramāṇa</s> — thus the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> considers. // Msv_5,4.52 //

children.text: na ceti viśeṣyo 'pi parvātadisvarūpeṇāvadhārita' so 'pi nānumeya ityāhaviśeṣya iti ||49||
children.translated_text: 'Na ca' — even the qualified [subject], ascertained in its own nature as mountain and such, is not to be inferred — thus he says 'viśeṣyaḥ' etc. // 49 //

children.text:
ato viśiṣṭatvenaiva rūpeṇājñānāt tasyaivānumeyatvamityāha---viśiṣṭatveneti /
atra codayati--- nanviti /
dhūmo 'pyagniviśiṣṭo 'numīyata ityuktaṃ, tadayuktam /
pratijñārthaikadeśatvāditi /
pariharati---naitaditi /
sāmānyaviśeṣyatātmā hi dhūma', tatra viśiṣātmanā pakṣīkṛtasya sāmānyatmanā hetutvamiti na pakṣaikadeśateti /
samadhigataṃ tāvadanumānasya viśiṣṭo viṣaya iti, svarūpameva kimasyeti na jñāyate /
tad yadi dhūmatajjñānādīnāmanumānatvamiṣyate, tata' pramāṇaphalayorviṣayabheda' sa cāyukta' /
ata eva bhikṣuṇā ekameva jñānaṃ pramāṇaphalarūpamiti pratyakṣamuktvā tadevānumāne 'pyatidiṣṭaṃ pūrvavat phalamasyeti /
yaditvanumeyajñānameva pramāṇamiṣyate tato 'pyatiriktaphalābhāva' /
ato vaktavyamanumānasya svarūpamityata āha--- dhūmatajjñāneti /
yattāvat bhikṣuṇā pramāṇa(phala?)meva phalamityekaviṣayatvalābhāvadāśritaṃ, tat pratyakṣavadihāpi pratiṣeddhavyam /
na hi sādhyarasādhanayorabhedaṃ laukikā manyante /
ko hi vṛkṣācchidayā sārdhaṃ paraśorekatvamātiṣṭhate /
viṣayabhedaparihārastu pratyakṣokta evehāpyanusandhātavya' /
yathā hīndriyādipramāṇapakṣe yatra phalaṃ niṣpadyate tadviṣayavyāpārāt samānaviṣayatvamupapāditam /
evamihāpi dhūmādipramāṇapakṣe tadvyāpārādeva puroditaṃ viṣayaikatvamitadeṣṭavyam /
ato dhūmastajjñānaṃ vā sambandhastatsmaraṇaṃ vā pramāṇamastu, vivakṣādhīnatvāt pramāṇaphalabhāvasyeti /
yattu buddhe' pramāṇa
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is in its qualified form alone that it is unknown, and hence it is inferable — thus he says 'viśiṣṭatvena' etc. Here he raises an objection — 'nanu' etc. It has been said that smoke too, qualified by fire, is inferred — that is improper, because it would be part of the thesis. He answers — 'naitad' etc. For smoke is of the nature of general and particular; when what has been made a thesis in its particular aspect is proved by reason in its general aspect, it is not a part of the thesis. It has thus been ascertained that the object of inference is the qualified. What is its own nature? — that is not known. If the inferability of smoke, its cognition, and such is accepted, then there would be a difference of object between <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) and <s>phala</s> (result) — and that is improper. For this very reason, the Buddhist has said that a single cognition has both the form of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>phala</s>, and having stated this regarding perception, has extended it to inference as well: 'the result belongs to it as before.' But if the cognition of what is to be inferred is accepted as the <s>pramāṇa</s>, then again there is no separate result. Therefore the own nature of inference is to be stated — hence he says 'dhūmatajjñāna' etc. Now, what the Buddhist has relied upon — that the <s>pramāṇa</s> itself is the result, by virtue of obtaining unity of object — that should be rejected here as in perception. For ordinary people do not think there is identity between what is to be accomplished and its means. Who indeed maintains the identity of an axe with the cutting of a tree? The resolution of the difference of objects, however, is to be investigated here as stated regarding perception. For just as in the position that the sense organ and such are the <s>pramāṇa</s>, the unity of object has been justified by the operation directed at that where the result is produced — so here too, in the position that smoke and such are the <s>pramāṇa</s>, the unity of object stated earlier from its operation is to be similarly understood. Therefore, whether smoke, its cognition, the relation, or its memory is the <s>pramāṇa</s> — since the status of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>phala</s> depends on what is intended — [any can serve]. As for the [view] that cognition is the <s>pramāṇa</s>—
And the statement of non-restriction to perception applies everywhere;
because what is grasped by inference is demonstrated by that very [cognition]. // Msv_5,4.53 //
For one wishing [to communicate] to others, the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) must be stated as before;
there, having pointed out the <s>dharmin</s> (subject), the <s>sādhya-dharma</s> (property to be proved) is predicated. // Msv_5,4.54 //

children.text:
(phala?)tve phalābhāva ityuktam /
bhāṣyakāro hi buddhireva pramāṇamiti darśayati yat kāraṇamasannikṛṣṭer'the buddhiriti vadati /
na ca phalābhāva', hānādereva phalatvāt /

children.translated_text: Nor is it a royal decree that only a homogeneous result [is acceptable].
From utility, the result may be either homogeneous or heterogeneous.

children.text: astu vā sajātīyameva phalaṃ hānādibuddhi' phalaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Or, let the result indeed be homogeneous — the cognition of avoidance and the like will be the result.
Or, memory arising from helpfulness and the like — with this in mind he says 'the cognition of the object to be known.' // 52 //

It was said that if it [cognition] were the result, there would be an absence of result. For the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> shows that cognition itself is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) when he says 'cognition arises regarding an object not in contact [with the senses].' Nor is there an absence of result, since avoidance and the like are themselves the result.

children.text: yadi bhāṣyakāra' pramayadhiya' prāmāṇyaṃ manyate, kathaṃ tarhi dhūmādipramāṇatvābhyupagama' ata āha---pratyakṣeti /

children.translated_text: It has been stated by us that the status of being a <s>pramāṇa</s> depends on the intention of the speaker.

children.text: tad yadā dhūmādīnāmeva prakṛṣṭasādhanatvamavagamyate, tadā tadeva pramāṇam /
children.translated_text: Thus, when the preeminent instrumentality of smoke and the like is understood, then that itself is the <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: bhāṣyakāreṇāpi buddhirvā janma vetyādinā pratyakṣaniyamaṃ darśayatā sarvatraivāniyamastulyayā darśita eva /
children.translated_text: Even by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, when showing the restriction of perception with 'whether cognition or origination,' the equal non-restriction in all cases has been shown.
Therefore, there is no contradiction with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> in accepting smoke and the like as <s>pramāṇa</s>. // 52 //

If the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> considers the cognition of the object to be known as valid, how then does he accept smoke and the like as <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)? Hence he says — 'perception.'

children.text:
tañcedamanumānaṃ dvedhā bauddhā vibhajante svārthaṃ parārthañceti /
yadāhu'----
anumānaṃ dvidhā svārthaṃ trirūpālliṅgator'thadṛk
parārthamanumānaṃ tu svadṛṣṭārthaprakāśakam||
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Buddhists</s> divide this <s>anumāna</s> (inference) into two kinds: <s>svārtha</s> (for oneself) and <s>parārtha</s> (for others). As they say: '<s>Anumāna</s> is twofold: <s>svārtha</s> (for oneself), which perceives the object through the triple-characterized mark (<s>liṅga</s>); and <s>parārtha</s> <s>anumāna</s> (for others), which illuminates the object seen by oneself.'

children.text:
iti /
tadidaṃ dvaividhyamanupapannamityabhiprāyeṇāha---anumāneti /
asyārtha'--- guruśiṣyasahādhyāyivirodhiprativādibhya' parebhyo 'numānagṛhītasyārthasya tenaivānumānena pratipādanaṃ vāñchatā yathā pūrvamasmābhi' pratipādita' pakṣo viśiṣṭo dharmī pramīyata iti sa vaktavya' /
idamatrākūtam /
svayamanumānena gṛhītamarthaṃ paraṃ pratipādayituṃ sādhanavākyameva prayujyate /
parastu tato vākyāt trirūpaṃ liṅgamanusandhāya svayameva sādhyaṃ vastu budhyate, tadasya svārtamevānumānam /
vakturapi svayamarthaṃ pratipannavata' svārthānumānameva, kataradatra parārthānumānamiti na vidma' /
vacanaṃ parārthamiti cet /
na /
ananumānatvāt /
vacanaṃ parārthamiti tu mṛṣyāmahe /
yadvadati darśanasya parārthatvāditi, na tu tadanumānam, atrirūpaliṅgajanitatvādanarthadṛk ca /

children.translated_text: This twofold division is untenable — with this in mind he says '<s>anumāna</s>.' The meaning is: One who wishes to communicate through that very inference the object grasped by inference to others — teachers, students, fellow-students, opponents, and respondents — should state the thesis as previously explained by us, namely that the qualified substratum (<s>dharmin</s>) is what is ascertained. The underlying intention is this: To communicate to another an object grasped by oneself through inference, only the proving statement (<s>sādhanavākya</s>) is employed. But the other person, from that statement, apprehending the triple-characterized mark, understands the object to be proved by himself — so this is his own <s>svārtha</s> (for-oneself) inference. For the speaker too, who has already understood the object by himself, it is only <s>svārtha</s> inference — so we do not know which one is the <s>parārtha</s> (for-others) inference. If [you say] the verbal statement is for others — no, because it is not inference. We do accept that the verbal statement is for others. As [the Buddhist] says, 'from the seeing being for others' — but that is not inference, since it is not born from the triple-characterized mark and does not perceive the object. 'Inference is that which perceives the object from the triple-characterized mark' — this is your own established conclusion. So how is a verbal statement inference? If it is figuratively called '<s>parārtha anumāna</s>' because the statement, capable of communicating the object brought within the scope of inference, is for others — then a statement that communicates an object perceived by direct perception, being for others, would also make perception 'for others.' If [you say] perception is not called 'for others' because perception has particular characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) as its object and those are beyond the reach of words — that is unjustified. For then, the verbal refutation of those who assert the opposite of what is perceived — that would not be tenable. For one who asserts something contradicted by perception, such as 'fire is not hot,' is refuted by communicating that very object of perception through words. But if the object of perception were beyond the reach of words, that would not be possible. Therefore, it must be accepted that words do express the objects of perception as well. And if so, since the verbal communication of the object of perception is also for others, who prevents perception itself from being 'for others'? Hence the twofold division is untenable. Therefore, only the thesis as previously stated should be articulated — this has been said. But this must now be stated: What is this thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>)? It is said: The thesis is the meaning of the proposition (<s>pratijñā</s>). What is a proposition? It is a statement that presents the object to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>). As they say: 'The statement of what is to be proved is the proposition.' Therefore, what is to be proved is the thesis — thus we declare, and 'the thesis should be stated' was said. He now presents that statement — 'therein.' Therein, in the thesis, after first pointing out the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>), the property to be proved, such as fire, is predicated. It amounts to saying: 'This mountain possesses fire.' But some do not accept this thesis-statement as an alternative name for the proposition. And they say: What is the use of this meaningless thing? Even without the thesis-statement, what is desired is established. For the reason (<s>hetu</s>) proves the object to be proved, not the statement of the thesis. Nor is this the traditional meaning, since it would render the statement of the reason purposeless. Following the authority, from the thesis-statement alone, the ascertainment would follow, making the statement of the reason purposeless. The opponent would be inclined merely to ascertain the merits and defects of the speaker. But when the determination depends on the reason, it is the power of the reason itself that is proper to examine — what use is the thesis-statement? And the power of the reason is established merely by showing the concomitance with the provable. Therefore, from the example and application alone — 'whatever is produced is impermanent, and sound is produced' — since the provable is established, the proposition is purposeless. Rather, the triple characterization of the reason alone is to be demonstrated. And that is stated through two examples and the application — so enough of excessive elaboration. If it be said that the proposition-statement is for announcing the dispute — that is not so, because it is not pervading [all debate formats]. Those who think: 'When this person asserts that sound is eternal, the other who holds it to be impermanent is roused, and then the debate begins' — that is not so, because it does not pervade [all cases]. This is not a pervading purpose of the proposition-statement, since it does not apply to <s>vāda</s> (honest discussion). For that [<s>vāda</s>] concerns the student. And the student is to be taught the truth — therefore it is proper that truth is communicated by demonstrating the power of the reason alone. Why should dispute be valued? For one should not argue with him. If [you say] it applies to <s>jalpa</s> (sophistical debate) — no, because it is accomplished otherwise. Here it may be objected: In <s>jalpa</s>, one who wishes to initiate a dispute puts forth a proposition. But that is not so, because it is accomplished otherwise — for even without the thesis-statement, it is observed: 'He infers that sound is impermanent' — the reason being that 'whatever is produced is impermanent, like a pot,' and then applying being-produced to sound: 'and sound is produced.' From that, debate will proceed regardless. As for <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (destructive criticism), it proceeds however it may once the thesis has been presented. For the <s>vaitaṇḍika</s> (destructive critic) has no object to prove other than defeating the opponent. He would dispute when, from the proposition-statement proving some object, he considers his own contrary position to be undermined and becomes alarmed. Therefore, the proposition-statement, being useless in all three types of discussion, should be disregarded — thus they object. To this we reply: It was stated by you yourselves that '<s>parārtha anumāna</s> is the illumination of an object seen by oneself.' And when one has understood by oneself, through some particular reason, something qualified by some property, it is proper that it be stated to another in exactly the same way. But without a proposition, the reason and the like would be without a basis, as if fallen from the sky. 'But [the opponent] did not know the object to be proved prior to the thesis-statement, so how does he state it to another in that way?' — do not say so. Although 'sound is impermanent' is not uttered in one's own cognition, nevertheless, because this cognition is conceptual (<s>savikalpaka</s>), there is indeed a definite conceptualization by the cognizer here — only the utterance is for others; that alone was not present in one's own cognition. But the other cannot be made to understand without uttered words — so he is made to understand through utterance. Thus, only the utterance of words is the additional element. As for what was said — that it is useless in <s>vāda</s> (honest discussion) — that is not so, because it is all the more useful. For in <s>jalpa</s> (sophistical debate) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (destructive criticism), both parties, desiring to win, proceed — so the proposition-statement would not be employed to deceive the other. But in honest discussion, where the student should not be confused, the proposition
The restriction is conceived from what is contradictory to it, not from what is not contradictory;
and by a speech that is not in contact [with the object], both [aspects] here are sought to be abandoned. // Msv_5,4.55 //

children.translated_text: As they say —
"The proposition is declared to be the essence of all practical transactions;
upon its loss, the disputant is defeated; one who maintains it becomes the superior."

children.text: iti sūkto vādivacanaprakāro dharmiṇamuddiśya sādhyadharmo vidhīyata iti ||53-54||
children.translated_text: Thus, the well-stated procedure of the disputant's speech is: The property to be proved is predicated with reference to the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>). // 53-54 //

is appropriately established through verbal statement. For there is no poverty of words such that we should torment with unclear speech one who has approached wishing to know the truth. Nor indeed is it useless in <s>jalpa</s> (sophistical debate). It has been stated: Without the thesis-statement, the reason and the like, being without a basis, would not function. For those, being subsidiary, are connected in relation to the primary object to be proved. And that is not possible without the statement of the provable (<s>sādhyanirdeśa</s>). For when the provable is stated, the reason is connected in response to the question 'why?' Then, when it is questioned 'how is this the pervading proof of that?' — the statement of pervasion follows. Otherwise, in the absence of unity of purpose, a single sentence would not even be formed. For consider: When it is said 'whatever is produced is impermanent,' the connection of being-produced with impermanence is restated. And again, 'sound is produced' — the connection of sound with being-produced is restated. But there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for the mutual connection [of these two statements]. One might suspect that these are two unconnected sentences. The doubt would arise that both are mere restatements of self-evident facts — that what is produced is impermanent and sound is produced. Or a different conclusion might be drawn — as 'just as what has the property of impermanence is produced, so too is what has the nature of sound' — thus the well-accomplished conclusion would be that 'all produced things have the nature of sound.' Therefore, the denial of the proposition, which is a component of the principal sentence, is fitting only for nihilists who deny everything, not for others. For the proposition is the essence of all practical transactions.
