Just as smoke, existing only in fire, is established as pervaded by fire — so is established the reversal of pervasion between the absences.

children.text:
yata eva cābhāvayorīdṛśo vyāpavyāpakabhāva' ata eva bhāvayorabhimatavyāptisiddhirityāha---tathānagnāviti /
anagnāvagnyabhāve dhūmābhāvena vyāpte dhūmastatra virodhivyāpteralabdhāvakāśo 'gnāveva bhavatītyevaṃ tadvyāpyatā tasya sidhyati /
tatheti /
yathā bhāvavyāptyapekṣayābhāvavyāpti' evamabhāvavyāptyapekṣayā bhāvavyāptirityartha' /
na caivamitaretarāśrayatā, bījāṅkuravadanāditayopapatteriti ||123 1/2||
children.translated_text: And precisely because there is such a pervaded-pervader relation between the absences, the desired pervasion between the positive entities is established — hence he says 'similarly, in the absence of fire.' When in the absence of fire — that is, in the absence of fire — the absence of smoke is the pervader, then smoke, finding no scope there due to the pervasion by the contrary, exists only in fire — and thus its pervaded-ness is established. 'Similarly' means: just as the pervasion of absences is established with reference to the pervasion of positive entities, so the pervasion of positive entities is established with reference to the pervasion of absences — that is the meaning. And there is no mutual dependence here, because, like seed and sprout, it is justified as beginningless.

children.text: vyāpakau tu yadocyete bhāvābhāvau tadā tata' // Msv_5,4.124 //
children.translated_text: But when existence and absence are said to be the pervaders, then from that —
not at all would the exclusion of the counter-thesis from the pervaded be stated.

children.text: tasmād dhūmena sādhyatvamagne' prārthayate yadā // Msv_5,4.125 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, when one wishes to prove fire from smoke,
one should state that non-fire is pervaded by non-smoke, and not otherwise.
In the mere co-occurrence of non-fire and non-smoke, or in the reversal of pervasion,
there would be no benefit to the subject at hand, or else something else would be undesirably established.

children.text: yatrāpyarthasya śūnytavaṃ dvābhyāmekena vā bhavet // Msv_5,4.127 //
children.translated_text: And where the example is devoid of meaning, by both or by one [of the two absences],

children.text:
kiṃ punarabhāvayorvyāptiviparyayāśrayaṇe prayojanamata āha---vyāpakautviti /
yadā hi ya eva bhāvo vyāpakastadabhāva eva vyāpakatayā vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta ucyate tadā tato vyāpyād dhūmādernaiva vipakṣasyānagnyāde' pracyuti' kathitā bhavet /
tatakathanārthaṃ ca va vaidharmyavacanaṃ(sa) prayojanaṃ bhavet /
na hi yatra dhūmastatrāgniritivat yatra dhūmābhāvastatrāgnyabhāva iti kathyamāne vyāpyād dhūmādanagnervipakṣasya nivṛttirdarśitā bhavatīti /
ato dhūmenāgniṃ siṣādhayiṣatā vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntenāgnidhūmābhāvayorvyāptiviparyayo vācya ityāha--- tasmāditi vācyo 'ntena /
yatrāgnirnāsti tatra dhūmo nāstītyevaṃ yadavṛttatadavṛttābhyāmuddeśyopādeyabhāvo darśayitavya ityartha' /
sa cānagniradhūmen vyāpta ucyamāno nānyathā vācya', kintu sādharmyoktenaivoddeśyopādeyaprakāreṇetyāha--- na cānyatheti /
prakāraścānantaramevokta iti ||124,125 1/2||
children.translated_text: "What then is the purpose of resorting to the reversal of pervasion between the absences?" Hence he says — 'when existence and absence are said to be the pervaders.' For when the very existence that is the pervader is stated as pervading in the <s>vaidharmya</s> example, through its own absence as the pervader, then from that pervaded — smoke and the like — the exclusion of the counter-thesis — non-fire and the like — would not at all be stated. And the <s>vaidharmya</s> statement would then have no purpose except that [exclusion]. For when it is stated 'wherever there is no smoke, there is no fire' — just as 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire' — the exclusion of non-fire (the counter-thesis) from smoke (the pervaded) is not shown. Therefore, one who wishes to prove fire from smoke should state, through the <s>vaidharmya</s> example, the reversal of pervasion between the absences of fire and smoke — hence he says 'therefore' etc. with the word 'should be stated.' The meaning is: 'Where there is no fire, there is no smoke' — by showing what is not present where what [else] is not present, the relation of what is to be indicated and what is to be adopted should be shown. And when non-fire is stated as pervaded by non-smoke, it should not be stated otherwise — rather, only in the manner indicated by the <s>sādharmya</s> (similarity) example, with the same pattern of what is to be indicated and what is to be adopted — hence he says 'and not otherwise.' And the manner has been stated immediately before.

children.text:
anyathāvacane doṣamāha---anagniyadhūmasāhityaiti /
yathaiva sādharmyadṛṣṭānte svaśaktyā śabdor'thaṃ vadati nārthaśaktimanurudhyata iti sāhityamātravacane vyāptiviparyaye vā neṣṭaṃ sidhyatītyuktam, evamihāpi bhavatīti bhāva' ||126 1/2||
children.translated_text: He states the fault in stating otherwise — 'the co-occurrence of non-fire and non-smoke.' Just as in the <s>sādharmya</s> (similarity) example, the word expresses its meaning by its own power and does not follow the power of the meaning — so when mere co-occurrence is stated or when the pervasion is reversed, the desired is not established. So it is here too — this is the purport.

children.text:
evaṃ (tadva?tāva) dihāpyartho na śabdavaśavartīti yatrārtho dṛṣṭāntarūpo dvābhyāṃ hetusādhyābhāvābhyāmekena vā tayo' śūnyo bhavati tatrāpi na prastutopakāro bhavati anyadvāniṣṭaṃ prasajyata ityāha---yatrāpīti /
samyak prayukte 'pi vākyer'thasyātadāyattatvānneṣṭasiddhiriti bhāva' /
atrodāharaṇamāha
children.translated_text: Thus, here too, the meaning is not subject to the words — so where the illustrative meaning is devoid [of content], by both — the absences of the <s>hetu</s> and the <s>sādhya</s> — or by one of them, there too there is no benefit to the subject at hand, or something undesired follows — hence he says 'and where.' The purport is: Even when the sentence is correctly employed, since the meaning is not dependent on it, the desired is not established. He gives examples here —
'Whatever is impermanent is corporeal, like atoms, like cognitions, like space' —

children.text: sādhyena vyāptisiddhyai hi vyātireko 'tra kathyate // Msv_5,4.128 //
children.translated_text: For it is for the establishment of pervasion with the <s>sādhya</s> (provable) that <s>vyatireka</s> (co-absence) is stated here.
That which does not have this — that <s>hetu</s> (reason), by that <s>sādhya</s>, is not pervaded;

children.text: tena dṛṣṭe 'pi sāhitye na sarvo gamya iṣyate // Msv_5,4.129 //
children.translated_text: therefore, even when co-occurrence is observed, not every [instance] is desired to be an indicator.
Mere co-observation is not a connection; and pervasion is not thereby [established];
therefore, even when a pot is accepted as having both corporeality and impermanence,

children.text:
yaditi /
nityo dhvaniramūrtatvādityatraiva prayoge yadaivaṃ vaidharmyamucyate yannityaṃ na bhavati tadamūrtamapi na bhavati yathā paramāṇuriti tadā sādhyābhāvaśūnyo dṛṣṭānta' /
paramāṇornityatayā tadabhāvasya tatra darśayitumaśakyatvāt /
buddhivaditi tu dṛṣṭānte hetvabhāvaśūnyatā /
buddheramūrtatayā tadabhāvasya vaktumaśakyatvāt /
khavaditi tūbhayābhāvaśūnyatā, nityāmūrte tasminnubhayābhāvo duradhigamo yata iti ||127 1/2||
children.translated_text: 'What is [said to be]' etc. In the very usage 'sound is permanent because of its incorporeality,' when the <s>vaidharmya</s> is stated thus: 'what is permanent does not also lack corporeality, like atoms' — then the example is devoid of the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, since it is impossible to show the absence of permanence in atoms, given their permanence. 'Like cognitions' — this illustrates the example being devoid of the absence of the <s>hetu</s>, since it is impossible to state the absence of incorporeality in cognitions, given their incorporeality. 'Like space' — this illustrates being devoid of both absences, since in space, which is both permanent and incorporeal, the absence of both is hard to ascertain.

children.text:
evaṃ sādharmyadṛṣṭāntavadvyāptivaikalye 'pyabhāsatā darśayitavyā /
tatsidadhyarthaṃ hi vipakṣāddhetorvyatireka' kathyate /
yasya tu vipakṣaikadeśādapi vyātireko nāsti, nāsau sādhyena vyāpto bhavatītyasatyāṃ vyāptāvanarthakaṃ tādṛśasya vaidharmyasya vacanamityabhiprāyeṇāha--- sādhyeneti ||128 1/2||
children.translated_text: Thus, just as in the <s>sādharmya</s> example, the pseudo-status due to deficiency of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) should be shown. For the <s>vyatireka</s> (co-absence) from the counter-thesis is stated for the purpose of establishing that [<s>vyāpti</s>]. But for one whose <s>vyatireka</s> does not exist even from a portion of the counter-thesis, it is not pervaded by the <s>sādhya</s> — and therefore, in the absence of <s>vyāpti</s>, the statement of such a <s>vaidharmya</s> is purposeless. With this in mind he says — 'with the <s>sādhya</s>.'

children.text: yataścaivañjātīyako na sādhyena vyāpyate tena kvacidabhāvayo' sāhitye dṛṣṭe 'pi na sarvatra gamyagamakabhāvo bhavatītyāha---teneti /
children.translated_text: And since one of this kind is not pervaded by the <s>sādhya</s>, therefore, even when the co-occurrence of the absences is observed in some cases, the indicator-indicated relation does not hold everywhere — hence he says 'therefore.'

children.text: yadyapi yannityaṃ na bhavati tadamūrtamapi na bhavati, yathā ghaṭa' kuḍyaṃ veti, kvacidabhāvayo' sāhityaṃ śakyate darśayitum /
children.translated_text: Although one can show in some cases the co-occurrence of the absences — 'what is not permanent also lacks corporeality, like a pot, like a wall' —

children.text: tathāpi na sarva(') śabdādi(') nityatayā viśiṣṭo 'nena hetunā gamya iṣyate /
children.translated_text: nevertheless, not every [entity] such as sound that is qualified by permanence is desired to be indicated by this <s>hetu</s>.
For some incorporeal things are permanent, like space and the like, while others are impermanent, like action and the like — this is the purport.

children.text:
kimiti neṣyate ata āha--- sahadṛṣṭiriti /
vipakṣaikadeśanivṛttyā hi sahabhāvamātraṃ heto' sidhyati /
na ca tanmātrasambandho 'numānāṅgam /
kiṃ tarhi, vyāpti' /
na cāsāvetāvatā sāhityamātreṇa sidhyatīti /
etadevodāharaṇena darśayati--- mūrtānityatvacayukte 'pīti /
idaṃ prāgeva vyākhyātamiti ||130 1/2||
children.translated_text: Why is this not desired? Hence he says — 'mere co-observation.' For by the exclusion from a portion of the counter-thesis, only the mere co-occurrence of the <s>hetu</s> is established. And mere co-occurrence is not a component of inference. What then? Pervasion. And that is not established merely by that amount of co-occurrence. This very point he illustrates with an example — 'even when having both corporeality and impermanence.' This has been explained earlier.
Here the Buddhists say: What is this —
It is not accepted as an example because of the absence of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) in action and the like;
and because of the requirement of [exhaustive coverage of] the entire [counter-thesis], and also because non-observation is easily achieved.
Even if the desired <s>vyatireka</s> (co-absence) here is a means of proof with respect to inference,

children.text: tāvatā na hyanaṅgatvaṃ yukti' śābde 'bhidhāsyate // Msv_5,4.132 //
children.translated_text: that alone does not make it non-subsidiary — the reasoning will be stated in [the section on] verbal testimony (<s>Śabda</s>).

children.text:

children.translated_text: It is said 'when <s>vyāpti</s> has been stated through <s>sādharmya</s> (similarity), <s>vaidharmya</s> (dissimilarity) is not required.' For when even a hundredth part of the <s>hetu</s>'s <s>vyatireka</s> from the counter-thesis is in doubt, there is no indicator-status. Therefore, the entirety of the counter-thesis is required for the inferrer to grasp the <s>vyatireka</s>. And that is not difficult to ascertain — because even one located in one place can easily see the non-existence [of smoke] everywhere. For seeing all the counter-instances is indeed difficult, but their absence is easily available. Nor should it be said that this non-observation, being the non-perception of an unfit object, does not suffice for the <s>vyatireka</s> of the <s>hetu</s>. For the invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) is not based merely on non-observation in the counter-thesis. Rather, it is grounded in identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) or causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>). But when [the <s>hetu</s>] is observed in the counter-thesis — an enemy of the invariable concomitance — it becomes impossible to grasp the invariable concomitance. And such [observation], for one located even in one place, simply does not exist — so observation operates only where there is actual occurrence in an opposing [instance]. Therefore, at the very moment it is understood that 'smoke is an effect of fire,' it is known that its own existence depends on that [fire] — it does not exist when that does not exist. And the <s>anvaya</s> (co-presence) knowledge alone is not the basis for the <s>vyatireka</s> (co-absence) cognition, because in the case of <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (uncommon) reasons, the former is impossible. For of the fire and smoke particular-instances observed in the kitchen alone, confined to that very place, there is no observation elsewhere, by which <s>anvaya</s> could be experienced. Then whence the <s>anvaya</s>? And even more so, whence the <s>vyatireka</s> based on it? And there is no general form that pervades the particulars as something in common, to be ascertained as the determining and the determined — because it is of the nature of a conceptual construction (<s>vikalpākāra</s>). Therefore, it is certain particulars alone, characterized by some exclusion, that indicate some particular through the exclusion from the counter-thesis — and so the statement of <s>vaidharmya</s> alone, for showing that, is proper. To them he replies — 'because of the requirement of the entire [counter-thesis]' etc. with [the rest of] the reasoning. The purport is: Although <s>vyatireka</s> is a component of inference, it is not established from mere non-observation alone. For its justification is also through arriving at that location. And it is not the case that from the ascertainment of being-an-effect, the absence in the absence of the cause follows — because that very thing is difficult to ascertain without <s>vyatireka</s>. For that which exists when something exists and does not exist when it does not — that is its effect. Therefore, without the absence being established,
the teaching of the distinctions would not follow, and will not occur due to non-pervasion.

children.translated_text: Nor, when co-presence is a component of inference, will reasoning be stated in the verbal [section];
because it has already been stated here by the term 'whose connection is known' (<s>jñātasambandha</s>).
For this very reason, the dependence of inference on co-presence has been established — this he will state.
Therefore, the explanation is exactly as stated. // 132 //

— must be arrived at. From that, the causality depends on that — but in this, there is mutual dependence. Or let there be exclusion from mere observation; and its ease [follows]. But even so much as this — that reasoning (<s>yukti</s>) is not a component with respect to inference — [is not correct]. For reasoning, connection, relation, co-presence (<s>anvaya</s>) — these are synonyms. It means: co-presence is not a non-component. For the origination of inference for all cognizers is precisely through that channel. Therefore, for the purpose of stating that, the example by similarity (<s>sādharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) too must indeed be stated. It cannot be rejected categorically. And this follows from the statement: The established conclusion is as stated — when the example by similarity is properly applied, the example by dissimilarity need not be relied upon. Because of the very primacy of co-presence, without which exclusion is not established. For when the connection of smoke with fire is known, the cessation [of smoke] in the absence of fire is established implicitly. Therefore, co-presence should first be shown through the positive method; but when the occasion arises, dissimilarity may also sometimes be stated. But for those who read 'non-component' (<s>anaṅgatvam</s>), this is the explanation: What constitutes the component-hood of the mark for inference is co-presence and exclusion — for through these two it becomes a component. Therefore, just as exclusion is a component, so too is reasoning, which is another name for co-presence. But [objection:] even in the case of the mark that is verbal in nature, co-presence that comes after cognition is indeed a non-component — hence he says 'in the verbal [section], it will be stated.' For in the verbal [<s>pramāṇa</s>], which is different from inference, it will be stated that reasoning that follows cognition is a non-component. As he will say: 'This construction of co-presence would not be a component for the cognitions of meaning.' But in inference, co-presence is everywhere a component of cognition. But those who explain by supplying 'by that much, co-presence is not a non-component' and say 'in this very sense, reasoning will be stated in the verbal [section]' — for them, the very supplying of the unheard word 'co-presence' is itself a fault.

children.translated_text: But there is such a thing — this will be demonstrated in the chapter on universals, by resolving all the objections raised by others.
And its pervading multiple places and times is understood — hence it is not the case that co-presence has no locus.
Nor is there the grasping of what is not as what is, because of its [the universal's] ultimate reality.

children.text: evaṃ ca yadanumānuprāmāṇyasiddhyarthaṃ parai' kimapi kāśaṃ kuśamavalambyate, tadapi mandaproyajanameveti ||133||
children.translated_text: And thus, whatever flimsy thing is resorted to by others for the purpose of establishing the validity of inference — that too is of little use. // 133 //

through [its] existence, the restriction of only that type of another [entity] can be experienced. For without that, no component of inference is possible — hence the absence of co-presence in those [particulars] is not a defect. If the consequence of apprehension does not apply to particulars, to what then has this been shown? No real universal form exists apart from the particulars — because it is of the nature of a conceptual construct. And even though inference arises at the present time through the very superimposition of the form apprehended at the time of ascertaining the pervasion — consider this: Since a thorough examination of that [individual form] is impossible, this is simply an error. If so, inference, operating through the superimposition of an unreal form, would not be a <s>pramāṇa</s> at all. True. But through the force of invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>), some particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), apprehended through some conceptual form as universal, presents another particular that is merely sketched by that conceptual form — and that is called a <s>pramāṇa</s>. For the criterion of our <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood is non-deviation (<s>avisaṃvāda</s>), and the criterion of non-deviation is the stability of purposive activity (<s>arthakriyāsthiti</s>). As they say: 'A <s>pramāṇa</s> is non-deviating knowledge; the stability of purposive activity is non-deviation.' And in inference, there is the attainment of a real entity capable of purposive activity — even though it appears through a non-real form. Hence inference is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. As it is said: 'From the grasping of what is not as what is, there is error; from non-deviation, valid knowledge.' Therefore, it is particulars alone that are the inferable and indicator. And they are not the locus of co-presence — hence what was said is justified. Therefore he says — 'there is.' The meaning is: This would be so if there were no universal real entity apart from the particulars.

children.translated_text: Here is the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'But that [inference] is twofold: that whose connection is seen through direct perception, and that whose connection is seen through general observation. Of these, inference whose connection is seen through direct perception is, for example, the cognition of the form of fire from seeing the form of smoke. And inference whose connection is seen through general observation is, for example, from observing that <s>Devadatta</s>'s reaching another place is preceded by movement, the memory of movement even in the sun.' By this, the twofold [nature of] inference is stated through the twofold [nature of] the object to be known. Here, some who consider themselves experts in logic think that what has been apprehended with its own particular characteristic is somewhere grasped generally through inference. To remove that error, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> said: 'But that is twofold — there exists inference that has as its object even a particular characteristic that has not been directly seen, as in the case of action and the like.' But how can the connection be seen with a particular characteristic that has not been directly perceived? — From the seeing of an effect that has been produced. Although the connection with the entity whose particular characteristic has not been ascertained is not known specifically, it is seen generally. For every occasional effect is seen to arise from some adventitious productive cause — like a cloth from the connections of threads. Therefore, observing <s>Devadatta</s>'s prior-and-subsequent separation-conjunction with different locations at different times, some adventitious cause is inferred. This is called inference whose connection is seen through general observation, because its object is a particular characteristic not previously observed through direct perception. But in the case of fire and such, because the particular characteristic has been previously ascertained through direct perception, they call it inference whose connection is seen through direct perception. And it should not be said that substance alone is the cause of conjunction and disjunction — because even when substance exists, [conjunction and disjunction] sometimes do not. Nor can the arrival of another substance be postulated — because that is contradicted by the recognition of the same prior substance. Nor is it appropriate [to say] that, being deceived by the successive production of similar [things], they do not cognize the difference — because even when there is difference in location and the like, there is no reversal of that non-cognition [of difference]. And the commentator has stated: 'The doctrine of momentary destruction is refuted precisely by recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>). Therefore, since the observed cause is possible, some unseen cause of conjunction and disjunction is inferred. And that is called <s>karman</s> (action). For this very reason, in other contexts too, action is imperceptible.' The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> shows this — as he will state: 'For they are not [objects of] perception.' And: 'What causes its substrate to reach another location is called action.' Clearly, he shows that action is to be inferred precisely through having the reaching of another location as its result. Thus, the exclusive domain of inference-through-general-observation for action and such is established. And thus, those who say that the twofold division of inference is established through the twofold nature of the objects to be known — to them he responds: 'The twofold [division] is not tenable.' The purport is: This twofold division of the stated kind is untenable. How is it untenable? Hence he says — 'just as,' with three quarters [of the verse]. For just as the connection between the forms of fire and smoke, both being perceptible, is seen through direct perception, so too of movement and reaching [another place] — since both of them too are perceptible.
For the connection between movement and reaching [another location] is likewise perceived directly. // Msv_5,4.138 //

children.translated_text: And he says —
"For examining <s>Devadatta</s> who has come into the field of vision,
By reading a poem stated in one's own conventional terms, one understands [the meaning] as if it were remote [i.e., indirectly].'

children.translated_text: But if action (<s>karma</s>) is to be inferred from its result, the unwanted consequence would arise that the sun is perceived like <s>Devadatta</s>. But this one [i.e., the perceiver] is not seen to perceive the sun as moving and trembling like <s>Devadatta</s>. For its orb is always observed as stationary. But conjunction and disjunction are perceived even for it [the sun] — hence, since [the situation] is equal, the inferential cognition from those two [conjunction and disjunction] would arise in both cases. Moreover, when action is inferred from [the process of] conjunction at the conclusion and disjunction at the commencement, the cognition 'it is going' — appearing in the present tense — would not arise, for that [action] is past; then how could it become an object of a cognition with the appearance of the present? In the case of fish that are stationary in the flowing water, an inferential cognition of motion would arise from the apprehension of the uninterruptedly produced conjunction and disjunction of water-parts [with the fish]. And in the case of a post from which a hawk has separated, action would be inferred [in the post] just as in the hawk. And thus that [post] too would become an object of the cognition 'it is going.' If it is held that action is not inferred from disjunction alone, but rather from conjunction preceded by disjunction — then the unwanted consequence would follow in the case where a single post, separated from a hawk, is conjoined with another [hawk]. And also for <s>Devadatta</s> who has moved and then stopped. If it is said: 'The conjunction with another place that belongs to the flying hawk cannot be produced by an action inherent in the post — hence there is no inference of action therein' — then let action be postulated for the hawk too [and not for the post], but the unwanted consequence regarding the post is simply not avoided. For the cognition of one whose sight is bound [to a particular spot] inevitably leads to a cognition of the cause of the binding, when the binding has been remembered. And in the post there is indeed the observation of a result bound to a cause [viz., conjunction/disjunction] — hence [the inference] cannot be blocked. If it is said: 'Since the conjunction and disjunction in the post too can be explained by the action inherent in the hawk alone, there is no inference of action belonging to the post' — that is wrong. For the procedure of inference does not follow purpose [i.e., what is useful]. For a pervading inferential mark, wherever it is seen, there indicates the pervader. <s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is averted by an alternative explanation, not inference. But if uninterruptedly produced conjunctions and disjunctions are the cause in the inference of action, then no motion whatsoever would be inferred, since future conjunctions and disjunctions are beyond the range of any <s>pramāṇa</s>. And initially, only a few [conjunctions/disjunctions] are perceived. If, then, the inference of action is caused by the conjunction and disjunction with respect to one's own place — the hawk is not called the 'place' of the post. Even so, the unwanted consequence regarding fish is simply not avoided, for water is indeed their own place. And for those who hold that the sky is imperceptible, the cognition 'the bird is going' would be unjustified with respect to a bird [in the sky], because the conjunction and disjunction with the sky are imperceptible, and hence inference from them is impossible. Nor is the cognition 'the bird is moving' grounded in the apprehension of the conjunction and disjunction with the particles of the illuminated expanse of the sky, because it [such cognition] occurs even in complete darkness. And darkness is not a real entity according to your system, since it is merely the absence of light. Hence, the determination of action caused by the conjunction and disjunction with that [darkness] too cannot be justified — therefore the twofold division is not viable when action is directly perceived. As for the statement 'na hi te pratyakṣe' [made elsewhere] declaring [action to be] imperceptible — we shall explain that differently in that very context. And the <s>sūtrakāra</s> [Jaimini], by saying '<s>rūpaśabdāvibhāgam</s>' (inseparable from form and sound), has maintained that [action] is indeed perceptual. And in the <s>Apūrvādhikaraṇa</s>, the statement 'we perceive the form of action' is intended in the sense that the form of action — as a manifest, extended, earlier-and-later-distinguished state — is not perceived [in its entirety]. Otherwise, if mere perception were denied, action would be eternally non-existent, like the horn of a hare. For therein, it is not mere perceptual apprehension that is denied. And 'that which causes its substrate to reach another place' is not intended to mean that [action] is inferred from its result. Rather what? It shows that action exists not in its own form but in the form of causing its substrate to reach another place — [thus showing] action's existence in an unprecedented [<s>apūrva</s>] form. 'Here too, having observed the reaching of another place preceded by motion for <s>Devadatta</s>' — since [both aspects of] the action of both [sun and Devadatta] are inferential, by what distinguishing feature is the inference of motion in the sun cited as an instance of <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (generally-observed inference)? For even in the case of <s>Devadatta</s>, the establishment of motion is through <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> alone. Hence [such a twofold division based on] the text or reasoning of this kind does not work — the well-said is ill-founded. For the twofold division applies when the two counter-parts do not intermingle. But here, what is —

For we indeed perceive directly that <s>Devadatta</s> is reaching another location and think 'he is going.' This conceptualization of action is not different from the conceptualization of universals and the like. Just like those, because of conforming to the co-presence and co-absence of the sense organs and because of appearing as directly present. But [objection:] in the case of <s>Devadatta</s>, we directly see some form of action beyond the conjunction and disjunction of locations. It is inferred only through seeing the effect. Or, what form of the universal is experienced as distinct from the individual, such that it is determined as an object of perception? The form itself is that of the individual — what need is there of another form for it? If so, what then is the form of action? For this too does not differ from that [conjunction and disjunction]. It is merely adventitious. Therefore, placing the conceptualization of action too, like the conceptualization of universals, in the domain of perception, we divide determinate perception into five kinds.
If [you say] there is non-apprehension in the sun, then [there should be] non-apprehension in the present location too;
If anywhere there is apprehension, let it be demonstrated in <s>Devadatta</s> as well. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.139)
If the <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (generally-observed) status depends on another property-bearer,
That same [status] would apply to the case of fire and smoke too; hence they describe it thus. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.140)
Of those two specific [instances] whose relation has been perceived directly,

children.text: pratyakṣadṛṣṭasambandhasya pratiyogitayopāttaṃ sāmānyato dṛṣṭasambandhaṃ tatrāpi gatiprāptyākṛtyo' pratyakṣadṛṣṭa eva sambandha iti na pratiyoginorasaṅkara iti ||138||
children.translated_text: The relation that was perceived directly, being taken up as a counter-part [of the generally-observed], — in that case too, the relation of motion and reaching, being perceived directly, means the relation is indeed perceived directly — hence there is no intermixing of the counter-parts. (138)

children.text:
yadi tu dṛṣṭānte pratyakṣatāyāmapi pakṣīkṛtādityagaterapratyakṣatvāt na pratyakṣadṛṣṭa' sambandha ityucyate /
tadetadāśaṅkate tāvat---āditye 'nupalabdhiścediti /

children.translated_text: He now refutes — 'na' (no).
He states the reason — 'in the present location too.'
'In the present location too' — meaning: in the location presently being cognized, there is apprehension only in a non-perceptual [indirect] manner — this is the meaning.

children.text: yadi tvagnidhūmākṛtyo' kvacinmahānasādau apratyakṣopalabandhiriṣyate sā tarhi devadatte 'pi gate' pratyakṣatvādastītyāha---kvaciditi ||139||
children.translated_text: If, however, non-perceptual apprehension [of the relation] between the forms of fire and smoke is accepted somewhere, such as in a kitchen, then it exists for <s>Devadatta</s>'s motion too, since that [motion] is directly perceptible — he says 'kvacit.' (139)

But if, even when [the relation is] directly perceived in the example, since the motion of the sun, which is the thesis-subject, is imperceptible, [someone says] the relation is not one perceived directly — he raises this objection: 'If there is non-apprehension in the sun...'

children.text:
evaṃ tāvat pratyakṣato dṛṣṭatā sāmānyato dṛṣṭatayā saṅkīryate ityuktam /
idānīṃ sāmānyato dṛṣṭatāpi pratyakṣato
dṛṣṭābhimatāgnyākṛtyanumāne saṅkīryata ityāha--- yadīti pādatrayeṇa /
yadi hi devadattādidharmyantarāpekṣaivāditye gatyanumānasya sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṣyate, sā tarhi mahānasādidharmyantarāpekṣayāgnidhūmayorapi gamyagamakatvenāvasthitayo' prāpnotyeva /
children.translated_text: For if the <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> status of the inference of motion in the sun depends on another property-bearer such as <s>Devadatta</s>, then the same would apply to fire and smoke, established as indicatable and indicator, through dependence on another property-bearer such as a kitchen.

children.text: sāmānyato hyavivakṣitadeśādibhedamidamavagataṃ dhūmavānagnimāniti, yathā deśāntaraprāptyadhikaraṇaṃ gatyadhikaraṇamiti /
children.translated_text: For this is understood generally, without specifying differences of place and so forth: 'what possesses smoke possesses fire' — just as 'what is the substrate of reaching another place is the substrate of motion.'
Therefore, being devoid of counter-part status, 'hence they describe it thus.'
Since the two-fold division as stated [above] is untenable, the two-fold division should be described in the manner to be stated — such is the purport. (140)

Thus it has been stated so far that the directly-perceived [type] is intermixed with the generally-observed [type]. Now [he shows that] the generally-observed too is intermixed with the directly-perceived — in the case of the fire-form inference that is considered directly-perceived — he says 'yadi' with three quarters of the verse.

children.text:
tatra pratyakṣasambandhaṃ tāvadudāharati--- pratyakṣeti budhyate 'ntena /
yadā hi yayorevagnidhūmaviśeṣayo', gomayendhano 'yamagni'--- gomayamindhanamasyeti
children.translated_text: He now illustrates the directly-perceived-relation [type] — from 'pratyakṣa' to the end 'budhyate.' When, of those very two specific [instances] — a specific fire and a specific smoke — having first formed the cognition through direct perception that 'this is a fire with cow-dung fuel' — '<s>gomayendhana</s>' being a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [compound] meaning 'this smoke that is born from that [cow-dung fuel]' — having made this [cognition] previously through direct perception, and then, after some delay, having gone elsewhere,
Having formed [a cognition] of [the specifics including] being born from cow-dung fuel and its effects — (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.141)
By that very [smoke] situated in that very place, having gone, even at another time,

children.text: yadāgnirbudhyate tasya parvabodhākat puna' puna' // Msv_5,4.142 //
children.translated_text: When [one] cognizes that [same] fire, from the repeated cognition of the aspect — (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.142)
From the cognition of the reality whose existence was in doubt, there is validity [as a <s>pramāṇa</s>];
And this is a case of <s>viśeṣadṛṣṭa</s> (particular-observed), as written by <s>Vindhyavāsin</s>. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.143)
And this is desired [to apply] only to the generic forms [of fire and smoke], through some particular distinguishing [feature];
The determination of reason and probandum [in this way] — no distinction has been shown. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.144)

children.text:
bahuvrīhi', tajjanyo 'yaṃ dhūmaviśeṣ iti ca prāk pratyakṣeṇa matiṃ kṛtvā punaśca kiyatā vilambanenānyatra kvacid katvā gata' san taddeśasthena tenaiva dhūmaviśeṣeṇa tamevāgniviśeṣaṃ budhyate, tadā tatpratyakṣadṛṣṭasambandhamanumānaṃ bhavatītyartha' /
anena ca viśeṣadṛṣṭameva pratyakṣadṛṣṭaśabdenocyata iti vyākhyātam /
pratyakṣaśabdena hi viśeṣo lakṣyate /
pratyakṣeṇa hyayamevaṃvidho 'vāntaraviśeṣo gomeyandhanatajjanyatvādirūpa' śakyate 'vagantum /
na pramāṇāntareṇa /
tadadvāreṇa tvanumānasyāpi tādṛśo viśeṣo viṣayo bhavatīti yuktaiva pratyakṣaśabdena viśeṣalakṣaṇā /
viśeṣadṛṣṭaṃ ca sāmānyato dṛṣṭasya bhavati pratiyogīti dvaividhyopapattiriti bhāva' /
nanu viśeṣadṛṣṭaṃ nāma(na) pramāṇabheda'o /
na cedaṃ pramāṇam,gṛhītaviṣayatvāt /
taddeśasthitenaiva hi dhūmena tasminneva deśe sa eva gomayendhanajanyāgniranumīyate /
ato deśabhedābhāvādaprāmāṇyameva, ata āha---tasyeti pādatrayeṇa /

children.translated_text: The validity of this <s>viśeṣadṛṣṭa</s> (particular-observed) [inference] comes from the cognition of a reality whose existence was in doubt.
Although there is no difference of place,
Due to the difference of time, for one who is doubting, validity is unimpaired through the removal of doubt.
And this has been illustrated by <s>Vindhyavāsin</s> too as a case of <s>viśeṣadṛṣṭa</s> (particular-observed) — he says 'viśeṣadṛṣṭam.' (143)

— being a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [meaning] 'this specific smoke born from that [fuel],' having first formed a cognition through direct perception, and then, after some delay, having gone elsewhere — when, by that very specific smoke situated in that very place, one cognizes that very specific fire — then that inference whose relation has been directly perceived arises — this is the meaning. And by this, it is explained that what is called '<s>viśeṣadṛṣṭa</s>' (particular-observed) is denoted by the term 'directly-perceived-relation.' For by the word 'direct perception,' what is indicated is the particular. For it is only through direct perception that this kind of sub-particular — [the details] like cow-dung-fuel-origin and such — can be understood, not through another <s>pramāṇa</s>. But through the medium of that [direct perception], inference too has such a particular as its object — hence the designation by the word 'direct perception' indicating the particular is indeed justified. And the <s>viśeṣadṛṣṭa</s> (particular-observed) serves as the counter-part of the <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (generally-observed) — hence the two-fold division is justified — such is the purport. Objection: <s>viśeṣadṛṣṭa</s> is not a division of <s>pramāṇa</s>. Nor is this a <s>pramāṇa</s>, because its object has already been grasped. For it is by that very smoke situated in that very place that the same fire, born from cow-dung fuel, is inferred in that very place. Hence, due to the absence of spatial difference, it is simply invalid — hence he says 'tasya' with the three quarter-verses.

children.text:
yadi viśeṣadṛṣṭodāharaṇamidaṃ kathaṃ tarhi bhāṣye ākṛtigrahaṇam /
evaṃ hi viśeṣa eva darśayitavyo bhavet /
ata āha---ākṛtyoreveti /
ayamartha'---kenacidgomayondhanatvādināvāntaraviśeṣeṇopadarśitayorākṛtyo
children.translated_text: If this is an example of <s>viśeṣadṛṣṭa</s>, how then is there reference to <s>ākṛti</s> (generic form) in the <s>bhāṣya</s>? For in that case, only the particular should be demonstrated. Hence he says 'ākṛtyoḥ eva.' The meaning is: Of the generic forms, distinguished by some sub-particular such as cow-dung-fuel-origin —
And when the 'other-ness' of fire and smoke is to be expressed, [they are] measured by general observation;
This is said to be exclusively <s>sāmānyadṛṣṭa</s> (generally-observed) — hence the sun is cited [as an example]. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.145)
And the perceptibility of the universal has been established;
The reality [of the universal] or the reason for both [universal and particular] is stated here. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.4.146)
Here is the reason-probandum relationship.
For here the cognition is thus:

children.text: sa evāyamadya yāvadanuvartamāno gomayendhanavikārasya dhūmasyākāro dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: 'This very form of smoke — a modification of cow-dung fuel — that has been observed up to now is continuing to persist.'
Therefore, fire whose source is that [cow-dung] fuel is also persisting' — hence the reference to <s>ākṛti</s> (generic form) is not unjustified. (144)
What is the need for the example of the sun?
Hence he says 'agnidhūmāntaratve ca.'

children.text: yathā hyagnidhūmākṛtyostuṇadārugomayenthanādijanmā suvyakto viśeṣa' sarvapramātṛsyasaṃvedyo bhavati, naivaṃ gatiprāptyākṛtyo' /
children.translated_text: For just as in the forms of fire and smoke, a clearly distinguishable particular — such as being born from chaff, wood, or cow-dung fuel — is accessible to all cognizers, the same is not the case for the forms of motion and reaching [another place].

children.text: ata' prāptyākṛtimātrād gatyākṛtimātrānumānamāditya ekāntata' sāmānyato dṛṣṭasambanthamiti yuktamevādityodāharaṇamiti ||145||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the inference of the mere form of motion from the mere form of reaching [another place] is, with respect to the sun, exclusively a case of <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (generally-observed) relation — hence the example of the sun is indeed appropriate. (145)

If so, then the 'other-ness' of fire and smoke — i.e., another [pair of] fire and smoke with unspecified sub-particulars — should be stated as the example of <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (generally-observed).

children.text:
kiṃ puna' sāmānyata' sambandhagrahaṇe pramāṇam /
na hyagṛhītayo' sambandhino' sambandhagrahaṇamasti /
na ca sāmānyayo' pratyakṣagrahaṇaṃ sambhavati /
tasya svalakṣaṇaikaviṣayatvāt /
nānumānamanavasthāpātāt /
ata āha---pratyakṣaviṣayatvamiti /
bhavedanavasthā,vadyanumānena sāmānyagrahaṇamiṣyate /
tasya tu savikalpakasiddhau pratyakṣaviṣayatvamupapādyānta upasaṃhṛtaṃ 'pratyakṣatvamata' siddhaṃ sāmānyasye'ti /
nanu yastveva na sāmānyaṃ kiñcidasti nāma /
tasya bhinnābhinnasyānirūpaṇādata āha---
vastutvaṃ ceti /
vastutvamapyākṛtigranthe vistareṇa pratipādadayiṣyate /
pratyakṣaviṣayatāpratipādanena ca pratyakṣe 'pi prasādhitaprāyameva /

children.translated_text: And here, in order to establish the <s>anvaya</s> (co-presence), namely 'universals exist in things,' the reality of universals has been adduced.
But this restatement is for the purpose of stating the reason.
As for one who relies on reasons and does not care for establishing [things] through other <s>pramāṇas</s> without a reason—
to him, we shall establish both through reason alone — thus he says 'atra' etc. // 146 //

But what is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) for the apprehension of the relation in general terms? For there is no apprehension of the relation without apprehending the two relata. And the perceptual apprehension of universals is not possible, since perception has only particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) as its object. Nor is it through inference, due to the fault of infinite regress. Therefore he says 'pratyakṣaviṣayatvam' (being an object of perception) etc. There would be an infinite regress if the apprehension of universals were admitted through inference. But since its being an object of perception has been established at the end of the proof of <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate perception), it has been concluded: 'therefore the perceptibility of universals is established.' Objection: But there is no such thing as a universal at all. Since its nature — as both different and non-different [from the particulars] — cannot be determined — therefore he says 'vastutvam' (reality/thinghood) etc. The reality too will be demonstrated at length in the <s>Ākṛti</s> (universal) chapter. And through the demonstration of perceptibility, it has been largely established even in the context of perception.
The inference of fire from smoke and such would have a real object;
because it is not measurable by absence or other <s>pramāṇas</s>, like the cognition of the ear etc. regarding its own object. // Msv_5,4.147 //
And the reality of universals, as well as their apprehensibility by perception—
because they are not measurable by absence or other [<s>pramāṇas</s>], like unique particulars. // Msv_5,4.148 //

children.text:
tatra vastutvaprasādhanārthaṃ tāvad hetumāha---dhūmādagnyanumānasyeti /
bauddhā hyavastusāmānyālambanamanumānamācakṣate /
sāmānyasya vikalpākāramātrābhyupagamāt /
ata eva bhrāntirevānumānaṃ, sambandhabalena svalakṣaṇarūpamupasthāpayatīti pramāṇityāhu' /
tāneva pratīdamucyate--- vastvālambanamanumānabhabhāvānyapramāmatvāt yathā svārthe śrotrādibuddhi' /
yā hi svaviṣaye śrotrādibhirindriyairbuddhirjanyate, sā vastvālambanaivapa /
yena ca yadindriyaṃ sannikṛṣyate sa tasya svārtha' prāpyakāritvādindriyāṇām /
tadiha mṛgatṛṣṇādijñānanirākaraṇārthaṃ svārthaviśeṣaṇam /
aviśeṣeṇopādāne tu nābāvānyapramāṇatvasya vastvālambanatayā vyāpti' kathitā bhavet /
bhrāntīnāmubhayavikalatvāt /
na hi tā' pramāṇam /
na ca vastvālambanā' /
anyasamprayuktendriyasyahi tā anyaviṣayā jāyante /
ūdṛśameva jñānamavastvālambanaṃ, na punaratyantāsadartham /
evaṃ vastvālambantve 'numānasya sādhite arthāt sāmānyaṃ vastvityuktaṃ bhavati /

children.translated_text: And this unreality of inference's object has been refuted by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> who employs the word <s>artha</s> (object/meaning).
The Buddhists think that inference has a non-real object.

children.text: yadvaditi(?) svapratibhāse 'narther'thādhyavasāyena pravartamānā bhrāntirapyarthasambandhena pravṛttestadavyabhicārāt pramāṇamanumānamiti, teṣāmidamuttaram artha' sāmānyamanumānasya viṣayo bāhya eva /
children.translated_text: Just as — even an error, which operates by superimposing reality upon the unreal in its own appearance, is a <s>pramāṇa</s> because of its connection with the real object and because of its non-deviation in operation — thus inference is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. To them, the reply is: The object of inference — the universal — is external and real.
It is not merely the form of conceptual construction — this will be demonstrated at length in the <s>Ākṛti</s> chapter. // 147 //

There, first, to establish reality, he states the reason — 'dhūmādagnyanumānasya' etc. For the Buddhists claim that inference has an unreal universal as its object. Because they accept universals as being merely the form of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpākāra</s>). And for this very reason, inference is actually an error — but because, through the force of relation, it presents something of the nature of a particular, it is called a <s>pramāṇa</s> — so they say. Against them this is stated: Inference has a real object, because it is not measurable by absence or other <s>pramāṇas</s> — just as the cognition produced by the ear and other sense organs regarding its own object. For the cognition generated by the sense organs — ear etc. — regarding its own object, has indeed a real object. And that with which the sense organ is brought into contact — that is its own object, because sense organs operate through contact. Here, the qualifier 'own object' is for the purpose of excluding cognitions like mirage etc. For without the qualifier, the <s>vyāpti</s> of having a real object with 'not being measurable by absence or other <s>pramāṇas</s>' could not be stated. Because erroneous cognitions lack both — they are not <s>pramāṇas</s>, and they do not have real objects. For they arise concerning another object, through a sense organ in contact with something else. Only such a cognition has an unreal object — but not one that has an absolutely non-existent object. When the reality of inference's object is thus established, the reality of universals is thereby implicitly stated.

children.text: evamarthād vastutvaṃ prasādhyāhratya prasādhayati---sāmānyasya ca vastutvamiti /
sāmānyaṃ vastu abhāvānyaprameyatvādasādhāraṇavastuvaditi vakṣyamāṇena sambandha iti /
children.translated_text: Universals are real — the connection is with what will be stated: 'because they are not measurable by absence or other <s>pramāṇas</s>, like unique particulars.'
He now demonstrates perceptibility through a formal argument — 'pratyakṣa' etc. with three quarters [of a verse].
Whatever is not measurable by absence or other <s>pramāṇas</s>, that is apprehended by perception.
Just as the unique particulars accepted even by the Buddhists. // 148 //
Having thus implicitly established reality, he now directly establishes it — 'sāmānyasya ca vastutvam' etc.
A universal is not cognized by anyone without inference;
and inference does not operate without an inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>). // Msv_5,4.149 //
And no one accepts a non-universal as an inferential mark;

children.text: na cānavagataṃ liṅgaṃ kiñcidasti prakāśakam // Msv_5,4.150 //
children.translated_text: and no unapprehended inferential mark has any illuminating power. // Msv_5,4.150 //
Or, its cognition too would be through another inference;
and the production of that would be from an inferential mark combined with the cognition of universals. // Msv_5,4.151 //
And since that too would be inferential, it would arise from an inferential mark;
and with the postulation of yet another inference-based cognition — // Msv_5,4.152 //
from the infinity of inferential marks, inferred objects, and inferences, in a single subject of inference,
even in many thousands of ages, [inference] would never be accomplished. // Msv_5,4.153 //
But if, even in an inferential mark that is a universal, cognition could arise from another
<s>pramāṇa</s> or non-<s>pramāṇa</s> — then similarly, the cognition of the inferred object would arise [without inference]. // Msv_5,4.154 //

children.text: bauddhānāmeva tu sāmānyamanumānaikaviṣayaṃ manvānānāmanavasthā prasajyata ityāha--- sāmānyamiti pañcabhi' /
children.translated_text: But for the Buddhists alone, who consider universals to be cognizable only through inference, an infinite regress ensues — thus he says 'sāmānyam' etc. with five [verses].
The text is explained by recitation. // 149-153 //

children.text:
yadi tūcyate liṅgabhūtasāmānyagrahaṇārthamanumānāpekṣāyāmanavasthā bhavati, na tadagrahaṇārthamanumānamapekṣyate, dhūmādisvalakṣaṇadarśanaprabhavavikalpavedyatvāttasya /
na cāsāvapramāṇam, arthakriyāsamarthavastupratilabhāt /
na ca pramāṇamanarthaviṣayatvāt /
ato 'nirvacanīyavikalpasiddhatvāt liṅgasya nānavasthā bhavatītyāśaṅkyāha---atheti /
ayamabhiprāya'--- na tāvat pramāṇamapramāṇaṃ ca jñānaṃ sambhavati /
viruddhasvabhāvayorekatra pratiṣedhe 'nyatarāpatteraparihāryatvāt /
apramāṇasya ca prameyavyavasthāpanāśakteravaśyaṃ pramāṇameva tajjñānamabhyupagantavyam /
pratyakṣānumānānabhyupagamācca
pramāṇāntaramevāpadyeta /
children.translated_text: If, however, one says: 'In requiring inference for the apprehension of the universal that is the inferential mark, there is an infinite regress; but inference is not required for its non-apprehension, since it is knowable through the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) arising from the perception of the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) such as smoke. And that [vikalpa] is not a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>, because it results in the attainment of a thing capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>). Nor is it a <s>pramāṇa</s>, because it has a non-real object. Therefore, since the inferential mark is established through an indescribable <s>vikalpa</s>, there is no infinite regress' — anticipating this, he says 'atha' etc. The intention is: A cognition cannot be both a <s>pramāṇa</s> and a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>. Because when contradictory natures are negated in one, the obtainment of one or the other is inescapable. And since a non-<s>pramāṇa</s> lacks the power to establish what is to be measured, that cognition must necessarily be accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s>. And since neither perception nor inference is admitted [as its nature], it would turn out to be yet another <s>pramāṇa</s>.
Even thus, the permanent destruction of inference would follow;
that other <s>pramāṇa</s> alone would be the illuminator of universals. // Msv_5,4.155 //
Or, the cognition arising from an inferential mark that is known through a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>
would also always be false — like the cognition of fire from water vapor. // Msv_5,4.156 //
Objection: Even though not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, the memory of the relation is accepted [as a component];
just as it is a cause of the cognition of the inferred, so too the cognition of the mark would arise. // Msv_5,4.157 //
There, the prior cognition is accepted as having <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity);
and through the mere arising of that, the memory's purpose would be fulfilled. // Msv_5,4.158 //

children.text: pramāṇāntaraṃ ca sadyathā talliṅgaṃvedane pramāṇamiṣyate, evaṃ liṅginyapi prāpnoti /
children.translated_text: And this other <s>pramāṇa</s> would exist in such a way that just as the inferential mark is accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s> in knowing the inferred object, so too it would apply to the inferred object as well.
And thus the consequence to be stated would follow.
By saying 'from a <s>pramāṇa</s> or from a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>,' he shows the undetermined dual nature of <s>vikalpa</s>. // 154 //

children.text: astu tarhi liṅgino 'pi tathaivāvagama', ko doṣa', ata āha---evamapīti /
children.translated_text: Let there be cognition of the inferred object in the same way — what fault is there? Therefore he says 'evam api' etc.
The intention is: Even if one incurs the infinite regress, we prefer to demonstrate the destruction of inference.
For even with the acceptance of another <s>pramāṇa</s>, the destruction of inference follows.

children.text: tadeva hi pramāṇaṃ tadā sarvasya liṅgaliṅgisāmānyasyāvabodhakaṃ bhavediti ||155||
children.translated_text: For that very <s>pramāṇa</s> would then be the illuminator of all universals — of the inferential mark, the inferred, and so forth. // 155 //

But if, even on the acceptance of a single nature, the inferential mark cognition is admitted to be a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>, then from the mark cognized through a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>, the cognition of the inferred too would be false,
like the cognition of fire from water vapor [mistaken for smoke].
And thus there would be no inference.
That itself is the permanent destruction of inference — with this intention he says 'apramāṇāvabuddhāt' etc. // 157 //
Here he raises an objection — 'nanu' etc.

children.text: yathā hyapramāṇameva sambandhasmaraṇaṃ pramāṇakāraṇamiṣyate tathā liṅgajñānamapi bhaviṣyatītyartha' ||157||
children.translated_text: The meaning is: just as the memory of the relation, though itself a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>, is accepted as a cause of <s>pramāṇa</s>, so too the cognition of the inferential mark would be. // 157 //
He answers — 'tatra' etc.
For memory arises from prior cognition, and serves inference through the door of presenting that [prior cognition].

children.text: tacca pramāṇameveti tadanusārī nirṇayo yukta iti ||158||
children.translated_text: And that [prior cognition] is a <s>pramāṇa</s> itself — hence the determination following it is justified. // 158 //
But for the cognition of the inferential mark, no <s>pramāṇa</s> is possible;

children.text: tadabhāvāt smṛtiścātra na kathañcit pravartate // Msv_5,4.159 //
children.translated_text: due to its absence, memory too does not operate here in any way. // Msv_5,4.159 //
He who would say that this cognition is memorial and non-different [from valid cognition],
for him, surely even in the son of a barren woman there would be the capacity for remembering. // Msv_5,4.160 //
Nor is the unique particular (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) the cause of the cognition of universals,
because its invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) with that has never been observed in any way. // Msv_5,4.161 //

children.text: na caiṣa prakāro liṅgagatau sambhavatītyāha---na tviti /
children.translated_text: Nor is this mode possible in the cognition of the inferential mark — thus he says 'na tu' etc.

children.text: na hyatra prāgapi liṅgāvagame pramāṇaṃ kiñcidupapadyate, yat pramāṇajñānenopasthāpyata iti /
children.translated_text: For here, no <s>pramāṇa</s> is possible even for the prior apprehension of the mark, which could be presented through the memory of a valid cognition.
Nor should one say that the cognition of the mark too is merely memory.
Because of the very absence of a prior <s>pramāṇa</s> — thus he says 'tadabhāvāt' etc. // 159 //

children.text:
nanu nirvakalpagṛhītadhūmādisvalakṣaṇapariprāpakatayā liṅgajñānamapi smṛtireva /
ato 'trāpi nirvikalpapramāṇāntarato nirṇayo yukta eva /
ata āha---smārtamiti /
yathā samprati sambandhajñānaṃ gṛhītaprāpakatayā samaraṇam, evametadapi liṅgajñānaṃ nirvakalpakagṛhītaprāpakatayā tadabhedena smārtamiti yo vadati tasya vandhyāsutre 'pi smaraṇaśaktiranivāritā /

children.translated_text: For the settled principle is that memory has what was previously apprehended as its object.

children.text: na ca liṅgasāmānyajñānaṃ nirvakalpakagṛhītasvalakṣaṇālambanamiti kathaṃ smṛti' /
children.translated_text: And the cognition of the mark-universal does not have as its object a particular apprehended by non-conceptual perception — so how can it be memory?

children.text: yadatra prakāśate tanna gṛhītaṃ, yacca gṛhītaṃ sanna prakāśata iti na smṛtitvam /
children.translated_text: What appears therein was not apprehended, and what was apprehended does not appear — hence it is not memory.

children.text: agṛhītagocarāyāṃ tu smṛtau vandhyāsute 'pi smaraṇaprasaṅga iti ||160||
children.translated_text: And if memory had an unapprehended object, there would be the consequence of remembering even the son of a barren woman. // 160 //

Objection: Since the cognition of the mark, in its capacity to deliver the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) apprehended by non-conceptual perception, is itself memory — hence here too, the determination from a non-conceptual <s>pramāṇa</s> is indeed justified. Therefore he says 'smārtam' etc. Whoever says that just as the cognition of the relation is now memory by virtue of delivering what was previously apprehended, so too this cognition of the mark is memorial in its non-difference, by virtue of delivering what was apprehended by non-conceptual [perception] — for him, even in the son of a barren woman the capacity for remembering is not precluded.

children.text:
nanvanumānena liṅgasāmānyajñāne 'navasthā bhavati, yadi sāmānyātmakameva liṅgaṃ tadagrahaṇārthamiṣyate, tasyānumānavedyatvāt /
asādhāraṇa evārthātmā sāmānyajñāne liṅgaṃ bhaviṣyati, sa ca pratyakṣa eveti nānavasthā /
ata āha---na ceti /

children.translated_text: Why is it not a cause? — therefore he says 'yasmāt' etc.
An inferential mark must have its invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) observed.

children.text: na cāsya tena sāmānyenāvinābhāva' kathañciddeśata' kālato vā dṛṣṭa' /
children.translated_text: But the invariable concomitance of this [unique particular] with that universal has never been observed in any way — whether spatially or temporally.

children.text: asādhāraṇasya bhāvāntareṣvanusyūtyasambhavādekatra dṛṣṭasya ca tatraiva niruddhatvāditi ||161||
children.translated_text: Because a unique particular (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) cannot be threaded through other entities, and what is observed in one place is confined to that very place. // 161 //

Objection: An infinite regress in the cognition of the universal-mark arises through inference, if the mark is accepted as being only of universal nature, and inference is required for its non-apprehension, since it is cognizable only through inference. But the unique particular itself will be the inferential mark for the cognition of universals, and since it is perceptual, there is no infinite regress. Therefore he says 'na ca' etc.
Or, through the observation of relation, it would be a universal like 'being-produced' and such;

children.text: nahyasādhāraṇaṃ vastu pūrvatreha ca vidyate // Msv_5,4.162 //
children.translated_text: for a unique particular is not found here and previously. // Msv_5,4.162 //
Nor, for what is inexpressible and devoid of conceptual construction,
is the status of being an inferential mark possible without prior recognition. // Msv_5,4.163 //
And the particularities that are postulated — they too are non-indicative, due to non-co-presence;
for this very reason, the cognition of that too would be non-indicative. // Msv_5,4.164 //
Or, if it has the nature of a universal, there would be the same indeterminacy.
Or, if the observation of relation is admitted, it would follow that it has the nature of a universal, like 'being produced' etc. — thus he says 'syād vā' etc.
He states the reason here — 'na hi' etc. // 162 //

children.text:
itaścāsādhāraṇor'thātmā na liṅgamityāha---na ceti /
dhūmādarhidhūmo 'yamityādivikalpāspadīkṛto 'gnayāderliṅgamiti dṛṣṭam /
asādhāramastu kenacidrūpeṇāpyavyapadeśya' kathaṃ liṅgaṃ bhavediti /
liṅgatvaṃ nopapadyata iti vakṣyamāṇena sambandha iti /
nanu tiraścāmasatyeva śabdollekhe 'sādhāraṇarūpadarśināmevānumānaṃ dṛṣṭamato nāvyapadeśyatvādaliṅgatvamata āha---vikalpeti pādatrayeṇa /
ayamabhiprāya'---- mā nāma tiraścāṃ śabdollekho bhavet, arthavikalpastu teṣāmapi pūrvāparānusandhānātmako 'styeva /
children.translated_text: The purport is: Let there be no verbal designation for animals; but conceptual construction in the form of connecting the prior and the posterior does exist even for them.
Therefore, it is justified that for their inference too, how can the indesignatable be a mark?

children.text: na hi so 'yamityānārūḍho buddhau dhūmo 'gnerliṅgaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: For smoke that has not mounted upon the cognition as 'this is that' does not serve as a mark for fire.
And this is not possible for the <s>asādhāraṇa</s>, because it is beyond the scope of connecting the prior and the posterior.

For this further reason too, the <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (uncommon) essential nature is not a <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) — so he says 'na ca.' For we have observed that smoke, when made the basis of a conceptual construction such as 'this is smoke,' serves as a mark for fire and the like. But the <s>asādhāraṇa</s> — being indesignatable by any form whatsoever — how could it be a mark? That the mark-status is unjustified is connected with what will be stated. But animals, even without verbal designation, are seen to infer when they perceive <s>asādhāraṇa</s> forms — so the mark-status should not be denied on account of indesignability — hence he says 'conceptual construction' with three quarters [of a verse].

children.text: asmanmate 'pi ye 'sādhāraṇātmāno dhūmādayo viśeṣā vikalpyante te 'pyanvayābāvādaliṅgaṃ, kimaṅga punarnirvikalpakaikagocaro 'sādhāraṇor'thātmā ityāha---kalpyantaiti /
children.translated_text: Even in our view, those particulars of smoke and the like that are conceptualized as having an <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (uncommon) nature are not marks due to the absence of <s>anvaya</s> (co-presence). How much less, then, the <s>asādhāraṇa</s> essential nature that is the sole object of non-conceptual [cognition] — so he says 'are conceptualized.'

For this very reason — the absence of <s>anvaya</s> — the knowledge of the <s>asādhāraṇa</s> is also not a mark for the knowledge of the universal of the <s>liṅgin</s> (mark-possessor) — so he says 'for this very reason.'

children.text: yadi tvanvayasiddhyarthamasādhāraṇasya sāmānyarūpateṣyate, tato liṅgasāmānyagrahaṇa ivānavasthāprasaṅgāt tasyāpyanavadhāraṇamityāha---
children.translated_text: But if, for the purpose of establishing the <s>anvaya</s>, the <s>asādhāraṇa</s> is accepted as having a universal form, then, just as in the apprehension of the universal of the mark, there would follow the consequence of infinite regress, and therefore that too would remain undetermined — so he says:

children.text: kvacidvā dṛṣṭasambandhe sarva' pratyāyako bhavet // Msv_5,4.165 //
children.translated_text: or, if the connection is observed somewhere, everything would be an indicator of everything.
And the experience of the connection of the <s>liṅgin</s> (mark-possessor) must necessarily be posited;

children.text: anumānapravṛttestu prāṅmānaṃ tatra nāsti te // Msv_5,4.166 //
children.translated_text: but before the operation of inference, you have no <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) for it.
Nor is the origination of the mark-cognition possible from a mere <s>vāsanā</s> (dispositional impression);

children.text: liṅgijñānaṃ ca tadvat syāt trirūpālliṅgato na tat // Msv_5,4.167 //
children.translated_text: and the cognition of the mark-possessor would be likewise [from vāsanā] — [for] that is not from the triple-characterized mark.
'The universal' etc.

children.text: yadi tu kasmiṃścidevāsādhāraṇe sāmānyena jñātasambandhe 'nyadarśināpi sāmānyamanumīyate /
children.translated_text: If, however, in some particular <s>asādhāraṇa</s> whose connection is known through the universal, even one who has seen other [instances] infers the universal —

children.text: evaṃ tarhi sarva eva sarvasya pratyāyako bhavet /
children.translated_text: then, in that case, everything would be an indicator of everything,
because of the lack of distinction — so he says 'somewhere.'
Now he states that at the time of non-apprehension of the <s>anvaya</s>, there is also no <s>pramāṇa</s> for the cognition of the <s>liṅgin</s> (mark-possessor) either — he says:
'the experience of the connection' etc.
Without the <s>liṅgin</s> being apprehended, the mark connected with it cannot be understood.

children.text: na cānumānapravṛtte' prāk tasmin sāmānyātmani bhavata' kiñcit pramāṇamastyasmākamiva pratyakṣam, ato lliṅginyapyavagamyamāne 'navasthāprasaṅga ityabhiprāya' ||166||
children.translated_text: And before the operation of inference, for you, regarding that [mark-possessor] which is of a universal nature, there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> such as perception (as we have) — therefore, even with the <s>liṅgin</s> being unascertained, the consequence of infinite regress follows — this is the purport.
Thus it has been stated that there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for determining the mark.

children.text:
nanvanādikālīnavāsanāmātranibandhana evāyaṃ liṅgaliṅgisaṃvyavahāra', kimihātinirbandhena /
kācideva hi vāsanodbhūtā kiñcilliṅgākāraṃ vikpamāvirbhāvayantī kiñcidevānumāsaṃvyavahāraṃ pravartayati /
yathāhu'---'sa evāyamanumānānumeyavyavahāro buddhyārūḍhena dharmadharminyāyena , na bahi' sadasattvamapekṣata' iti, ata āha---na cāpīti /

children.translated_text: The cognition of the mark is not produced merely by <s>vāsanā</s>.
For <s>vāsanā</s> is a dispositional impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) deposited by prior experience.

children.text: nāsau lihgasāmānyasya śaśaviṣāṇādivadatyantāsata' sambhavatīti kathaṃ vāsanāmātrālliṅgajñānasya sambhava iti /
children.translated_text: That [dispositional impression] is not possible for the universal of the mark, which is absolutely non-existent like the horn of a hare — so how could the cognition of the mark arise from mere <s>vāsanā</s>?

children.text: tannibandhane liṅgajñāna iṣyamāṇe tadvadeva liṅgijñānopapattarenarthakaṃ trirūpāliṅgator'thadṛganumānamityanumānaprāmāṇyāśrayaṇamityāha---liṅgijñānaṃ ceti ||167||
children.translated_text: If the cognition of the mark is accepted as based on that [vāsanā], then the cognition of the mark-possessor would similarly be justified — making it pointless to resort to the authority of inference from the triple-characterized mark as an instrument for seeing objects — so he says 'the cognition of the mark-possessor too.'

"But this transaction of mark and mark-possessor is based merely on beginningless <s>vāsanā</s> (dispositional impressions) — why such insistence here? For some <s>vāsanā</s>-born [cognition], manifesting some mark-form through conceptual construction, gives rise to some inferential transaction. As they say: 'This very transaction of inference and inferrable, through the principle of property and property-bearer mounted upon cognition, does not depend on external existence or non-existence.'" Hence he says — 'nor also' etc.
Where the absence has the status of a mark, and that [absence] is not an object of inference,

children.text: pramāṇāntaragamyatvāt tatra doṣo na jāyate // Msv_5,4.168 //
children.translated_text: because it is cognized by another <s>pramāṇa</s> — in that case, no fault arises.
For one whose cognition of the mark-possessor arises from a mark apprehended by perception,

children.text: tasya nāto 'dhikaṃ kiñcit prārthanīyaṃ prasajyate // Msv_5,4.169 //
children.translated_text: for him, nothing further need be desired beyond this.
And where the cognition of the mark-possessor arises from an inferred mark,

children.text: tatrāpi maulikaṃ liṅgaṃ pratyakṣādeva gamyate // Msv_5,4.170 //
children.translated_text: even there, the primary mark is cognized through perception alone.
The mark-status in being-produced and the like, of the action or the <s>kāraka</s> (factor of action),

children.text: pratyakṣatvaṃ ca tasyeṣṭamiti dūraṃ na gamyate // Msv_5,4.171 //
children.translated_text: and the perceptibility of that is accepted — so one need not go far.

children.text: nanviyamanavasthā meghābhāvena vṛṣṭhyabhāvānumāne bhavato 'pi samānaiva, abhāvasyānupalabdhiliṅgatvāt /

children.translated_text: If a mark of the same kind is required for that, infinite regress would follow."
Hence he says — 'where' etc.

children.text: yatra hi vṛṣṭyabhāve meghābhāvo liṅgaṃ nāsāvanumeya', abhāvākhyapramāṇāntaragamyatvāt /
children.translated_text: For where, regarding the absence of rain, the absence of clouds is the mark — that [absence] is not something to be inferred, because it is cognized by another <s>pramāṇa</s> called <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence).
Therefore, the fault of infinite regress based on requiring a mark of the same kind does not arise here.
"But this infinite regress equally befalls you in the inference of the absence of rain from the absence of clouds — because absence has non-perception (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) as its mark.
But for those who hold that the universal is perceived — for us, there is no infinite regress at all — so he says 'from what is apprehended by perception' etc.
Therefore 'from perception' — that is the meaning.
"But then there would be an infinite regress in the case of inference from what is itself inferred" — hence he says 'and where' etc.

children.text: pratyakṣā hi deśāntaraprāptirmaulikaṃ mūle bhavaṃ liṅgaṃ, tena gatimanumāyāditye gatisādhane 'numīyamāne nāvasthetyabhiprāya' ||170||
children.translated_text: For the arrival at another location is perceptible — that is the primary mark, existing at the root — by which, having inferred movement, when movement is further inferred as the means of reaching the sun, there is no infinite regress — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanvanitya' śabda' kṛtakatvāt, kṛtakatvaṃ catatra darśanādityevaṃ karmānantarabhāvitayā kṛtakatve sādhyamāne karmaṇo 'pi hetvantarādanumāne 'navasthā bhavedata āha--- liṅgatvamiti /
"kṛtakatvānumāne hi karmaike tatra darśanād" /
iti kārakavyāpārāntarabhāvitvaṃ liṅgamuktam /
tatra ca kārakāviśiṣṭā kriyā tadviśiṣṭaṃ vā kārakamantarabhāvitāṃ viśiṣalliṅgamāpatati /
ubhayaṃ
children.translated_text: "But 'sound is impermanent because of being-produced, and being-produced is there because of perception' — thus, when being-produced is established as conditioned by being subsequent to effort, and when that effort too requires another reason for inference, there would be infinite regress" — hence he says 'mark-status' etc. In the inference of being-produced, 'the action alone is the mark there, because of its being seen.' Thus, the conditioned-ness by another <s>kāraka</s> operation is stated as the mark. And therein, either the action not differentiated from the <s>kāraka</s>, or the <s>kāraka</s> qualified by that [action], constitutes the specific mark of the conditioned entity. Both
thus, in the case of verbal testimony, analogy, and the like too, there is dependence on the universal;
by its instability, instability would follow everywhere.
Therefore, being preceded by perception is accepted in the case of other <s>pramāṇas</s>;

children.text: pratyakṣatvaṃ ca sāmānye nānyatā hi gatirbhavet // Msv_5,4.173 //
children.translated_text: and the perceptibility of the universal — for no other course is possible.
And how could the particular be an object of perception,

children.text: yadā vastvamtarāpekṣa' sāmānyāṃśa' sa kīrtyate // Msv_5,4.174 //
children.translated_text: when the aspect called 'universal' is declared to require another real entity?
For color and the like are all a universal relative to blue and the like as their own [specifics];
and then, similarly, relative to their own specifics, the equality of blue and the like [is a universal].

children.text:
ca tatpratyakṣam /
kriyāyāstāvat pratyakṣatvamanantarameva sādhitam /
kārakamapi tadvat pratyakṣameva /
śaktistu parokṣā /

children.translated_text: And that, for now, is not a mark here.
Nor is it an inferrable.
Therefore, since both action and <s>kāraka</s> are perceptible, one need not go far afield.
For even those who hold that the action is inferrable — due to the settling upon the result, there is no infinite regress; and all the more so for us.
and that is perceptible. The perceptibility of action has been established just previously. The <s>kāraka</s> too is likewise perceptible. But capacity (<s>śakti</s>) is beyond the senses.

children.text: evaṃ tāvadanumāsyāsati sāmānyasya vastutve pratyakṣatve ca dausthityamuktam idānīṃ sarvameva pramāṇajātaṃ sāmānyasya
children.translated_text: Thus, the instability of inference has been stated when the universal lacks reality and perceptibility. Now, the entire class of <s>pramāṇas</s> would become unstable in the instability of the universal,
because they too depend on the universal.
And that [pramāṇa-class] is not non-authoritative, due to the reasoning to be stated — with this purport he says 'thus.'

children.text: ato 'vaśyaṃ pramāṇāntarāṇāṃ pratyakṣapūrvakatvameṣṭavyaṃ sāmānyasya ca pratyatvam, itarathā tvanavasthā prāpnotītyupasaṃharati---tasmāditi ||173||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the precedence of perception for other <s>pramāṇas</s> must necessarily be accepted, and the perceptibility of the universal — otherwise infinite regress would follow — so he concludes: 'therefore.'

children.text: evaṃ tāvat sāmānyasya pratyakṣatvaṃ vastutā copapāditā idānīṃ viśeṣā eva pratyakṣeṇa gṛhyanta iti ye vadanti tān pratyāha---pratyakṣeti /
children.translated_text: Thus, the perceptibility and reality of the universal have been justified. Now, to those who say that only particulars are grasped by perception, he replies — 'perception' etc.

children.text: viśeṣo hi yadi tāvadavayavī dravyamabhimata', cāvayavavastvantarāpekṣa' sāmānyāṃśo 'smābhi' kīrtyata iti kathaṃ pratyakṣa iti ||174||
children.translated_text: For if the particular is accepted as a substance possessing parts (<s>avayavin</s>), we declare it to be the universal aspect, requiring another real entity as a part — so how could it be perceptible?

children.text:
yadi tvavayavirūpādaya eva viśeṣā iṣyante, tadapyayuktam /
te 'pi hi svaviśeṣanīlādyapekṣayā sāmānayamevetyāha---rūpādayo hīti /
children.translated_text: But if the particulars are accepted as being color and the like themselves, that too is unjustified. For they too are simply a universal relative to their own specifics, blue and the like — so he says 'color and the like.'

children.text: te cāpi tāvat sāmānyaṃ yāvat syu' paramāṇava' /
children.translated_text: And those too are a universal, all the way down to atoms;

children.text: dvyaṇukasyāpi yadarūpaṃ taddhi sādhāraṇaṃ dvayo' // Msv_5,4.176 //
children.translated_text: and the form of even a dyad — that is common to both.
And with the ultimate particular, no one has any practical dealings;

children.text: na ca pratyakṣatātsaya saṅghāte kevalasya vā // Msv_5,4.177 //
children.translated_text: nor is there perceptibility of that — whether in an aggregate or separately.
What is not grasped through difference cannot attain graspability through non-difference;
and of what is different, the possibility of a cognition of non-difference as an object to be grasped does not exist.

children.text: yadi tu nīlādaya eva viśeṣā iti matam /
children.translated_text: But if the view is that blue and the like alone are the particulars —
that is not so,
because they too have the form of universals relative to their sub-specifics of blue etc. — so he says 'relative to their own specifics.'

children.text:
yadi tvekabhramarādidravayanīlimaiva viśeṣa iṣyate, tanna /
tasyāpi pakṣādisvāvayavāśritanīlaviśeṣāpekṣayā sāmānyarūpatvāt /
pakṣanīlimāpi tadavayavanīlāpekṣayā sāmānyameva /
evaṃ ca aparamāṇubhya' prasaṅgo darśayitanya ityāha---te cāpīti /
nirbhāgā hi paramāṇava iti tadarūpamasādhāraṇameveti || tebhyastu prāk dvyaṇukarūpamapi dvayo' sādhāraṇamityāha--- dvyaṇukasyāpīti ||176||
children.translated_text: But if the blue-ness of a single bee or such substance alone is accepted as the particular — that is not so. Because even that has the form of a universal relative to the blue-specifics inhering in its own parts such as wings. The blue of the wings too is simply a universal relative to the blue of its sub-parts. Thus, the consequence [of regress] is to be shown all the way down to atoms — so he says 'and those too.' For atoms are partless, so their form is uncommon — from them onwards, however, even the form of a dyad is common to both [atoms]. So he says 'and of even a dyad.'

children.text: nanvastu paramāṇurūpameva viśeṣa', sa eva na' pratyakṣo bhaviṣyatyata āha---na cāntyeneti /

children.translated_text: For a <s>pramāṇa</s> is sought for the purpose of practical activity, not out of compulsive interest.

children.text: na cāntyena viśeṣeṇa vyavahāra' kasyacidastīti kiṃ tatpratyakṣatayeti /
children.translated_text: And with the ultimate particular, no one has any practical dealings — so what use is its perceptibility?

children.text: nanūpekṣāphalamapi pramāṇaṃ bhavatyeva, ata āha---na ceti /
children.translated_text: "But even a <s>pramāṇa</s> whose result is disregard does exist" — hence he says 'nor' etc.

children.text: na na' kaparamāṇūnāṃ rūpaṃ sthūle vartamānānāṃ tantūnāmiva paṭe pratyakṣaṃ vibhaktānāṃ veti na kathañcid viśeṣaviṣayatā pratyakṣasyeti ||177||
children.translated_text: For us, the form of atoms — whether present in gross [objects] like threads in a cloth, or separated — is not perceptible; thus, there is no way the particular can be the object of perception.
"But let the form of the atom alone be the particular — that alone will be perceptible for us" — hence he says 'and with the ultimate' etc.

children.text:
nanu paramāṇava eva bhinnā' sañcitā gṛhyante na kāryadravyamekam /
ata' kathaṃ tatsāvayaveṣu sāmānyamityucyate /
sañcitā eva cānanyavṛttitayā viśeṣāsādhāraṇādipadavācyā iti te pratyakṣā bhaviṣyanti /
mā nāmaikaikata' paramāṇurakṣagocaro bhavedata āha--- bhedeneti /
