children.text: nyāyyavacanavyaktiparicayāt pūrvaṃ śabdādanekārthā' pariplavante,tathā liṅge 'pi dhūmādāvasphuṭavidite 'nekārthapratibhānandaṣṭameva /
children.translated_text: Before familiarity with the particular instances of conventional usage, from words multiple meanings waver — similarly, even in the case of an inferential mark like smoke etc. when not clearly known, the appearance of multiple meanings has indeed been observed.

children.text: bhavati hi dūrād dhūmo 'yamāhosvid dhūlisantāna iti saṃśayānasyāgnivātāvartayoranavasthito vitarka iti ||32||
children.translated_text: For one who doubts 'Is this smoke from afar or a stream of dust?' — the deliberation between fire and a whirlwind is unsettled. // 32 //

children.text: tathā śabde dṛṣṭāntānabhidhānamapi dhūmādau vyabhicārānna bhedaheturityāha---dṛṣṭānteti /
children.translated_text: Similarly, regarding verbal testimony, the non-statement of the example in the case of smoke etc. too is not a cause of difference, due to deviation — thus he says 'dṛṣṭānta' etc.
How is there deviation? — therefore he says 'prasiddhatvāt' etc. // 33 //

children.text: nanvaprasiddhe tāvadasti dṛṣṭāntāpekṣā, śabde tu tadapi nāstītyata āha---anabhyastaiti /
children.translated_text: Objection: When unfamiliar, there is indeed a need for the example; but in the case of words, even that does not exist — therefore he says 'anabhyasta' etc.
He shows the need itself — 'atra' etc.

children.text: yatra hyaprasiddhapadārthagocara' saṃśayo bhavati, tatra yāvadayaṃ śabdo 'muṣminnarthe vṛddhairācarita iti cireṇa praṇidhāya na budhyate, na tāvat tamarthaṃ niścinuyāditi /
children.translated_text: For where there is doubt regarding the referent of an unfamiliar word, as long as one does not discern through careful investigation that 'this word is used by the learned in this meaning,' one does not ascertain that meaning.

children.text: tadevaṃ tāvad bhedavādibhirna bhedahetava' samyaguktā iti darśitam ||34||
children.translated_text: Thus it has been shown that the proponents of difference have not properly stated the reasons for difference. // 34 //

children.text:
bauddhoktābhedahetunirāso 'pi tairna kṛta ityāha--- paroktā iti /
tānevābhedahetūnupanyasyati--- śabdānumānayoriti
sārdadvayena /
asyārtha'--- yathā dhūmādagnyanumānamanvayavyatirekajam, ekasya ca dhūmasya pratyakṣadarśanāt,
children.translated_text: The refutation of the Buddhist reasons for non-difference too has not been made by them — thus he says 'paroktā' etc. He presents those very reasons for non-difference — 'śabdānumānayoḥ' etc. with two and a half [verses]. The meaning is: just as the inference of fire from smoke is born from positive and negative concomitance, and from the perceptual observation of a single [instance of] smoke,
because it is other than perception, because it conveys an unseen object,
because it has universals as its object, and because it pertains to all three times— // Msv_5,5.37 //
by some <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, difference has been stated here on the ground of a different object;
for scripture operates regarding a meaning not determined by the first two [pramāṇas]. // Msv_5,5.38 //

children.text:
sambandhapūrvakaṃ ca bhavati, evaṃ śabdādapi jñānaṃ jāyamānamevaṃ jāyate /
pratyakṣācca tadanyat pramāṇaṃ, pratyakṣādṛṣṭaṃ cārthaṃ bodhayati, sāmānyaviṣayaṃ ca śābdaṃ, traikālyāśrayaṃ ca /
ato na bhidyate /
idaṃ ca sādhanavākyasyārthakathanam /
sādhanaprayogāstvevaṃ darśayitavyā'---- śābdaṃ jñānamanumānamanvayavyatirekajatvāt agnyanumānavaditi /
ekapratyakṣadarśanotpatte', tadvadeva sambandhapūrvakatvaṃ(vā?ca) hetu' /
tāveva sādhyadṛṣṭāntau /
na ca katavācyamanvayavyatirekajatvāt sambandhapūrvakatvaṃ na bhidyate, anvayavyatirekātmakatvādanumānasambandhasyeti /
pūrvaṃ hi sambandhaviśeṣajatvaṃ heturukta' idānīṃ tvavivakṣitaviśeṣaṃ sambandhasāmānyapūrvakatvamiti /
children.translated_text: For previously, arising from a specific relation was stated as the reason; now, however, it is being preceded by the relation in general, without specifying the particular.
Similarly, in the remaining three [reasons] too, the arrangement of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> should be made as before.
In the fourth, however, the inference of fire is merely illustrative.
It should be shown even in inferences regarding future and past events that have not [yet/no longer] occurred. // 35-37 //

and is preceded by [knowledge of] the relation — so too the cognition arising from words arises in the same way. And it is a <s>pramāṇa</s> other than perception; and it conveys a meaning not seen by perception; and verbal cognition has universals as its object; and it pertains to all three times. Therefore there is no difference. And this is the statement of the meaning of the proof-sentence. The formal proofs are to be shown thus: 'Verbal cognition is inference, because of arising from positive and negative concomitance, like the inference of fire.' 'Because of arising from the observation of a single perceptible [instance]' — likewise 'because of being preceded by the relation' — these are the reasons. The <s>sādhya</s> and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> are the same. Nor should it be said: 'Being preceded by the relation is not different from arising from positive and negative concomitance, since the relation of inference is of the nature of positive and negative concomitance.'

children.text:
mīmāṃsakaikadeśināṃ bhedahetumidānīṃ dūṣayitumupanyasyati---kaiściditi /
viṣayāntarameva darśayati--- pūrvābhyāmiti /
ayamabhiprāya'--- yadayadaparicchinne pavartate tat tato bhidyate, anumānamiva pratyakṣāt /
śāstraṃ ca pūrvadvayāparicchinner'the pravartate /
tatastābhyāṃ bhidyate /
kiṃ puna' pratyakṣād bhedapratipādanena prayojanam, na hi tadabheda' kaiścidāśrita', yannirākriyate /
ucyate /
astyeva keṣāñcid vibhrama', śrotravyāpārāśrayājjāyamānamidaṃ śābdaṃ śrotrapratyakṣameva,tadanvayavyatirekānuvidhānāt /
ata eva badhirasya na bhavatīti /
tadanena pratyakṣato bhedapratipādanena nirākriyate /
evaṃ hi manyate--- vidyamānopalambhanaṃ pratyakṣamiti darśitam /
children.translated_text: For he thinks thus: It was shown that perception is the apprehension of what is present.

children.text: idaṃ tu śābdaṃ trikālārthaviṣayamata' kathaṃ pratyakṣe 'ntarbhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: But verbal knowledge (<s>śābda</s>) has as its object things of all three times — so how would it be subsumed under perception?
And the deaf person does not know the object because he does not hear the words, not because he does not hear the objects.

children.text: prayogaśca bhavati--- śābdaṃ pratyakṣād bhinnaṃ tadaparicchinnaviṣayatvād anumānavaditi ||38||
children.translated_text: And the argument can be formulated: Verbal knowledge (<s>śābda</s>) is different from perception, because its object is not ascertained by that [perception], like inference.

He now presents, for the purpose of refuting, the reason for distinction held by some <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> of a particular school — 'by some.' He shows a different subject-matter — 'from the previous two.' The purport is: Whatever operates on an object not ascertained [by the previous two] is different from them, just as inference is different from perception. And scripture operates on objects not ascertained by the preceding two [pramāṇas]. Therefore, it is different from them. "But what is the purpose of establishing the difference from perception? — for no one holds that non-difference." It is said: There is indeed confusion on the part of some, who think that verbal knowledge (<s>śābda</s>), arising through the operation of the ear, is simply auditory perception — because it conforms to the co-presence and co-absence of that [ear]. Therefore, the deaf person does not have it. This is refuted by establishing the difference from perception.
Even there, it would not be <s>āgama</s> (scripture), since it is spoken by a person; and if it be so —

children.text: pratyaya' kinnimittor'the vaktṛbuddhe' kuto vasau // Msv_5,5.39 //
children.translated_text: the cognition has what cause? What is the basis for confidence in the speaker's cognition regarding the object?

children.text:
tadimaṃ pratyakṣato bhedamabhyupetyānumānād bhedakāraṇaṃ nirākaroti---tatrāpīti /
evaṃ hi manyate--- yadyanumānāparicchinnaviṣatayā bhedo 'bhidhīyate, tarhi puṃvākyānāmanāgamatvam, pramāṇāntaraparicchinnaviṣayavāt, vedavākyānyeva tu mānāntarāviṣayārthāni bhidyante ityavyāpako heturiti /
kiṃ punaridamaniṣṭamāpāditam, nanviṣyata eva puṃvacasāmanāgamatvam, āgamo hi śāstram,aprāpte śāstramarthavaditi /
vakṣyati /
imāni puna' pramāṇāntaraprāptaviṣayapratipādakānītyanuvādavākyānyeva /
ata eva śāstrameva vedavākyaṃ bhinnatayā pakṣīkṛtaṃ 'śāstramarthe pravartata'iti /
tadbhedasthaivopayogāditi bhāva' /
tadetadāha--- yatheti /
atra dūṣaṇamāha--- pratyaya iti /
evamayaṃ paṃvacanāprāmāṇyāvādī vaktavya' /
kimasti tebhyor'thapratyayo na vā, na tāvannāsti, sarvalokavyavahārocchedaprasaṅgāt /
satastu nānimittotpatti' sambhavatīti nimittaṃ vācyam /
na ca śabdādanyannimittamasyopapadyata iti jātamasandagdhamabādhitaṃ ca jñānāntareṇa pramāṇameva puṃvacanajanitaṃ jñānamiti nāsyānāgamatvābyupagamo yukta iti /
itarastvanumānāntarbhāvābhiprāyeṇāha--- vaktṛbuddheriti /
ayamabhiprāya'--- visaṃvādabhūyiṣṭāni hi puṃvacanāni, tannaitāni śrutamātrāṇyevārthaṃ niścāyayanti /
na cāniścitor'tho jñāto bhavati, niścayasyaiva jñānatvāt /
ata' praṅ(?) niścayotpatterjñānābhāva evanti kiṃ nimittaprayatnena /
yadā tu
vaktaivamavadhāritavyāptirbhavati--- 'na cāyamanavagataṃ bravītī'ti, tadā tadvākyādeva jñānakāryāt kāraṇabhūtaṃ jñāyamanumāya jñānasyārthāvyabhicāreṇārtho niścīyate /
tasyāṃ cāvasthāyāṃ jñānaliṅgāvagatatvādarthasya vākyamanuvādakameva /

children.translated_text: Therefore, it is not <s>āgama</s>.
But the <s>siddhāntin</s> (proponent of the established conclusion) says — 'from where indeed.'
The purport is: For the cognition that is ascertained does make the object certain.

children.text: na cāsyā' kiñcidavagame kāraṇastīti vakṣyāma iti ||39||
children.translated_text: But there is no means of ascertaining it — this we shall state.

Having accepted this difference from perception, he now refutes the reason for difference from inference — 'even there' etc. For he thinks thus: If the difference is stated on the ground that the object is not ascertained by inference, then human statements would not be <s>āgama</s>, since their object is ascertained by another <s>pramāṇa</s>; only <s>Vedic</s> sentences, dealing with objects not within the scope of any other <s>pramāṇa</s>, would be different — and so the reason would be non-pervasive. "But what undesirable consequence is thereby produced? — for we do accept that human statements are not <s>āgama</s>. For <s>āgama</s> is <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative teaching), and scripture operates on what is not otherwise available" — so it will be stated. And these [human statements], dealing with objects available to other <s>pramāṇas</s>, are merely restatements (<s>anuvāda</s>). For this very reason, only the <s>Vedic</s> sentence, being adopted as the thesis of a distinct [<s>pramāṇa</s>], was stated as '<s>śāstra</s> operates on its object.' Its utility lies precisely in that distinctive status — this is the purport. He states this — 'as it is' etc. He raises an objection to this — 'the cognition' etc. This opponent who denies the non-validity of human speech is to be asked: Is there a cognition of the object from those [human statements], or not? It is not the case that there is none — because there would follow the destruction of all worldly transactions. And given that it exists, its arising is not possible without a cause — so the cause must be stated. And no cause other than the word is possible for it — so the knowledge generated by human speech, being born, undoubted, and unsublated by another cognition, is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Therefore, it is not proper to accept its non-<s>āgama</s> status. The other [opponent], with the intention of subsuming it under inference, says — 'of the speaker's cognition.' The purport is: Human statements are mostly unreliable; therefore, these, merely upon being heard, do not produce certainty regarding the object. And an object not ascertained is not known, since only certainty is knowledge. Therefore, before the arising of certainty, there is an absence of knowledge itself — so what use is effort regarding the cause? But when the speaker's invariable concomitance has been ascertained thus: 'This person does not speak what he has not understood' — then from his very statement, the cognition (which is the effect) is inferred, and through the cognition, the cause — namely, the object — is inferred; and through the non-deviation of cognition from the object, the object is ascertained. And in that state, since the object has been ascertained through the mark of cognition, the sentence is merely a restatement.

children.text: na śabdārthasya sā liṅgaṃ na śabdo 'syā' kathañcana /
children.translated_text: That [speaker's cognition] is not a mark of the word's object, nor is the word in any way [a mark] of it;

children.text: viśeṣo gamyate tābhyāṃ na caitasyānumeyatā // Msv_5,5.40 //
children.translated_text: a specific [content] is understood from those two, but inferability of this [verbal meaning] does not follow.
Therefore, when the speaker's intention is not ascertained by perception and the like,
even a human statement attains the status of <s>āgama</s> (scripture) for the listener.

children.text:
ata' svayamevānavagatā nārthasya liṅgamityāha--- neti /
nanūktaṃ kāryāt śabdādanumāsyate, ata āha--- na śabda iti /
yatā nobhayamubhayatra liṅgaṃ, tathā darśayati--- viśeṣa iti /
anumānaṃ hi vyāptibalena bhavati, iha ca vākyasāmānyaṃ jñānasāmānyena vyāptamavagatamiti tatastat sidhyed, jñānamātrāccārthamātram, na ceha tathā, jñānārthaviśeṣayoranumitsitatvāt /
tayośca sambnadhagrahaṇābhāvenānanumeyatvāt /
nanu yatrāpto vākyaṃ prayuṅkte tadeva jñātvā prayuṅkta iti vijñānaviśeṣeṇaiva sambandho 'vagata' /
ata' sa evānumāsyate /
yadyevam, avagatastarhi prāgeva vākyādartha', na hyanyathā yatra prayuṅkta iti śakyate pratinirdeṣṭum /
na cārthoparāgamantareṇa jñānasya viśeṣa' sambhavati yo 'numīyate /
na cākarmakaṃ jñānamātramanumīyate /
na ca tator'thaviśeṣastidhyati /
na cāniścitaṃ jñānaṃ, saṃśayātmano vijñānavidhāyā darśitatvāt /
na caivaṃ puṃvākyebhya' sandeha' /
yā tu kvacid vyabhicārādaprāmāṇyāśaṅkā sā āptatvādinā nirākriyata ityuktam /
yadi tveva jñānaviśeṣāvagatirucyate, ya evamavadhārito bhavati--- nāyamananvitārthāni padāni prayuṅkte, na cānavagatānvayāni, tannūnamamīṣāmanenānvayo jñāta iti /
kimidānīṃ viditapadapadārthasaṅgati' śrotā puṃvākyādarthaṃ na budhyata eva /
yadyevamanuttarā gurava' /
jātā tu buddhirasandigdhāviparyastā ca na vaidavākyajanitāyā dhiyo viśiṣyeta /
children.translated_text: And the cognition that has arisen — undoubted and unreversed — would not differ from the cognition generated by a <s>Vedic</s> sentence.

children.text: śaṅkāmātraṃ tu kathañcid vede 'pi vākyatvādinā bhavatīti na tāvatā tadaprāmāṇyam /
children.translated_text: And mere doubt, through word-ness and the like, arises to some extent even in the <s>Veda</s> — so that alone does not make it non-authoritative.
'From those two' —
means: from cognition and word — that is the meaning.

Therefore, since [the speaker's cognition] is itself unascertained, it is not a mark of the object — so he says 'not' etc. "But it was said that it is inferred from the effect — the word" — hence he says 'nor the word.' Since neither of the two is a mark of the other, he shows this — 'a specific.' For inference operates by the force of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion). And here, the general statement is understood as pervaded by general cognition — so from that, that would follow; and from mere cognition, mere meaning. But it is not so here, because the specific cognition and specific object are what one desires to infer. And because of the absence of apprehending their connection, they are not inferable. "But where a trustworthy person makes a statement, he states precisely what he knows — so the connection is understood with a specific cognition. Therefore, that specific [cognition] is inferred." If so, then the object is already known prior to the statement — for otherwise, one cannot specify what exactly he states. And without the coloring of the object, no specific form of cognition is possible that could be inferred. Nor is mere objectless cognition inferred. Nor does a specific object follow from that. Nor is it an uncertain cognition, because the nature of doubt as a form of cognition has been shown. And there is no doubt from human statements in this way. As for the suspicion of non-validity arising from occasional deviation — that is refuted by the trustworthiness [of the speaker] and such, as stated. But if you do say that a specific cognition is understood — one who has been ascertained thus: 'This person does not employ words with unconnected meanings, nor with connections he has not understood — so surely the connection of these [words] is known by him' — then what? Does not a listener who knows the relations of words and their meanings understand the object from a human statement?
Therefore, when the speaker's intention is not ascertainable, and perception and the like as <s>pramāṇas</s> are impossible, in the absence of that ascertainment,
nor can the non-inferability of the object of <s>āgama</s> be maintained;

children.text: liṅgaṃ hi śabda evāsya dhūmo 'gneriva kalpate // Msv_5,5.42 //
children.translated_text: for the word alone is its mark, just as smoke is supposed [to be the mark] of fire.
And from its non-inferability, it does not follow that it is cognizable by another <s>pramāṇa</s>;
for form's non-audibility does not mean it is accepted as non-perceptible.
The matter being thus, some of our own school, without excessive effort,
[say]: this is a special kind of inference that communicates such a <s>dharma</s> (property).
But the mark in the form of the object will be refuted in [the discussion of] <s>dharma</s>.

Because the inference of the object is unjustified, human speech too, which conveys to the listener an object not previously obtained, is <s>āgama</s> (scripture) just like the <s>Veda</s> — so he says 'therefore.'

children.text:
yadapi cedamucyate /
vedastāvad bhinnaviṣayatayā pramāṇāntarameveti, tadapi manorathamātramevetyāha---na cāpītī /

children.translated_text: The intention is: it cannot be said.
Why can it not be said?
Hence he says — 'mark.'

children.text: yadā pūrvoktairhetubhiraviśeṣeṇa sarvameva śābdamanumānādabhinnamityukaṃ, tadā kathaṃ tadgocarasyānanumeyatvaṃ bhaviṣyatīti bhāva' ||42||
children.translated_text: When it has been stated above, by the aforementioned reasons, that all verbal [testimony] without distinction is non-different from inference — then how will the non-inferability of its object be possible? — this is the purport.
And what is also said — 'At least the <s>Veda</s>, having a different subject-matter, is indeed a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>' — even this is mere wishful thinking — so he says 'nor also.'

children.text: nanvarthātmanā tāvadalliṅgenānanumitapūrvamarthaṃ vedo bodhayatīti pramāṇāntaraṃ bhaviṣyatītyata āha---na ceti /
children.translated_text: "But at least the <s>Veda</s>, by a mark in the form of the object, communicates an object not previously inferred — and so it will be a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>" — hence he says 'nor' etc.
For even though there are sub-differences among smoke-ness, being-produced, and the like, just as they are all inference without abandoning the triple characterization — so it would be here too.

children.text: yadi tu tadeva nāstītyucyate, tat tarhi vacanīyam, kimavāntarabhedopanyāseneti ||43||
children.translated_text: But if it is said that that [triple characterization] itself does not exist — then it must be stated what is the use of presenting sub-differences.

children.text:
anye tu prakṣīṇaśaktayo 'bhedamevāśrityaikadeśina' pratyavasthitā', tad darśayati---evaṃ sthitaiti /
ayaṃ hi teṣāmabhiprāya'--- codanāprāmāṇyaṃ hi pratijñātaṃ, taccānumānatve 'pi vedavaca' sidhyatyeva /
yathaiva hi śabdamadhyād veda' pramāṇam /
evamanumānebhyo vedānumānamiti kimatiprayatnato bedapratipādaneneti /
nanu"bhaviṣyatvād dharmo nānumīyate"ityuktaṃ bhāṣyakāreṇa /
ato 'numānatvābhyupagame tadvarodho bhaved ata,āha--- bhaviṣyatīti /
artharūpaliṅgābhiprāyeṇa tannirākṛtamityartha' ||44 1/2||
children.translated_text: But others, whose strength is exhausted, relying only on non-difference from a particular school-position, stand their ground — he shows this: 'the matter being thus.' For their purport is: The authoritative-ness of <s>codanā</s> (injunction) is what was claimed, and that is established even when verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) has the status of inference. For just as the <s>Veda</s> is authoritative among [the various types of] word, so <s>Vedic</s> inference would be authoritative among inferences — so what is the need of excessive effort to establish a separate [<s>pramāṇa</s>]? "But the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> said: '<s>Dharma</s> is not inferred because it is future-oriented.'" Therefore, if inference-status is accepted, there would be contradiction with that — hence he says 'will be.' The meaning is: that was refuted with the intention of the mark being in the form of the object.
But the desire for mere nominal inference-status would not be a fault even in the case of <s>āgama</s>.
But if the non-difference of verbal testimony and inference is maintained on the basis of a common definition,
then the non-validity of <s>Vedic</s> knowledge would follow, because it does not possess that definition.
For in the case of human statements, from the commonality of reliable-person-statement and non-deviation,
the validity is established through inference-status by definition.
But in the <s>Veda</s>, due to the absence of a reliable human, and without the experience of a connection,
the definition of inference does not apply — and so non-validity would follow.
"But if even partial truth of that [Veda] is granted, it would have inference-status —
from <s>Veda</s>-hood, in cases like <s>Agnihotra</s>, just like the statement about wind-thrown [offerings]."
He refutes this too — 'mere name' etc.

children.text: yadi paścānmānasāmānyādanumānatvaṃ tadastu, na ca tadabhyupagame doṣa ityartha' /
children.translated_text: If the inference-status follows later from the commonality of means of knowledge — let it be so; and there is no fault in accepting that — this is the meaning.

children.text: lakṣaṇaikatvena tvabheda iṣṭe 'numānalakṣaṇābhāvāt pramāṇāntarānabyupagamāccāprāmāṇyameva vedavacasāmāpadyata ityāha--- lakṣaṇeneti ||46||
children.translated_text: But if non-difference is desired on the basis of the unity of definition, then, due to the absence of the definition of inference and the non-acceptance of a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>, non-validity alone would befall <s>Vedic</s> sentences — so he says 'by definition.'
"But was not the unity of definition stated on the basis of the commonality of reliable-person-statement and non-deviation?" — to this he replies: 'reliable-person-statement' etc.

children.text: puṃvākyānāmanena prakāreṇānumānatvāt prāmāṇyaṃ siddhyati na vedavacasāmiti bhāva' ||47||
children.translated_text: The purport is: By this mode, the validity of human statements is established through inference-status, not of <s>Vedic</s> sentences.
Hence he says — 'but in the Veda.'
Due to the absence of a reliable human, non-deviation cannot be inferred through reliable-person-statement-hood.
And the experience of the connection of the <s>Vedas</s> with supersensuous objects is not established — so they would be simply non-authoritative.
That the <s>Vedas</s> are not produced by a reliable person — this will be stated in the <s>Vedādhikaraṇa</s> (chapter on the authority of the Veda).
Why is it not established?

children.text: nanu pramāṇāntarakasaṅgatārthāni vedaikadeśabhūtāni kṣepiṣṭhādivākyāni dṛṣṭvā itarāṇyapyagnihotrādivākyāni vedatvāt satyārthānyanumāsyante /
children.translated_text: "But having observed that <s>Vedic</s> statements that are part of the <s>Veda</s> — such as the <s>kṣepiṣṭha</s> (wind-thrown) statements — are in accord with objects established by other <s>pramāṇas</s>, the other statements too — like those about the <s>Agnihotra</s> — are inferred to have true objects, because of their <s>Veda</s>-hood.
Therefore, inference-status by definition does exist" — hence he says 'but.'
Not in 'one should tie [the animal] to the sun-pillar' — because of inconclusiveness; or like that, there could be figurative usage.
Therefore, the counter-inferences — in this manner, by the direction previously stated —
therefore, if the authority of the verbal <s>pramāṇa</s> is established by the distinction of definition,

children.text: samā loke ca vede ca siddhā vedapramāṇatā // Msv_5,5.51 //
children.translated_text: equally in the world and in the <s>Veda</s>, then the authority of the <s>Veda</s> is established.
And thereby, 'instruction by a reliable person' would not be the definition of <s>āgama</s>;

children.text: nāptasya sambhavo vede loke nāsmāt pramāṇatā // Msv_5,5.52 //
children.translated_text: a reliable person is not possible in the <s>Veda</s>, and in the world, authority does not come from this.

children.text: purastād varṇitaṃ hyetat tasmāt śabdena yā mati' /
children.translated_text: For this has been described before; therefore, the cognition that arises from word —

children.text: tasyā' svata' pramāṇatvaṃ na cet syāddoṣadarśanam // Msv_5,5.53 //
children.translated_text: its authority is intrinsic (<s>svataḥ</s>), unless there is the perception of a defect.

children.text:
etadapi dūṣayati---nādityeti /
ādityayūpavākye vartamāno vedatvaheturanaikāntika iti /
nanu nedaṃ vākyamasatyārtham, ādityaśabdo hi sārupyād gauṇo yūpe vartata iti tatsiddhisūtre vakṣyate, ata āha--- tadvaditi /
children.translated_text: "But this statement is not false in meaning — for the word 'sun' (<s>āditya</s>) figuratively refers to the sacrificial post due to resemblance" — so it will be stated in the <s>Tatsiddhisūtra</s>. Hence he says — 'like that.'
Even the statements about the connection of ritual action and its result could likewise be figurative.

children.text: api ca prāk svamahimnā vedaprāmāṇyabalenāprāmāṇyānumānāni pratyuktāni /
children.translated_text: Moreover, previously the inferences of non-validity were refuted by the inherent strength of the Veda's validity.
But if [inference] were accepted [as the basis], being of equal strength, its spread would be irresistible—hence he says—'therefore not.' // 50 //
He refutes this too — 'not in the sun-pillar' etc. The reason of <s>Veda</s>-hood, operating in the statement about the sun-pillar, is inconclusive.

children.text: ato lakṣaṇabhedenaiva śabdasya pramāṇāntaratve iṣyamāṇe vedā' pramāṇaṃ bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the independence of word [as a pramāṇa] is accepted through a difference in definition, the Vedas become a means of valid knowledge.
And the validity of both the mundane and the Vedic is equally established—hence he says—'therefore.' // 51 //

children.text: lakṣamamapi yathā parairāśritam--- 'āptopadeśa' śabda' iti, tathāpyacāptābhāvānna prāmāṇyaṃ vedsayeti tannāśrayaṇīyamityāha---teneti vedāntena /
children.translated_text: Even as the definition adopted by others is 'verbal testimony is the instruction of a trustworthy person'—even so, since no trustworthy person exists [for the Veda], the Veda would have no validity. Therefore that [definition] should not be adopted—hence he says—'by that,' meaning by that conclusion regarding the Veda.

children.text: loke 'pi nāptatvaṃ prāmāṇye kāraṇamityāha--- loka iti ||52||
children.translated_text: Even in the mundane [domain], trustworthiness is not the cause of validity—hence he says—'in the world.' // 52 //
For [the establishment of] trustworthiness merely removes the suspicion of invalidity.

children.text: prāmāṇyaṃ tu sarvasaṃvidāṃ sahajameveti svata'prāmāṇyevāde varṇitamiti /
children.translated_text: But the validity of all cognitions is innate—this has been explained in the doctrine of intrinsic validity (<s>svataḥprāmāṇya</s>).
What then is the definition of scripture? Hence he says—'therefore.'
The cognition generated by a definitive word is a means of valid knowledge. // 53 //
He states the reason—'previously.'
And the validity of this [verbal testimony] has only [this much] in common with inference;

children.text: pade tāvatkṛto yatna' parairityatra varṇyate // Msv_5,5.54 //
children.translated_text: others have first made an effort regarding the word—this is explained here.
The object appears to be different for the inferential mark and for the word;
and [the author] will establish that the word has a universal as its object.
It has been established that the locus of the mark (<s>liṅgin</s>) is the property-bearer qualified by the property;

children.text: na tāvadanumānaṃ hi yāvat tadviṣayaṃ na tat // Msv_5,5.56 //
children.translated_text: for it is not inference so long as it does not have that [qualified entity] as its object.
But in verbal [testimony], the domain of the sentence is something over and above the universal;
because of the inferability from capacity, even when another word is unheard.

children.text: evañjātīyakasya śabdasya cānumānena prāmāṇyameva samaṃ, na lakṣaṇamityāha---anumāneneti ||53 1/2||
children.translated_text: And the validity of word of this kind has only [this much] in common with inference, not its definition—hence he says—'with inference.' // 53½ //
Now, about to state according to his own view the difference of the word from inference, he states the reason for that exposition—'the word.' // 54 //

children.text: yadyapi padasya padārthe pramāṇatvānna tadbhedapratipādanamupayujyate, tathāpi parai' padānyudāhṛtya vicāra' kṛta iti tadbhedameva pratipādayāma' /
children.translated_text: Although, since the word is a means of valid knowledge for the word-meaning, the exposition of their difference is not required, still, since others have raised the issue citing the word, we shall demonstrate that very difference.
'Here' means:
regarding the word—such is the meaning. // 54 //
He now states the reason for the difference—'the object.'
He demonstrates the very difference of objects—'universal.'
For in the <s>Ākṛtyadhikaraṇa</s> (the section on form/universal), the fact that the word
has a universal as its object will be established. // 55 //
<s>Liṅgin</s> means: that which has a mark.
The mark exists for proving that qualified [entity].

children.text: nanvanumāne vyāptibalena dharmasāmānyamanumīyata ityata āha--- na tāvaditi /
children.translated_text: But is not the general property inferred in inference through the force of pervasion? Hence he says—'not so long as.'

children.text: yāvat tadanumānaṃ tadviṣayaṃ viśiṣṭaviṣayaṃ na bhavati tāvadanumānameva na bhavati, na dharmamā(traṃ?traviṣayaṃ) siddhatvādityuktamiti ||56||
children.translated_text: So long as that inference does not have the qualified [entity] as its object, it is not even inference—the property alone [is not the object] since it is already established—thus it was stated. // 56 //
But inference has as its object the property-bearer qualified by a property—this was established in the chapter on inference—hence he says—'property-bearer.'

children.text:
nanu padamapi viśiṣṭagocaraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā--- ko rājā yātīti pṛṣṭe para' pratibravīti , pāñcālarāja iti /
tadā kevalādeva pāñcālarājapadāt kriyāviśiṣṭa' puruṣo 'vagamyate, ata āha---sāmānyāditi /
yadeva
children.translated_text: But the word too is seen to have a qualified [entity] as its domain—for example, when asked 'Which king is going?', the other replies 'The king of Pāñcāla.' Then, from the single word 'the king of Pāñcāla,' a person qualified by action is understood. Hence he says—'over and above the universal.' Whatever
if the word-meaning possesses number and the like, that is not [the case] in indeclinables and such;

children.text: yatrāpi te pratīyante tatra vyakterviśeṣaṇam // Msv_5,5.58 //
children.translated_text: and where they are understood, there the qualification belongs to the individual.
Since the word-meaning expressible by another word has the purpose of an action-nature,

children.text: vākyārthe 'pi padaṃ yatra gomadādi prayujyate // Msv_5,5.59 //
children.translated_text: even in the sentence-meaning, wherever a word like 'possessing cows' is employed—
even though there is qualification here, it is not a thesis, since it is already established;

children.text: tāvāneva hi tatrāptho ya' pūrvamavadhārita' // Msv_5,5.60 //
children.translated_text: for the meaning there is exactly that which was previously ascertained.

children.text: kiñcit śābde sāmānyādatiriktamavagamyate sa vākyasyaiva viṣaya' /

children.translated_text: For it is the sentence itself, with the additional word attached, 'The king of Pāñcāla is going.'

children.text: nanvastu śrutasyānuṣaṅga' , aśrute 'pi padāntare padādekasmād viśiṣṭabodho dṛṣṭa', yathā--- dvāramityukte vivriyatāmiti, atra kathamata āha--- sāmarthyāditi /
children.translated_text: But let there be the attachment of what is heard. Even when another word is unheard, from a single word a qualified cognition is observed—for example, when 'door' is said, 'let it be opened' [is understood]. How then [is it not inference]? Hence he says—'from capacity.'

children.text: kārakaṃ hi kriyayā viditavyāptikam, vyāptisāmarthyādeva kriyāpadamanumāpayati /
children.translated_text: For the instrumental cause (<s>kāraka</s>), whose pervasion with the action is known, through the very force of that pervasion, causes the action-word to be inferred.
Even there, the cognition of the qualified meaning arises from the sentence alone, through the inferred action-word. // 57 //
whatever is understood in verbal [testimony] over and above the universal, that is the domain of the sentence.
He resolves it—'not so.'

children.text: yatra hi saṅkhyādayo 'vagamyante tatra kathamata āha--- yatrāpīti /
children.translated_text: Where indeed number and the like are understood, how [do they relate]? Hence he says—'and where.'
For a qualification becomes meaningful through possibility and non-deviation.

children.text: ākṛtistu na tāvadekatvaṃ vyabhicarati, dvitvādayastvekatvānna sambhavantīti tadākṣiptāyā vyaktereva viśeṣaṇaṃ saṅkhyādaya iti ||58||
children.translated_text: But the universal does not deviate from unity, and duality and the like are not possible from unity—therefore, number and the like are qualifications of the very individual presupposed [by the universal]. // 58 //
He raises an objection—'number.'

children.text:
tadevaṃ tāvadanurañjanena vyakterviśeṣaṇamityuktam, tādarthyena tu kriyāṃ bhāvanāṃ saṅkhyādayo viśiṣanti /
tatra hi śrutyādibhirviniyujyante /
yathā paśorekatve 'ruṇādiṣu ca vakṣyata ityāha--- padantareti /
padāntareti /
padāntaratvenātyantaviprakṛṣṭāviśeṣaṇatāṃ darśayatīti ||58 1/2||
children.translated_text: Thus, it has been stated that by way of coloring [i.e., secondary function], number and the like are qualifications of the individual. But by way of purpose, number and the like qualify the action, the <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force). For in that [context], they are applied through <s>śruti</s> and the like. As will be stated regarding the oneness of the animal and in the <s>Aruṇa</s> and such [discussions]—hence he says—'of what is expressible by another word.' 'By another word'—he shows the extreme remoteness of the non-qualification-status. // 58½ //

children.text:
yattarhi vākyārthavṛttiviśiṣṭaviṣayaṃ gomadādipadaṃ tadanumānaṃ bhaviṣyatyata āha--- vākyārtha iti /
yadyapi tāvadidaṃ viśiṣṭārthagocaram, tathāpi nānumānatvam /
siddho hi dharmī kenacid dharmeṇāsiddhena viśiṣṭa' sādhyamāna' pakṣo bhavati /
iha tu padoñcāraṇāt prāṅ na kiñcit pratipannam /
uccarite tu pade viśiṣṭa' pratipanna eveti kiṃ sādhyamiti /
siddhatvameva
children.translated_text: If then the word 'possessing cows' and the like, which has a qualified [entity] residing in the sentence-meaning as its object, will be [regarded as] inference—hence he says—'in the sentence-meaning.' Although this indeed has a qualified meaning as its domain, still it is not inference. For a property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) established by some means, when qualified by an unestablished property to be proved, becomes the thesis. But here, before the utterance of the word, nothing has been apprehended. And when the word has been uttered, the qualified [meaning] is already apprehended—so what is there to be proved? The very established-ness
and the dissimilarity of the cognition of difference, of the meanings of the root and the suffix,
and the non-independent grasping of the qualifier and the qualified—
and the cognition there is preceded by the qualified, while here it is the reverse.

children.text: atha śabdor'thavattvena pakṣa' kasmānna kalpyate // Msv_5,5.62 //
children.translated_text: But then, since the word has meaningfulness, why should a thesis not be postulated?
For the reason would then become a part of the thesis-meaning;

children.text: pakṣe dhūmaviśeṣe ca sāmānyaṃ heturiṣyate // Msv_5,5.63 //
children.translated_text: and in the thesis, in the case of a particular smoke, a universal is accepted as the reason.
[He] shows—'that much only.'
One who has not grasped the relation [between word and meaning] does not understand the qualified from the word.

children.text: gṛhītasambandhastu pratipadyamāno vyutpattikālāvagatānana kiñcidadhikaṃ pratyetīti kathamanumānaṃ bhavatīti ||60||
children.translated_text: And one who has grasped the relation, when understanding, cognizes nothing beyond what was understood at the time of learning—so how can it be inference? // 60 //

children.text:
api cātra bhinnayoreva prakṛtipratyayātmano' padabhāgayorbhinnāvevārthopratipannau viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabāvamanubhavata iti siddhaṃ
vaiṣamyamityāha---bhedabuddheriti /
idaṃ tu pācakādiśabdeṣu yuktaṃ vaktum, tatra hi (dhātunā) pāka' pratyayena cakartṛmātramupāttam /
ārthastu viśiṣṭapratyaya' /
gomadādau tu tadasyāstīti viśiṣṭa evārthe taddhita' smaryata iti kuto vaiṣamyam, uktamatra 'tāvāneva hī'ti vyutpattikālāvagatādanadhikaviṣayatvam, idaṃ tu pācakādiśabdārtha(me?e)voktamiti /
children.translated_text: But in [words like] 'possessing cows' (<s>gomad</s>) and the like, since the <s>taddhita</s> suffix is remembered as denoting the qualified meaning 'he has that'—whence is there dissimilarity? It was stated 'that much only'—meaning that the domain is no more than what was understood at the time of learning. This, however, was stated regarding the meaning of words like 'cook' only.

children.text: kiñcānumāne svatantragṛhīta eva parvatādirviśeṣya' svatantrasmṛtenāgnyādinā viśeṣaṇena viśiṣṭo 'vagamyate /
children.translated_text: Moreover, in inference, the qualified [entity]—such as the mountain—is grasped independently, and through the qualifier—fire and the like—which is independently remembered, the qualified [entity] is cognized.
But in the case of word, there is no independent grasping of both—hence he says—'qualifier.' // 61 //
'Grasping' is meant figuratively, [including] remembering as well—such is the meaning.

Moreover, here, the two distinct parts of the word—having the nature of root and suffix—being distinct, present two distinct apprehended meanings that experience the relation of qualifier and qualified. Thus the dissimilarity is established—hence he says—'of the cognition of difference.' But this is appropriate to say for words like 'cook' (<s>pācaka</s>), for there the root [presents] cooking and the suffix [presents] merely an agent. The qualified cognition, however, is through meaning.
He states another dissimilarity—'preceded by the qualified.' // 61½ //
He objects—'but then.' // 62 //

children.text: atrāpi śabdasyaiva pranthamāvagatasyārthaviśiṣṭatvena sādhyatvānna kramavyatikramo bhaviṣyatīti ||62||
children.translated_text: Even here, since the word itself, being first apprehended, is to be proved as being qualified by meaning, there will be no reversal of sequence.

children.text:
atra dūṣaṇamāha--- pratijñārtheti /
pratijñārtha' pakṣa' sa ca dharmaviśiṣṭo dharmī, viśiṣṭāpekṣayā dharmyekadeśa ucyate /
sa eva hetu' prasajyate /
śabdo hi dharmitayopātta' sa eva heturiti /
nanu yadā dūrād dhūsyādhāraviśeṣo na lakṣyate tadā dhūmo 'gnimattayā sādhyate, hetuśca bhavati /
tadvadihāpi bhaviṣyatyata āha--- pakṣa iti /
dhūmaviśeṣo hi samprati
children.translated_text: To this he states the refutation—'a part of the thesis-meaning.' The thesis-meaning is the thesis, and that is the property-bearer qualified by a property. Relative to the qualified [entity], a part of the property-bearer is called [such]. That very [part] becomes the reason. For the word, taken up as the property-bearer, is itself the reason. But when the specific support of smoke is not discerned from afar, the smoke is to be proved as possessing fire, and it also serves as the reason. Similarly here too—hence he says—'in the thesis.' For the particular smoke presently
word-hood is not the indicator here; cow-word-hood will be rejected;
the individual alone [becomes] the qualified, and thus one [and the same entity] as the reason is entailed.
It might be so from the difference of manifestors; but such a cognition does not exist for us.

children.text: kathaṃ vāsya viśiṣṭatvaṃ na tāvad deśakālata' // Msv_5,5.65 //
children.translated_text: And how is its qualification [established]? Not from place and time, to begin with.
If [it is] qualified by the cognition of that [meaning]—then what further is to be inferred?
And the denotative capacity is not inferred as belonging to the qualified [entity].

children.text: dṛśyamāna' pakṣa' pūrvāvagata' sapakṣa' tadanugataṃ ca sāmānyaṃ heturiti pakṣasapakṣahetuvibhāgopapattiriti ||63||
children.translated_text: [the smoke] being presently seen is the thesis, the previously known [smoke] is the similar instance, and the universal pervading both is the reason—thus the distinction of thesis, similar instance, and reason is justified. // 63 //

children.text: nanvihāpi śabdaviśeṣaṃ pakṣīkṛtya śabdatvaṃ hetuṃ vakṣyāma', ata āha--- śabdatvamiti /
children.translated_text: But here too we shall make a particular word the thesis and word-hood the reason—hence he says—'word-hood.'

children.text: arthaviśeṣo hyanumitsita', na cāsya śabdatvaṃ gamakamanaikāntikatvāditi /
children.translated_text: For a particular meaning is what is to be inferred, and word-hood is not its indicator, being inconclusive.

children.text: nanvavāntarasāmānyaṃ tarhi gośabdatvaṃ heturbhaviṣyatyata āha--- gośabdatvamiti /
children.translated_text: But then a subordinate universal, cow-word-hood, will be the reason—hence he says—'cow-word-hood.'

children.text: ato 'traikaiva vyaktirarthena viśeṣyāhetutayā cābhidhātavyeti duṣpariharaṃ pratijñārthaikadeśatvamityābhiprāyeṇāha--- vyaktiriti ||64||
children.translated_text: Therefore, here the single individual must be designated as both what is qualified by meaning and the reason—hence the being-a-part-of-the-thesis-meaning is irresolvable. With this purport he says—'individual.' // 64 //

children.text:
nanu vyañjakabhedabhinnaikaiva vyakti' pakṣīkariṣyate ityāha--- bhavediti /
pariharati--- na tviti /
naupādhiko bhedo vastu bhinatti, tatpratyayānapāyāditi bhāva' /
children.translated_text: An adventitious difference does not split a real entity, because the cognition of it does not depart—such is the purport.

children.text: api ca viśiṣṭatā sambandhe sati bhavati, tadiha kīdṛśor'thaśabdayośabdayo' sambandha ityāha--- kathaṃ veti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, qualification exists when there is a relation. What kind of relation exists here between the meaning and the word?—hence he says—'and how.'

children.text: na tāvat śabdadeśer'tho dṛśyate,mukhe hi śabda' bhūmāvartha' /
children.translated_text: The meaning is not seen at the place of the word, for the word is in the mouth and the meaning is on the ground.

children.text: nāpi śabdakāle, kalau kṛtayugārthasyābhāvādityāha--- na tāvaditi ||65||
children.translated_text: Nor at the time of the word, because an object of the Kṛta age does not exist in the Kali age—hence he says—'not from place.' // 65 //
But the single individual, differentiated by the difference of manifestors, will be made the thesis—hence he says—'it might be.' He resolves—'but not.'

children.text:
arthārthapratītyā viśiṣṭa' śabda' sādhyate, asti hi sā śabdakāla iti tadetadāśaṅkate--- tatpratītiriti /
etadapi dūṣayatīti--- paramiti /
pratītyā viśiṣṭe 'numīyamāne sā tāvat pūrvasiddhā grahītavyā /
sā cet jñātā kimaparamanumīyata iti /
nanu sampratyupalabhyamānaṃ dutādiviśeṣaṃ pakṣīkṛtya tasya pratyāyanaśaktiviśiṣṭatā sādhyate sapakṣaṃ ca vyutpattikālā
children.translated_text: The word is proved as qualified by the cognition of the meaning of the meaning. For that [cognition] exists at the time of the word—he raises this doubt: 'by the cognition of that.' He refutes this too: 'what further.' When the [word] qualified by the cognition is to be inferred, that [cognition] must be established first. If that is already known, what further is to be inferred? But suppose the particular of rapidity and such, being presently apprehended, is made the thesis, and its being qualified by denotative capacity is to be proved, and the similar instance is the time of learning—
for particulars do not have the capacity in one locus, like the fire-universal;

children.text: sāmānyasyaiva śaktve pakṣo hetustathaiva ca // Msv_5,5.67 //
children.translated_text: if the capacity belongs to the universal alone, the thesis and reason remain the same.
Therefore, the word qualified by meaning is not to be inferred.

children.text: kathaṃ ca pakṣadharmatvaṃ śabdasyeha nirupyate // Msv_5,5.68 //
children.translated_text: And how is the property of being a property of the thesis established for the word here?
Without the relation of action and agent, there is no connection anywhere;

children.text: rājā bhartā manuṣyasya tena rājña' sa ucyate // Msv_5,5.69 //
children.translated_text: the king is the lord of a person, and by that [relation] he is called 'of the king.'

children.text: vagataviśeṣam,ubhayānugataṃ gośabdasāmānyaṃ hetuṃ kariṣyāma', na pratijñārthaikadeśatā bhaviṣyatyata āha --- na pratyāyaneti ayamabhiprāya' na drutādiviśeṣāṇāṃ deśādinibandhanor'thena sambandho vidyate /
children.translated_text: [continuing] —the specific [instances] learned, the cow-word-universal pervading both will be made the reason—there will be no being-a-part-of-the-thesis-meaning. Hence he says—'not the denotative capacity.' The purport is: there is no relation of the specifics such as rapidity and the like with the meaning based on place and the like.
And the qualification by denotative capacity is also not possible for them. // 66 //

children.text: yathā pakṣīkṛtasya mahato dhūmasyaikadeśe 'dhastādagnirastīti tadviśiṣṭo dhūma' sādhyo bhavati /
children.translated_text: Just as, when a large [column of] smoke is made the thesis, fire exists in one part below it, and the smoke qualified by that is what is to be proved.
Not so is the connection of denotative capacity with particulars such as rapidity and the like.
Because of the deviation of those [reasons], it is said that they do not convey [the intended conclusion].

children.text: yattu teṣāṃ sāmānyaṃ gośabda' sapratyāyanaśaktiviśiṣṭa' tatra ca pakṣe sa eva pakṣo hetuścetyuktamevetyāha sāmānyasyeti ||67||
children.translated_text: But as for their universal — the word 'go' (cow) qualified by the power of conveying — and in that <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis), the thesis itself is the reason — this has already been stated. Hence he says 'sāmānyasya.' (67)
Why is it not possible? Hence he says—'of the particulars.'
Concluding that a word qualified by meaning is not an object of inference, he says — 'tasmāt.' (67½)

children.text: evaṃ tāvat śabdo na pakṣa ityuktam /

children.translated_text: But if, making the meaning the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis), the word is said to be the <s>hetu</s> (reason) —
that too is unjustified,
because it is not a property of the <s>pakṣa</s> — hence he says 'kathaṃ ca.'
The sense is: how can it be ascertained? (68)
Thus far it has been stated that the word is not the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis).

children.text: kasyāñcit kriyāyāṃ kartṛtayā sambaddhaṃ kiñcit kasyacit sambandhī bhavati, kriyākārakasambandhapūrvakatvāt śeṣasambandhānāṃ svasvāmyādīnāmiti /
children.translated_text: Something connected as an agent in some action becomes related to something else, because subsidiary relations such as ownership and the like are preceded by the action-<s>kāraka</s> (case-factor) relation.
Among these, the owner-owned relation is preceded by the action-<s>kāraka</s> relation — hence he says 'rājā.'
For first, the king and the servant, having entered into the agent-object relation in the act of sustaining,
experience the owner-owned relation. (69)
Why can it not be ascertained? To this he says — 'na kriyā.'

children.text: vṛkṣastiṣṭhati śākhāsu tā vā tatreti tasya tā' /
children.translated_text: The tree stands upon its branches, or they upon it — thus 'its' and 'those';

children.text: deśe 'gnimati dhūmasya kartṛtvaṃ bhavanaṃ prati // Msv_5,5.70 //
children.translated_text: in a place possessing fire, the smoke has agency with respect to occurrence. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.70)
In cause-effect relation and the like, action is found everywhere;
and a relation whose nature has not been ascertained cannot be understood to exist. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.71)
And in the absence of a relation, neither a genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound [is possible],
therefore, the determination that 'this is a property of the <s>pakṣa</s>' is not possible. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.72)
Even those who, when the relation elsewhere is negated, by virtue of being directed toward that [particular] object,
would assert <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (property-of-the-thesis) of the word, like non-apprehension — (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.73)

children.text:
evamavayavāvayavisambandho 'pi kriyāgarbha ityāha---vṛkṣaiti /
vṛkṣo 'vayavī hyavayaveṣu tiṣṭhatīti pratīti' /
kadācittvavayavā eva śākhādayastasminniti pratīti' /
tadevaṃ sthitikriyākartṛbhāvanibandhano 'vayavāvayavisamambandha iti /
evaṃ saṃyogo 'pi kriyāgarbha evetyāha--- deśa iti /
agnimaddeśe bhavane kartā bhavan dhūmo 'gnimato deśasya saṃyogī bhavatīti||
children.translated_text: Thus the whole-part relation too involves action — hence he says 'vṛkṣa.' For the tree, being the whole, 'stands upon' the parts, i.e., the branches — this is the cognition. Sometimes, the parts themselves — branches and such — [are said to be] 'in that' — this is the cognition. Thus the whole-part relation is grounded in the agent-relation of the action of standing. Similarly, conjunction too involves action — hence he says 'deśa.' Smoke, being the agent of occurring in a place possessing fire, becomes conjoined with the place possessing fire.

children.text:
evaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvādayo 'pi sambandhā' kriyākārakasambandhapūrvakā ityāha---kāryeti /
kiṇvaṃ hi surāyā bījaṃ surātmake pariṇāme kartṛbhavatsurāyā' kāraṇamityucyate /
tathā samūhasamūhisambandho 'pi /
senākāryaṃ pratipakṣajayamaṃśena kurvan hastī senāyā' sambandhitayocyata iti /
śabdārthayostu na kaścidevabākāra' sambandhasyāvagamyate /
na cānirūpitākāra' sambandho 'stīti śakyate vaktumityāha--- na ceti /
children.translated_text: And a relation whose form has not been ascertained cannot be said to exist — hence he says 'na ca.'

children.text: na ca sambandhamantareṇa pakṣasya dharma iti vigrahagatā ṣaṣṭhī pakṣadharma iti ca tatpuruṣasamāso vā ghaṭata ityāha---na cāstīti /
children.translated_text: And without a relation, neither the genitive [case ending] involved in the analysis 'property of the <s>pakṣa</s>,' nor the <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound '<s>pakṣadharma</s>,' is possible — hence he says 'na cāsti.'
Neither the compound nor its analysis is established.
He concludes — 'tasmāt.' (72)

Thus cause-effect relation and other relations too are preceded by the action-<s>kāraka</s> relation — hence he says 'kārya.' For ferment is the seed of liquor, and being the agent in the transformation that has the nature of liquor, it is called the cause of liquor. Similarly, the relation of collectivity and collective too — an elephant, performing the collective's task of conquering the enemy with its part, is said to be related to the army. But between word and meaning, no such form of relation is ascertained at all.
Others, however, assert the property-of-the-thesis status [of the word] precisely as 'the word has the meaning as its object.'
Just as non-apprehension will be stated to be a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) for absence,
he presents this — 'nivṛtte.' (73)
But even by them, this must be examined: how is the word directed toward that [meaning]?

children.text: na taddeśādisadbhāvo nābhimukhyādi tasya vā // Msv_5,5.74 //
children.translated_text: There is no presence of that [meaning] in the location [of the word] and so on, nor is there orientation of that [word toward the meaning] and so forth. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.74)
Therefore, since this [word] produces a cognition directed toward the meaning,

children.text: tena tadviṣaya' śabda iti dharmatvakalpanā // Msv_5,5.75 //
children.translated_text: thereby the word has the meaning as its object — such is the supposition of [its] being a property [of the thesis]. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.75)
And when <s>vācakatā</s> (denotative capacity) is already established, the property-of-the-thesis status
does not become a constituent of the cognition, and thus there is no inferential character. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.76)
If the property-status is because of [its] indicative capacity, and the indicative capacity is because of property-status,
there would be mutual dependence; therefore this supposition too is not tenable. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.77)
And those who have not grasped the [word-meaning] relation, apart from the bare form [of the word],
do not know the word [as a property of anything], whereby there could be a cognition of it as a property of the <s>pakṣa</s>. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.78)
This too is untenable — hence he says 'tair api.'

children.text: na kenāpi prakāreṇa viṣayaviṣayibhāvo ghaṭata ityartha' /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: by no means whatsoever can the object-objecthood relation be established.

children.text: yathā na ghaṭate tadetadāha--- na taditi ||74||
children.translated_text: How it cannot be established — that he states: 'na tat.' (74)

children.text: sarvaprakārāsambhavāt pāriśeṣyeṇa tadviṣayabuddhijanakatayā tadviṣayatā vaktavyā, evaṃ ca tadviṣayabuddhijanakatvasya vācyavācakabhāvamantareṇānupapattestadabhyupamaga' kāra' /
children.translated_text: Since all other modes are impossible, by elimination, the object-directedness must be stated as consisting in the capacity to generate a cognition directed toward that [meaning]. And since such capacity to generate cognition directed toward that [meaning] is impossible without the <s>vācyavācakabhāva</s> (denotation relation), that [relation] must be accepted as the ground.
And when that is established, the property-of-the-thesis status does not become a constituent of the cognition,
and a cognition not generated by a property-of-the-thesis
is not inference — hence he says 'tasmāt' with two [verses]. (75, 76)
But if it is held that the property-of-the-thesis status itself is the reason for generating cognition directed toward that [meaning],

children.text: tatastavyatirekeṇa pakṣadharmatāyā evapānupapatteritaretarāśrayatvamato neyamapi kalpanā ghaṭata ityāha---gamakatvāditi ||77||
children.translated_text: then, since the property-of-the-thesis status itself cannot be established without that [cognition], there is mutual dependence. Hence this supposition too does not hold — so he says 'gamakatvāt.' (77)
And for this reason too it is not a property of the <s>pakṣa</s> — he says 'na ca.'

children.text: anavagatavācyavācakasambandhā' svarūpātirekeṇa na śabdaṃ kasyacid dharmatayā jānanti /
children.translated_text: Those who have not grasped the <s>vācyavācaka</s> (signified-signifier) relation do not know the word, apart from its bare form, as a property of anything,
whereby there could be a cognition of the word as a property of the <s>pakṣa</s>. (78)
And it is not the case that mere knowledge of the form [constitutes] the <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (property-of-the-thesis) of smoke and the like,
nor does this [property-of-the-thesis status] arise depending on prior [knowledge of the] relation. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.79)
'This possesses smoke' — thus even for one who has no prior [knowledge of the relation], there arises
the cognition of property-of-the-thesis; hence it differs from the subsequent characteristic. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.80)
But here, the property-of-the-thesis status is not anything more than [what comes from] the prior relation,
and prior to the cognition of meaning, this [property-of-the-thesis status] cannot be a constituent [of knowledge]. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.81)

children.text: na ca dharmī gṛhīto 'tra yena taddharmatā bhavet /
children.translated_text: And the <s>dharmin</s> (subject-locus) is not grasped here, whereby there could be property-of-that-[subject] status,
as a mountain or other location [is grasped] prior to the determination of property-status. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.82)

children.text: yaścātra kathyate dharmī prameyo 'sya sa eva na' /
children.translated_text: And that which is called the <s>dharmin</s> (subject-locus) here — it is precisely that which is to be proved by this [inference],
and when that is not ascertained, there can be no determination of its being a property of that. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.83)

children.text: svarūpamātravijñānaṃ tu na dhūmādau pakṣadharmatāyāṃ hetu', api tu dharmisambandha' /
children.translated_text: Mere knowledge of the form, however, is not the cause of <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (property-of-the-thesis) in the case of smoke and the like; rather, it is the connection with the <s>dharmin</s> (subject-locus).
And that [connection] does not exist [in the case of the word] — with this intention he says 'na ca.'

children.text: nanvatrāpyarthena dharmiṇā pratamaṃ vyutpattikāle sambandho 'vagata eva, āha--- na cāpīti ||79||
children.translated_text: Objection: Even here, the relation with the meaning, which is the <s>dharmin</s> (subject-locus), has already been grasped at the time of linguistic training. He says — 'na cāpi.' (79)

children.text: pūrvasambandhanirapekṣa evāyamavyutpannasambandhasyāpi pakṣadharmasambandho māsate, na cātra tathetyāha---dhūmavānitimatirantena /
children.translated_text: Even without dependence on prior relation, for one whose relation has not been learned, the property-of-the-thesis connection is established — but here it is not so — hence he says 'dhūmavān iti matir' and so forth.

children.text: yata eva tannirapekṣo 'yaṃ pakṣadharmasambandha', ata eva taduttarasmāt sapakṣasattvalakṣaṇād bhidyate, anyathā tadabheda eva syādityāha--- teneti /
children.translated_text: Precisely because this property-of-the-thesis connection is independent of that [prior relation], it therefore differs from the subsequent characteristic, namely the presence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue); otherwise there would be non-difference between them — hence he says 'tena.'

children.text: trīṇi hetorlakṣaṇāni pakṣadharmatā sapakṣe sattā vipakṣād vyāvṛtti' /
children.translated_text: The three characteristics of the <s>hetu</s> (reason) are: <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (property-of-the-thesis), presence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue), and exclusion from the <s>vipakṣa</s> (heterologue).
And he designates the relation to the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue) — which is subsequent to <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> — as the 'subsequent characteristic.' (80)

children.text:
śabde tvevaṃ nāstītyāha--- na tvatreti /
pūrvasambandhāpekṣayā ceyamavagamyamānārthapratītyuttarakālamavagamyate /
ato na tadaṅgamityāha--- naceti||
children.translated_text: But in the case of the word, this is not so — he says 'na tvatra.' And this [property-of-the-thesis status], being understood dependent on the prior relation, is understood only after the cognition of meaning has arisen. Therefore it is not a constituent [of the inference] — hence he says 'na ca.'
And for this reason too there is no <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> — he says 'na ca dharmī.'

children.text: arthādanyastāvad dharmī na pramīyata iti bhāva' ||82||
children.translated_text: The sense is: no <s>dharmin</s> (subject-locus) other than the meaning is cognized. (82)

children.text: yastvasāvartho dharmitayā kalpanīya', yaddharmatayāvagata' śabda' pakṣa
children.translated_text: But as for that very meaning which is to be supposed as the <s>dharmin</s>, and the word which is known as its property — the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) —

children.text: prāk sa cet pakṣadharmatvād gṛhīta' kiṃ tata' param /
children.translated_text: if that [meaning] is grasped first, prior to the property-of-the-thesis status, then what further [need is there]
for inference through knowledge of property-of-the-thesis and the rest? (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.84)

children.text: anvayo na ca śabdas prameyena nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: And the <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) of the word with the object of knowledge cannot be ascertained,
for the concomitance of all [things] is cognized through [their] operation. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.85)
Where there is smoke, there fire exists — the <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) is clear;

children.text: na tvevaṃ yatra śabdo 'sti tatrārtho 'stīti niścaya' // Msv_5,5.86 //
children.translated_text: but it is not the case that 'where there is a word, there the meaning exists' — there is no such certainty. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.86)
First, that [meaning] is not apprehended in the same place [as the word] or at the same time,
and if [one argues that it is] because of the eternality and all-pervasiveness [of the meaning], then it would be the same for all meanings. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.87)
Therefore, since [the meaning] is seen everywhere, and since <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) does not obtain,
the cognition of all meanings from all words would absurdly follow. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.88)
Now, if by [the fact of] non-existence in a [particular] place and time, a construction [of the relation is attempted],
someone might propose a cognition of the denotative [relation], connected with the cognition of the meaning. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.89)

children.text: dharmo bhavati, parastādapi sa tāvāneva pramātavya' /
children.translated_text: becomes a property [of the thesis]. Beyond that too, exactly that much remains to be cognized.

children.text: tad yadi pakṣadharmatvamavagantumasau prathamamevāvagamyate, tato gṛhīte tasmin kiṃ parabhāvinā pakṣadharmādijñānena ato nānumānatetyāha---yaścetidvayena ||83,84||
children.translated_text: If, in order to ascertain the property-of-the-thesis status, that [meaning] is itself grasped first, then once it is grasped, what [need is there] for subsequent knowledge of property-of-the-thesis and the rest? Hence it is not inference — he says 'yaśca' with two [verses]. (83, 84)
Now he criticizes the <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) — 'anvaya.'
How can it not be ascertained? To this he says — 'vyāpāreṇa.' (85)
He demonstrates this very point — 'yatra.'
But here it is not so — he says 'na tu.' (86)
How is it not [so]? To this he says — 'na tāvat.'
And this has already been stated earlier.

children.text: nanu vaibhavācchabdasya nityatvāccārthasya śabdārthayo' śakyate 'nvayo darśayitumityāha--- bhavediti /
children.translated_text: Objection: Because of the all-pervasiveness of the word and the eternality of the meaning, the <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) of word and meaning can be shown — hence he says 'bhavet.'
He refutes — 'sarvārthoṣu.' (87)
What follows from that? If so — hence he says 'tena.' (88)
He anticipates the relation through another mode — 'athaivam.' (89)
Even so, there is no [concomitance] seen, for sometimes even without the cognition of meaning,
we [observe] a cognition of denotation toward persons who have not learned [the language]. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.90)
And in the second and subsequent uses, there might be a construction of concomitance,

children.text: śatakṛtva' prayukte 'pi na ca dṛṣṭārthadhī' kvacit // Msv_5,5.91 //
children.translated_text: but even when used a hundred times, no cognition of the meaning is ever seen [for the unlearned]. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.91)
Objection: For those who know the relation, the seen concomitance is clear;
if so, then some relation of word and meaning prior to [this] concomitance is being accepted. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.92)
This construction of concomitance would not be a constituent of the cognition of meaning,
and it is established that inference depends on concomitance for its generation. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.93)
When the capacity to produce cognition is [already] known, [the cognition] arises necessarily by virtue of that [capacity] alone;
how then can the subsequent concomitance be called a cause? (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.94)
He criticizes this too — 'naivam.'
He states the reason — 'dṛṣṭo hi,' by us, and so forth.
Where is it seen? To this he says — 'avyutpanna.' (90)
Objection: In the second and subsequent uses, the concomitance of word and cognition of meaning will be grasped — he anticipates this: 'dvitīyādi.'
He criticizes this too — 'śatakṛtva.'
Even when used a hundred times, one who does not desire to learn does not cognize the relation,
and one who does not know the relation does not cognize the meaning. (91)
Objection: For one who knows the relation, at least, word-cognition does not deviate from meaning-cognition,
and it is precisely that [cognition] which is claimed to be inferential — hence he says 'nanu.'
He refutes — 'yadyevam.'

children.text: yadi jñātasambandhasyānvaya', anya eva tarhi sambandha' śabdārthayorabhyupagamyata iti ||92||
children.translated_text: If there is concomitance for one who knows the relation, then some other relation of word and meaning is being accepted [prior to it]. (92)
What follows from that? To this he says — 'nāṅgam.'
If it is not a constituent, what of it? To this he says — 'anvaya.'
The sense is: in the absence of <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance), the cognition is not inference. (93)

children.text: anvayastu pūrvāvagatapratītisāmarthyānusāreṇaiva jāyamāno nārthagrahītau kāraṇamityāha--- jñāta iti ||94||
children.translated_text: But the concomitance, arising merely by following the previously grasped capacity to produce cognition, is not a cause of apprehending the meaning — hence he says 'jñāta.' (94)
Therefore, the power of the word is cognized independently of that [concomitance];
and it is not the case that the denotative capacity [of the word] is ascertained prior to the concomitance, as in [the case of] smoke. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.95)
And if [one proposes] <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) from a meaning whose [relation to the word] is unknown,
that too, being subsequent [to the cognition], is not a means of establishing the cognition of meaning. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.5.96)
But the relation that we shall state — the cause of its determination
Would be positive concomitance and negative concomitance; but those two are not [the means of] the apprehension of meaning. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.97)
Therefore, the non-inferential nature of verbal [cognition] would obtain, like perception,
Because of lacking the triple characteristic, and because of excluding such [inferential] objects. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.98)
And when its <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood is established, the examination of difference and non-difference

children.text: yuktā na tu padajñānāt padārtho 'tra pramāyate // Msv_5,5.99 //
children.translated_text: Is appropriate; but here, the word-meaning is not measured from word-cognition. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.99)
He concludes — 'tasmāt' (therefore).
But in inference, the indicative capacity is not established prior to positive concomitance — he says 'na ca.' (95)
He now refutes negative concomitance — 'vyatireka.'

children.text: na hyanavagater'the tajjñānena vinā śabdajñānaṃ bhavatīti vyatireka' śakyate 'vagantum /
children.translated_text: For when the meaning has not been apprehended, it cannot be ascertained that verbal cognition does not arise without the cognition of that [meaning] — this is [the difficulty in establishing] negative concomitance.
But if the meaning has been apprehended, what is the use of resorting to negative concomitance? (96)
Now, [if asked] are positive and negative concomitance entirely useless with respect to words? — he says 'sambandham.'

children.text: śaktini (ṣkarṣe) yorvyāpāro vācyavācakarūpa' śabdārthayo' sambandha iti ||97||
children.translated_text: Their operation — in the form of the relation between denoted and denoting — is [useful for] the extraction of the capacity [of words] — that is the relation of word and meaning. (97)

children.text:
evaṃ ca trailakṣaṇyaparityāgenānanumānatvaṃ prasādhya prayogeṇa darśayati---tasmāditi /
śabdo nānumānaṃ trairūpyarahitatvāt

children.translated_text: Like perception.
Because of excluding such [inferential] objects.
'Tādṛk' means: similar to that [perception].
And the exclusion of objects [of the inferential type] has already been described by 'for having universals as its object' and so forth. (98)

And having thus established the non-inferential nature [of verbal cognition] through the abandonment of the triple characteristic, he demonstrates it through a formal argument — 'tasmāt.' Verbal [cognition] is not inference, because of lacking the triple characteristic,

children.text: idaṃ ca padasyānumānād bhedapratipādanaṃ prauḍhipradarśanārthamasmābhi' kṛtam /
children.translated_text: And this demonstration of the difference of the word [as <s>pramāṇa</s>] from inference has been made by us for the purpose of displaying [our] expertise.
But [we do not claim that] the word [alone] is a <s>pramāṇa</s> — he says 'sati.' (99)
For a word being employed is employed with respect to meaning in four ways:

children.text: pratyakṣe ca parokṣe ca jñāte 'jñāte 'pi vā purā // Msv_5,5.100 //
children.translated_text: With respect to what is perceptible and what is imperceptible, and with respect to what is known and what is unknown before. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.100)
Therein, when it is employed with respect to what is previously known and perceptible,
Since it is employed with respect to what is already measured, it is a mere re-statement, without [conveying] anything additional. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.101)
But with respect to what is not seen before, [the word produces] either non-cognition [of the meaning] or merely the cognition of the relation;

children.text: sambandho na ca tasyārtho yor'tha' sa tvakṣagocara' // Msv_5,5.102 //
children.translated_text: And the relation is not the [proper] meaning of that [word]; and as for that whose meaning [it is], it is within the range of the senses. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.102)
With respect to what is imperceptible and not previously experienced, there can be no cognition of what is denoted;
And for what is imperceptible but previously experienced, memory is what is accepted [to arise]. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.103)
And since it operates with respect to what is already measured, memory does not have <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood;
For <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood arises from having the result of determination. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.104)

children.text: yathā na pramāṇaṃ tathā darśayati--- padamiti /
children.translated_text: He shows how it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> — 'pada' (word).
And he states those very four types — 'pratyakṣa.' (100)

children.text: eṣvartheṣu prayuktasya yathā na prāmāṇyaṃ tathāha--- tatreti ||101||
children.translated_text: When employed with respect to these [four types of] meanings, the lack of <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood [is shown] — he says 'tatra.' (101)
But with respect to what is not previously seen and presently perceptible, the invalidity is characterized merely by non-production [of new knowledge] — he says 'adṛṣṭapūrva.'

children.text: sambandhajñānameva vā tadā jāyata ityāha--- sambandheti /
children.translated_text: Or [when the word is employed regarding something presently perceived but previously unseen], only the cognition of the relation arises at that time — he says 'sambandha.'

children.text: na ca sambandha eva padasya prameya iti vācyam, tasyārthāpattiprameyatvādityabhiprāyeṇāha--- sambandha iti /
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that the relation is the proper object of measurement of the word, because the relation is the object of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — with this intention he says 'sambandha.'
But that whose meaning is understood from perception and such — he says 'yo 'rthaḥ.' (102)
With respect to what is imperceptible and not previously experienced, there is simply non-production of cognition — he says 'parokṣa.'

children.text: anubhūte tu parokṣe smṛtirityāha--- parokṣa iti ||103||
children.translated_text: But with respect to what is imperceptible and previously experienced, [there is] memory — he says 'parokṣa.' (103)

children.text: nanu smṛtimeva janayat pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatyata āha--- pramita iti /
pramitaviṣayā hi smṛti', sannikṛṣṭārthagocaraṃ ca pramāṇamiti sthitiriti /
children.translated_text: For memory has an already-measured object, and it is established that a <s>pramāṇa</s> has as its domain an object that is in proximity.

children.text: kathaṃ puna' pramitaviṣayaṃ na pramāṇamata āha--- paricchedeti /
children.translated_text: But how is what has an already-measured object not a <s>pramāṇa</s>? Hence he says 'pariccheda.'
For a <s>pramāṇa</s> has determination as its result.

children.text: na ca smṛtyā kiñcit paricchidyate, pūrvavijñānamātropasthāpakatvāditi ||104||
children.translated_text: And memory does not determine anything, since it merely presents what was previously cognized. (104)
Objection: Even while producing memory, it will be a <s>pramāṇa</s> — hence he says 'pramita.'
Why is <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood — in the form of having the result of contemporaneous determination —

children.text: pratyabhijñānavat kasmāt smṛte 'pi na kalpyate // Msv_5,5.105 //
children.translated_text: Not postulated for memory too, as for recognition? (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.105)
Only as much as was previously determined is apprehended

children.text: smṛtyā tadanusāreṇa tadā sattve 'sya naiva dhī' // Msv_5,5.106 //
children.translated_text: By memory, in accordance with that [prior cognition]; there is no cognition of its [present] existence at that time. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.106)
A word, due to the absence of anything additional, is not distinguished from a memory-trigger;

children.text: yadādhikyaṃ bhavet kiñcit tatpadasya na gocara' // Msv_5,5.107 //
children.translated_text: And whatever additional [content] there might be, that is not within the domain of [a single] word. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.107)
Even if the cognition from the word were a <s>pramāṇa</s> or inference,
Since the sentence-meaning is [what qualifies as] the object of <s>āgama</s> (scripture), there is no defect for the proponents of <s>āgama</s>. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.108)
Here he raises an objection — 'tādātvika.'

children.text: yadyapi pūrvamasāvartho 'vagata', tathāpi tadānīṃ sattāṃ bodhayantī pratyabhijñānavat smṛti' pramāṇaṃ kimiti na bhavatīti ||105||
children.translated_text: Even if this meaning has been previously apprehended, still, memory that communicates its existence at that time, like recognition, why should it not be a <s>pramāṇa</s>? (105)
He replies — 'yāvān.'

children.text: utpadyate smṛtiranyadā, na tu pratyabhijñānavat tadanīṃ vastu' sattāṃ niścāyayati, pūrvajñānānusāritvāditi ||106||
children.translated_text: Memory arises at another time, but unlike recognition, it does not ascertain the present existence of the thing, because it follows the prior cognition. (106)

children.text:
nanu pūrvasaṃskāramātrajā hi smṛti', idaṃ tu pratyutpannakāraṇakaṃ padāt padārthajñānaṃ grahaṇameva, kathaṃ smṛtirucyate /
ata āha---padamiti /
mā bhūt smaraṇaṃ, grahamapīdamanadhikaviṣayamevādhikapratibhāsābhāvāt, ato na padaṃ smārakebhya' sadṛśādṛṣṭādibhyo viśiṣyata ityapramāṇamiti /
children.translated_text: Let it not be memory — this too is an apprehension whose object has no additional [content], due to the absence of any additional appearance. Hence the word is not distinguished from memory-triggers such as similar [objects], dreams, and the like — and so it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
Objection: When one of the two — action or instrument — is uttered, the connection of the other with the other necessarily arises in the mind.

children.text: ata' kathamucyate nādhikyamavagatamyata ityata āha--- yadādhikyamiti /
children.translated_text: Hence how is it said that no additional [content] is apprehended? — Therefore he says 'yadādhikyam.'
That [additional content] is the grace of another word, not of a single word alone — this is the meaning. (107)

Objection: Memory is born merely from prior impressions, but this cognition of word-meaning from the word, having a presently operative cause, is apprehension itself — how can it be called memory? Hence he says 'pada.'

children.text: idaṃ cāsmābhi' sauhṛdamātreṇa śiṣyebhya' kathyate na padaṃ pramāṇamiti /
na tu tatpramāṇatve vākyārtho nāgamārtho bhavati /
children.translated_text: But it is not the case that, if it were a <s>pramāṇa</s>, the sentence-meaning would not be the object of <s>āgama</s> (scripture).

children.text: tena hi pramāṇenāpi bhavatāvaśyaṃ padārthe bhavitavyam /
children.translated_text: For even with that [word-level] <s>pramāṇa</s>, there must necessarily be [cognition of] the word-meaning.
Therefore, a sentence that conveys a meaning not ascertained by any other <s>pramāṇa</s> is indeed a <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: evamanumānāntargatatve 'pi padasya na kācit kṣati', vākyārthasyānanumeyatvādityāh--- pramāṇamiti ||108||
children.translated_text: Thus, even if the word were subsumed under inference, there is no harm, because the sentence-meaning is not inferable — he says 'pramāṇam.' (108)
And this is stated by us to our students merely out of friendliness — that a word is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
But regarding sentence-meaning, from word-meanings, without the prior experience of the relation,
A cognition arises; therefore, that [sentence-cognition] is different, like sensory cognition. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.109)
And in the <s>Vākyādhikaraṇa</s> (topic on the sentence), the establishment of this reason will come;

children.text: sarveṣāṃ ca paroktānāṃ vākyād buddhāvasiddhatā // Msv_5,5.110 //
children.translated_text: And the unestablished-ness of all [reasons] stated by others [will be shown] regarding cognition from a sentence. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.110)
He says: How is the non-inferential nature of sentence-meaning cognition [established]? For that too, being a deliberate sequential apprehension, is inference itself — hence he says 'vākyārtha.'
The word-meanings, even without their mutual relation having been grasped, convey the sentence-meaning.
Therefore, sentence-meaning cognition is not inference.

children.text: evañca darśayitavyaṃ vākyārthabuddharanumānād bhinnā sambandhanubhavādṛte jāyamānatvād akṣabuddhivaditi ||109||
