children.translated_text: And thus it should be demonstrated: 'Sentence-meaning cognition is different from inference, because it arises without prior experience of the relation, like sensory cognition.' (109)

children.text:
kathaṃ punarapratibaddhamarthāntarasya pratipādakam, evaṃ hyatiprasaṅga' /
atosiddho heturata āha---vākyeti /
ye ca parai' padārthabuddheranumānādabhedahetava uktā', te tāvad bahavo vākyārthabuddhāvasiddhā ityāha--- sarveṣāmiti /
vākyārthabuddhirhi na tāvadanvayavyatirekajā /
nāpa sambandhatvāt /
sāmānyaviṣayatvamapyasiddhaṃ viśiṣṭaviṣayatvāt /
pratyakṣānyapramāṇatvatadadṛṣṭārthabodhane tūpamānādīni prasādhya naikāntikīkārye /
tadadṛṣṭārthabodhanaṃ cānumānābhāsairapyanaikāntikam /
evaṃ trikālaviṣayamapyanumānābhāsetatrāpyasiddhameva /
uktaṃ hi śabdaśaktinirdhāraṇe 'tayorvyāpāro na buddhijanmanī'ti /
sambandhapūrvakatvaṃ tu yadyaviśeṣitaṃ tat pratyakṣeṇaivānaikāntikam, tadapi hīndriyārthasambandhapūrvakameva /
children.translated_text: As for 'being preceded by the relation' — if unspecified, it is inconclusive even through perception, for that too is preceded by the sense-object relation.
If 'being preceded by a relation that is a component of inference' — that is unestablished, for <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is the component of inference.

children.text: na ca padāt padārthajñāne vyāpti' kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: And <s>vyāpti</s> is not the cause in the cognition of word-meaning from the word.

And 'having universals as its object' is inconclusive even through pseudo-inference; 'being a <s>pramāṇa</s> other than perception' and 'conveying a meaning unseen by that' — [these are inconclusive] through analogy and such too. (110)

But how can what is unrestricted [by prior relational knowledge] be a conveyor of a different meaning? For there would be over-extension. Hence the reason is unestablished — he says 'vākya.' And those causes of non-difference of word-cognition from inference that were stated by others — many of them are unestablished with regard to sentence-meaning cognition — he says 'sarveṣām.' For sentence-meaning cognition is, first of all, not born from positive and negative concomitance. Nor is it preceded by [knowledge of] the relation [between the component meanings]. 'Having universals as its object' is also unestablished, since it has particular [qualified] objects. 'Being a <s>pramāṇa</s> other than perception' and 'conveying a meaning unseen by that [perception]' — when analogy and such are established [as satisfying these], they become inconclusive. And 'conveying a meaning unseen by that [perception]' is also inconclusive through pseudo-inferences. Similarly, 'pertaining to all three times' is also unestablished even through pseudo-inference. For it has been said in the determination of word-capacity: 'The operation of those two [<s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>] does not give rise to cognition.'

children.text:
yata evaivaṃ vākyārthabuddha' sahārthairadṛṣṭeṣvapi vākyeṣu padārthamātravido jāyate /
ato 'syā' sphaṭataramanumānād bhedaṃ paśyanta' saugatāstato 'vatīryāgamasyāmānavyatirekāt vibhyata' padābedavicāraṇāyāmeva kliṣṭā' /
evaṃ hi
children.translated_text: Since this is so — that sentence-meaning cognition, even for one who knows only the word-meanings, arises from sentences even when [the specific relations are] not previously seen — therefore the Buddhists, seeing the difference from inference even more clearly [in this case], descending from [the debate about] the non-difference of <s>āgama</s> (scripture) from inference, are troubled and distressed by the examination of the non-difference of [individual] words [from inference]. For thus —
Seeing that even from previously unseen sentences that have meaning, the cognition arises for one who knows merely the word-meanings,
Frightened of the difference from inference, they labor over the examination of the non-difference of words [from inference]. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.5.111)
Thus [ends] the <s>Śabda Vārttika</s> (section on verbal testimony).
Now the <s>Upamāna Pariccheda</s> (section on analogy).
When asked by city-dwellers 'What does a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) look like?' —
A forest-dweller utters the statement: 'A <s>gavaya</s> is like a cow.' (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.6.1)
He considers:
Let the word [as an individual unit] be indeed non-different from inference.

children.text: etāvatāpīha śabdānumānayoraikyamiti vākya pravartata sopahāsamāha --- vākyeṣviti ||111||
children.translated_text: Even with this much, the identity of verbal testimony and inference [does not follow with respect to sentences] — he responds with laughter, saying 'vākyeṣu.' (111)
Thus, in the <s>Kāśikā Ṭīkā</s> composed by the teacher <s>Sucaritamiśra</s>, the <s>Śabda Pariccheda</s> (chapter on verbal testimony) is concluded.

children.text:
athopamānapariccheda' /
'upamānamapi sādṛśyamasannikṛṣṭer'the buddhimutpādayati /
yathā gavayadarśanaṃ gosmaramasye'ki bhāṣyam /
asyāyaṃ tātparyārtha'--- upāmānamapi na parīkṣaṇīyam, evaṃ lakṣamakatvenāvyabhicārāditi /
avayavārthastvekatra dṛśyamānaṃ sādṛśyaṃ pratiyogyantare dṛśyamānapratiyogisādṛśyaviśiṣṭatayāsannikṛṣṭer'the yāṃ buddhimutpādayati 'etatsādṛśyaviśiṣṭo 'sā'viti, sopamānamiti, sopamānamiti ca yattadoradhyāhāra' /
na ca vācyaṃ viṣayaviśeṣānupādānāt kathaṃ sādṛśyaviśiṣṭaviṣayā buddhiravagamyata iti, prasiddhapramāṇānuvādena hyatrāparīkṣā pratipādyate /
loke ca sādṛśyaviśiṣṭaviṣayaiva
children.translated_text: Now the <s>Upamāna Pariccheda</s> (chapter on analogy). Here is the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'Analogy too — the similarity of an object not in proximity — produces cognition of the meaning. For example, the seeing of a <s>gavaya</s> [produces] the memory of a cow.' The purported meaning of this is: Analogy too need not be examined [separately], since as a [valid] definition it is non-deviating. The meaning of the components is: When similarity observed in one [object] produces, with respect to the other counter-part not in proximity, a cognition of the form 'that one is qualified by this similarity' — qualified by the similarity of the counter-part observed [elsewhere] — that is analogy; and the word 'sa' means 'with analogy.' Nor should it be said: 'Since the specification of the object is not mentioned, how is it understood that the cognition has the similarity-qualified [entity] as its object?' — for here, the non-necessity of examination is being taught through the restatement of a well-known <s>pramāṇa</s>. And in common usage, the cognition
This [is what constitutes] analogy-hood in common usage; but in [the view of] <s>Śavara</s> [Svāmin],
Since that falls outside of <s>āgama</s> (scripture), it has been described differently. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.6.2)
There, the meaning is understood through the cognition of the person [i.e., the informant] alone.
[That the cognition] qualified by similarity is [what constitutes] analogy — this is well established.
Therefore, there is no defect. (Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika 5.6.3)

children.text:
dṛśyamānaviśeṣamekadeśadarśanāditivadanupāttamiti ced na /
udāharaṇe upādānāt /
evaṃ hyāha--- 'yathā gavayadarśanaṃ gosmaraṇasye'ti /
asyārtha'--- dṛśyate 'sminniti darśanaṃ, adhikaraṇe lyuṭ /
gavayo darśanamasyeti gavayadarśanam /
sādṛśyamanyapadārtha' /
etaduktaṃ bhavati--- gavaye dṛśyamānaṃ sādṛśyamiti /
atrodāharamānusāreṇa lakṣamavākye 'pi
dṛśyamānameva sādṛśyamānameva sādṛśyamabhimatamiti gamayte /
gosmaraṇasyeti ca 'nandigrahī' (pā-3-1-134) tyādinā kartari lyu' /
gāṃ smarata' pramātu' /
yathā gavaye dṛśyamānaṃ sādṛśyametatsadṛśāgauriti buddhimutpādayatīti /
saṅgatistu prasiddhibāhulyāt śābdānantaramupamānamiti pragevoktam /
atra codayati--- prasiddhapramāṇānuvādenātrāparīkṣā pratipādyate /
ato yathā naiyāyikoktamupamānaṃ pramāṇamāśrīyate, evaṃ taduktamevopamānalakṣaṇamāśrayitumucitam /
evaṃ hi tairuktaṃ--- 'prasiddhasādharmyāt sādhyasādhanamupamānami'ti /
asyārtha'--- prasiddhena gavādinā sādharmyāt sādhyasyāprasiddhasya gavayāde' kañcidanabhijñaṃ prati sādhanaṃ prajñāpanaṃ yādṛśo gaustādṛśo gavaya ici vākyaṃ, tajjanitā vā buddhirupamānamiti /
tadetatparihāreṇa lakṣaṇāntarapraṇayane kāraṇaṃ vācyamityata āha--- kīdṛgiti dvayena /
satyaṃ naiyāyikairidamuktam /

children.translated_text: but it is not correct,
because of its falling outside <s>āgama</s> (verbal testimony), as stated just above.
For this is cognition of an object not directly present, arising from verbal knowledge;
therefore in the <s>Śābara</s> system, <s>upamāna</s> is described quite differently. // Msv 5,6.2 //

[Objection:] The specific [similarity] that is being perceived — since it is not mentioned [in the definition], like seeing a part [only], [the definition is incomplete]. [Reply:] No, because it is mentioned in the example. For he says thus: 'Just as the perception of a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) [is the cause of] the remembrance of a cow.' The meaning of this is: 'that in which something is perceived' is <s>darśana</s> (perception); the suffix <s>lyuṭ</s> is used in the locative sense. '<s>Gavaya</s>-perception' means that in which a <s>gavaya</s> is perceived. The similarity is the other word-meaning. What is stated amounts to this: the similarity perceived in the <s>gavaya</s>. Here, following the example, it is understood that even in the definitional statement, the intended meaning is the similarity that is being perceived. And 'of the remembrance of the cow' — by [the rule] '<s>nandigrahi</s>' (<s>Pāṇini</s> 3.1.134) etc., <s>lyu</s> is in the agent sense: 'one who remembers the cow,' i.e., the knower. Just as the similarity perceived in the <s>gavaya</s> produces the cognition 'this is similar to a cow' — thus [the definition is complete]. The connection [of this topic with what precedes] — because <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) comes after <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) due to the preponderance of common understanding — was stated earlier. Here he raises an objection: Through a restatement of the commonly accepted <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge), the examination here is established. Therefore, just as the <s>upamāna</s> stated by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> is accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s>, so it is fitting to adopt the very definition of <s>upamāna</s> stated by them. For they have stated thus: '<s>Upamāna</s> is the establishment of what is to be proved through [its] similarity with what is well-known.' The meaning of this is: through the similarity with a well-known [entity] such as a cow, the establishment — i.e., the making known — of the unknown entity such as the <s>gavaya</s> to someone unacquainted [with it], by means of a statement such as 'the <s>gavaya</s> is like the cow,' or the cognition produced by it, is <s>upamāna</s>. Since this [objection requires] refutation and [the need to] formulate an alternative definition must be stated, he says with two [verses beginning with] 'kīdṛg' etc. True, the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> have stated this —

children.text: evaṃ hi naiyāyikānāṃ śābdalakṣaṇam 'āptopadeśa' śabda' iti /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>' definition of <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) is: '<s>Śabda</s> is the instruction of a trustworthy person (<s>āptopadeśa</s>).'

children.text: atrāpi cāptapuruṣapratyenaivāparidṛṣṭe gavayādau sādṛśyena sampratyayo bhavati /
children.translated_text: And here too, it is through the statement of a trustworthy person that the understanding of the previously unseen <s>gavaya</s> and the like arises through similarity.
And since there is agreement [of the statement] with [the testimony of] more than one trustworthy person,

children.text: ata āptasyaivedaṃ vacanamavyabhicārarīti matvā tadabalabhāvī niścayo jāyate, teṣāmapyāgama eveti ||3||
children.translated_text: therefore, thinking 'this is indeed the statement of a trustworthy person, unfailing,' the resultant certainty arises — [so] for them too it is nothing but <s>āgama</s>. // 3 //
He states that even following the <s>Naiyāyika</s> definition of <s>āgama</s>, [the Naiyāyika <s>upamāna</s>] is understood to be <s>āgama</s> itself — 'puruṣa' etc.
Because it is the statement of such [a trustworthy person], therefore it is nothing but <s>āgama</s>. // 3 //
The cognition that arises from [seeing] a similar [object] regarding another similar [object] —

children.text: dhyānādismṛtitulyatvāt sā pramāṇaṃ kathaṃ bhavet // Msv_5,6.4 //
children.translated_text: since it is equivalent to a memory produced by meditation and the like, how can it be a <s>pramāṇa</s>? // Msv 5,6.4 //
Just as elsewhere [an object] is distinguished by differences of place, time, and so forth,
the object of knowledge is not [so distinguished] here — [one merely recalls it] in accordance with [what was seen] in the city. // Msv 5,6.5 //
The cognition regarding the <s>gavaya</s> in the forest, arising from hearing the <s>atideśa</s> (analogical extension) statements —
that is <s>upamāna</s> for some, colored by [the recollection of] similarity with the cow. // Msv 5,6.6 //

children.text:
nanu śābare 'pi hyadṛśadarśanāt sadṛśāntare jñānamupamānamiti varṇitam /
etadapi smaraṇābahirbhāvādapramāṇameva /
yathā hi kiñcid dhyāyata' smaraṇaṃ bhavati, evaṃ sadṛśadarśino 'pi sadṛśāntare smaraṇam, ato na dhyānādijanmanā smṛtyā sahāsyā' kaścid viśeṣa' /
children.translated_text: For just as one who is meditating on something has a memory [of it], so too one who sees a similar thing has a memory regarding the other similar thing; therefore this [cognition arising from <s>upamāna</s>] has no distinction from memory produced by meditation and the like.
Therefore it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> — he says 'sadṛśāt' etc.
The <s>Naiyāyika</s> definition, to begin with, falls outside <s>āgama</s>.
But the <s>Śābara</s> definition takes in what is simply not a <s>pramāṇa</s>. // 4 //

[Objection:] But even in the <s>Śābara</s> system, it is described that <s>upamāna</s> is the knowledge regarding another similar thing from seeing a similar one. This too, being outside the domain of memory, is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> at all.

children.text: nanu smṛtisambhinnamapi deśādibhedena jāyamānaṃ pratyabhijñānaṃ pramāṇaṃ dṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>), even though mixed with memory, is seen to be a <s>pramāṇa</s> when it arises through differences of place and the like.

children.text: evamihāpi gāṃ nagare dṛṣṭavato vane gavayadarśanastadbhānaṃ pramāṇaṃ bhavatyata āha---deśakālādīti /
children.translated_text: Likewise here too, for one who has seen a cow in the city, the cognition of it upon seeing a <s>gavaya</s> in the forest is a <s>pramāṇa</s> — therefore he says 'deśakālādi' etc.

children.text: na khalu deśādibheda' sanmātratayā prāmāṇye kāraṇam, api tarhi prameyatayā, na ceha deśāntarādiviśiṣṭo gau' pramīyate, api tu nagarāvagata' sampratyapi tatstha eva smaryata iti ||5||
children.translated_text: The difference of place and the like, merely by existing, is not the reason for validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>); rather, [it must function] as the object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>). And here, the cow qualified by a different place and the like is not being known [anew]; rather, [the cow] understood in the city is even now remembered as being located there itself. // 5 //
He presents the view of some <s>Naiyāyikas</s> — 'śruta' etc.

children.text: yena kilātideśavākyaṃ śrutaṃ yādṛśo gaustādṛśo gavaya iti, tasya śrutādideśavākyasya vanaṃ prāptasya yat svayamasau gosadṛśo gavaya iti sādṛśyānurañjitaṃ gavayajñānamidamupamānamiti ||6||
children.translated_text: For one who has heard the <s>atideśa</s> statement 'the <s>gavaya</s> is like the cow,' when he, having heard that <s>atideśa</s> statement, reaches the forest, his cognition of the <s>gavaya</s> — 'this is similar to a cow' — colored by the recollection of similarity, is <s>upamāna</s>. // 6 //
The <s>gavaya</s> is [known] through direct perception; but the [recollection of] similarity here is —

children.text: nanu sādṛśyayukter'the na smṛtirnaindriyād gati' // Msv_5,6.7 //
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But since the object is qualified by similarity, it is neither memory nor sensory cognition. // Msv 5,6.7 //
If there is nothing additional in [the cognition of] the <s>gavaya</s> beyond [what was known from] the prior [analogical] statement,
then since it is no different from memory, the conjunction [of the two sources] does not constitute a [distinct] <s>pramāṇa</s>. // Msv 5,6.8 //
But if there is some additional element through the power of perception and the like,
then to the extent that the cognition is connected with the sense organ, that is considered perception. // Msv 5,6.9 //

children.text:
etadapi dūṣayati---pratyakṣa iti /
gavayastāvadindriyasannikarṣāt pratyakṣeṇa pratīyate /
gosādṛśyamapyatideśavākyādavagataṃ smaryata iti nopameyamastīti /
atra codayati--- nanviti /
ayamabhiprāya'--- gosādṛśyaviśiṣṭo hyatra gavayo 'vagamyate /
na ca tatpratyakṣaṃ, gorapratyakṣatvāt /

children.translated_text: The <s>gavaya</s> qualified by that [similarity] is the object of <s>upamāna</s>.
For it is not ascertained by perception, since [perception's] object is merely the <s>gavaya</s> [alone].
Nor is it known through <s>āgama</s> and remembered, since <s>āgama</s> has a general [content as its] object.
And here, because there is a cognition of the particular — 'this is that' — [<s>upamāna</s> is distinct]. // 7 //

He refutes this too — 'pratyakṣa' etc. The <s>gavaya</s>, to begin with, is cognized by perception through sense-contact. The similarity with the cow, known from the <s>atideśa</s> statement, is merely remembered — so there is no separate object of <s>upamāna</s>. Here he raises an objection — 'nanu' etc. The intended meaning is: what is cognized here is the <s>gavaya</s> qualified by similarity to the cow. And that is not perception, because the cow is not [presently] perceived.

children.text:
etadapi vikalpya dūṣayati---pūrvetisārdhena /
idamatra vikalpanīyam---- atideśavākyādavagatāt kiñcidadhikamavagamyate na vā, yadi netyāha, tata' smaraṇādaviśiṣṭā saṅgatiriyamapramāṇam /
yathā padāt padārthajñānaṃ pratyutpannakāraṇajatvenāsmaraṇamapyanadhikavi,yatvādapramāṇam, evamihāpyatideśavākyāvagatagosādṛśyaviśiṣṭavagayajñānam /
yadi
tarhi pratyakṣādeva labhyata iti na pramāṇāntarāvakāśa iti ||8 1/2||
children.translated_text: He considers alternatives and refutes this too — in 'pūrva' etc. with one and a half [verses]. Here the following must be considered: Is something additional cognized beyond what was known from the <s>atideśa</s> statement, or not? If not, he says: then this conjunction [of knowledge sources], being no different from memory, is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Just as the knowledge of a word-meaning from a word, even though it is not memory due to being produced by a present cause, is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> because it has no additional object — so too here, the cognition of the <s>gavaya</s> qualified by similarity to the cow, as known from the <s>atideśa</s> statement, [is not a separate pramāṇa]. But if [something additional is cognized], then it is obtained from perception itself, and there is no scope for another <s>pramāṇa</s>. // 8½ //

children.text: nanuktamasannihite gavitatsādṛśyasyāpratyakṣātvānna tadviśiṣṭo gavaya' pratyakṣeṇāvagantuṃ śakyata iti sāvakāśaṃ pramāṇāntaramityata āha--- yāvaddhīti /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But it has been said that since the cow is not present and its similarity is not perceptible, the <s>gavaya</s> qualified by that [similarity] cannot be cognized by perception — therefore there is scope for another <s>pramāṇa</s>. Hence he says 'yāvaddhi' etc.
Whatever appears directly (<s>aparokṣa</s>) immediately following the operation of the sense organ — that is our perception.

children.text: tathā ca sādṛśyaviśiṣṭo gavaya iti kathamapratyakṣo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: And accordingly, how will the <s>gavaya</s> qualified by similarity be non-perceptual?

children.text: pratijāti kṛtsnaparisamāptameva jātivat sādṛśyamityapratyakṣe 'pi gavi tatsādṛśyaviśiṣṭagavayapratyakṣamupapadyata eveti bhāva' ||9||
children.translated_text: For similarity, like a universal (<s>jāti</s>), is fully present in each individual of the class; therefore, even when the cow is not [presently] perceived, the perception of the <s>gavaya</s> qualified by its similarity is perfectly established — this is the purport. // 9 //
And in the discrimination of the part that is being remembered, there is no invalidity;
moreover, the qualification 'having heard the <s>atideśa</s> statement' is not very useful. // Msv 5,6.10 //
For even those who have not heard that [<s>atideśa</s>] statement — for them too this [cognition] arises,
for those who have perceived cow-ness by direct perception, [and then] see a <s>gavaya</s> in the forest. // Msv 5,6.11 //
If [it is argued that] for them there is no linking of the name [to the <s>gavaya</s>] — [this is] what is maintained,

children.text: na nām, vastu tattāvat sarvathā tai' pratīyate // Msv_5,6.12 //
children.translated_text: [but] no, for that very entity is in every way cognized by them. // Msv 5,6.12 //
And the word-meaning relation is not the object of knowledge here — that is our position;
for in the [<s>atideśa</s>] statement, once the similarity is ascertained, it [the relation] is known from the statement itself. // Msv 5,6.13 //

And there is no invalidity from the admixture of memory of words and so forth, since the discrimination between what is being grasped and what is being remembered has been established in the establishment of <s>savikalpaka</s> [perception] — he says 'smaryamāṇasya' etc.
The meaning is: when there is discrimination [between the perceptual and memorial components], there is no invalidity.
He says that even the adoption of the qualification 'having heard the <s>atideśa</s> statement' yields no result — 'śruta' etc. // 10 //
How is it not useful? — 'ye 'pi' etc.

children.text: gosādṛśyaviśiṣṭagavayadarśanaṃ cedupamānamabhimataṃ tadāśrutatadvākyānāmapi nagare gāṃ dṛṣṭavatāṃ vane gavayaṃ paśyatāmastyeveti mandaṃ viśeṣaṇaphalamiti ||11||
children.translated_text: If the cognition of a <s>gavaya</s> qualified by similarity with a cow is the intended [meaning of] <s>upamāna</s>, then even for those who have not heard that [<s>atideśa</s>] statement, who have seen a cow in the city and see a <s>gavaya</s> in the forest — [this cognition] does indeed exist; hence the qualification yields meager result. // 11 //

children.text: nanvaśrutātideśavākyānāmayamasau gavaya iti saṃjñānusandhānaṃ nāsti, itareṣāmastītyayamasti viśeṣa ityāha---athati /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But for those who have not heard the <s>atideśa</s> statement, there is no linking of the name 'this is a <s>gavaya</s>'; for others there is — this is the distinction. Hence he says 'atha' etc.
He refutes — 'na nāma' etc.
What is accepted as the object of <s>upamāna</s> — that very thing they too know;
let the name-designation not be linked [— it makes no difference]. // 12 //

children.text:
syānmatam--- saṃjñāsajñisambandha evopamānasya viṣaya' /
yathoktaṃ nyāyavistare---"samākhyāsambandhapratipattirupamānārtha"iti /
vivṛtaṃ ca---"yathā gauriva gavaya ityukte gavā samānārthamindriyasannikarṣādupalabhamāno 'sya gavayaśabda' saṃjñeti saṃjñāsaṃjñisambandhaṃ pratipadyata' iti /
na cāśrutātideśavākyasya śabdamaviduṣa' samākhyāsambandhapratipatti' sambhavatīti phala
children.translated_text: The view might be: the relation of sign (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and signified (<s>saṃjñin</s>) is itself the object of <s>upamāna</s>. As stated in the <s>Nyāyavistara</s>: 'The apprehension of the relation of designation is the purpose of <s>upamāna</s>.' And it is explained: 'When told "the <s>gavaya</s> is like a cow," one who perceives through sense-contact something having the same meaning as [the word] "cow" understands that [the word] <s>gavaya</s> is a name, and thus apprehends the relation of sign and signified.' And for one who has not heard the <s>atideśa</s> statement, who does not know the word, the apprehension of the designation-relation is not possible — hence the result [of the qualification —
And recognition does not arise anew for it in the forest;
since the two capacities [of word and meaning] are supersensory, it is accepted as memory alone. // Msv 5,6.14 //
Even in cognition pervaded by words, perception has been established;
therefore let the object — meaning qualified by similarity — be called unprecedented. // Msv 5,6.15 //
He states the reason — 'sādṛśya' etc.

children.text: ati deśavākyādeva gosādṛśyena gavayaśabdavācyer'thevadhārite vyaktirūpeṇānavagato 'pi śabdārthasambandho 'vagata eva /
children.translated_text: From the <s>atideśa</s> statement itself, when the object denoted by the word '<s>gavaya</s>' has been determined through similarity with the cow — even though the word-meaning relation was not known in its particular instantiation, it is indeed known [in general].
For this is what was known at that time: 'the entity that is similar to a cow is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>.'

children.text: etāvacca sambandhasya svarūpam, ata' sūktaṃ viśeṣaṇānarthakyamiti ||13||
children.translated_text: And this is the very nature of the [word-meaning] relation; therefore, the purposelessness of the qualification is well-stated. // 13 //
— is a qualification]. Hence he says 'na ca' etc.

children.text:
nanu jñātasyāpi sambandhasya pratyabhijñāne prāmāṇyamavihatamevāta āha---na ceti /
atra kāraṇamāha--- śaktyoriti /
vācyavācakaśaktiniyamo hi śabdārthayo' sambandha' /
sa cātīndriyatvānneha pratyabhijñāyate /
pūrvāvagata evānyūnānatirikta' smaryate /
kimidānīmatīndriye naiva pratyabhijñānamasti, yadyevamanumānena kathaṃ pūrvānubhūtamagnyādi pratyabhijñāyate /
āha ca--- 'gṛhīte 'pi deśādibhedabhinne puna' pramāpratyabhijñānumānātsāt pratyakṣavadavadhārite 'pī'ti /
ihāpi ca vakṣyati---
'yena nāma pramāṇena grahaṇaṃ buddhikarmaṇo'' /
iti /
satyam /
na brūma' parokṣaṃ na pratyabhijñāyata iti, yadetadayamasau gosādṛśyaviśiṣṭo gavaya itīndriyajamaparokṣāvabhāsaṃ pratyabhijñānam---
asya śabdārthasambandha' śaktirūpo na gocara' /
gosādṛśyena vijñānatapūrvo gavaya eva tu||
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But even for a relation that is already known, there is unimpaired validity in recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>). Hence he says 'na ca' etc. He states the reason — 'śaktyor' etc. The relation of word and meaning is the fixed capacity (<s>śakti</s>) of the word and its referent. And since that is supersensory, it is not recognized here [by perception]; [rather,] what was previously known is merely remembered, neither more nor less. [Question:] Is there then no recognition at all of what is supersensory? If so, how is fire and the like, previously experienced, recognized through inference? And he says: 'Even when grasped [before], though differentiated by place and the like, [it is recognized] again through the <s>pramāṇa</s> of recognition-inference, just as when determined by perception,' etc. And he will say here too: 'By whichever <s>pramāṇa</s> the grasping of a mental act [is accomplished]' — etc. True. We do not say that what is remote is never recognized. This recognition — 'this is that <s>gavaya</s> qualified by similarity to the cow' — which is sensory and appears directly — its word-meaning relation, being of the nature of capacity, is not within sensory range; [what is recognized is] the <s>gavaya</s> itself, previously known through similarity with the cow.
Thus [it is stated].

children.text: ata eva 'na cāsye'ti sambandhasya pratyabhijñānaviṣayatvaṃ nirākaroti /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, by [the verse] 'na cāsya' etc., he denies that the [word-meaning] relation is an object of recognition.
But the <s>gavaya</s>, previously known through similarity with the cow,
is recognized here — and there is nothing problematic in this. // 14 //

children.text:
athocyeta (vṛ?pratya) kṣād vyavartayituṃ viśeṣaṇopādānam /
śrutaśabdollisvatamidaṃ gavayajñānamato na pratyakṣasya viṣaya isyupamānasya bhaviṣyatītyata āha---śabdeti /
śabdānuviddhabodhe 'pi hīndriyasambandhā
children.translated_text: [Objection:] It might be said that the qualification [of having heard the statement] is adopted in order to distinguish [<s>upamāna</s>] from perception. This cognition of the <s>gavaya</s>, shining forth with the word heard [earlier], is therefore not the object of perception — it will be the object of <s>upamāna</s>. Hence he says 'śabda' etc. Even in cognition pervaded by words, perception has been established —
But if it is held that perception has the nature of determination (<s>vyavasāya</s>),

children.text: jātyādivat tadā tena sādṛśyaṃ kiṃ na mīyate // Msv_5,6.16 //
children.translated_text: then, like universals (<s>jāti</s>) and the like, why is similarity not measured by it? // Msv 5,6.16 //
This, however, is a semblance of perception for the proponents of <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate perception);
and because of the non-existence of the real object to be known, [their] claim to validity is not accepted [by us]. // Msv 5,6.17 //

children.text: nusāri jñānaṃ śabdaśaktiparāmarśajameveti pratyakṣameveti varṇitamityato naikatrāpi lakṣaṇe upamānasya prameyamadhikaṃ paśyāma iti vācyamasyāpūrvaṃ prameyamityupasaṃharati--- tasmāditi ||15||
children.translated_text: [continuing] the cognition following the sense-contact is born from the reflection on word-capacity itself, and so is perception—as has been explained. Therefore, even in either definition [of analogy], we do not see any additional knowable [object] for analogy—hence one should say: its knowable is unprecedented. He concludes—'therefore.' // 15 //

children.text: yadi tūcyate--- pratiyogisāpekṣaṃ sādṛśyagrahaṇam ato na pratyakṣam, arthendriyasāmarthyamātrajaṃ hi pratyakṣaṃ jñānaṃ, na tatpūrvamaparaṃ vānusandhatte /
ata' pratyakṣe 'pi dharmiṇi parokṣameva sādṛśyamiti na tadviśiṣṭasya pratyakṣatvamiti sāvakāśamupamānamityata āha---vyavasāyeti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even when the property-bearer is perceptual, similarity is mediated—and so the perception of what is qualified by it [is not straightforward]. Hence analogy has scope—thus he says—'determination.'
This is the established doctrine of the Buddhists: that which is non-conceptual and arises at the first glance is perception.
But the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> hold a doctrine of determinate perception.

children.text: ato jātyādivatsādṛśyamapi teṣāṃ kiṃ na pratyakṣema pramīyata iti ||16||
children.translated_text: Therefore, why is similarity not known by perception for them, just like universals and the like? // 16 //

But if it is said: the grasping of similarity depends on a counter-correlate, and therefore is not perception. For perceptual knowledge arises merely from the capacity of the object and sense-organ, and it does not coordinate with what came before or what comes after.

children.text:
nirvikalpakavādināmapi nedaṃ pramāṇāntaraṃ,pratyakṣābhāsatvādityāha--- pratyakṣeti /
evaṃ tāvat sādṛśyasya vastvantaratvamaṅgīkṛtya tatpratyakṣatayopamānasya viṣayābhāvenāprāmāṇyamuktam /
idānīṃ bauddhamatena sādṛśyāpalāpamāha---prameyeti /
nirvikalpakapratyakṣavādināmapi sādṛsyaprameyābhāvādapamānasya pramāṇatā nābhipretā /
atasteṣu spardhamāneṣu kathamupamānaṃ pramāṇam /
ayaṃ ca teṣāmabhiprāya'--- sādṛśyaṃ hi na tāvadāśrayebhyo bhinnamupalambhāt /
abhede cāśrayāt tanmātrāpātāt /
kathaṃ cāśrayeṣu vartate /
na tāvat kārtsnyena vṛttamanyatrāpi tathaiva vartata iti sāmpratam /
na ca bhāgaśa', tadabhāvāt /
kiñcedaṃ sādṛśyaṃ na tāvad dravyaguṇakarmaṇāmanyatamam, padārthapaṇḍitaisteṣvanupasaṃkhyātatvāt /
na hi navasu dravyeṣu caturviśatyāṃ guṇeṣu pañcasu vā karmasu sādṛśyamantargataṃ paśyāma' /
na ca sāmānyameva sādṛśyaṃ, taddhi tadbuddhau karaṇaṃ, tadvadbuddhivedyaṃ ca sādṛśyaṃ, tatsādṛśye ca gotvādāvapi tathātvaprasanaṅga' /
avayavasāmānyāni sādṛśyamiti ced /
na /
teṣvapyaikaikaśyenasādṛśyabuddherupajananāt /
bhūyāṃsi sādṛśyamiti ced /
na /

prayogyapekṣayā sāmānyāni sādṛśyamiti ceti /

kintu tattvāntaramevedaṃ dravyajātiguṇakarmabhyo vyatiriktaṃ guṇabhedo vā /
yathāha guru'--- 'na sāmānyaṃ sādṛśyam /
kiṃ tarhi?tadeva tat, gotvāderakatvā'diti /

śyenavyaktijātyo' svabhāvanirmitapakṣatvagrasamāṃsalohitāsthiśira' pṛṣṭhapādodarādyavayavārabdhāvayavisamavāyitveneṣṭakābhiraśakyasampādanatvāt /
yadi cāvayavasāmānyāni sādṛśyamiṣyante tatasteṣāmihābhāvāt sādṛśyamapi du' sampādanamiti so 'nārabhyor'tha' pratijñāto bhavet 'śyenacitaṃ cinvīte'ti /
evaṃ cānavayaveṣvapi gandhādiṣu sādṛśyasaṃvidupapatsyata iti /
tacca naivam /
tattvāntare hi sādṛśye gāmanapekṣyāpi gavayaṃ sadṛśamiti jānīyu' /
tatra hi tanniravaśeṣameva sādṛśyaṃ parisamāptamiti kimanyadapekṣate /
kathamanapekṣite gavi tatsādṛśyaviśiṣṭo 'vagamyata iti cet kasatsya gavā sambandha' /
samavāya iti cet, so 'pi tarhi gavayavad gosadṛśatayā jñātavya' /
api ca samavetaṃ nāma tatsādṛśyaṃ gavayagatasādṛśyagrahaṇe 'pi kimityapekṣyate /
na hi gotvaṃ śābaleye samavetamiti
children.translated_text: Even for the proponents of non-conceptual [perception], this is not a separate means of knowledge, because it is a semblance of perception—hence he says—'perception.' Thus far, by accepting the reality of similarity as an entity, the non-validity of analogy due to the absence of an object has been stated by [showing] its perceptibility. Now, he states the denial of similarity according to the Buddhist view—'knowable.' For even the proponents of non-conceptual perception do not intend analogy to have the status of a means of knowledge, due to the absence of similarity as a knowable. Therefore, when they compete [in denying its independent status], how can analogy be a means of knowledge? And their reasoning is as follows: Similarity is not, to begin with, perceived as distinct from its substrata. And if it is not different from its substratum, the mere substratum would follow. And how does it reside in substrata? Not in its entirety, for then it would exist in the same way elsewhere too—and that is inappropriate. Nor partially, because there are no parts [of similarity]. Moreover, what is this similarity? It is not one of substance, quality, or action, since it has not been enumerated among those categories by the experts on categories. For we do not see similarity included among the nine substances, twenty-four qualities, or five actions. Nor is similarity simply the universal, for that is the cause of the cognition 'that [is such],' while similarity is known through the cognition 'like that'—and in the case of the similarity of cow-ness and such, there would be the undesired consequence [that universals are similarities]. If you say 'part-universals are similarity'—no, because even from each one individually, the cognition of similarity arises. If you say 'many [part-universals] are similarity'—no, because even when many are gathered in one [entity], without reference to the counter-correlate, the cognition of similarity does not arise. For those entities are certainly gathered in one [individual], yet they are not grasped through the cognition of similarity—for no one knows a cow as 'this is similar' without reference to the counter-correlate. If you say 'the universals are similarity in dependence on the counter-correlate'—then is similarity relative? Indeed. If so, is it manifested or produced by the [cognition of the] correlate? It is not produced [by it], like duality [which depends on the cognition of pairing but is not produced thereby], because it is naturally established. But the manifestors such as light and the senses exist [already]—so what else does it require? And if part-universals are similarity, then in the case of twins, since there are no such [part-universals], there would follow the absence [of similarity]. And if similarity is accepted even there, then upon the destruction of the twins, since the universal would be destroyed, the established doctrine would be violated. And in [the case of] a tortoise and such, since the physical parts such as hands and head do not exist in their transformed form—in the absence of the universal, there would be an absence of similarity. The same consequence should be shown for smell and the like as well. Due to the absence of sub-parts of the parts such as ears—there would be dissimilarity. But if you hold: 'True, part-universals are not similarity. Rather, this is a different category altogether, distinct from substance, universal, quality, and action—or a subdivision of quality.' As the teacher says: 'Similarity is not a universal. What then? It is that very thing [a separate entity], due to its being different from cow-ness and the like.' And thus it makes sense that the purpose of the injunction regarding the <s>Śyena</s> ritual is merely the approximation of what is similar. For the natural wings, talons, flesh, blood, bones, head, back, feet, belly, and other parts of the <s>Śyena</s>-bird, being constituted by their individual and universal [features], cannot be produced with bricks. And if part-universals are accepted as similarity, then since they would be absent here [in the brick construction], similarity too would be difficult to produce—and thus that purpose declared as 'One should construct the <s>Śyena</s> fire-altar' would be unattainable. And thus, even for partless entities like smell and such, the cognition of similarity would be justified. But that is not so. For if similarity were a separate category, then even without reference to a cow, one would know a <s>gavaya</s> as similar. For in that case, all that similarity would be fully complete [in the gavaya itself]—so what else does it require? If you say, 'how is what is qualified by that similarity apprehended without reference to the cow?'—then what is its relation with the cow? If you say 'inherence'—then that too should be known as similar to a cow, like a <s>gavaya</s>. Moreover, that similarity, being inherent, why is it required even in the grasping of the similarity residing in the <s>gavaya</s>? For cow-ness, being inherent in a dappled cow—
The reality of similarity too cannot be denied;
it is the preponderance of part-universals' conjunction, or [it is] a different category.

bāhuleye tadabodhe 'pi tadapekṣā dṛṣṭā /
tathedaṃ gavi gavayasādṛśyamiti na tadapekṣāheturupalabhyata iti /
api cāpekṣatāṃ nāma gau',
dūrād gāmupalabdhavato(')viditāvayavasāmānyavibhāgasyāpi gosadṛśyagavayajñānaṃ bhavet /
avayavasāmānyānyapi tadbodhe 'pyapekṣyanta iti cet /
vaktavyo 'pekṣārtha' /
yadi matam, abhivyañjakāni tasyāvayavasāmānyānīti, tāni tarhi gavayavartīni tasyābhivyañjakāni, santi ca tāni gave(?vi) iti kiṃ gogatadvedanena, ato gavyavagate 'navagateṣu cāvayavasāmānyeṣu gosādṛśyajñānaṃ jāyeta /
jātyorhi tatsādṛśyam, avagate ca te iti kimanyadapekṣyate /

syānmatam, vyañjakāni tāni tasya /
bhavati cābhivyañjakaprakarṣe 'bhivyaṅgyabuddhiprakarṣa' /
yathā ghaṭādau tadvadihāpi bhaviṣyatīti /
tanna /
na hi buddhimātramatra prakṛṣyate /
api tarhi vastveva sātiśayamupālabhāmahe /

children.translated_text: For precisely this reason, when the primary [object] is unavailable, one who desires what is similar substitutes what is very similar,
not what is slightly similar—and even this amounts to something.

children.text: ata' kalpanāmātrakalpitaṃ dvicandrālātacakrādivad bhrāntikaraṇaṃ sādṛśyaṃ na prāmāṇikamiti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, similarity, fabricated by mere conceptual construction alone, like the double moon or the fire-wheel [of a whirling brand], is an error-producing [cognition], not veridical.

children.text: prameyābhāvādapi nopamānāṅgamanyad vā sadṛśye pramāṇamityāpekṣa iti ||17||
children.translated_text: And since there is no knowable, analogy cannot be a component of [any means of knowledge], nor is there any other means of knowledge for similarity—such is the expectation. // 17 //

[continuing] even in the case of a brown [cow], where that [cow-ness] is not cognized, the dependence [on the counter-correlate] is observed. So too here, the similarity of the <s>gavaya</s> with the cow—no reason for its dependence [on the cow] is found. Moreover, let the cow be required! Then even for one who has perceived a cow from afar, without knowing the distinction of part-universals, the knowledge of the <s>gavaya</s> as similar to a cow would arise. If you say even the part-universals are required for that cognition—the purpose of the requirement must be stated. If you hold that the part-universals are the manifestors [of similarity], then those manifestors of it are present in the <s>gavaya</s>; and they also exist in the cow—so what is the use of knowing the cow? Therefore, even when the <s>gavaya</s> is understood and the part-universals are not understood, the knowledge of similarity with the cow would arise. For that similarity belongs to the universals, and those [universals] are cognized—so what else is required? And this [preponderance of] part-universals as constituting similarity—this would not hold if similarity were a separate category, since [in that case] it would be [complete and] equal everywhere. You might hold: those [part-universals] are its manifestors. And there is an increase in the cognition of what is to be manifested when the manifestor is more intense—as in the case of a pot and such. So it would be the same here too. But that is not so. For here it is not merely the cognition that is intensified; rather, we observe the thing itself as having degrees.

children.text:
atra samādhimāha---sādṛśyasyeti /
ayamabhiprāya'--- nedaṃ kalpanāmātrakalpitaṃ, mithyātvahetudvayāsambhavāt /
dvicandrādipratyayā hi kutaściddoṣādutpannā' kālādibhedeṣu bādhyante /
sādṛśyaṃ tu jātyādivatatsatyamevaṃ sādṛśyamapīti kimapahnūyate /
tadidamavagatamasaṃśayitamavādhitaṃ ca deśāntarādiṣvapītyasti tāvat sādṛśyaṃ, pramāṇabalena yathā tadupapadyate tathā kalpanīyam /
na hi dṛṣṭe 'nupapannaṃ nāma kiñcidastīti||
children.translated_text: To this he gives the resolution—'the reality of similarity.' The purport is this: this [similarity] is not fabricated by mere conceptual construction, because the two causes of falsity are both absent. For cognitions like the double moon arise from some defect and are sublated in different times and places. But similarity, like universals and the like, is real. When similarity is thus [real], what is there to deny? This [similarity] is cognized, free of doubt, and unsublated even in other places and such. Therefore, similarity does exist, and it should be postulated in whatever way it is justified by the force of the means of knowledge. For nothing observed is unjustified.

children.text:
tatra yattāvaduktaṃ kimasya svarūpamiti /
tatrottaramāha---bhūyovayaveti /
asyārtha'--- bhūyobhiravayavasāmānyairyo jātyantarasya yoga' tat sādṛśyam /
jātyantarāvayavasāmānyagrahamamupalakṣaṇārtham, vyaktisādṛśyamapi yamādiṣu dṛṣṭameva /
evamavayavasāmānyairvināpi guṇakarmādisāmānyayogenāpi sādṛśyaṃ dṛṣṭameva,yathā citrādiṣu /
etena yaduktaṃ citrādau kathaṃ sādṛśyamiti tat parihṛtam /
evamagnāvapi saṃsthānaparimāṇasāmānyaṃ darśayitavyam /
yamayostvavayavasāmānyābhyupagame yānupapattiruktā, asau parihariṣyata eva /
guṇānāṃ tvasatyapyavayavasāmānye 'vayavaguṇasāmānyamevāvayaviguṇānāṃ sādṛśyam,avayavasāmānyasyopalakṣaṇārthatvāditi /
tattvāntaravādināṃ cedamāśrayapāratantryād guṇāntargatamevāstheyam /
na pañcamamalaukikatvāt /
jātidravyaguṇakriyā' padārthā iti lokasiddham /
ato 'sya guṇasya sato gumakarmaṇoranupapanna eva samavāya' /
atha dravyasamavetameva guṇakarmaṇī api sadṛśatayā bodhayati, ekārthasamavāyāt /
yati, ekārthasamavetasamavāyādityucyate /
na /
dravyasamavāye pramāṇābhāvāt, avayavasāmānyāni hi karṇādīni vyaktisamavetāni pratyakṣāṇi /
sādṛśyaṃ tu sadṛśabuddhyā grahītavyam /
na ca gandhādisadṛśaṃ dravyamiti ato 'vayavasāmānyameva sādṛśyamiti /
nanvekatraiva bhūyasāmavayavasāmānyānāmupalambhāt sādṛśyabodhaprasaktirityuktam, parihṛtamidaṃ jātyantarasyeti vadatā /
jātyantarasamavāyināṃ jātyantare samavāyāt sādṛśyam, na svarūpamātram, na ca bhūyastvam /
etañcopariṣṭād vivariṣyata eva /
ato jātyantaragrahaṇamapekṣitavyam /
yattu na tena tajjanyata iti /
satyam /
abhivyajyate tu tat /
yathoktam---
sāmānyāni ca bhūyāṃsi guṇāvayavakarmaṇām /
bhinnapradhānasāmānyavyaktaṃ sādṛśyamucyate||
children.translated_text: Now, as for what was said—'what is its nature?'—to that he gives the answer—'preponderance of parts.' The meaning is: the conjunction with a different universal through a preponderance of part-universals—that is similarity. The mention of 'grasping part-universals of a different universal' is for the sake of indication; the similarity of individuals, as in the case of twins and the like, is also indeed observed. Thus, similarity through the conjunction of universals of qualities, actions, and the like, even without part-universals, is also observed—as in paintings and such. By this, the objection 'how is there similarity in a painting and the like' is answered. Similarly, in the case of fire, similarity of configuration and measure should be shown. And the difficulty stated regarding accepting part-universals in twins will indeed be resolved. And for qualities, even in the absence of part-universals, the similarity of the part-quality-universals themselves is the similarity of the parts-possessors' qualities—because 'part-universal' is meant indicatively. And for the proponents of [similarity as] a separate category, since it would be dependent on its substrate, this should be accepted as included within quality. Not as a fifth [category], because of its being unheard-of in the world. 'Universal, substance, quality, and action are the categories'—this is established in the world. Therefore, for this quality, inherence in quality and action is quite unjustified. But if what is inherent in substance itself makes even quality and action known as similar, [it is] through co-inherence in a single entity. If it is said 'through co-inherent-inherence'—no, because there is no means of knowledge for its inherence in substance. For the part-universals, such as ears and the like, inherent in individuals, are perceptual. But similarity is to be grasped through the cognition 'similar.' And substance is not [cognized as] 'similar to smell' and the like. Therefore, part-universals alone are similarity. But it was objected that from the apprehension of many part-universals in a single [entity], the cognition of similarity would follow [even without a correlate]—this has been answered by saying 'of a different universal.' The similarity consists in the co-inherence in a different universal of what is co-inherent in a different universal—not the mere form, nor the mere preponderance. And this will be elaborated further below. Therefore, the mention of 'a different universal' must be attended to. As for what was said—'it is not produced by that [correlate]'—true. But it is manifested by it. As stated: 'The universals that are many, of qualities, parts, and actions— similarity is said to be manifested by a different primary universal.'

children.text:
iti /
yaddhi yasyopalabdhau nimittaṃ, tattadabhivyañjakam /
ata ekaikatrāpi svarūpamātreṇa sāmānyāni gamyanta eva /
jātyantarasamavāyātmanā
children.translated_text: For whatever is the occasion for the apprehension of something is its manifestor. Therefore, even in each individual, universals are indeed cognized through mere own-form. Through the nature of co-inherence in a different universal—
But where there is the state of having similar parts, as in 'lotus-petal-eyed'—
that will be [explained as] due to the preponderance of their own part-universals.

children.text:
evaṃ jātiguṇadravyakriyāśaktisvadharmata' /
tu tāni sādṛśyam, samavāyātmā ca nāpratisaṃhite jātyantare 'bhivyakto bhavatīti yuktaiva tadapekṣā /
na ca yadarthāntarāpekṣapratibhāsaṃ tadavastu bhavati /
na hi devadattasya pitṛtvaṃ putrāpekṣā pratīyata iti, tadavastu /
children.translated_text: For the fatherhood of <s>Devadatta</s> is apprehended in dependence on a son—yet it is not unreal.
Therefore, relative entities of this kind cannot be denied.
For precisely this reason, the cognition of 'very similar' and so on is justified through the accumulation and non-accumulation of part-universals.
Therefore, it is established that similarity consists in universals of qualities, parts, and such, delimited by a different individual and universal. // 18 //

Thus, from one's own properties of universal, quality, substance, action, and capacity— but those [universals], when the different universal has not been withdrawn, are not manifested as similarity—and so the dependence on that [correlate] is entirely justified. And it is not the case that whatever appears in dependence on something else is unreal.

children.text:
nanu padmadalākṣīyamaṅganeti padmāvayavena dalenāṅganāyāścakṣurupamīyate, yadi cāvayavasāmānyaṃ sādṛśyaṃ, na tadiha sambhavati, svayamevāvayavatvāt, na hi cakṣuṣaścakṣurādyavayavāntaramasti /
ata āha---sadṛśeti /

children.translated_text: It is not necessarily the case that the part-universal of the great-part-possessor is what constitutes similarity.
Rather, it was stated that part-universals are similarity.
And that [applies] to the parts such as the eye and the like as well—

because of the abundance of the universals belonging to its own parts, it is indeed possible — thus the cognition of similarity (<s>sādṛśya</s>) regarding limbs and so forth with similar parts is justified, he says. //19//

But in the expression 'this woman is lotus-petal-eyed,' the eye of the woman is compared to a part of the lotus, namely the petal. If part-universals are similarity, that is not possible here, since [the petal] is itself a part—for the eye does not have sub-parts like the eye and the like. Hence he says—'having similar parts.'

children.text:
astu tāvadavayaveṣvavāntarāvayavasāmānyayogāt sādṛśyam, vināpi tu tāni tatra tatra sadṛśabodho dṛṣṭa' /
sa kathamupapadyate ata āha---evamiti /
nedamavayavasāmānyagrahaṇaṃ tantram /
yadeva tu kiñcid guṇādisāmānyaṃ sadṛśadhiyamupajanayati tadeva sādṛśyamato nātraikarūpyameva /
vicitratā tu sādṛśyasya yathādarśanamaṅgīkartavyam /
tad yathā--- jātisādṛśyam 'agnirvai brāhmaṇa' iti, agnisadṛśa ityartha' /
kimanayo' sādṛśyam, ekasmād brahmaṇo mukhājjātīrutpattirityartha' /
idaṃ ca tatsiddhisūtre vakṣyate /
kuta' punaranayo' samānābhijananatvamavagamyate /
śrute' /
evaṃ hyāha--- 'prajāpatirmukhatastrivṛtaṃ chandasāṃ niramimīta agniṃ devatānāṃ brāhmaṇaṃ manuṣyāṇāmi'ti /
loke ca samānābhijananayordarśayitavyam /
guṇasāmānyaṃ tu citrādau suprakāśameva loke, vede ca 'ādityo yūpa' iti /
children.translated_text: Granted, there is similarity in parts due to the connection of intermediate-part universals. But even without those, a cognition of similarity is observed here and there. How is that to be explained? Therefore he says — 'evam' (thus). It is not [exclusively] the grasping of part-universals that is the principle here. Rather, whatever universal of quality and so forth gives rise to a cognition of similarity — that itself is <s>sādṛśya</s> (resemblance). Therefore there is no single-form [definition] here. Rather, the variety of <s>sādṛśya</s> must be accepted as observed. For example: similarity of <s>jāti</s> (genus) — 'Fire indeed is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' — meaning, similar to fire. What similarity is there between these two? The meaning is: both are born from the mouth of <s>Brahman</s> — identity of origin. And this will be stated in the <s>Tatsiddhisūtra</s>. But whence is this common origin understood? From <s>śruti</s>. For thus it says: '<s>Prajāpati</s> from his mouth produced the threefold [meter] of the <s>Chandas</s>, <s>Agni</s> among the deities, and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> among humans.' And in the world, [similarity] of common origin is to be shown. Similarity of quality (<s>guṇa</s>) is quite evident in the world regarding paintings and so forth; and in the <s>Veda</s>: '<s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>).'
The variety of this [resemblance] is due to the distinction of one, two, three, or all [properties being] similar. // Msv 5.6.20 //

children.text: na dharmā eva sādṛśyaṃ bhūyastā vā tadāśrayā /
children.translated_text: It is not the properties (<s>dharmas</s>) themselves that are <s>sādṛśya</s> (resemblance), nor is the abundance [of properties] that is their basis;
rather, [that substrate] such as <s>jāti</s> (genus) and so forth which possesses the abundance [of common properties] is perceived as similar. // Msv 5.6.21 //

children.text:
dravyasādṛśyaṃ samālaṅkāradhāriṇorloke, vede ca "lohitopṇīṣā ṛtvija' pracarantīti" /
kriyāsādṛśyamadhyayanādisāmānyālloke, vede ca yajñavihaṅgamayornipatyādānasāmānyāt /
evaṃ hyāha---"yathā vai śyeno nipatyādatte, evamayaṃ dviṣantaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ nipatyādatte"iti /
śaktisādṛśyaṃ tu bhīmo malla iti loke, vede ca somapūtīkayo' /
avagamyate hi pūtīkānāṃ sāmaśaktirarthavādāt /
tatkāryatvenāvagamāt /
kāryasya cakāraṇānuvidhāyiśaktikatvāt /
uktaṃ ca---"somasya yoṃ'śa' parāpatat sa pūtīko 'bhavad" iti /
children.translated_text: And it is stated: 'That portion of <s>Soma</s> which fell aside became <s>pūtīka</s>.'

children.text: svadharmasādṛśyaṃ kecit triśikhā' kecit pañcaśikhā iti loke triśikhādīnāmanyonyasādṛśyaṃ, vede ca vasiṣṭhātryādīnāṃ narāśaṃso dvitīya' prayāja iti /
children.translated_text: Similarity of specific properties (<s>svadharma</s>): in the world, 'some have three tufts, some have five tufts' — the mutual similarity of those with three tufts and so forth; and in the <s>Veda</s>, of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Atri</s>, and the like — 'the <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> is the second <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary oblation).'

children.text: dharmaniyama eva hi tatra sādṛśyam, prakṛtivikṛtikarmaṇośca dharmasāmānyameva sādṛśyamityuktameva /
children.translated_text: For the restriction of properties itself is the resemblance there; and between the primary (<s>prakṛti</s>) and modified (<s>vikṛti</s>) rituals, the commonality of properties itself has been stated to be the resemblance.

children.text: ete ca jātyādaya ekaikaśo dviśastriśa' samastaśaśca samānā bhavanta' sādṛśyasya vicitratāmāpādayantīti ||20||
children.translated_text: And these — <s>jāti</s> and so forth — being similar singly, in twos, in threes, and all together, produce the variety of resemblance. //20//

Similarity of substance (<s>dravya</s>): in the world, [between] those wearing similar ornaments; and in the <s>Veda</s>: 'the priests go about with red turbans.' Similarity of action (<s>kriyā</s>): in the world, from the commonality of studying and so forth; and in the <s>Veda</s>, from the commonality of swooping-and-seizing between the sacrifice and a bird of prey. For thus it says: 'Just as a hawk, swooping down, seizes [its prey], so this one, swooping down, seizes the hostile rival.' Similarity of capacity (<s>śakti</s>): in the world, '<s>Bhīma</s> is a wrestler'; and in the <s>Veda</s>, [the similarity] between <s>Soma</s> and <s>pūtīka</s>. For the capacity of the <s>pūtīkas</s> for intoxication is understood from the <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage), from its being understood as an effect of that [capacity], and because the effect conforms to the capacity of its cause.

children.text:
nanu yatra sādṛśyaṃ samavaiti tatsadṛśabuddhyā gṛhyate /
yadi cāvayavasāmānyāni sādṛśyaṃ, tāni tarhyavayaveṣu samavayantīti teṣveva sadṛśadhiyaṃ janayeyu' /
atha teṣāṃ bhūyasastā, sā cāvayavasāmānyeṣviti tānyeva sadṛśāni syu' /
kathaṃ jātyantare sadṛśabuddhirata āha---na dharmā iti /
satyam /
ata eva hetorna dhmākhyāvayavasāmānyāni tadabhūyastā vā sādṛśyaṃ, teṣu sādṛsyabuddhyanutpatte' /
yadeva hi teṣāṃ bhūyastayā yuktaṃ jātyantaraṃ gavayādi vyaktyantaraṃ vāgneyasauryādi, tadeva sadṛśabuddhyā gṛhyate /

children.translated_text: Therefore, the inhering of those [part-universals] in a different genus itself is the resemblance.
But in their own nature, individually, those universals are the basis of a cognition of unity alone, like the principal universal (<s>pradhānasāmānya</s>).

children.text: piṇḍitāni tu jātyantarasamavāyopahitāni sādṛśyam, ayaṃ ca bhūyo 'vayavasāmānyetyasyaiva /
children.translated_text: When collected together, however, [and] endowed with [the fact of] inhering in a different genus, they constitute the resemblance. And this is merely an elaboration of 'the abundance of part-universals.'

Objection: Wherever resemblance inheres, that is grasped by the cognition of similarity. If the part-universals are the resemblance, then since they inhere in the parts, they should generate the cognition of similarity in those [parts] alone. Or if their abundance [is the resemblance], and that [abundance] resides in the part-universals, then those alone should be similar. How then is there a cognition of similarity in a different genus (<s>jāti</s>)? Therefore he says — 'na dharmā' (not the properties). True. For this very reason — the properties called part-universals, or their abundance, are not the resemblance, since no cognition of similarity arises regarding them. Rather, whatever different genus such as <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) etc., or different individual such as <s>āgneya</s>, <s>saurya</s>, etc., is endowed with the abundance of those [part-universals] — that alone is grasped by the cognition of similarity.
How then [do you account for] the [similarity] of twins? Since it is observed, what is being stated here?
For this [resemblance] is sometimes [based on] an abundance [of common properties], sometimes also on a paucity. // Msv 5.6.22 //
The reality of that [resemblance] is not diminished by this degree of difference;
and these universals are not perishable through the destruction of their substrates. // Msv 5.6.23 //
And because of the connection with infinite substrates, destruction does not occur elsewhere;

children.text: tena sarvaṃ na sāmānyaṃ nityatvena prakalpyate // Msv_5,6.24 //
children.translated_text: therefore, not every universal is to be postulated as eternal. // Msv 5.6.24 //

children.text:
atra codayati--- yamayoriti /
jātyantarasyeti yāvacchrutagrāhiṇa' paricodanamidam--- yadi jātyantarasya bhūyo 'vayavasāmānyayogata' sādṛśyaṃ kataṃ yamayorvyaktisādṛśyamiti /
itarastu--- pradarśanamātraṃ jātyantasyeti keyamatraivāsthā, tadayamarbhako barāka ityapahasati--- dṛṣṭatvāditi /
yatraivaṃ sādṛśyaṃ dṛśyate jātau vyaktau vā, tatraiva tadāśrayaṇīyam /
kimekatraivālasthāṃ badhnāsīti /
syādetat /
ekasvabhāvā hi bhāvā jātyādaya' /

children.translated_text: So this resemblance too should be of a single nature accordingly.

children.text: yadi tāvadalpavṛttisvabhāvaṃ vyaktyoreva yuktam, atha bahuvṛttisvabhāvaṃ tato jātyoreva /
children.translated_text: If its nature is of limited occurrence, it would be appropriate only between [two] individuals; if its nature is of extensive occurrence, then only between [two] genera.
But a half-and-half [nature] would lead to unreality. Therefore he says — 'kvacit' (sometimes).
The purport is: since both [cases] are tenable because observation is not contradicted. //22//

Here he raises an objection — 'of twins.' This is a challenge by the literal-minded, as far as [the case of] a different genus: 'If the resemblance of a different genus is produced by the connection of abundant part-universals, how [do you explain] the similarity of individual twins?' The other [interpretation], however — 'the mention of a different genus was merely illustrative' — [the objector] dismisses this young child [of an argument] with: 'Since it is observed.' Wherever resemblance is observed — whether in a genus or an individual — there alone it should be accepted. Why do you fixate on one [explanation] alone? One might object: entities such as <s>jāti</s> and so forth have a single nature.

children.text: nanu sāmānyāni sādṛśyaṃ, tāni ca vyaktināśena naśyeyu' /
children.translated_text: Objection: If universals are the resemblance, they would perish with the destruction of individuals.
Therefore, [the doctrine that] the universal is eternal would be undermined. Hence he says — 'sāmānyāni' (universals).

children.text: etāni tāvannāśīni bhavantu , sāmānyāntarāṇi gotvādīni nityānyeveti na kaścillokavirodha
children.translated_text: Let these [part-universals] be perishable; the other universals such as <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness) and so forth are eternal — thus there is no contradiction with the world.

children.text:
ka' puna' sāmānyāntareṣu viśeṣa',ata āha---ananteti /
ananto hi gotvādīnāmāśraya' /
tadekasya nāśe 'pyāśrayāntare pratyabhijñānānnaikāntiko nāśa iti /
nityasāmānyavādo 'pi na na' sārvatrika ityāha---teneti /
children.translated_text: But what is the distinction in the case of the other universals? Therefore he says — 'ananta' (infinite). For the substrate of <s>gotva</s> and so forth is infinite. Therefore, even when one [substrate] perishes, because of recognition in other substrates, the destruction is not absolute. He says the doctrine of eternal universals is not universal for us either — 'tena' (therefore).
Or the destruction of a universal is nowhere admitted;
for every [universal] has some substrate in another place and so forth. // Msv 5.6.25 //
If the resemblance is surpassed by the abundance of those [part-universals],

children.text: tāni vyastāni santyevaṃ pratyakṣe 'pi kvacit kvacit // Msv_5,6.26 //
children.translated_text: those [universals], taken separately, do indeed exist here and there even in [the domain of] perception. // Msv 5.6.26 //
But where the [property of] being a part of a similar [thing] is perceived —
that too, for the parts, would be [due to] having similar sub-parts. // Msv 5.6.27 //
Thus, since there is no postulation of difference from another up to this point,

children.text: tata' paraṃ tu sāmānyaṃ bhavet sādṛśyavarjitam // Msv_5,6.28 //
children.translated_text: beyond that, however, there would be a universal devoid of resemblance. // Msv 5.6.28 //
But where a single universal of the principal [entities] is perceived —
or alternatively, he says that even the part-universals do not undergo absolute destruction — 'sāmānyasya' (of the universal).
He states the reason — 'sarvasya' (of every). //25//
If [a substrate] exists there too, there must be a cognition of similarity. Therefore he says — 'teṣām' (of those).

children.text: bhūyastayā teṣāṃ sāhaśyamatiriktaṃ bhavati, na tvekaikaśo na santīti /
children.translated_text: The resemblance surpasses by the abundance of those; but individually they are not non-existent.
Not only is the universal not without a substrate — the existence of a substrate in another place and so forth is postulated.

children.text: api tu pratyakṣe 'pi kvacidarthe tānyupalabhyanta evetyāha---tānīti ||26||
children.translated_text: Moreover, even in the domain of perception, in some objects, those [universals] are indeed perceived — he says — 'tāni' (those). //26//

children.text:
nanvakṣyādīnāṃ svāvayavasāmānyabhūmnā sābaśyamuktaṃ, tadavayavānāṃ tu kathaṃ sāhaśyaṃ bhaviṣyatyata āha---anyatheti /
dvedhā hyanupapannam--- kiñcidanupapannameva yanna kathañcidupapādayituṃ śakyam, kiñciccāsati kalpane 'nupapannam /
tatra yadekāntamanupapannaṃ tadupekṣyata eva /
yattu kalpite ksmiṃścidupapadyate anyathā nopapadyate tadupapattiranyakalpamanayāvasīyate /
evameva hi sarvalaukikaparīkṣakā budhyante /
na ca viparyayo deśāntarādiṣu dṛṣṭa' /
ata' pramāṇamevedam /
yathā cānumāne niścitarūpaṃ liṅgaṃ gamakam, evamihāpi kenacitpramāṇenāvagataṃ pramāṇāntareṇotthāpitavitarkamam /
na cātrānyataratrāpi prāmāṇye saṃśaya', kintu niścitaprāmāṇyoreva dvayo' samarthanāpekṣāmātraṃ kathamidamubhayamupapadyatāmiti /
ṣoḍaśina iva grahaṇāgrahamasāstrayo' /
na tatraikaparityāgenetaradupapādayituṃ śakyate /
ato yathā tatra kathamidamubhayamupapadyatāmityapekṣite prayogabhedenobhayamupapādyate, evamihāpi pramāṇapratipannamubhayaṃ niścitasadbhāvamarthāntaraparikalpanayā sama
children.translated_text: Objection: The resemblance of eyes and so forth was stated [to be] due to the abundance of their own part-universals. But how will there be resemblance for the parts of those [parts]? Therefore he says — 'anyathā' (otherwise). For there are two types of impossibility: something that is absolutely impossible and cannot be explained in any way, and something that is impossible only in the absence of a postulate. In the former case, what is absolutely impossible is simply disregarded. But when something can be explained by one postulate and cannot be explained otherwise, then the explanation requires acceptance of that alternative postulate. For this is exactly how all worldly people and critical examiners understand things. And no contrary [instance] is observed in other places and so forth. Therefore this itself is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge). And just as in inference, a sign (<s>liṅga</s>) of ascertained form is probative, so too here, what is ascertained by one <s>pramāṇa</s> is not to be overturned by doubt raised by another <s>pramāṇa</s>. And here there is no doubt regarding the validity of either [pramāṇa]; rather, both being of ascertained validity, there is merely the need for reconciliation — 'how can both be explained?' — like the grasping or non-grasping of the sixteenth [cup] according to [different] <s>śāstra</s> [traditions]. One cannot establish one by abandoning the other there. Therefore, just as there, when reconciliation is sought, both are explained through a difference in application — so too here, both [facts], being established by <s>pramāṇa</s> and of ascertained existence, are reconciled through the postulation of another entity.
... Msv 5.6.29cd - Msv 5.7.29cd missing!
And the invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāvitā</s>) here is postulated only at that point;
it was not ascertained before; therefore, otherwise [understood], this is not a cause [of inference]. // Msv 5.7.30 //
The absence from the house and the being outside are not necessarily observed together;

children.text: sāhitye tu pramāṇaṃ ca tayoranyanna vidyate // Msv_5,7.31 //
children.translated_text: and for their co-occurrence, there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> other [than <s>arthāpatti</s>]. // Msv 5.7.31 //
For it is precisely through the impossibility of [explaining it] otherwise that one thing is understood from another;

children.text: tathā na kalpyate taccet sāhityaṃ na pratīyate // Msv_5,7.32 //
children.translated_text: if that [relation] were not so postulated, the co-occurrence would not be understood. // Msv 5.7.32 //

children.text:
arthyate /
tādrūpyeṇaiva pratibhānāt /
vilakṣaṇāni hi pramāṇāni vilakṣaṇasāmagrīkāṇi /
ata eva parasparato bhidyante /
aprāmāṇyakāraṇāni ca saṃśayaviparyayāvajñānaṃ vā, taccārthāpattāvapi nāstīti kathamapramāṇatā /
children.translated_text: And the causes of non-validity are doubt, error, or ignorance — and none of these exists in <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) either. So how can it be non-valid?
If [one asks]: how can there be a valid cognition from an unknown relation?

children.text: na sambandha' prāmāṇye kāraṇam, api tu bādhaviraha' /
children.translated_text: The relation is not the cause of validity; rather, the absence of sublation [is]. And that [absence of sublation] is equally present here too.

children.text: sa cehāpyaviśiṣṭa iti na kaścid doṣor'thāpattāvasmākaṃ pratibhātīti ||29||
children.translated_text: Therefore no fault in <s>arthāpatti</s> appears to us. //29//

[This is] understood. Because of its appearing in just that form. For the <s>pramāṇas</s> are of distinct forms and have distinct conditions of operation. For this very reason they differ from one another.

children.text: nanu gṛhābhāvo nāntareṇa bahirbhāvamupapadyate ato nāntarīyaka', nāntarīyakācca yadarthāntarajñānaṃ tadanumānam, ato 'numānamevedaṃ bahirbhāvajñānamata āha----avineti /
children.translated_text: Objection: The absence from the house cannot be explained without the being outside; therefore it is an invariable concomitant (<s>nāntarīyaka</s>). And the knowledge of a different thing from an invariable concomitant is inference (<s>anumāna</s>). Therefore this knowledge of the being outside is inference alone. Hence he says — 'avina' (invariable concomitance).

children.text: ayamabhiprāya'--- nāntarīyakārthadarśanaṃ tadvido 'numānamiti kecit paṭhanti, teṣāmapi tadvido nāntarīyakatāvida eva nāntarīyakadarśanamanumānamabhipretam, na ceha nāntareṇa bahirbhāvaṃ gṛhābhāvo bhavatīti prāgavagatam, tadaiva hyarthāpattyā bahirbhāvaṃ parikalpyāyamanena vinā na bhavatītyavinābhāvitā kalpyate /
children.translated_text: This is the purport: some read 'the seeing of that which is invariably concomitant, by one who knows it, is inference.' Even for those [who read thus], what is intended [by them as] 'inference' is the seeing of the invariable concomitance by one who knows the invariable concomitance [already]. But here, the [fact] that 'the absence from the house does not occur without the being outside' was not previously ascertained. For it is precisely through <s>arthāpatti</s> that, having postulated the being outside, [the understanding arises that] 'this [absence] does not occur without that' — thus the invariable concomitance is postulated [only then].

children.text: ata' sā svarūpasatyapi na pūrvamavagateti na jñānotpattau kāraṇamiti ||30||
children.translated_text: Therefore, that [invariable concomitance], even though it exists in its own nature, was not previously ascertained — hence it is not a cause in the production of knowledge. //30//

children.text:
nanvavagatasambandhasya tarhyanumānaṃ syādata āha---gṛhābhāvetitāntena /
na tāvadanniyamena sarvaireva dvayo' sāhityamavagatam, aviditasāhityasya tāvat siddhaṃ pramāṇāntaramityabhiprāya' /
yenāpi tayo' sāhityamavagataṃ tasyāpi
nāgṛhītayostayo' sāhityagraha' sambhavati, na ca tayorekagrahaṇe 'paradarśanamarthāpattyā vinā sambhavati /
anyathānupapapattyaiva tvekena gṛhābhāvena
children.translated_text: Objection: Then for one who has ascertained the relation, there would be inference. Therefore he says — 'gṛhābhāve' (in the absence from the house) etc. To begin with, not all [people] have necessarily ascertained the co-occurrence of the two. For one who has not known the co-occurrence, it is established that this is a different <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is the purport. And even for one who has ascertained their co-occurrence, the grasping of their co-occurrence is not possible without the two being grasped [individually]. And when one of the two is grasped, the cognition of the other is not possible without <s>arthāpatti</s>. By the impossibility of [explaining it] otherwise alone, by one [thing] — namely the absence from the house —
at the time of the [ascertainment of the] relation, one of the two relata is certainly
to be understood through <s>arthāpatti</s>; afterwards, however, there is the nature of inference. // Msv 5.7.33 //
But one who, standing at the door of the house, would postulate the being outside —

children.text: yadaikasminnayaṃ deśe na tadānyatra vidyate // Msv_5,7.34 //
children.translated_text: when this [person] is in one place, he is not at that time found in another. // Msv 5.7.34 //
Even then, the non-existence [in the house] is not cognized everywhere;
and from the non-existence in one place, there will be no pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) of the reason. // Msv 5.7.35 //
Objection: The non-existence here is cognized from non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>);
and since that [non-apprehension] is accomplished without effort, it applies only to one who is present [in that place]. // Msv 5.7.36 //
or, one of the two is to be cognized as being outside—

children.text: evaṃ cākalpymāne 'nyatarasya sambnadhino 'gṛhītatvāt sāhityapratītireva na syāt, ata' sāhityārthamarthāpattirarthanīyeti siddhaṃ pramāṇāntaramityabhiprāyeṇāha--- pramāṇaṃ ceti pratīyate 'ntena /
children.translated_text: And when thus not being imagined, since one of the two relata has not been grasped, the cognition of co-presence itself would not arise. Therefore, <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is to be resorted to for the purpose of [establishing] co-presence—thus it is established that it is an independent <s>pramāṇa</s>—with this purport he says—'pramāṇaṃ ca' etc., which is understood through the end [of the verse].
He elaborates the purport—'tena' etc. // 31-32 //

children.text:
nanu ca nāvaśyamarthāpattyaivānyatara' sambandhī grahītavya', śakyate hi gṛhadvārāvasthitenābhāvapratyakṣābhyāmubhayaṃ viditvā sambandho 'nubhavitum, tathā viditasambandhācca gṛhābhāvād bahirbhāvānumānamityāśaṅkate tāvat--- gṛhadvārīti ||34 ||atrottaramāha--- tadāpīti /
ayamabhiprāya'--- sidhyatyevaṃ gṛhābhāvād bahirbhāvānumānam, na punarevameva sarveṣāmavagati', agṛhītasambandhānāmapi pratītibhāvāt /
eṣo 'pi ca prakāro naikatra bhāvena sarvatrābhāvāvagame sambhavati, na hi jagadabhāvenaikatra bhāvo 'nvita' śakyo 'vagantum /
jagadabhāvasya pratyetuśakyatvādityabhiprāya' /
nanvevaṃ tadāvagataṃ yadāyamekatra bhavati tadā paratra tatsamīpe na bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But in this way, this much is cognized: 'when this person is in one place, then he is not in another place nearby'—
And thus, when the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is known, from the presence in one place, the inference of absence everywhere will follow.
Therefore he says—'na ca' etc.
For the <s>vyāpti</s> of the reason with the absence in all three worlds is not established merely by the non-existence in one place. // 35 //

Objection: But it is not necessarily the case that one of the relata must be grasped through <s>arthāpatti</s> alone. For it is possible for one standing at the door of a house, having known both through the perception of absence, to experience the relation. And from the relation thus known, the inference of being outside from the absence in the house [would follow]—he first raises this doubt—'gṛhadvārī' etc. // 34 // Here he gives the reply—'tadāpi' etc. The purport is as follows: the inference of being outside from the absence in the house is indeed established in this way, but not everyone cognizes in this way alone, since cognition occurs even for those who have not grasped the relation. And this method too is not possible where the absence everywhere is to be cognized through the presence in one place. For one cannot cognize the presence in one place as concomitant with the absence in the entire world. Because the absence in the entire world cannot be perceived—such is the purport.

children.text: kiṃpunarjagadabhāvena sambandho nāvagamyate, tasyānavagateriti ced, nanvanupalabdhirabhāvāvagame kāraṇam, yathā caikatra san devadatto deśāntare
children.translated_text: Objection: Why then is the relation with the absence in the entire world not cognized? If [you say] because of the non-cognition of that—well, is not non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) the cause of the cognition of absence? Just as when <s>Caitra</s>, being in one place,
the real absence of a thing is not cognized here through this non-apprehension;

children.text: taddeśāgamanāt sā hi dūrastheṣvasti satsvapi // Msv_5,7.37 //
children.translated_text: for that [non-apprehension] exists even when things that are far away are present, because of not having gone to that place. // Msv_5,7.37 //

children.text: gatvā gatvā tu tān deśān yadyartho nopalabhyate /
children.translated_text: But having gone and gone to those places, if the object is not apprehended,
then, due to the absence of another cause, it is cognized as non-existent. // Msv_5,7.38 //
Objection: But even in the absence of fire and such, of those that are distinct from smoke and such,

children.text: taddeśāgamanāt spaṣṭo vyatireko na sidhyati // Msv_5,7.39 //
children.translated_text: the <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) is not clearly established because of not having gone to that place. // Msv_5,7.39 //

children.text:
'nupalabhyamāno nāstīti niścīyate /
evamekatra san sarvatra nopalabhyata iti sarvatraiva nāstīti śakyamavagantum /

na hi darśanavadadarśanamapi prayatnamapekṣate, darśanaṃ hi kāryaṃ svakāraṇarthendriyasannikarṣādyapekṣamāṇamekatra sato na sarvatra sambhavati, darśanābhāvastu na kiñcidapekṣata iti codayati---nanvatreti /
children.translated_text: For non-seeing does not require effort like seeing does. For seeing, being an effect, depends on the contact of the sense organ with its own cause and object, and hence the seeing of what is in one place is not possible everywhere. But the absence of seeing does not depend on anything—thus he raises the objection—'nanu atra' etc.
'Atra' refers to one particular place.
In this one particular place, non-existence is cognized from non-apprehension.
And that is the same everywhere as well. // 36 //
[A thing] not being apprehended is ascertained as non-existent. Thus, something being in one place and not being apprehended everywhere—it can be cognized as non-existent everywhere.
Here he gives the refutation—'na etayā' etc.

children.text: kimiti na pratīyate ata āha--- taddeśeti /
children.translated_text: Why is it not cognized? Therefore he says—'taddeśa' etc.

children.text: upalabdhiyogyasya hyanupalabdhirabhāvaṃ vyavasthāpayati, dūrastheṣu tvayogyatvādeva satsvapyanupalabdhi' sambhavatīti nābhāvaniścaya iti ||37||
children.translated_text: For the non-apprehension of what is fit to be apprehended establishes its absence. But in the case of things far away, since they are unfit [to be apprehended], non-apprehension is possible even when they exist—hence there is no ascertainment of absence. // 37 //

children.text: yaditu sarvagrāmanagarasaritkāntārādideśā' prāptā' bhaveyu', evaṃ caitrasya teṣvabhāva' śakyāvagama', na cedaṃ śakyakaraṇamityabhiprāyeṇāha---gatvā gatveti ||38||
children.translated_text: If, however, all the places—villages, cities, rivers, forests, and so on—were reached, then the absence of <s>Caitra</s> in them could be cognized. But this is impossible to carry out—with this purport he says—'gatvā gatvā' etc. // 38 //

children.text: ayamabhiprāya'--- na tāvad vipakṣādavyāvṛtto heturgamaka', na ca sarve vipakṣā gatvopalabdhuṃ śakyante, ato 'vaśyamekadeśasthasyaivānupalabdhyā vipakṣād hetorvyatireko grahītavya' /
children.translated_text: The purport is as follows: a reason that is not excluded from the counter-positive (<s>vipakṣa</s>) is not probative. And not all counter-positives can be reached and observed. Therefore, the <s>vyatireka</s> (exclusion) of the reason from the counter-positive must necessarily be grasped through non-apprehension in one place alone.
It will be the same here too.
'Smoke and such' are those that are distinct [from fire], and 'those distinct from smoke and such' [means those that deviate when fire etc. are absent].

children.text: agnyādyabhāve ye vyatirekiṇo dhūmādayasteṣāmagnyādyabhāvadeśāgamanād vyatireko na sidhyatīti ||39||
children.translated_text: The <s>vyatireka</s> of smoke and such, which are absent when fire and such are absent, is not established because of not having gone to the places where fire and such are absent. // 39 //
Here he raises an objection—'nanu ca' etc.
For one whose object of proof is the absence of another real entity, that [argument] is flawed;
but for me, what is merely unseen, being a companion, is probative. // Msv_5,7.40 //
Objection: But in that case too, the relation through non-apprehension—
is justified because the being of <s>Caitra</s>'s absence has been observed. // Msv_5,7.41 //
Because of the limited extent of the co-presence of fire and smoke, which is well known,
and because of the non-observation of <s>vyatireka</s>, the probative power is established. // Msv_5,7.42 //

children.text:
pariharati---yasyeti /
vyatirakepradhānavādino hi bauddhasyāsati vipakṣād vyatirekagrahaṇe na heturgamako bhavati, vastvantarābhāvo hi tasya prameya', agnyādervastuno /
anyasyānagnyāderabhāva iti yāvat /
sa hi sarvānagnivyatirekamantareṇa na sambhavati, mama tu sahacāriṇo heturgamaka', anvayamātraniyamena /
