sa ca vipakṣādarśanamātreṇa dvitraireva darśanai' sidhyatīti ||40 ||nanvanvayavādino 'pyajātātivṛttakapratyutpannānantadeśavartivahnisahacaritadhūmadarśanaṃ durlabhameva /
atha katipayāgnisāhityadarśanādevāsahitāvagatā api vahnayo 'numīyante, evaṃ tarhīhāpi caitrābhāvasya jagadavartina ekadeśabhāvena sambandha upapadyata eva /
children.translated_text: If, however, from the seeing of co-presence with just a few fires, fires that are not seen to be accompanied [by smoke] are also inferred—then here too, the relation of <s>Caitra</s>'s absence, which pervades the world, through the presence in one place, is indeed justified.

children.text: atrāpi hyekatra caitre bhavati katipayeṣu tadabhāvo dṛṣṭa eva, tāvatā ca sarvatrābhāvo 'vumāsyata ityāha--- nanvevamiti ||41||
children.translated_text: For here too, when <s>Caitra</s> is in one place, his absence in a few [other places] has indeed been observed, and from that much, his absence everywhere would be inferred—thus he says—'nanu evam' etc. // 41 //

He refutes—'yasya' etc. For the Buddhist, who prioritizes <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance), when the <s>vyatireka</s> from the counter-positive is not grasped, the reason is not probative. For what is to be proved for him is the absence of another real entity—of fire and such real things. 'Of another'—meaning of what is not fire and such—'the absence'—thus far [is the meaning]. For that [absence] is not possible without the exclusion from all non-fire [instances]. But for me, a companion reason is probative through the restriction of positive concomitance alone. And that is established by merely not seeing [it] in the counter-positive, through just two or three observations. // 40 // Objection: But even for the proponent of <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance), the seeing of smoke accompanied by fire in infinite places—past, future, and present—is indeed difficult to obtain.

children.text:
atra parihāramāha---sāhityaiti /
ayamabhiprāya'--- na hi no vyaktiviṣayamanumānam, api tarhyākṛtiviṣayam, ākṛtyośca prativyaktikṛtsnasamavāyātsulabhameva sāhityadarśanam, sakṛddarśanenaiva hyākṛtyo' sāhityamavagamyate /
ata eva dvitrādidarśanamapi vyabhicārāśaṅkāyāṃ niyamārthamabhyarthyate /
avagate hi sāhitye bhavati śaṅkā--- kimayamaupādhika' saṃsargo dhūmasyāgninā saha āhosvit sahaja eveti, tatrāsakṛddarśane 'nvayāvyabhicārādupādhyantarapraveśakāraṇābhāvātsvābhāviko 'syāgninānvaya iti bhavati mati' /
agnestu prathamamavagatasambandhasyāpi dhūmena darśanāntare vyabhicāradarśanādārdrendhanādirupādhiranupraviśati /
naca deśādibhede vyabhicārā śaṅkā, sakṛddarśanāvadhāritasāhacaryayorhi dvayorapyagnestāvad vyabhicāro dṛṣṭo
children.translated_text: Here he gives the refutation—'sāhitya' etc. The purport is as follows: our inference does not have individuals as its object, but rather universals (<s>ākṛti</s>) as its object. And since the universal is completely inherent in each individual, the observation of co-presence is easily obtained. For through a single observation, the co-presence of the universals is cognized. For this very reason, even the two or three additional observations are sought for the purpose of establishing invariability when there is a suspicion of deviation. For when co-presence is cognized, the doubt arises: 'Is this association of smoke with fire conditional (<s>aupādhika</s>) or innate (<s>sahaja</s>)?' There, from repeated observation, due to the non-deviation of positive concomitance and the absence of any cause for the entry of another condition, the thought arises: 'This positive concomitance with fire is its natural property.' But even for one who has first cognized the relation of fire [with smoke], upon observing deviation in a subsequent observation, a condition such as wet fuel and the like enters. And there is no suspicion of deviation in different places and the like. For of two things whose companionship has been ascertained through a single observation, deviation of fire has indeed been seen—
here, this is indeed the co-presence of one companion;
because of existing in infinite places, it cannot be established for now. // Msv_5,7.43 //
Objection: But is not another place cognized as empty of <s>Caitra</s> in this way?
Because of being different from the place [occupied by Caitra], like the nearby place. // Msv_5,7.44 //
The non-deviating and non-contradictory nature is understood in exactly the same way;
because of being different from the nearby place, like the place occupied by <s>Caitra</s>. // Msv_5,7.45 //
But the complete apprehension of a person in one place—

children.text:
dvitrādidarśanenaiva,tad yadidhūmo 'pyagniṃ vyabhicaret, asyāpi hi dvitricaturaireva darśanairvyabhicāro dṛśyeta, na ca dṛśyate /
ato 'gnyanvitasvabhāvo 'yamiti niścīyate /
yasya tvevamapyanāśvāsa' /
tasya sarvapramāṇeṣveva kvacid vyabhicāradarśanādanāśvāsa' syāt /
vipakṣavyatireko 'pi caivamarthādeva siddho bhavati /
sa hi prathamamanvicchato vipakṣadeśānāmanantatvād durlabho bhavati /
svabhāvaniyame tu jñāte svabhāvasyāvyabhicārāt sulabho vyatireka' /
children.translated_text: But when the natural restriction is known, the <s>vyatireka</s> is easily obtained because of the non-deviation of the natural property.

children.text: na hi svābhāvikamuṣṇatvamantareṇa kvacit kadācidagnirbhavatīti kaścidāśaṅkate /
children.translated_text: For no one suspects that fire ever exists anywhere without its natural heat.
'Mitadeśatvāt' (because of limited extent)—
means 'because of being of limited extent.' // 42 //

through just two or three observations—this [applies]: if smoke too were to deviate from fire, its deviation too would be seen through just two, three, or four observations—but it is not seen. Therefore it is ascertained: 'This [smoke] has fire-accompaniment as its nature.' But for one who even so has no confidence, there would be no confidence in any <s>pramāṇa</s> at all, since deviation is seen somewhere in every [pramāṇa]. And the <s>vyatireka</s> from the counter-positive too is established precisely in this indirect manner. For that [vyatireka], when first sought, is difficult to obtain because of the infinitude of counter-positive loci.
But in the case of presence-in-one-place and absence-in-the-world, the cognition of co-presence does not arise in this way—thus he says—'iha' etc.

children.text: eko hyatra sarvatrābhāva' sahabhāvayanantadeśavartī, na tvagnidhūmākṛtivat parimitadeśa', ato 'tra durgrahaṃ sāhityamiti ||43||
children.translated_text: For here, one of the two—the absence everywhere—is a companion that exists in infinite places, and is not of limited extent like the universals of fire and smoke. Therefore, the co-presence is difficult to grasp here. // 43 //
Here he raises an objection—'nanu' etc.
The absence of <s>Caitra</s> in another place is cognized through inference.
For one would infer thus:
'All unseen lands are connected with the absence of <s>Caitra</s>, because they are different from the place occupied by him, like the nearby place'—// 44 //
He refutes—'viruddha' etc.
How is the non-deviating and non-contradictory nature [established]? Therefore he says—'tadvat' etc.
'Tadvat'—like <s>Caitra</s>, another place—
therefore, the absence everywhere is to be cognized through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) alone; there is no other way. // 45 //

children.text: tathātu taṃ gṛhītvāsāhityagrahaṇapura' saraṃ yadyanumānamiṣyate tadarthāpattipūrvakam, etāvatā ca siddhamarthāpatte' prāmāṇyamityabhiprāyeṇāha--- puruṣa
children.translated_text: Moreover, having grasped him, before the grasping of co-presence, if inference is desired for that purpose, it is preceded by <s>arthāpatti</s>. And by this much, the validity of <s>arthāpatti</s> as a <s>pramāṇa</s> is established—with this purport he says—'puruṣa'—

children.text: tasyānyathā na siddhi' syādityanyeṣvasya nāstitā // Msv_5,7.46 //
children.translated_text: there would be no establishment of that otherwise—hence its non-existence in others. // Msv_5,7.46 //
Therefore, the being-preceded-by-<s>arthāpatti</s>, here and in whatever cause—
from the observation of the effect, the existence of the capacity is cognized. // Msv_5,7.47 //

children.text:
syetyatrāntena /
yastu vadati--- svātmanastāvadekatra sata' sarvatrābhāvena sambandho dṛṣṭa' ato 'nyasyāpyanuminotīti /
sa vaktavya' svātmana eva sarvatrāsattā kathamavagamyate, yadyabhāvena, kasyeti vaktavyam, na tāvatpratyakṣasya nivṛttyā dūradeśeṣvabhāva' śakyate 'vagantum, dūratvādeva teṣāmanupalabdhiyogyatvānna svātmano 'bhāvasteṣu śakyate 'vagantum /
atha tatra sato dūrasthatvameva na syāt, ata' sahaiva deśāntare svaśarīramupalabdhiyogyaṃ bhavati, yogyatvāccopalabhyet, yo hi yatra bhavati tasya sahaivādhāreṇātmopalabdhiyogyo bhavati, na ceha tathā, ato na deśāntareṣavastīti /
evaṃ cānumānena deśāntarābhāvo grahītavya' /
na pratyakṣābhāvena /
tatra ca viruddhāvyabhicāritoktaiva--- deśāntarāṇi vimatipadāni caitravanti caitravaddeśasamīpavyatiriktadeśatvāccaitravaddeśavaditi /
yatra ca pratihetunā sandeha' kriyate tatra balavatānyena sarvatrābhāvena samartham /
sā hyevaṃ pravartate, yadetadekatra kārtsnyena caitrasyopalambhanaṃ tannopapadyate, yadi deśāntare caitro bhavet, dvedhā hi bhāvā' prādeśikā vibhavaśca, vibhavo 'pi dvedhā, sarvavyāpina' svāśrayavyāpinaśca /
pūrve gaganādaya' /
uttare jātyādaya' /
yaddhi sarvasaṃyogibhiranāgatairagataṃ sambadhyate, tadvibhutayā prasiddham, tayā cātmākāśādaya iti vibhava ityucyante /
na tāvadākāśavaccaitra', ekatra parisamāpto hi parimaṇḍala' so 'vagamyate /
na ca yathāvayavī svāvayaveṣu vartate tathā deśāntare vartitumarhati /
yadi hi tasyānyatra bhāgā' bhaveyu' iha kṛtsno nopalabhyeta /
bhavanvāntarāle vicchedādanyo bhavet /
na ca jātivad vartitumarhati /
jātirhyamūrtā, saikatra nahīdaṃ sāmānyam /
saṃyogo 'sya deśāntareṇa sambandha' /
sa ca nāgatasya sambhavati /
gatvā hyavaṃ deśāntarai' saṃyujyamāno dṛśyate /
ata eva na vibhu' /
children.translated_text: —by 'sya' in this [compound ending]. But one who argues: 'First, [the individual] being present in one place, its absence everywhere else is observed as the relation, and therefore one infers [the absence] of another [individual] as well' — to him it must be said: How is the non-existence of the individual itself everywhere ascertained? If by absence [of perception] — of what? It cannot be said that the absence in distant places is ascertained by the cessation of perception, for since those [places] are too far for perception, the absence of the individual there cannot be ascertained. Or rather, if existing there, being far away itself would not be possible; hence, simultaneously with being in another place, one's own body would become perceivable, and being perceivable, it would be perceived — for whatever exists somewhere, together with its substratum, is perceivable by its very self, and this is not the case here; therefore, the thing does not exist in other places. Thus, absence in other places must be grasped by inference, not by the absence of perception. And there, the [inference] is stated as having an undeviating contrary [reason]: 'Other places are the objects of doubt; they contain <s>Caitra</s> — because they are places other than those near <s>Caitra</s>'s place, like <s>Caitra</s>'s own place.' And where a counter-reason creates doubt, a stronger [reason] is capable [of establishing] the absence everywhere by overpowering it. For it operates thus: This complete perception of <s>Caitra</s> in one place is not possible if <s>Caitra</s> were to exist in another place — for entities are of two kinds: localized (<s>prādeśika</s>) and all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>), and the all-pervading is also of two kinds: those pervading everything and those pervading their own substratum. The former are space (<s>gagana</s>) and the like. The latter are universals (<s>jāti</s>) and the like. For that which is connected with all conjuncts, past and future, is known as [having] all-pervasiveness, and by that [pervasiveness], the self (<s>ātman</s>), space (<s>ākāśa</s>), and the like are called 'all-pervading.' Now, <s>Caitra</s> is not like space — for he is ascertained as complete and finite in one place. Nor can he exist in another place as a whole exists in its parts. For if he had parts elsewhere, he would not be completely perceived here. Existing in the interval, by discontinuity, he would be another. Nor can he exist like a universal — for a universal is formless (<s>amūrtā</s>); this is not such a universal. His connection with another place is conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>). And that is not possible for one who has not gone [there]. For he is seen going and then conjoining with other places. For this very reason, he is not all-pervading.
[Objection:] But is not the effect a <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark)? No — because the relation is not required.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sambandhitāṃ caiṣā śaktirgamyeta nānyathā // Msv_5,7.48 //
children.translated_text: And this capacity (<s>śakti</s>) can be known only after observing the relation, not otherwise. // Msv_5,7.48 //
And since perception and the like are impossible at the time of seeing that [capacity],

children.text: arthāpatte' pramāṇatvaṃ trailakṣaṇyād vinā bhavet // Msv_5,7.49 //
children.translated_text: <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) would have the status of a <s>pramāṇa</s> without the three characteristics [of inference]. // Msv_5,7.49 //

children.text:
ato 'syana kathañcidekatra sato 'nyatra sattvamupapadyata ityanyatrābhāvamantarbhāvya kṛtsnabodha' samarthyate, kā punaratrānupapatti', nātra kṛtsnabodhasya kenacit pratighāto daśyate /
bhāvānumānenaiva kevalaṃ tu durbale pratighātahetau tadabādhenaivārthāpattirātmānaṃ labhate /
durbalaṃ ceha bhāvānumānaṃ pratihetuviruddhatvāt /
yatra tu tulyabalamubhayamekatropanipatitaṃ bhavati, tatrārthāntarakalpanayopapattiriti na kiñcidanupapannamiti /
evaṃ tāvadabhāvapūrvikāyā arthāpatteranumānād bheda ukta', pratyakṣapūrvikāyā bhedamidānīṃ darśayituṃ tatpratijñānaṃ tāvadāha--- yatra ceti /
children.translated_text: Thus, the distinction of absence-based <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) from inference has been stated. Now, in order to show the distinction of perception-based [<s>arthāpatti</s>], he first states the thesis — 'where also.'

children.text: yatrāpi dāhādikāryadarśanādagnyāde' kāraṇasya śaktirastīti kalpyate tatrāpyarthāpattireva prathamā /
children.translated_text: Even where the capacity of a cause such as fire is postulated from observing an effect like burning, there too <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is primary.
If inference follows afterward, let it.

children.text: bhāṣyodāhṛtatvāccābhāvapūrvikāyā eva prathamamanumānād bhedo varṇita iti ||46,47||
children.translated_text: And since the absence-based [<s>arthāpatti</s>] was exemplified in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, the distinction from inference was first described for that alone. // 46, 47 //

Therefore, since the existence elsewhere of this [individual] that somehow exists in one place is not possible, by including the absence elsewhere, complete cognition is established. But what exactly is the impossibility here? No obstruction to complete cognition is seen by anyone here. It is only through a weak counter-reason that the existence-inference [opposes it], but since the obstruction-cause is weak, <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) establishes itself precisely through the non-overriding [of that weak objection]. And here the existence-inference is weak because it is contradicted by a counter-reason. But where both [the inference and the counter-inference] are of equal strength and converge on a single point, the impossibility is resolved by postulating something additional — so nothing is unaccounted for.

children.text:
atrānumānavādināṃ liṅgamupanyasyati---kāryasyeti /
evaṃ hi manyante--- dvividhamanumānaṃ dṛṣṭasvalakṣaṇaviṣayamadṛṣṭasvalakṣamaviṣayaṃ ca saṃyogavibhāgādibhya iva kriyādyanumānam /
kāryaṃ hi kāraṇena sāmānyato jñātasambandhamiti tatastatpratītiranumānabhevedamiti /
etadapi dūṣayati--- na sambandheti /
yena hyekadā bījādaṅkuro dṛṣṭa' so 'nyadā tathāvidhādeva punaranupalabhamāna' svabhāvānumānena janayitavyo 'nenāṅkura ityanumimāna evātrā śaṅkate kathamaṅkuro na jāyata iti, tata' kalpayati--- asti kaścid bījasamavāyī śaktibhedo yadvaśāt prāk kāryamāsīdadya ca nāstīti /
taccedamanapekṣitasambandhasyaiva purātanedānīntanāṅkuradarśanādarśanavicārādeva jñānaṃ jāyamānaṃ kathamanumānamiti /
api ca sambandhagrahaṇādhīnameva sarvamanumānaṃ na tadagṛhītayo' sambandhino' sambhavati /
na ceha tayoratīndriyā śakti'
children.translated_text: Here he presents the inferential mark of those who advocate inference — 'of the effect.' For they think thus: Inference is twofold — that whose object is a perceived particular (<s>dṛṣṭasvalakṣaṇa</s>) and that whose object is an unperceived particular (<s>adṛṣṭasvalakṣaṇa</s>), like the inference of action and such from conjunction, disjunction, and the like. For the effect is something whose relation with the cause is known in a general way, and therefore the cognition from it is a variety of inference — this is [their argument]. He refutes this too — 'not the relation.' For one who once observed a sprout from a seed, not perceiving [a sprout] another time from the same kind [of seed], infers by the inference of essential nature, 'a sprout is to be produced by this' — and right there suspects 'how is the sprout not arising?' Then he postulates: 'There is some particular capacity (<s>śaktibheda</s>) inhering in the seed, by virtue of which the effect was [produced] before and is not [produced] now.' This cognition, arising from the examination of seeing and not seeing the former and present sprouts without requiring [the apprehension of] the relation — how can it be inference? Moreover, all inference depends on the apprehension of a relation, and without that, no relation between the relata is possible. And here, the capacity of those two is supersensible.
Since [<s>arthāpatti</s> is] not different from inference, victory and defeat are not stated
as existing in the relation of the slayer and the slain among serpents, mongooses, and the like. // Msv_5,7.50 //

children.text: pīno divā na bhuṅkte cetyevamādivaca' śrutau // Msv_5,7.51 //
children.translated_text: '[<s>Devadatta</s>] is fat [and] does not eat during the day' — upon hearing such a statement... // Msv_5,7.51 //
Some construe that [<s>arthāpatti</s>] as having a thing (<s>artha</s>) as its object; others as having a word (<s>śabda</s>) as its object;
and they declare it non-different from <s>āgama</s> (scriptural testimony). // Msv_5,7.52 //

children.text:
pramāṇāntareṇa śakyate 'nubhavitum, ata eva ca na tadvato 'pi grahaṇaṃ sambhavati, ata' kathamagṛhītasambandhāt
kāryācchaktitadvato' siddhiriti /
tadetadāha--- dṛṣṭaveti /
nanvavagataṃ tāvat kāryasāmānyaṃ kāraṇasāmānyena vyāptamiti, atastadanumāsyate /
satyam, kintu śaktikakalpanayā vinā kāraṇākhyaiva na nivartate /
children.translated_text: True, but without the postulation of the capacity, the very designation 'cause' does not cease [to be problematic].

children.text: aṅkuro hi bījabhāvabhāvī vyabhicaritabhāvāntaraśca bījakāraṇaka ityavagata' satyapi tu bīje 'jāyamānastadapi vyabhicaratīti kāraṇāvagatirevāvasīdati, tāṃ śaktikalpanayottabhnāti /
children.translated_text: For the sprout, existing when the seed exists and deviating when other [conditions] are present, is known to have the seed as its cause; but when [the sprout] does not arise even though the seed is present, that too deviates — so the very cognition of causation collapses, and he supports it by postulating a capacity.

children.text: kḷptāyāṃ ca śaktau kāraṇasambandhinyāmarthāpattyā yadi sambandho 'vagamyate tadastu siddhāntavacchaktisiddhāvarthāpatti' pramāṇamiti /
children.translated_text: And when the capacity, being related to the cause, is postulated, if the relation is ascertained through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), then let it be so — just as in the established view (<s>siddhānta</s>), <s>arthāpatti</s> is the <s>pramāṇa</s> for establishing the capacity.
He concludes that <s>arthāpatti</s>, arising without the characteristic mark of inference, is a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> — '<s>arthāpatti</s>.' // 49 //

cannot be experienced by another <s>pramāṇa</s>, and for that very reason the apprehension of what possesses it is also not possible — therefore, how can the capacity and its possessor be established from an effect whose relation [with the cause] has not been apprehended? This he states — 'having observed.' But is it not the case that the universal 'effect-ness' is known to be pervaded by the universal 'cause-ness,' and therefore the latter is inferred from the former?
He refutes the example cited in another <s>vṛtti</s> (sub-commentary) — 'from inference.'

children.text: jayo hi parājayena viditavyāptiriti tamekatra ghātake nakule dṛṣṭvā pratipakṣasya parājayo 'vagamyate /
children.translated_text: For victory, being known to be pervaded by defeat, upon observing it in the mongoose — which is the slayer in one [encounter] — the defeat of the adversary is ascertained.
From observing defeat, the victory of the adversary [is inferred].
This should not be cited as an example of <s>arthāpatti</s>. // 50 //
It was said that <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> (presumption from heard testimony) would be illustrated; he now illustrates that — 'fat.' // 51 //
And regarding the object of this [<s>śrutārthāpatti</s>], there is a dispute.
In order to determine one [view], he presents [the alternatives] — from 'some construe it as having a thing as its object' to 'they declare.'
And [he states] that all [thinkers] maintain it to be outside of <s>āgama</s> (scripture) — he says '<s>āgamāt</s>.' // 52 //
And most of the procedure in the <s>Veda</s> is established through this [<s>arthāpatti</s>];

children.text: so 'vaidika' prasajyeta yadyeṣā bhidyate tata' // Msv_5,7.53 //
children.translated_text: if this [<s>arthāpatti</s>] were differentiated from [the <s>Veda</s>], then that [procedure] would become non-Vedic. // Msv_5,7.53 //
That meaning too is accepted by some as belonging to the very sentence that is heard;
by others, when its [direct] meaning is disrupted, it is held to belong to another sentence. // Msv_5,7.54 //
Now, this meaning is not accepted as belonging to the sentence being heard,

children.text: na hyanekārthatā yuktā vākye vācakatā tathā // Msv_5,7.55 //
children.translated_text: for multiple meanings are not proper in a sentence, nor [multiple] denotative powers. // Msv_5,7.55 //
For the sentence-meaning is cognized in the form of the connection of word-meanings;
and the word-meanings pertaining to night and the like are not cognized from the daytime-sentence. // Msv_5,7.56 //
Night-eating is neither a conjunction of the word-meanings pertaining to 'during the day' and the like,

children.text: na bhedo yena tadvākyaṃ tasya syāt pratipādakam // Msv_5,7.57 //
children.translated_text: nor a differentiation — by which that sentence could be its communicator. // Msv_5,7.57 //
He states the intended purpose of accepting non-difference from <s>āgama</s> (scripture) — 'mostly.'

children.text: phalāpūrvavidhyantādisiddhau bhūyānasyā vede upayoga', sarvo 'nāgamatvevaidika' syāditi ||53||
children.translated_text: If <s>arthāpatti</s> has great usefulness in the <s>Veda</s> for establishing results (<s>phala</s>), unprecedented duties (<s>apūrva</s>), injunctions (<s>vidhi</s>), and the like, then were it not [classified as] <s>āgama</s>, all [those results] would become non-Vedic. // 53 //
He presents the subsidiary disagreement even among those who accept it as belonging to <s>āgama</s> — 'of the sentence.'
Here he shows the conclusion — 'not indeed.'
He states the reason — 'for not.'
A sentence is indeed non-denotative [of multiple meanings], let alone of many meanings. // 55 //
And this will be discussed in the <s>tadabhūtādhikaraṇa</s> (section on what is not part of that).

children.text: nanu rātryādivākyārtho yadi divāvākyenānabhihita' padārthānvayarūpeṇaiva svārthavad gamayiṣyate /
children.translated_text: But [objection:] if the meaning of the night-sentence is not expressed by the daytime-sentence, it will be conveyed in the form of the connection of word-meanings, just like its own meaning.
Hence he says — 'not night and the like.'

children.text: na hi divāvākye rātryādipadārthā' santi, kutastatra teṣāmanvaya iti ||56||
children.translated_text: For in the daytime-sentence, the word-meanings pertaining to night and the like do not exist — so whence their connection there? // 56 //
If it is non-denotative, how is meaning cognized from the sentence? Hence he says — 'of the word-meanings.'

children.text: nanu divādipadārthānvayādeva rātryādivākyārtha' pratyeṣyate, ata āha---na divādīti ||57||
children.translated_text: But [objection:] the meaning of the night-sentence would be understood precisely from the connection of the word-meanings pertaining to 'during the day' and the like — hence he says 'not of those pertaining to day.' // 57 //
And because [the sentence] is engaged with another meaning, there is no postulation of a second meaning;
therefore, this [meaning] is cognized through another sentence that exists in the mind. // Msv_5,7.58 //
And even if that [<s>arthāpatti</s>] is classified as belonging to <s>āgama</s>, still, for that sentence which is cognized,

children.text: pramāṇaṃ tasya vaktavyaṃ pratyakṣādiṣu yad bhavet // Msv_5,7.59 //
children.translated_text: the <s>pramāṇa</s> must be stated — which among perception and the like it might be. // Msv_5,7.59 //
For when a sentence has not been uttered, perception at least is not accepted [as the means];

children.text: nānumānaṃ na cedaṃ hi dṛṣṭaṃ tena saha kvacit // Msv_5,7.60 //
children.translated_text: nor inference — for this [sentence] has never been observed together with that [heard sentence]. // Msv_5,7.60 //
But if it is accepted as an inferential mark even when the relation has not been apprehended,
then by mere utterance, every sentence would follow [from any other]. // Msv_5,7.61 //
And it is not the case that all sentences of all [speakers] are cognized
as connected through <s>arthāpatti</s>, such that inference could apply to them. // Msv_5,7.62 //
He elaborates on what was said — 'for multiple meanings are not proper' — 'because of being engaged with another meaning.'
Therefore, this is the meaning of another sentence, not of the daytime-sentence — he says 'therefore.' // 58 //

children.text: evaṃ tāvanna mūlāgamasyāyamartha', yena tu vākyāntareṇa buddhisthenāyamartho 'vagamyate, tasyaiva pratyakṣādiṣu madhye pramāṇaṃ nirdhāraṇīyamityāha--- tasyeti ||59||
children.translated_text: Thus, first, this is not the meaning of the root <s>āgama</s>; but the <s>pramāṇa</s> for the very other sentence by which this meaning is cognized through the mind must be determined among perception and the like — he says 'of that.' // 59 //

children.text: tatra pratyakṣaṃ tāvanna tatsiddhau pramāṇamityāha---na hīti /
children.translated_text: There, first, perception is not the <s>pramāṇa</s> for establishing that — he says 'for not.'

children.text: anumānamapi tena sambaddhasya divāvākyasyādarśanānna sambhavatītyāha--- nānumānamiti ||60||
children.translated_text: And inference too is not possible because the daytime-sentence connected with it has not been observed — he says 'not inference.' // 60 //

children.text: aviditasambandhe tu divāvākye liṅga iṣyamāṇe 'vyavasthetyāha---yadi tviti ||61||
children.translated_text: When the daytime-sentence, whose relation is unknown, is accepted as an inferential mark, there would be no restriction — he says 'but if.' // 61 //

children.text: yadi tūcyate sambandhamevadivāvākyasya rātrivākyenagṛhītvā tatastadanumāsyata iti, sidhyatyevam, na tuśrutārthāpattivedyāni sarvāṇi lokavedavākyāni sarvai' pratipādakavākyai' sambaddhānyavagatāni /
children.translated_text: But if it is said that having apprehended the relation of the daytime-sentence with the night-sentence, one then infers from it — this would work, but it is not the case that all sentences in the world and the <s>Veda</s> that are knowable through <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> are known as connected with all the sentences that convey them.
Therefore, how can those be inferred from these? Hence he says — 'and not.' // 62 //
And neither by inference of existence nor otherwise is the particular inferred;
for here, only the existence of a particular sentence is ascertained. // Msv_5,7.63 //
A previously established independent meaning, qualified by an independent [qualifier] —
the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>), qualified by the property (<s>dharma</s>), is not cognized here as something to be inferred. // Msv_5,7.64 //
Or if the qualification of the heard sentence is measured,
then the thesis would have an unestablished qualifier. // Msv_5,7.65 //
Moreover, if this [sentence] has the status of an inferential mark in the absence of another mark,
then, like a word [being part of the thesis], it would be subject to the fallacy of being a mere part of the thesis. // Msv_5,7.66 //
In just the same way, the property-property-bearer relation of sentences is to be rejected.

children.text: nāgṛhīte hi taddharmo gṛhīte nānumeyatā // Msv_5,7.67 //
children.translated_text: For when it [the sentence] has not been apprehended, its property [status] does not hold; and when it has been apprehended, there is no inferability. // 67 //
For this further reason too it is not inference — hence he says 'na ca' (nor also).

children.text: kenaciddhi sāmānyātmanā jñātasambandhena viśiṣṭaṃ kiñcidanumīyate na vastusattāmātram /
children.translated_text: For something specific is inferred through something known in its relation by way of a general nature — not mere existential reality.

children.text: na ca viśiṣṭa', ajñātasambandhatvāt iha tu tadubhayaṃ viparītamiti ||63||
children.translated_text: And the specific [entity here] has an unknown relation; but here, both of those are reversed. // 63 //

children.text: yataścātra vākyāsvarūpameva prameyamata' parvatādiriva pūrvasiddha' svatantro 'sambaddha' kenacidagnyādineva svatantreṇa kenacid viśeṣito dharmī dharmaviśiṣṭo nāstītyāha--- pūrvasiddha iti ||64||
children.translated_text: And since here the very form of the sentence is what is to be known, there is no independently established, self-sufficient property-bearer — unconnected with anything — like a mountain, qualified by some independent [property] like fire — hence he says 'independently established.' // 64 //

children.text: atha śrutameva vākyaṃ dharmitayopādāyāśrutavākyaviśiṣṭatā sādhyate tatastadaprasiddheraprasiddhaviśeṣaṇa' pakṣa ityāha--- atheti ||65||
children.translated_text: Now, if the very sentence that has been heard is taken up as the property-bearer, and the qualification by the unheard sentence is to be proved, then, because the latter is unestablished, the thesis has an unestablished qualifier — hence he says 'now if.' // 65 //

children.text: api ca śrute vākye 'śrutavākyaviśiṣṭe sādhyamāne na tāvat kiñcilliṅgamupalabhyate, na cāliṅgakanumānaṃ bhavati, tad yadi tadeva punarliṅgamiṣyate tata' pratijñārthaikadeśitvam, yathā pade pakṣīkṛter'thaviśiṣṭe sādhyamāne 'bhihitamityāha---kiñceti ||66||
children.translated_text: Moreover, when the heard sentence is to be proved as qualified by the unheard sentence, no inferential mark whatsoever is perceived; and there is no inference without a mark. If it is desired that the very [sentence] itself is the mark, then there follows being-a-part-of-the-thesis-meaning — just as was stated when the word was made the thesis to prove the qualification by meaning — hence he says 'what mark?' // 66 //

children.text:
dharmadharmibhāvo 'pi divāvākyarātrivākyadayo' śabdārthayoriva nirākārya ityāha--- tadvadeveti /
yathā tatrārthe dharmiṇyapratipanne na padaṃ taddharma ityuktam, evamihāpi nāpratipanne rātrivākye taddhadharmatayā divā
children.translated_text: The property-property-bearer relation, too — [between] the day-sentence and the night-sentence — is to be rejected, just as between word and meaning — hence he says 'in just the same way.' Just as there, when the meaning as property-bearer is not apprehended, the word was said not to be its property, so here too, when the night-sentence is not apprehended, its property-status with respect to the day-sentence
is not established; for without the relation of action and agent (<s>kriyā-kāraka</s>), there is no property-status.
And because of the non-denotative nature of this [day-sentence with respect to the night-sentence], it is not a property by way of being an object. // 68 //
If [you say] the denotative capacity [is established] from the fact of cognition — then the undesirable consequence of manifold capacities follows;

children.text: anumāviṣayotthaṃ tu dharmatvaṃ niṣphalaṃ bhavet // Msv_5,7.69 //
children.translated_text: and the property-status arising from being an object of inference would be fruitless. // 69 //
That sentence is not cognized from the word-meanings either, because of the absence of connection;
for the general [meanings of words] indicate the specific [sentence-meaning] only through the impossibility of being otherwise established. // 70 //
the sentence is cognized.

children.text: atha tu pakṣadharmatāpratipattyarthaṃ tat prathamamavagatamityucyate tato 'numeyābhāva ityabhiprāya' /
children.translated_text: But if it is said that it [the sentence] is first apprehended for the purpose of ascertaining the property-of-the-thesis status — then the absence of something to be inferred [follows] — this is the intention.
The intention
he elaborates — 'when not apprehended.' // 67 //

children.text:
api ca tatraiva pade varṇitam--- na kriyākārakasambandhādṛte sambandho bhavatīti /
ato yathā padasya na kaścit
kriyānivandhanor'thasambandho 'stīti na taddharma ityuktam, evaṃ divāvākyasyāpi rātrivākyadharmata nirākāryetyāha---kriyeti /
children.translated_text: and therefore is not its property — so the property-status of the night-sentence with respect to the day-sentence is also to be rejected — hence he says 'action' (<s>kriyā</s>).

children.text: na cātra viṣayaviṣayibhāvarūpāpi dvayārvākyayo' śabdārthayoriva sambandho bhavati ucyate hi śabdenārtha', na tu vākyaṃ vākyāntarasya vācakamityāha--- avācaketi /
children.translated_text: And here, there is not even a connection in the form of the object-cognizer relation between the two sentences — as there is between word and meaning. For meaning is expressed by the word, but a sentence is not the denoter of another sentence — hence he says 'non-denotative.'
In the case of the word, the absence of something to be inferred was shown by accepting its object-status through its capacity to generate the cognition of meaning.

children.text: iha tu vākyasyāvācakatvāt tadviṣayatvameva pratyetuṃ na śakyate iti viśeṣa' ||68||
children.translated_text: But here, because the sentence is non-denotative [of another sentence], its very object-status cannot be understood — this is the distinguishing point. // 68 //

Moreover, in that very [discussion of] the word, it was explained — 'without the relation of action and agent, there is no connection.' Therefore, just as it was said that the word has no connection with meaning based on action,

children.text: yadi tūcyate pratīyate tāvad divāvākyād rātrivākyam, atastasyāpi tadvācakatvamityasti viṣayaviṣayilakṣaṇa' sambandha iti, tatraikaṃ vākyamanekārthamabhyupagataṃ bhavet, svārthaṃ hi tatpratipādayati rātrivākyamapi, na caivaṃ nyāyyamityabhiprāyeṇāha---pratīteriti /
children.translated_text: But if it is said: 'The night-sentence is indeed cognized from the day-sentence, therefore the day-sentence too has denotative capacity with respect to it — so the connection in the form of object and cognizer does exist' — then a single sentence would be accepted as having multiple meanings, for it conveys its own meaning and also the night-sentence; and this is not proper — with this intention he says 'from the fact of cognition.'

children.text: athocyeta--- mābhūdavācakatayā tdaviṣayatvam,tena tu tadvākyamanumīyate, atastalliṅgamanumānaviṣayatayā liṅgameva divāvākyaṃ taddharmatayābhidhīyata iti /
children.translated_text: But suppose it is said: 'Let there not be object-status due to non-denotative nature; but the night-sentence is inferred by that [day-sentence], and therefore the day-sentence, being a mark by way of being an object of inference, is designated as having property-status [with respect to the night-sentence]' —
the property-status that arises from being an object of inference is fruitless, since that inference is already established beforehand — hence he says 'from inference.' // 69 //

children.text:
evaṃ tāvad divāvākyamaliṅgamityuktam, tadgatapadārthānāmapyevameva liṅgatā nirākāryetyāha---padārthairiti /
nanvagṛhītasambandhā eva padārthā
children.translated_text: Thus it has been stated that the day-sentence is not a mark; the mark-status of the word-meanings contained in it is also to be rejected in the same way — hence he says 'from word-meanings.' Now, the word-meanings whose relation has not been grasped

children.text: na tu vākyāntareṇaiṣāṃ vinā kiñcinna sidhyati /
children.translated_text: but nothing of those [word-meanings] is established without the other sentence;

children.text: na cāpyanya' prakāro 'sti tena vākyena saṅgatau // Msv_5,7.71 //
children.translated_text: nor is there any other mode of connection with that sentence. // 71 //
Now, if another sentence is postulated as expressing this [meaning], then likewise [for that sentence too];

children.text: prasaṅgāt tatra dūre 'pi nāsambandhāt pramucyate // Msv_5,7.72 //
children.translated_text: by force of that [regress], even for one far [removed], freedom from the absence of connection is not achieved. // 72 //
Therefore, it is better to know from the very first [sentence] which is unconnected;

children.text: anvayavyatirekau ca pratiṣedhyau pade yathā // Msv_5,7.73 //
children.translated_text: and <s>anvaya</s> (co-presence) and <s>vyatireka</s> (co-absence) are to be denied, just as in the case of the word. // 73 //

children.text: yathā vākyārthaṃ gamayanti, evaṃ rātrivākyamapi kiṃ na gamayanti, ata āha--sāmānyeti /
children.translated_text: Just as [word-meanings] convey the sentence-meaning, why do they not similarly convey the night-sentence? — hence he says 'the general.'

children.text: kriyāsāmānyaṃ kārakasāmānyaṃ vā pratipannamalabdhetaretaravyatiṣaṅgamanyathā na sidhyatīti taṃ viśeṣaṃ gamayati, yaścāsau viśeṣa' sa eva tu vākyārtha ityucyate iti ||70||
children.translated_text: The general [aspect] of action or the general [aspect] of the agent, once apprehended, without having obtained the mutual connection of one with the other, does not become established otherwise — and so it conveys that specific [meaning]; and that very specific [meaning] is what is called 'sentence-meaning.' // 70 //

children.text:
na caiṣa prakāro rātrivākyapratipādane sambhavatītyāha---na tviti /
yadyapi divāvākyaṃ na rātrivākyasya vācakam, tathāpi kalpayiṣyāma', tataśca tatpratyeṣyata iti /
tadidamāśaṅkete tāvat --- athaitadvācītyanyadantena /
atra dūṣaṇamāha--- tathaiveti /
atra tāvadevaṃ vākyāntarakalpanāyāṃ pramāṇameva nāstīti tadanādṛtya tāvadanavasthāmāpādayati, yadapi kalpitaṃ vākyaṃ tadapi na rātrivākaymavagamayituṃ śaktam /
children.translated_text: Here, to begin with, there is simply no <s>pramāṇa</s> for postulating another sentence — so, disregarding that, he brings about an infinite regress: even the postulated sentence is incapable of making the night-sentence understood.

children.text: na ca tadasambaddhameva tasya gamakamiti yuktam /
children.translated_text: And it is not proper that something unconnected with it should be its indicator.
If yet another sentence is postulated, the same fault [arises].

children.text: evaṃ yadeva kiñcid vākyaṃ kalpayitumiṣyate tadeva nāsambaddhaṃ gamakamityanavasthāpata iti ||72||
children.translated_text: Thus, whatever sentence one wishes to postulate, that very [sentence], being unconnected, is not an indicator — so infinite regress results. // 72 //

And this mode is not possible in conveying the night-sentence — hence he says 'but not.' Although the day-sentence is not the denoter of the night-sentence, still we shall postulate [it], and thereby [the night-sentence] will be understood — he raises this doubt: 'now, if another sentence is expressing this' — with the other ending. To this he states the refutation — 'likewise.'

children.text:
atha tvantimamasambaddhameva gamakamiti kalpyate, tad varaṃ prathamasyaiva tathāvidhasya gamaktavaṃ kalpatum, kiṃ vākyāntarakakalpanayā /
naca tadyuktamityabhiprāyeṇāha--- tataśceti /
evaṃ tāvat pakṣadharmatvādyasambhavena rākṣivākyasyānumeyatvaṃ nirastam, anvayavyatirekayorapi padavat pratiṣedho darśayitavya ityāha--- anvayeti /
nahi satyeva rātrivākye divāvākyaṃ
children.translated_text: But if the last [sentence], though unconnected, is postulated as an indicator, then it is better to postulate the indicator-status of the very first such [sentence] — what is the use of postulating another sentence? And that [first postulation] is not justified — with this intention he says 'therefore.' Thus, the inferability of the night-sentence has been refuted by the impossibility of property-of-the-thesis status and the like. That <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> too are to be denied, just as in the case of the word — hence he says '<s>anvaya</s>.' For when the night-sentence exists, the day-sentence
A heard sentence has no resemblance whatsoever with an unheard one;
therefore, the object too cannot be known by analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) in this way. // 74 //
When the analogy-status has been blocked with respect to the sentence by the mark of analogy-status,

children.text: arthe 'pi caivameva syāt tasmāt pūrveṣvasambhava' // Msv_5,7.75 //
children.translated_text: it would be the same with respect to the object too — therefore, [there is] impossibility in the preceding [<s>pramāṇas</s>]. // 75 //
Therefore, the conveying of the meaning by the heard sentence —

children.text: tadātmalābha eva syād vinā netyetadiṣyate // Msv_5,7.76 //
children.translated_text: that would be its self-attainment alone, without something else — this is what is maintained. // 76 //

children.text: etadarthād vinā nāyamityartha' kiṃ na kalpyate /
children.translated_text: 'Without this meaning, this [sentence] does not [stand]' — why is this meaning not postulated?
And just as the sentence-meaning, why is not this meaning of <s>āgama</s> (scripture) cognized? // 77 //
[the night-sentence] does not exist — so <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> do not obtain, because of the absence of connection with that place, that time, and so on.

children.text: na ca jñānānvayo 'satyapi rātrivākyajñāne vyutpannasya divāvākyajñānād, vijñānottarakālabhāvinoścānvayavyatirekayostadanupayogādityādipadavaddarśayitavyamityabhiprāya' ||73||
children.translated_text: Nor does the <s>anvaya</s> of cognition [obtain] in the absence of cognition of the night-sentence for one who has acquired understanding from the cognition of the day-sentence; and since <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> occurring after the cognition are of no use to it — this and other [arguments] are to be shown just as in the case of the word — this is the intention. // 73 //

children.text: evaṃ tāvat pratyakṣānumānāgamairna rātrivākyaṃ pratīyata ityuktam, upamānamapi tatra na pramāṇamiti darśayati---śrutavākyeti tvamantena /
children.translated_text: Thus it has been stated that the night-sentence is not cognized through perception, inference, or <s>āgama</s>. He shows that analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) too is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> there — 'heard sentence' ending in the word 'tu.'

children.text: divāvākyavacca tadarthenāpi na rātrivākyamupamīyata ityāha--- arthasyeti ||74||
children.translated_text: And the night-sentence is not analogized through the day-sentence or its meaning either — hence he says 'of the object.' // 74 //

children.text: yathā ca rātrivākyasya divāvākyatatadarthābhyāmupamānaṃ nirastamevaṃ rātrivākyārthasyāpi tābhyāṃ nirasanīyamityāha--- upamānatveti syādantena /
children.translated_text: And just as the analogy of the night-sentence has been rejected through the day-sentence and its meaning, so the [analogy] of the night-sentence's meaning too is to be rejected through those two — hence he says 'analogy-status' ending in 'syāt.'
He concludes — 'therefore.' // 75 //
Therefore, in the absence of any other <s>pramāṇa</s>, <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) alone is the refuge for understanding the night-sentence — hence he says 'therefore.'

children.text: pratyakṣadṛṣṭaṃ pīnatvaṃ bhojanapratiṣedhena pratihanyate, pīnatvena divābhojanam, ata' parasparapratighātād divāvākyasya svārthapratipādanamevānupapadyamānaṃ rātrivākyamanupraveśayati, ata' tadrātrivākyaṃ kalpyata iti ||76||
children.translated_text: The directly perceived plumpness is contradicted by the prohibition of [daytime] eating; the plumpness [contradicts] the daytime eating; therefore, from the mutual contradiction, the conveying of its own meaning by the day-sentence, being otherwise impossible, brings in the night-sentence — and so the night-sentence is postulated. // 76 //

children.text:
tāmarthaviṣayāmiti yadktaṃ tadidānīṃ dūṣayitumupanyasyati---etadarthādvineti /
ayamabhiprāya'--- pīntavaṃ hi bhojanapratiṣedho vā paraspareṇa pratihanyate tayoścārthakalpanayaivātmalābha' /
pīnasya hi divā niṣiddhe
children.translated_text: That [<s>arthāpatti</s>] is object-directed — what was stated to this effect, he now sets forth in order to refute it — 'without this meaning.' The intention is this: The plumpness and the prohibition of eating are mutually contradicted, and the self-attainment of both is through the postulation of meaning alone. For when the eating of the plump person is prohibited during the day, the plumpness is accounted for only through nighttime eating — not through the night-sentence; therefore, the postulation of meaning alone is proper.
The word (<s>śabda</s>) is first cognized through conceptual (<s>savikalpaka</s>) cognitions;

children.text: labdhaprayojane vākye paraṃ nāgamikaṃ ca na' // Msv_5,7.78 //
children.translated_text: when the sentence has attained its purpose, thereafter, [<s>arthāpatti</s>] is not <s>āgamika</s> (scripture-based) for us. // 78 //

children.text: bhojane, rātribhojanenaiva pīnatvamupapadyate, na rātrivākyenātor'thakalpanaiva yukteti /
children.translated_text: nighttime eating — the plumpness is accounted for through that alone — not through the night-sentence; therefore, the postulation of meaning alone is proper.

children.text: api ca, yathā parairabhidhīyamāno 'pi padārthānupapattyā gamyamāno vākyārtha āgamārtho bhavati /
children.translated_text: Moreover, just as the sentence-meaning cognized through the impossibility of word-meanings — even though stated by others — is said to be the meaning of <s>āgama</s>,
so too the meaning cognized through the impossibility of sentence-meaning — why does it not fall within <s>āgama</s>? — hence he says 'like the sentence-meaning.' // 77 //

children.text:
prathamaparicodanāṃ tāvat pariharati---savikalpaketi /
savikalpako hi śrutārthāpattibodha' savikalpajñānāni ca śabdapura' sarāṇi /
ata' śabdaparyavasitāyāmarthāpattau śabdādeva sidhyannartho nārthāpatterviṣaya iti /
nanvevaṃ sarvapramāṇavikalpeṣu samānamidam, indriyaliṅgābhyāmapi śabdapura' saramevāgni' pratīyate, tatastayorapi śabdaparyavasāyitaiva bhavet atastatra smṛtistha eva śabdo 'pratyāyaka', tadihāpi samānam /
yathā hi karmendriyamarthenaiva sannikṛṣṭamiti tameva prakāśayati liṅgaṃ cārthena sambaddhamiti ta gamayati, na śabdam, evamihāpyanupapadyamānor'thenaivopapadyate na śabdena /
tathā ca dṛṣṭārthāpattayor'thaviṣayā eva /
atrocyate /
satyamarthadvārikeva vākyāntaramevākāṅkṣati, yathā padaṃ padāntaram /
na hi pacatītyukte odanapratyakṣeṇākāṅkṣā nivartate, kiṃ tarhi odanamiti padena, evaṃ vākyamapyanupapadyamānatayāvagataṃ vākyāntaramevākāṅkṣati, na tu tamarthaṃ svarūpeṇa /
ata eva nirvāpamantre 'tideśād vikṛtiṃ gate prākṛtadevatāyā abhāvāt tatpadanivṛttau tasya sthāne sūryāyeti padamūhyate /
chedanamantre tviṣetvetyatra chinadmīti padamadhyāhriyate /
hṛdayasyāgne 'vadyati atha jihvāyā atha vakṣasa ityatrāpadyatipadānuṣaṅga' /
na cārtha evānuṣajyate 'anuṣaṅgo vākyasamāpti' sarveṣu pekṣyate śabdollekhenāpi gṛhyamāṇa', kinnvartharūpeṇaiva, tamarthaṃ vikalpayani śabdantvastu nāma sanmātratayā /
yadi tu tatrāpi śabdo 'pekṣyate tiraścāmarthavikalpo na syāt, sa ca nāsti dṛśyeta hi teṣāmapi hitāhitaprāptiparihārārtha' prayatna' /
tṛṣitā hi gāvastaṭākāni gacchanti, varṣātapābhi
children.translated_text: He first resolves the first objection — '<s>savikalpaka</s>' (conceptual). For the cognition of <s>arthāpatti</s> based on what is heard is conceptual, and conceptual cognitions are preceded by word. Therefore, when <s>arthāpatti</s> culminates in word, the meaning being established from the word itself is not the domain of <s>arthāpatti</s>. Now, if this is the same for all varieties of <s>pramāṇas</s> — fire too is cognized as preceded by word through the sense-organ and the mark — then those [perception and inference] too would culminate in word; therefore, the word that is merely present in memory is non-communicative there; the same applies here too. Just as the action-organ, being in contact with the object itself, illuminates that very [object], and the mark, being connected with the object, conveys that — not the word — so here too, it is accounted for by the otherwise-impossible object itself, not by the word. And thus, in the case of seen <s>arthāpatti</s>, [the content] is indeed object-directed. To this he replies: True — through the medium of the object, [<s>arthāpatti</s>] seeks another sentence, just as a word [seeks] another word. For when 'he cooks' is said, the expectancy is not satisfied by the perception of rice, but rather by the word 'rice' — so too, a sentence apprehended through its being otherwise impossible seeks another sentence, not that meaning in its own form. For this very reason, in the case of the <s>nirvāpa</s> (offering) <s>mantra</s>, when the primary deity is absent due to modification through transfer (<s>atideśa</s>), upon the dropping of that word, the word '<s>sūryāya</s>' (to the Sun) is supplied in its place. But in the cutting <s>mantra</s>, at '<s>iṣetvā</s>' the word '<s>chinadmi</s>' (I cut) is supplied. In '[he cuts] the heart, then of the tongue, then of the chest' — there is the continuation of the word '<s>avadyati</s>' (he cuts). And it is not the meaning alone that is continued — 'the continuation is looked for up to the completion of the sentence by all, being grasped even through the trace of the word — what then, through the form of meaning alone?' But if the word is required even there, then animals would not have conceptual cognition of the meaning — and that is not so, for one sees that even they make effort for the attainment and avoidance of the beneficial and harmful. For thirsty cows go to ponds, and from rain and heat
But when the relation does not exist, or when it exists but has not been ascertained,
this sentence [whose meaning is] to be understood would turn out to be non-authoritative. // 79 //

children.text:
bhūtāśca tatpratīkārakṣamaṃ deśam /
ato 'śabdajñānāmapyanumānādivikalpadarśanānna tatra śabdāpekṣāstīti niścīyate /
śrutārthāpattibodhastu tiraścāṃ nāstyeva, śabdavyutpattijo hyasau, na ca teṣāmasāvastīti pratyakṣe 'pi varṇitam /
anyeṣāmapyavyutpannamaśabdānāṃ śrutārthāpattibodho na dṛśyate /
kiṃ punastiraścām /
atho 'nvayavyatirekābhyāmagamyate 'sti śabdāpekṣā śrutārthāpattau' /
anumānādiṣu tu saṃskārodabodhenāvarjanīyatayāstu nāma śabdasmṛti', na tu śabdāpekṣā /
ato 'tra vākyasyānupapannasya vākyāntaramevārthavadupapādakaṃ na tvarthamātraṃ śabdamātraṃ vā /
ata evāgṛhītasambandhasyārthamaviduṣa' śrute 'pyupapādake vākye nānupapannavākyārthajñāne 'nupapatti' śāmyati, pratipannārthasyāpyāśayakalpanā /
ato na śrutavākyasya nyūnatābuddhirnivalabdhaprayojana iti /
yāvaddhayakṛtārtha' śabdastāvad bodho 'vagamyate, sa tadartho bhavati /
prayojanavacano hyarthaśabda' /
ata eva vākyārtha āgamārtho bhavati /
tu kriyākārakasaṃsarge labdhaprayojanaṃ vākyamiti tata' paramarthāntaramavagamyamānaṃ nāgamikaṃ bhavati /
na hi prayojanatvāvagatārthānupapattyā yadavagamyate nāsādyata iti yuktaṃ vākyārthasya pūrvāvagatasyāgamārthātvam /

children.translated_text: What then is the distinction? It is stated:

children.text: śrutāgamārthatve yadi pramādāt tannāśo bhavati tato yajurvedādivihitanāśanimittaṃ prāyaścitam, itarathā tvavijñātanāśanimittamiti yadyavijñāto bhūrbhuva' sva' svāheti mahāvyāhṛtī' samāhṛtya prāyaścitaṃ samupadiśati /
children.translated_text: If the <s>āgama</s>-nature [of what is known] through hearing [is accepted], and if through carelessness its destruction occurs, then the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) is for a cause of destruction enjoined by the <s>Yajurveda</s> and such; but otherwise, for an unknown cause of destruction — [hence], if one who does not know recites the <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances) '<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā</s>' together, a <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) is prescribed.

children.text: śrutārthāpattivedya eva hi vedo 'vijñāta ityucyate, sa hyṛgādīnāṃ nānyatamatvena
children.translated_text: For the <s>Veda</s> that is knowable through <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> (presumption from what is heard) is called 'unknown,' since that [Veda]
is not known as belonging to any one among the <s>Ṛg</s> [Veda] and other [Vedas]. (78)

And the beings [perceive] a place capable of serving as an image of that. Therefore, even for non-verbal cognitions, since alternatives such as inference and the like are observed, it is ascertained that there is no dependence on words in those cases. But the cognition through <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> (presumption from what is heard) does not exist at all for animals, for it arises from linguistic competence, and they do not possess that — this has been explained even in the section on perception. And even for other beings who are unlearned and non-verbal, the cognition through <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> is not observed — how much less for animals? Now, if through <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) it is ascertained that 'there is dependence on words in <s>śrutārthāpatti</s>' — in inference and the like, however, let there be a memory of words due to the unavoidable arising of latent impressions, but there is no dependence on words. Therefore, here, the corroborating sentence for an anomalous sentence is itself another meaningful sentence, not mere meaning alone or mere word alone. For this very reason, even for one who has not grasped the relation and does not know the meaning, even when the corroborating sentence is heard, the incompatibility in the knowledge of the anomalous sentence's meaning does not cease — even for one who has understood the meaning, there is [merely] a supposition of intention. Therefore, the cognition of deficiency in the heard sentence does not [arise] without having obtained a purpose. For as long as the word has not fulfilled its purpose, that much cognition is apprehended, and that becomes its meaning. For the word 'artha' (meaning) denotes purpose. For this very reason, the sentence-meaning becomes the <s>āgama</s> (scriptural) meaning. But when the sentence has obtained its purpose in the action-<s>kāraka</s> combination, whatever further meaning is apprehended beyond that is not <s>āgamika</s> (scriptural). For it is not proper [to say] that what is apprehended through the incompatibility of a meaning whose purposiveness has been grasped 'is not reached' — [hence] the <s>āgama</s>-nature of the previously grasped sentence-meaning [is established].

children.text:
atra codayati---nanu ceti /
na tāvad divāvākyarātrivākyayo' sambandho 'sti, sannapi vā na vidita', na
cāviditasambandhānyadarśa
children.translated_text: Here he raises an objection — 'nanu ca.' There is no relation between the daytime-sentence and the nighttime-sentence, or even if there is, it is not known; and from [statements] whose relation is unknown —
The <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood (validity) of the relation is established — but is it by the command of the Lord?

children.text: pratyakṣasya pramāṇatvaṃ kathaṃ vā saṅgatervinā // Msv_5,7.80 //
children.translated_text: How can the <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood (validity) of perception [be established] without contact? (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.7.80)
If [you say] there exists a contact between the sense organ and the object — then, because of [that contact] not being required,

children.text: na hi pratyakṣavelāyāṃ sarveṇāsau nirūpyate // Msv_5,7.81 //
children.translated_text: for no one ascertains that [contact] at the time of perception. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.7.81)
And even by whomever it might be ascertained subsequently through experience,

children.text: na syādeva pramāṇāṅgamasatā tulya eva sa' // Msv_5,7.82 //
children.translated_text: it would not be a constituent of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) — when non-existent, it is exactly the same. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.7.82)

children.text: aprāpyakāriṇī yeṣāṃ cakṣu' śrotre ca te yathā /
children.translated_text: For those who [hold that] the eye and ear operate without contact, just as
they accept the <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood (validity) of that cognition — so it shall be [here too]. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.7.83)

children.text: tasmādasattve sattve vā sambandhasya yadeva na' /
children.translated_text: Therefore, whether the relation exists or not, whatever cognition arises for us

children.text: jāyetābhaṅguraṃ jñāna tasyaiva syāt pramāṇatā // Msv_5,7.84 //
children.translated_text: that is non-defective — that alone would have <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood (validity). (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.7.84)
The supposition of another [cause] is not justified, because of overextension.

children.text: pratibaddhasvabhāvaṃ hi pratibandhabalādeva pratibandhakamupasthāpayati, apratibanadhena tvanyakalpanāyāṃ na pratiniyame kāraṇamasti /
children.translated_text: For that which has a bound nature, by the force of that very binding, presents its binding [cause]; but in the supposition of another [cause] without binding, there is no ground for restriction.
Therefore, this cognition of the nighttime-sentence is simply not a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition). (79)
He refutes — 'sambandhasya.'
The meaning of '<s>prāmāṇya</s>' is 'being the instrument of valid cognition.'
And the word '<s>pramāṇa</s>' [means] instrument and means.
He demonstrates that the relation is not a cause in [establishing] validity — 'pratyakṣasya.' (80)

children.text: nanvindriyārtasannikarṣajameva pratyakṣamato nākāraṇaṃ prāmāṇye sambandha iti codayati---astīticedantena /
children.translated_text: Objection: Since perception is born of the contact of the sense organ with its object, therefore the relation is not a non-cause in [establishing] validity — he raises this objection with 'asti iti ced' and so forth.
He refutes — 'nānapekṣaṇāt.'
He demonstrates the non-dependence — 'na hi.'

children.text: nirūpito hi sambandha' pramāṇotpattau kāraṇamanumāne, na ceha tatheti ||81||
children.translated_text: For a relation that has been ascertained is a cause in the generation of inference as a <s>pramāṇa</s>, but here it is not so. (81)
But the ascertainment that comes after perception is not a constituent of <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood — hence he says 'yenāpi.' (82)

children.text: api cāprāpyakārīndriyavādipakṣe svarūpasattvamapi sambandhasya nāstyeva, ato yathā te pratyakṣajñānasya pramāṇatāmicchanti, evamihāpi bhaviṣyatītyata āha---aprāpyeti ||83||
children.translated_text: Moreover, on the view of those who hold that the senses operate without contact, even the very existence of the relation does not obtain. Therefore, just as they accept the <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood (validity) of perceptual cognition, so too it shall be here — hence he says 'aprāpya.' (83)

children.text: tenānādṛtyaiva sambaddhamutpannamasandigdhamaviparītaṃ ca deśādibhede 'pi jñānaṃ pramāṇamitayāśrayaṇīyamityāha---tasmāditi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, disregarding the relation entirely, a cognition that has arisen, is undoubting, and non-erroneous — even when there is difference of place and the like — should be relied upon as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) — hence he says 'tasmāt.'
'Jāyate' (arises) removes the invalidity characterized by non-arising; 'abhaṅguram' (non-defective) [removes] doubt and error. (84)
And no one disputes the <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood (validity) of this [arthāpatti];

children.text: bhedābhede visaṃvāda' kṛtastatra ca nirṇaya' // Msv_5,7.85 //
children.translated_text: the disagreement was about [its] difference or non-difference [from inference], and the determination regarding that has been made. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.7.85)

children.text: ṛte yatra ca sambandhād buddhareva na jāyate /
children.translated_text: And where, without the relation, the cognition itself does not arise,

children.text: tatra kiṃ kriyatāṃ so 'pi prāmāṇye naiva kāraṇam // Msv_5,7.86 //
children.translated_text: there, what can be done? That [relation] too is not a cause in [establishing] validity. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.7.86)

children.text: smṛtyā śrutiryā parikalpyate 'smin liṅgādibhiryā viniyojikā ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>śruti</s> (scripture) that is constructed through <s>smṛti</s> (tradition), that which is the enjoiner through <s>liṅga</s> (indicative marks) and the like,

children.text: phalādibhiryat paripūraṇaṃ ca sambandhadṛk tatra na kācidasti // Msv_5,7.87 //
children.translated_text: and the completion through results and the like — in those [cases] there is no perception of the relation at all. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.7.87)
Moreover, the dispute that <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> is extraordinary [i.e., contrary to common practice].

children.text: na hi tayā pravartamānānāṃ pravṛtti' pratihanyate /
children.translated_text: For the activity of those who proceed by means of it is not obstructed,
and the capacity to motivate action is validity.

children.text: anumānād bhedābhedayorasti vivāda', tatra cāsmābhi' kṛto nirṇaya ityāha---na cāpīti ||85||
children.translated_text: There is a dispute about whether [<s>arthāpatti</s>] is different from or identical with inference, and we have made the determination regarding that — hence he says 'na cāpi.' (85)
If so, then in inference too, the relation would turn out not to be a constituent — hence he says 'ṛte.'

children.text: tatra hi buddhirevāsati sambandhajñāne na jāyata iti tadutpattau kāraṇamāśrīyata eva /
children.translated_text: For there, the cognition itself does not arise in the absence of knowledge of the relation — therefore, [the relation] is necessarily resorted to as a cause of its generation.
But validity, even there, is simply [established by] the absence of sublation. (86)

children.text:
vedopayogamarthāpatterdarśayati---smṛtyeti /
bhūyān khalu vedabhāga' śrutārthāpattipramāṇaka' sa tāmantareṇa na sidhyeta, yathaiva hi pāṭhenābhivyaktā śrutirātmānaṃ labhate, evaṃ śrutārthāpattipramāṇakā hi /
yadāha---
'yathaiva pāṭha' pratipattyupāyastathaiva sāmarthyamapi śrutīnām /
tenaiva caikāṃ na samāmananti sahasrabhāgaṃ tu samāmaneyu' ||' iti /
yathā tāvadaṣṭakādiviṣayāṃ manvādismṛtimupalabhya tanmūlakāraṇānvicchāyāmasambhbhavatsu
bhramavipralipsānubhavapuṃvākyāntareṣu smṛte' svamūlakāraṇamantareṇānupapattyā śrutireva mūlatayā kalpyate /
tathā liṅgādibhi' svaviniyojikā śrutirupakalpyate---- yathā tāvat prakaraṇāmnāte mantre svādhyāyavidhyadhyāpite prayojanamantareṇānupapadyamāne kratvapekṣayā kaca sāmānyata' kratūpakārāvagatau viśeṣāpekṣāyāṃ mantraśaktinirīkṣayā yacchaknuyādityupabandhena śakyārtha
children.translated_text: He demonstrates the usefulness of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) for the <s>Veda</s> — 'smṛtī.' Indeed, a great portion of the <s>Veda</s> has <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> (presumption from what is heard) as its <s>pramāṇa</s>, and without it, that could not be established. For just as <s>śruti</s> (scripture) manifested through recitation obtains its own [authority], so too that which has <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> as its <s>pramāṇa</s>. As it is said: 'Just as recitation is the means of understanding, so too is the capacity of the <s>śrutis</s>; by that very [capacity] they do not recount a single [meaning], but would recount a thousandth part.' Thus, first, upon finding a <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) of <s>Manu</s> and others concerning the <s>aṣṭakā</s> rites and similar topics, in the search for its root cause — when error, deception, and the statements of other persons who have experienced [these] are impossible [as explanations] — by the impossibility [of the <s>smṛti</s> existing] without its own root cause, <s>śruti</s> (scripture) alone is postulated as the root. Similarly, the <s>śruti</s> that is its own enjoiner is postulated through <s>liṅga</s> (indicative marks) and the like — as follows: when a <s>mantra</s> mentioned in a context and learned through the injunction of Vedic study has no purpose [apparent], through the expectation of a rite and the general understanding of service to the rite, in the expectation of a specific [application], through examination of the power of the <s>mantra</s>, with the restriction 'whatever it is capable of' — the meaning amenable to its capacity —
All that and the rest would be incoherent, if this [<s>arthāpatti</s>] were not [accepted as] different from inference;

children.text: evaṃsvabhāvāpyanumānaśabdaṃ labheta cedasti yathepsitaṃ na' // Msv_5,7.88 //
children.translated_text: even if having such a nature, if it were to receive the designation 'inference,' then what we desire is established. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.7.88)

children.text:
iti arthāpattivārttikam /
viṣayā mantrasya viniyojikā śrutirukalpyate /
yathā barhirmantre 'nena lunīyāditi so 'yaṃ laiṅgiko viniyoga' /

children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the <s>Arthāpattivārttika</s> (section on presumption). The <s>śruti</s> that is the enjoiner of the scope of the <s>mantra</s> is postulated. As in the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass) <s>mantra</s>: 'By this one should cut' — that is the <s>laingika</s> (mark-based) application. But by the sentence: in that very <s>mantra</s>, the word 'dāmi' (cutting), being capable of [denoting] cutting, is applied through that <s>liṅga</s> (indicative mark), while the other words [are applied] through the sentence itself as their co-utterance. The contextual application, however, is [for example] of <s>samidh</s> (fuel-sticks) and the like from the context of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon sacrifices) — for they have an expectation of purpose, and the rite has an expectation of service. Thus, when there is this mutual expectation, 'by these one should serve the rite' — such a <s>śruti</s> is postulated. The application by position, however, is as follows: of the <s>mantra</s> called '<s>dadhirnāmāsi</s>' (thou art curds), which has been studied in connection with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites in the sequence of the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> (quiet oblation) — the <s>śruti</s> that 'by this one should serve the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s>' is heard, that 'the <s>adhvaryu</s> (priest) should perform these.' And in rites whose results and procedural details are not heard — such as the <s>Viśvajit</s>, <s>Saurya</s>, and the like — a <s>śruti</s> capable of completion is postulated: 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s>'; 'One who desires the splendor of <s>Brahman</s> should offer the <s>Saurya</s> oblation'; 'The procedural details are like those of the <s>Āgneya</s>.' The usefulness of <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> for the <s>Veda</s> is of this very kind, and abundantly so. And this cannot be established through inference alone. For here, no one has observed any relation between the postulated [śruti] and what is [otherwise] impossible. And inference does not occur without requiring a relation — therefore, <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) alone is the refuge here. 'Sambandhadṛk' — the seeing is figurative, applied to cognition. If <s>arthāpatti</s> is not accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s>, all this would be incoherent — hence he says 'tatsarvam.' But if, though different in definition, it is desired to be spoken of by the word 'inference' on account of the general [similarity to] inference — let that be; [for us] it is established that [arthāpatti] is a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> — hence he says 'evam.'
Thus, in the <s>Kāśikā</s> commentary composed by the teacher <s>Sucaritamiśra</s>, the chapter on <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is concluded.

children.translated_text: Now the <s>Abhāvapariccheda</s> (chapter on absence/non-existence). Here is the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'Even regarding absence, the condition of being a <s>pramāṇa</s> — [applies to] the meaning "does not exist," which is not in proximity [to any other <s>pramāṇa</s>].' But what is being defined by this? Not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, certainly. For it is not proper that a <s>pramāṇa</s> be defined by the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s>. If it is said that the absence of the previously stated <s>pramāṇas</s> is the definition — then this would be common to all <s>pramāṇas</s>, for all <s>pramāṇas</s> can be said to be 'absence of [other] <s>pramāṇas</s>' in the sense that each has the form of the absence of every other. And there is no single definition common to all [five] <s>pramāṇas</s>, by whose absence a sixth could be defined. Moreover — a <s>pramāṇa</s> is that which establishes some <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge). We do not know what is established by this [alleged sixth <s>pramāṇa</s>]. 'But it was stated: "the meaning 'does not exist,' which is not in proximity [to other <s>pramāṇas</s>]."' What does this mean? Does it mean: absence is the <s>pramāṇa</s> for [the cognition] 'does not exist' — an object not within the scope of perception and the rest? That is improper. 'Does not exist' — the meaning is: this is not cognized here. And it cannot be maintained that what is not cognized is a <s>prameya</s>. And of which <s>pramāṇa</s> is this the <s>prameya</s> — if of the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s>? No. For the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> is the non-arising of cognition. And that [non-arising] being a <s>pramāṇa</s> appears almost absurd. If it is held that — the cognition 'does not exist' is indisputably established for all worldly people and examiners, and [whether] the cognition lacks a [real external] object or has its own aspect as its object — this has already been discussed in the <s>Vijñānavāda</s> (idealist doctrine). Therefore, a <s>prameya</s> is postulated for the purpose of strengthening this very cognition. That is the domain of absence. Thus, they consider: the cognition 'does not exist' is the <s>pramāṇa</s>, and the absence of a pot and such is the <s>prameya</s>. For this very reason, they divide absence into four types: prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) and so forth. For division of a non-entity is not possible. But if absence is not accepted as a separate category (<s>tattvāntara</s>), then what is the absence of curd in milk — which they call prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>)? And so this is the absence of milk in curd — what is its support (<s>ālambana</s>)? If [one says] the ground itself — no, because of the unwanted consequence that it would apply even when a pot is present. If [one says] the bare ground alone is the support — then what separate category is established? The <s>prameya</s>-distinction is established [merely by different cognitions], and from the distinction of <s>prameya</s>, the distinction of <s>pramāṇa</s> [follows]. For the contact of the sense organs is only with existing things, not with absences. And even without the operation of that [sense-object contact], the arising of the cognition 'does not exist' is observed — as when, having seen merely the form of a house and such, upon going to another place and being asked about someone's absence, that absence is ascertained right then. Thus, this cognition 'does not exist,' arising even without sense-object contact, is not perceptual. Nor is there any inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that generates it. If it is said that non-apprehension is the inferential mark — no, because [non-apprehension] is not cognized. For an inferential mark whose nature is unknown does not cause the inference of the inferred object. Nor [does it work] when the relation [between mark and marked] is unknown. And non-apprehension, when known as such, does not illuminate [merely] real absence. Because that [non-apprehension] too, being of the nature of absence, would require dependence on another of its own kind, leading to infinite regress. Therefore, this [cognition of absence] must stand as a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>, for the purpose of establishing the non-confusion of existing things. And among the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, it is well known that this is indeed the sixth <s>pramāṇa</s>. Therefore, this text has as its purpose the definition of that [sixth <s>pramāṇa</s>]. That is improper. For by this [text], a <s>pramāṇa</s> is not [established]. For from the text, only the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> is ascertained, not a <s>pramāṇa</s>. And even when 'does not exist' is uttered, ordinary people understand only the absence of a <s>prameya</s>, not any positive <s>prameya</s>. Therefore, a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> is not in accordance with the text, nor does it accord with reasoning. For the examination of whether an already-established cognition is a <s>pramāṇa</s> or not is proper. But there is no cognition 'does not exist' other than the apprehension of the bare ground. For that very [cognition] manifests in two ways: accompanied by something and unaccompanied. When the ground is apprehended as accompanied by a pot and such, the usage 'the pot exists' proceeds. But when mere [ground] alone is cognized, [the usage is] 'does not exist.' Nor should it be said that even when subtle entities are present, the cognition of the mere [ground] is observed, and therefore even there [the cognition] 'does not exist' manifests — for that very [cognition] manifests in two ways. For the cognition of the mere [ground] is of two kinds: when the counter-positive is visible, or when it is invisible. Therein, the cognition of the mere [ground] when the counter-positive is visible — that itself is the non-existence of the pot and such. Even for those who accept absence as a <s>prameya</s>, the absence is ascertained precisely from the non-seeing of the visible [counter-positive] as 'does not exist.' Therefore, this cognition of the mere [ground], established by all schools, is itself designated as 'does not exist.' And whatever is accepted as the cause of absence — let that be accepted as the cause of this cognition of the mere [ground], which is established by both parties. Therefore, precisely where there was previously a composite cognition [of ground-with-pot], there, upon the occurrence of a different kind of cause, the cognition of the mere [ground] alone arises — not the absence of pot and such as a [separate entity]. And this must necessarily be accepted. For otherwise, absence cannot be grasped — since the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> is the <s>pramāṇa</s> for it, and [absence] cannot be established by what is not [itself] grasped. For even a person in deep sleep has the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s>, yet there is no ascertainment 'does not exist.' Therefore, ungrasped non-seeing does not produce the ascertainment of absence; and the non-grasping of that [non-seeing] too, being of the nature of absence, [would require] another non-seeing — thus leading to infinite regress. And if mere existing [non-seeing] itself produces the ascertainment, then even when non-seeing has ceased, formerly <s>Devadatta</s>
Where the five-fold [system of] <s>pramāṇas</s> does not arise with respect to the nature of a thing,

children.translated_text: [the cognition] 'did not exist' would not arise. But this does happen sometimes. He who was not seen somewhere, upon being seen again in that very place — even without non-seeing, the prior knowledge of absence [persists]. If there were no non-seeing, that [knowledge of prior absence] would not arise. Therefore, it must be said that the knowledge [of absence] is born precisely from the reflection on prior non-seeing. And thus, only when [non-seeing] is grasped does it illuminate absence. But in the grasping [itself], there is the problem of infinite regress. However, if the cognition of the mere [ground] itself is accepted as non-seeing, there is no fault. For that [cognition], being self-luminous and constituting the result [of knowledge], does not require another illumination. Therefore, the experience of the mere [ground] alone is designated as the absence of that [object]. Hence, absence is not a separate <s>prameya</s>. Nor is the cognition 'does not exist' a <s>pramāṇa</s> — [it might be] like an illusion, and thus we do not know what is being defined here. Here he says — 'What is not known here? As you yourself have stated, from the text, the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> is ascertained. Some indeed maintain a [sixth] <s>pramāṇa</s> called absence — the effort of the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> is precisely for refuting that.' How is it refuted by this? Listen. What some say — 'the meaning "does not exist," which is not in proximity [to other <s>pramāṇas</s>]' — [meaning] absence is the <s>pramāṇa</s> for what is not within the scope of perception and the rest — that is not so, for that is the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> — meaning: it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>. And the reason for its non-<s>pramāṇa</s>-hood has been stated. This too is not tenable. If this meaning is explained in accordance with the text, then there is a clear contradiction with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> elsewhere. For then, [the statement that] 'the enumeration pertaining to <s>pramāṇas</s> divides practical usage' would amount to refuting the opposing view by mere assertion — and that is correct. Therefore, this must be explained [differently]. Here he says — '<s>pramāṇa</s>' etc. The meaning is this: this is precisely the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>. As for what was said — 'how can that [sixth <s>pramāṇa</s>] be defined by its absence?' — True. The word '<s>pramāṇa</s>' is not used with the intention of [referring to] <s>pramāṇa</s> in general, but rather — what does it mean? — the absence of the previously stated five-fold <s>pramāṇa</s> system. And there is one common property (<s>upadhāna</s>) of the five — namely, 'existence' (<s>bhāva</s>), for all [five] are positive <s>pramāṇas</s>. Therefore, the <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood of absence [is defined as operating] with respect to positive <s>pramāṇas</s>—

The <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood of absence [applies] where the five-fold [system of positive] <s>pramāṇas</s> does not arise with respect to the real nature of a thing, for the purpose of cognizing the non-existence of that thing. (<s>Mīmāṃsāślokavārttika</s> 5.8.1)
