Therefore, it is established that absence is different from a <s>pramāṇa</s> having the nature of existence — he concludes — 'tasmāt' etc. // 55 //

children.text:
vedopayogamabhāvasya darśayati---karmāṇīti /
yo 'yaṃ sarvakarmaṇāṃ phalāsaṅkara' parasparāsaṅkaraśca paraspamaṅgāṅgibhāvābhāva', nāsāvabhāvaprāmā
children.translated_text: He demonstrates the usefulness of absence for the <s>Veda</s> — 'karmāṇi' etc. The non-confusion of fruits of all ritual actions, the non-confusion with one another, and the absence of subsidiary-principal relationship with each other — this, without the <s>pramāṇa</s> of absence,
this [matter] has been investigated here through reasoning and scripture, having divided the <s>pramāṇas</s> into a group of six in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>;

children.text: tato 'dhikaṃ yad dvayamiṣṭamanyairbhedo na tasyetyapi siddhametat // Msv_5,8.57 //
children.translated_text: the two additional [pramāṇas] that are accepted by others — it has also been established that there is no difference of those. // Msv_5,8.57 //

children.text: iha bhavati śatādau sambhavādyā sahasrānmatiraviyutabāvāt sānumānādabhinnā /
children.translated_text: Here, in hundred and the like, the cognition called <s>sambhava</s> (inclusion) arising from a thousand — since it is not separated from being, it is not different from inference and the like.

children.text: jagati bahu na tathyaṃ nityamaitihyamuktaṃ bhavati tu yadi satyaṃ nāgamād bhidyate tat // Msv_5,8.58 //
children.translated_text: In the world, much that is called <s>aitihya</s> (tradition) is not true constantly; but if it is true, it is not different from <s>āgama</s> (scripture). // Msv_5,8.58 //
would not be established without [the pramāṇa of absence].
(As stated—
as far as, in the manner stated—) 'iha' etc.
indicates the <s>Veda</s>. // 56 //

children.text: nanu ca vyāsamatānusāriṇopamānātiriktaṃ pramāṇadvayamupavarṇitam, ṛṣiṇā ca sambhavaitihyayorapi pramāṇatvamāśritam, tatparityāge kāraṇaṃ vaktavyamata āha----yuktīti /

children.translated_text: For the group of six <s>pramāṇas</s> alone is consistent with reasoning.
And it conforms to scripture (<s>āgama</s>).

children.text: āgamaśca mīmāṃsātantram, ato yuktyāgamābhyāmiha śābare bhāṣye pramāṇaṣaṭkameva pravivicya tarkitam /
children.translated_text: And the scripture is the <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> system. Therefore, through reasoning and scripture, in this <s>Śabara</s> <s>Bhāṣya</s>, the group of six <s>pramāṇas</s> alone has been investigated and determined.
The two additional [<s>pramāṇas</s>] that are desired [by others] are subsumed within these very [six]. // 57 //

Objection: But two <s>pramāṇas</s> beyond analogy have been described following the opinion of <s>Vyāsa</s>, and by the sage [<s>Jaimini</s>], the <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood of <s>sambhava</s> (inclusion) and <s>aitihya</s> (tradition) too has been relied upon. The reason for abandoning them must be stated — therefore he says — 'yukti' etc.

children.text:
(ka'?kva) punastasyāntargatirata āha---iha bhavatīti /
yā tāvat sahasrācchate mati' sambhavākhyaṃ pramāṇamiṣyate sānumānānna bhidyate /
sahasrācchatamaviyutibhāvādavinābhāvādavagamyate /
atastāvadanumānānna bhidyate /
aitihyapramāṇamuktaṃ tāvadasatyameva /
nidhiprāptyasurakanyāvaśīkaraṇādi, draupadīpañcabhartṛketyādi , yadi tat satyaṃ tadāgamād (na) bhidyate /
āptāgamo hyasau /
uktaṃ ca--- 'puruṣoktirapi śroturāgamatvaṃ prapadyate' iti /
ato 'numānāgamayorantarbhāvānna sambhavaitihyayo' pṛthagupanyāsa' siddha'||
children.translated_text: Where then is their subsumption? Therefore he says — 'iha bhavati' etc. The cognition of a hundred from a thousand, which is accepted as the <s>pramāṇa</s> called <s>sambhava</s> (inclusion), is not different from inference. [For] a hundred is cognized from a thousand through the inseparability [of the part from the whole], i.e., through <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance). Therefore, to begin with, it is not different from inference. The <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>aitihya</s> (tradition) that is spoken of — that, to begin with, is simply untrue: such as finding a treasure, gaining power over celestial maidens, and the like; '<s>Draupadī</s> had five husbands' and such. If that is true, then it is not different from <s>āgama</s> (scripture). For that [tradition, when true,] is [based on] the <s>āgama</s> of trustworthy persons. As it was said: 'Even the utterance of a person acquires the status of <s>āgama</s> for the hearer.' Therefore, since <s>sambhava</s> and <s>aitihya</s> are subsumed under inference and <s>āgama</s>, their separate enumeration is not warranted.
Thus, in the <s>Kāśikā</s> commentary composed by the teacher <s>Sucaritamiśra</s>, the chapter on absence (<s>abhāvapariccheda</s>) is concluded.
Now [begins] the <s>Citrākṣepa</s> (objection regarding the <s>Citrā</s> sacrifice).
Previously, the injunctions whose fruits pertain to the next world were objected to by others;
now, the objection regarding this-worldly [fruits] is stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras). // Msv_5,9.1 //

children.text:
bhāṣyapāṭho vicārya',atra bhāṣyam--- 'nanu bhavantvanyāni pramāṇāni, śabdastu na pramāṇam, kuta'? animittaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvāt' iti /
asyārtha'--- yadyapi sarvapramāṇāvyabhicārānna pramāṇasāmānayabhāvinā dharmeṇa śabdo 'pi na pramāṇam, viśeṣeṇa tvātmabhāvinā dharmeṇāpramāṇam /
tathā hi citrayā paśavo bhāvyanta iti citrayā yajetetyasyāratha' /
kṛtacitrasyāpi yajamānasyānantaramavikalasakalendriyairapi paśavo na dṛśyante /
tanna nūnamiṣṭi' paśuphaleti bhavati mati' /
tadidamuktam 'animittaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvāt' iti /
kimuktaṃ bhavati--- upalambhanāni hi cakṣurādīni paśūnāṃ vidyante /
na ca paśukāmeṣṭyamantaraṃ paśava upalabhyante /
tasmāduktavisaṃvādādapramāṇaṃ citrācodaneti /
sa punarayamākṣepo gatārtha upalakṣyate /
codanāsūtre hi 'nanvatathābhūtam' ityādinā bhāṣyakāreṇākṣepaparihārāvuktau /
ata' punaruktamidamityāśaṅkyāha---- paraloka iti /
asyārtha' paralokaphalā hi tatra svargakāmo yajetetyevamādicodanā vedabāhyaboddhādiparamatenākṣiptā' /
idānīmaihikaphalāścitrādicodanā ākṣipyante /
nanūbhayīmapi codanāmākṣeptuṃ śakyata eva vākyatvādayo hetava' /
ta eva tatra bhāṣyakāreṇa 'yat kiñcana laukikaṃ vanacam' iti darśayatāntarṇītā' /
vārtikakṛtāpi---'yadi vā puruṣādhīnaprāmāṇyā' sarvacodanā' iti vivṛtā' /
tasmādasadetat paralokaphalā eva tatrākṣiptā iti /
yadapi cedanīmaihikākṣepa ityuktaṃ tadayuktam, ihāpi ca---'evaṃ dṛṣṭāpacārasya vedasya svargādyapi phalaṃ nāstīti manyāmaha' iti sarvākṣepa' kṛta' /
vārtikakāreṇāpi ca
'evaṃ satyagnihotrādivākyeṣvapi mṛṣārthatā'
iti vadatā /
tasmādubhayatrāpyubhayākṣepameva nyāyyaṃ manyante /
keyaṃ vyavasthā /
atrocyate /
satyamubhayatrāpyabhayākṣepa',
tathāpi hetubhedādapaunaruktyam /
tathāhi--- tatra vākyatvādaya' parairuktā ākṣepahetava',
children.translated_text: The reading of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is to be examined. Here the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [states]: 'Let there be other <s>pramāṇas</s>; but the word (<s>śabda</s>) is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Why? Because of being an apprehension of what exists without a cause.' Its meaning is: Although, due to the non-deviation of all <s>pramāṇas</s>, the word too is not a non-<s>pramāṇa</s> by virtue of a property common to all <s>pramāṇas</s>, it is specifically a non-<s>pramāṇa</s> by virtue of a property peculiar to itself. Namely: the meaning of 'by <s>citrā</s>, animals are to be consecrated' is 'one should sacrifice with <s>citrā</s>.' But even when the sacrificer has performed the <s>citrā</s> [rite], immediately afterward, even with all sense organs unimpaired, the animals are not seen. Hence the thought arises: 'Surely the <s>iṣṭi</s> (sacrifice) does not have animals as its fruit.' This is what was said: 'because of being an apprehension of what exists without a cause.' What is meant is: the organs of apprehension — the eyes and the like — for animals do exist. Yet animals are not apprehended immediately after the sacrifice aimed at obtaining animals. Therefore, due to the stated contradiction, the injunction regarding <s>citrā</s> is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>. But this objection is recognized as having its purpose already served [by a previous discussion]. For in the <s>codanā</s> (injunction) <s>sūtra</s>, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) has stated the objection and its resolution through 'but that which is not of that nature' and the like. Therefore, suspecting that this is a repetition, he says — 'paraloka' etc. Its meaning is: the injunctions whose fruits pertain to the next world — such as 'one who desires heaven should sacrifice' and the like — were objected to there according to the doctrine of non-Vedic thinkers and others. Now, the injunctions with this-worldly fruits — the <s>citrā</s> and the like — are being objected to. Objection: But both kinds of injunctions can be objected to — for reasons such as being sentences [of human origin] and the like apply [to both]. Those very [reasons] were subsumed by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> there, when he showed 'whatever worldly utterance.' The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> (Kumārila) too elaborated: 'If the validity of all injunctions depends on persons.' Therefore, it is incorrect that only injunctions with other-worldly fruits were objected to there. And what is said now — that this is an objection regarding this-worldly [fruits] — that too is incorrect, for here too: 'Thus, of the <s>Veda</s> whose observed [promises are] violated, even the fruit of heaven and the like does not exist — so we hold' — a comprehensive objection was made. And the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> too, in saying 'Thus, even in the sentences about <s>agnihotra</s> and the like, there would be falsity of meaning' — [makes the same point]. Therefore, in both places, it is proper to hold that there is a comprehensive objection [covering both kinds]. What then is the [basis for the] distinction? To this it is replied: True, there is a comprehensive objection in both places. Nevertheless, because of the difference in the reasons, there is no repetition. Namely: there, the reasons for the objection stated by the opponents are being sentences [of human origin] and the like,
the injunctions regarding the fruit of animals in the <s>citrā</s> and the like are false;
because even in the section on perception and the like, there is inconsistency of the content with those [injunctions]. // Msv_5,9.2 //

children.text:
idānīṃ tuśabdaśaktiparāmarśadvāreṇābhyantarā eva hetava upapatsyante /
tathā coktam---
ānantaryamanuktaṃ cenna sāmarthyāvabodhanāt /
iti /
sāmarthyaṃ hi sarvākhyātānāmarthaṃ bruvatāṃ sahakāri /
tad yadyapi neṣṭiranantaphaleti śruti', tathāpyarthasāmarthyātadavagamyate, kathamaparathā'yadāsau vidyamānāsīt tadā palaṃ na dattavatī, kālāntare punarasatī kathaṃ dāsyati' iti na ca paśavo 'nantasamabhavadbhāvanā', svargo hi nānākṣiptaviśiṣṭadehendriyādiparigraho bhavitumutsahate, ato mābhūdanantaram, amī puna' paśava' sambhavanti yajamānasyātraiveti svahetusamanantaramanupalabhyamānā dṛṣṭapratigrahādihetvantarā' śrutacitrādiphalatayā na śakyante 'vagantum /
ayameva tu śabdaśaktiparāmarśo vārtikakṛtā tārkikaprakriyāmanuvidadhānena 'na vā paśuphale'tyādinā sādhanaprayogairupadarśita' /
tadevamaihikaphalāsu citrācodanāsvākṣiptāsu tatsāmānyāditarāsu tathātvamiti punarapyagnihotrādicodanākṣepe 'vatiṣṭhate /
sa cāyamaihikākṣepadvāreṇāpinocyate /
ata eva caihikākṣepa ityuktam /
etaduktaṃ bhavati--- aihikaphalānāmāmuṣmikaphalānāṃ cāyamaihikākṣepapuraskāreṇaivākṣepa', yadāmuṣmikasvargādi tanmā nāma karmānantaramupalabhyatāmaihikaphalaṃ tu paśvādi kiṃ nopalabhyate, na cedamupalabhyate, tanna nūnaṃ tat phalamiti aihikaphalakarmacodanāvyabhicāreṇānyāsāmapi paralokaphalānāṃ tatsāmānyādākṣepa' /
pūrvaṃ tu tā' parata' prāmāṇyamāśritya paroktairaiva vākyatvādibhirhetubhirākṣiptā' /

children.translated_text: That has been stated — 'by the opponent.'
He states another resolution — 'the <s>sūtra</s>.'

children.text: ayamabhiprāya'--- codanāsūtre bhāṣyakṛtā sūtrakāreṇa vakṣyamāṇākṣepaparihārāvanāgatāvekṣaṇena pratijñāsamarthanārthabhupavarṇitau /
children.translated_text: The intention is this: In the <s>Codanāsūtra</s> (aphorism on injunction), the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) described the challenge and resolution that the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> (aphorist) was going to state, looking ahead, for the purpose of supporting the thesis.

children.text: idānīṃ tu sūtrakāreṇa svayamevocyata iti tenedameva sarvacodanākṣepakṣetramityuktamiti ||1||
children.translated_text: But now, the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> himself states it — therefore, by him, this alone has been stated as the field of challenge for all injunctions. // 1 //

Now, through the consideration of the power of words, internal reasons themselves will be justified. And thus it has been stated: 'If the immediacy is not stated — [still it is understood] because of the comprehension through capacity.' For 'capacity' (<s>sāmarthya</s>) is a co-operative factor of all finite verbs that express their meaning. Therefore, although the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) [says] 'the <s>iṣṭi</s> (sacrifice) has inexhaustible results,' still, through the capacity of the meaning, this is understood — for how otherwise could [the injunction], when it was existing, not have given the result, and at a later time, being non-existent, how will it give [the result]? And animals are not [beings whose] <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force) has arisen immediately — for heaven, involving the possession of a supremely excellent body, sense-organs, and the like, is not able to come about. Therefore, let there be no immediacy [of the result]; but these animals do come into being for the sacrificer right here — and, not being apprehended immediately after their own cause, and having no other cause such as a seen acceptance-ceremony, they cannot be understood as having some other result like the <s>citrā</s> (the varied [sacrifice]). But this very consideration of the power of words was demonstrated by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> (author of the <s>Vārttika</s>), who follows the logician's method, through inferential arguments beginning with 'nor is <s>citrā</s> one whose result is animals.' Thus, when the <s>citrā</s> and other injunctions having this-worldly results have been challenged, through the commonality with those, the other [injunctions] too have the same status. And this [challenge] is stated even through the medium of the this-worldly challenge. For this very reason, it was called 'the this-worldly challenge.' What this amounts to is: This challenge — through the precedence of the this-worldly challenge — applies to both injunctions with this-worldly results and those with other-worldly results. As for the other-worldly [result] such as heaven — let that indeed not be apprehended immediately after the ritual action; but the this-worldly result such as animals — why is that not apprehended? If this is not apprehended, then surely that is not the result. Thus, through the non-deviation of the injunctions of rituals with this-worldly results, the challenge extends to the other [injunctions] with other-worldly results as well, through their commonality. But previously, those [injunctions] were challenged by the reasons already stated by the opponent — such as sentence-hood — relying on the authority-from-extrinsic-factors.

children.text:
atra parihāre pūrvokta evākṣepaheturiti, tamupanyasyati--- citreti phalānītyantena /
ayamartha'--- citrāpaśuphalatvādiviṣayāścodanā dharmiṇya'
children.translated_text: In this resolution, the very reason for challenge stated previously [is taken up] — he presents it: '<s>citrā</s>' ending in 'results.' The meaning is: the <s>citrā</s> and other injunctions pertaining to varied animal-results are the property-bearers (<s>dharmin</s>),
if it is like this, then it is false — as is seen in the speech of one who wishes to deceive;

children.text: nadītīre phalānīti tatrādṛsyāni tāni cet // Msv_5,9.3 //
children.translated_text: 'There are fruits on the riverbank' — if those are not seen there. // 3 //

children.text: na vā paśuphalā citrā svakāle tadadānata' /
children.translated_text: Or the <s>citrā</s> is not one whose result is animals, because of the non-giving of those at the time;

children.text: snānabhujyādivat te 'pi tatsādhyā na bhavanti vā // Msv_5,9.4 //
children.translated_text: like bathing, eating, and the like — or those [animals] too are not accomplished by it. // 4 //
Because of its non-existence at the time of their production — like heaven, satisfaction, pleasure, and the like;
by dissimilarity in both [arguments] — pleasure and rubbing would apply. // 5 //
And the immediacy, even though not stated — [is understood] because of the comprehension through capacity.

children.text:
mṛṣeti sādhyo dharma' /
adhikṛtai' pravṛttiyogyairapi pratyakṣādibhirarthānavagate' /
yadīdṛśaṃ tanmṛṣā--- yathā vipralipsorvaca' /
ādiśabdenāgnihotrādiviṣayā api codanā' pakṣīkaroti /
nanu vipralipsuvākyamatra dṛṣṭānta' /
na ca tanniyamena pratyakṣādyasaṅgatārthamasatyaṃ ca /

children.translated_text: Therefore, the example is deficient in both [respects].
Hence he says — 'there.'
Only a statement employed with respect to a false object — such as the riverbank statement — is the example here.

children.text: prāyeṇa caitrañjātīyakaṃ vipralipsureva prayuṅkta iti vipralipsorityuktamiti ||2,3||
children.translated_text: And because such types of statements are generally employed only by one who wishes to deceive, 'of one who wishes to deceive' was said. // 2, 3 //

'False' is the property to be proved. Because the meaning is not ascertained by perception and the like, even though they are competent [cognizers] who are engaged. If it is like this, then it is false — like the speech of one who wishes to deceive. By the word 'and the like' he includes injunctions pertaining to the <s>Agnihotra</s> and similar [rituals] within the thesis as well. Now, the speech of the deceiver is the example here. But that is not necessarily one whose meaning is incompatible with perception and the like, nor is it necessarily false.

children.text:
idānīmaihikākṣepa ityuktaṃ vivṛṇoti--- na veti vadantena /
citreṣṭirdharmiṇī, na paśuphaleti sādhyam, svakāle paśvadānāt, snānādivaditi /
prayogāntaramāha--- te 'pīti /
te paśavo na citrāsādhyā' , citrotpattāvasadbhāvāt svargatṛptisukhādivat /
ādiśabdenātra bhojanajanyā tṛptirabhipretā /
etau ca prayogau 'neṣṭi' paśuphalā,karmakāle ca karmaphalena bhavitavyam' iti bhāṣyoktau veditavyāviti /
children.translated_text: And these two arguments should be understood as stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'the <s>iṣṭi</s> does not have animals as its result, and the result must exist at the time of the ritual action.'

children.text: atrānantaraṃ 'yatkālaṃ hi mardanaṃ tatkālameva mardanasukham' iti bhāṣyakāreṇoktam, tad vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntatayā prayogadvaye yojayati--- vaidharmyeṇeti /
children.translated_text: Immediately after this, what was stated by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> — 'for at whatever time there is rubbing, at that very time there is the pleasure of rubbing' — he joins that to both arguments as a dissimilarity example — 'by dissimilarity.'

children.text: citrā na paśuphalā paśavo na tatsādhyā ityubhayatrāpi prayoge vaidharmyeṇa sukhamardane bhavetām, īdṛśī cātra vaidharmyaracanā, yadyatsādhyaṃ tattatsakāle prasūte, mardanamiva sukham /
children.translated_text: In both arguments — that the <s>citrā</s> does not have animals as its result, and that the animals are not accomplished by it — by dissimilarity, pleasure and rubbing would apply. And the dissimilarity construction here is: whatever is accomplished [by something], that is produced at the time of that [cause], like pleasure [from] rubbing.

children.text: yacca yatsādhyaṃ tat tadutpattau bhavatyeva sukhamiva mardanotpattāviti ||4,5||
children.translated_text: And whatever is accomplished [by something], that exists at the time of the production of that — like pleasure at the time of the production of rubbing. // 4, 5 //

Now he elaborates what was called 'the this-worldly challenge' — 'nor' with the word 'stating.' The <s>citrā</s> sacrifice is the property-bearer; 'not having animals as the result' is the property to be proved; because of the non-giving of animals at the time; like bathing and the like. He states another argument — 'those too.' Those animals are not accomplished by the <s>citrā</s>, because of [the <s>citrā</s>'s] non-existence at the time of their production — like heaven, satisfaction, pleasure, and the like. By the word 'and the like' here, the satisfaction born from eating is intended.

children.text:
nanūktivisaṃvādādaprāmāṇyamuktam /
na ca kiñcidiha visaṃvāda', na hi kṛte karmaṇi tāvatyeva phalena bhavitavyamiti śabdo brūte, kintu asyedaṃ
children.translated_text: Now, the non-authority was stated because of the discrepancy between the statement and [the observed result]. But there is no discrepancy here at all. For the word does not say that the result must exist at the very same time the action is performed — rather, 'this is the result of this action'
— that [immediacy] has been communicated by that [capacity] which is a portion of the word. // 6 //
Because of not specifying a later time, and also because of the nature of ritual action,
immediacy is a qualification of the <s>citrā</s> and the like that are being challenged. // 7 //
Here, to begin with, there is discrepancy, and in what follows, contradiction;
for the becoming-ashes that is seen here contradicts the going to heaven. // 8 //

children.text:
phalamiti /
etāvati ca paryavasānāt /
ata' kālāntare phalaṃ dāsyati /
tadetaduktam--- 'kālāntare phalaṃ dāsyatīti cet'iti, tadetadāha---ānantaryamiti /
pariharati--- nasāmarthyeti /
sākṣādanuktsayānantaryasyāpyatra sāmarthyenāvabodhanaṃ kṛtam,yaiva hyasyedaṃ phalamityuktaṃ tadaivamarthādevāvagamyate anantaramanena bhavitavyamiti /

children.translated_text: For how could what does not exist at a later time give the result at a later time?

children.text: nanvevamapi sāmarthyalabhyamānantaryamanantaraphalānupalambhanena bādhyatām, aviśeṣapravṛttā tu codanā kataṃ bādhyate ata āha--- śabdeti /
children.translated_text: Now, even so, let the immediacy obtained through capacity be sublated by the non-apprehension of the immediate result; but how can an injunction that operates without distinction be sublated? Hence he says — 'the word.'

children.text: na hi sāmarthyaṃ nāma pṛthak pramāṇam, api tarhi sarvākhyātānāmarthaṃ bruvatāṃ śakti' sahakāriṇīti śabdaikadeśa eva /
children.translated_text: For capacity is not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>; rather, it is the power (<s>śakti</s>) co-operative with all finite verbs that express their meaning — and thus it is merely a portion of the word [itself].

children.text: ata' sruvāvadānamivāpyadravyeṣvarthādanantarameva phalaṃ niścīyata iti tadbodhe 'pi śābdabodho bhavatyeveti ||6||
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as in the case of the <s>sruva</s> (ladle) oblation and the like, with respect to non-material [offerings], the result is determined as [arising] immediately — and in the cognition of that too, verbal cognition indeed occurs. // 6 //

'the result' — and since [the meaning] terminates at this much. Therefore, [the action] will give the result at a later time. This is what was stated: 'if it will give the result at a later time.' He states this — 'immediacy.' He resolves — 'not — because of the comprehension through capacity.' Even though the immediacy is not directly stated, its comprehension here has been accomplished through capacity. For the very [statement] 'this is the result of this' — from the capacity of that very meaning, this is understood: 'it must come about immediately after [the action].'
For this further reason too, immediacy is understood — hence he says 'a later time.'

children.text: yadi hyatra phalaṃ dāsyatīti ḷṅśroṣyat tadā tatsāmarthyena kalpanā kācidapyabhaviṣyat /
children.translated_text: For if [the scripture] were to hear [i.e., employ] the optative (<s>liṅ</s>) form 'it will give the result,' then some postulation through its capacity might arise.

children.text: adya punarasyedaṃ karmaṇa' phalamiti paryavasite vacasi sarvakarmaṇāmanantaraphalopalambhād vaidikasyāpi citrādeścodyamānasyāpi karmaṇastatsvābhāvyādānantaryaṃ viśeṣaṇatayāvatiṣṭhata iti ||7||
children.translated_text: But now, when the statement terminates at 'this is the result of this action,' because of the observation of immediate results for all [ordinary] actions, the immediacy stands as a qualification for even the <s>Vedic</s> <s>citrā</s> and other ritual actions being challenged, because of their common nature with [ordinary] actions. // 7 //

children.text:
atrānantaramaparaṃ bhāṣyam--- 'dṛṣṭaviruddhamapi kiñcit vaidikaṃ vacanaṃ 'sa eṣa yajñāyudhī yajamāno 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokaṃ yātī'ti /
tad yena viśeṣeṇoktaṃ tamāha---atreti /
atra hi citrādivākyeṣūktivisaṃvādādaprāmāṇyuktam /
uttaratra yajñāyudhivākye pratyakṣādivirodha iti virodhamabhidyotayati--- svargayāna iti /
yajamānasya niratiśayānandātmana' svargādatidūramapabhraṣṭo bhasmībhāva' pratyakṣamupalabhyate, citrādicodanā
children.translated_text: Immediately after this, there is another <s>Bhāṣya</s> [passage]: 'Even a <s>Vedic</s> statement contradicted by what is seen — "This sacrificer, armed with sacrificial implements, goes directly to the heavenly world."' He states the distinguishing feature by which this was said — 'here.' For here, in the case of the <s>citrā</s> and similar statements, the non-authority was stated because of discrepancy between statement and [observation]. In what follows — in the <s>yajñāyudhi</s> (armed-with-sacrificial-implements) statement — [there is] contradiction with perception and the like. He brings out the contradiction — 'the going to heaven.' The becoming-ashes of the sacrificer, who is infinitely far removed from heaven — which is of the nature of unsurpassed bliss — is directly perceived. The <s>citrā</s> and other injunctions
The <s>yajñāyudhi</s> (sacrificial-implements) statement is false, because of contradiction with perception;
the stone-statement [is the example] by similarity; the speech of a trustworthy person [is the example] by dissimilarity. // 9 //

children.text: śarīdād yadi cānya' syānnāsau yajñāyudhī bhavet /
children.translated_text: And if there were someone other than the body, he would not be 'armed with sacrificial implements';

children.text: na cāsya yajamānatvaṃ sadbhāvo 'pi ca durlabha' // Msv_5,9.10 //
children.translated_text: nor would his status as a sacrificer [be possible], and even his existence is hard to establish. // 10 //

children.text: su tvanantaraphalānupalambhamātraṃ na tu viruddhopalambha' kaścidastīti syādapi kālāntare phalakalpanā, bhasmībhūtaṃ tu śarīraṃ kālāntare 'pi svargaṃ lokaṃ yāsyatīti na sambhavatīti pūrvasmād viśeṣa' ||8||
children.translated_text: [In the former case,] there was merely the non-apprehension of the immediate result — not the apprehension of something contradictory — so there could still be the postulation of the result at a later time. But that the body which has become ashes will go to the heavenly world at a later time too — that is not possible — this is the distinguishing point from the former. // 8 //

children.text: aparamapi ca 'evañjātīyakaṃ pramāṇaviruddhaṃ vacanamapramāṇam--- ambuni majjantyalābūni, grāvāṇa' plavanta iti yathā ' iti bhāṣyam, tad vyācaṣṭeyajñeti vākyamantena /
yajñāyudhavaco dharmī, mṛṣeti sādhyo dharma', pratyakṣavirodhāt, yatpratyakṣaviruddhaṃ tanmithyā, yathā grāvāṇa' plavanta iti śilā vākyaṃ sādharmyeṇa yatheti darśayitavyamiti /
children.translated_text: The <s>yajñāyudhi</s> statement is the property-bearer; 'false' is the property to be proved; because of contradiction with perception; whatever is contradicted by perception is false — like the stone-statement 'stones float' — to be shown by similarity with 'like.'
He states the dissimilarity example — 'by dissimilarity.'
'Whatever is not false is not contradicted by perception — like the speech of a trustworthy person.'

children.text: pūrvaṃ tu mardanasukhayorvaidharmye dṛṣṭāntaratayopanyāsācchilāvākyamapi vaidharmyeṇa bhāṣyakṛtoktamiti bhrāntimapanetuṃ sādharmyavaidharmyaviveko vārtikakṛtā darśita' ||9||
children.translated_text: But previously, when the dissimilarity of pleasure and rubbing was presented as a different example, the stone-statement too, stated by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, might be confused as [being an example] by dissimilarity — to remove this confusion, the distinction of similarity and dissimilarity was shown by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>. // 9 //

Moreover, [there is] also [this <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage]: 'A statement of this kind, contradicted by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, is non-authoritative — like "gourds sink in water, stones float."' He explains the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — '<s>yajña</s>' ending in 'statement.'

children.text:
nanu pratyakṣavirodhāditi hetusiddha eva, asti hi paralokaphalabhoktā cetana' karmaṇāṃ kartā, sa svargaṃ lokaṃ yāsyatīti /
tamevābhipretya svargaṃ lokaṃ yāsyatītyuktam /
ata' ko virodho 'ta āha---śarīrāditi /
yadi hi śarīrādanyaścetano bhavet, bhavedapi na tasya yajñāyudhairasti kaścit sambandhaprakāra', śarīrasyaiva tu srukkapālādiyajñāyudhai' sambandha', yadyajñāyudhī yajamāna iti tadabhiprāyeṇa matvarthasaṃyogo ghaṭate /
api ca 'sa eṣa' ityaparokṣapratinirdeśa', so 'pi śarīrasyaiva pratyakṣatvādupapanno nātmana' /
tadetadapi bhāṣyakāreṇoktaṃ hi --- 'śarīrakaṃ vyapadiśati'iti /
kiñca yajamānaśabdo hyātmanyasamañjasa', yāgasya hi kartā yajamāna ityucyate, na ca yathācoditavitatapūrvāparībhūtānekakarbhakṣaṇātmakakratukriyākartṛtvamātmana' sambhavati, vibho' pūrvāparadeśavibhāgasaṃyogayogaphalakarmaṇāmasamavāyāt /
tadetadāha--- na
children.translated_text: Now, the reason 'because of contradiction with perception' is already established — for there exists a conscious [self], the agent of ritual actions, who will enjoy the other-worldly result; it is with reference to that very [self] that 'he will go to the heavenly world' is stated; so where is the contradiction? Hence he says — 'from the body.' For if there were a conscious [entity] other than the body, there might exist [such a goer to heaven]; but that [entity] has no mode of connection with the sacrificial implements — the ladle, skull-cup, and so on — for the connection belongs to the body alone. [The statement] 'the sacrificer armed with sacrificial implements' — with this intention, the connection through the <s>matup</s> (possessive) suffix is justified. Moreover, 'this very one' (<s>sa eṣa</s>) is a directly demonstrative reference, and that too is justified only for the body, because of its perceptibility — not for the self. This very point was stated by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>: 'it designates the corporeal [entity].' Furthermore, the word 'sacrificer' (<s>yajamāna</s>) is inappropriate for the self, for the agent of the sacrifice is called 'the sacrificer,' and the agency of the self in the ritual activity — which is a <s>kratu</s> (sacrifice) consisting of many action-moments spread out in prior and posterior [parts] as performed according to injunction — is not possible, because, for the all-pervading [self], actions that are the results of conjunction with spatial distinctions of prior and posterior positions do not inhere [in it]. This he states — 'nor
If there were an optative (<s>vidhi</s>) form here, the difference would not arise from mere non-observation;

children.text: viśeṣo 'syeti bhedena nopāttaṃ syādidaṃ tata' // Msv_5,9.11 //
children.translated_text: [saying] 'this has a distinctive feature' — by this distinction, this [challenge] would not have been taken up. // 11 //
If the future-ness of the result is postulated through the optative form,
then the contradiction would be resolved — but even in the present [tense], that [resolution] does not exist. // 12 //

children.text: phalaṃ ca na bhavedevaṃ bhasmībhāvād vidhāvapi /
children.translated_text: And the result would thus not exist — because of the becoming-ashes; even in the injunctive [interpretation],

children.text: tatsāmarthyena yānyapi kalpanā tāṃ niṣedhati // Msv_5,9.13 //
children.translated_text: by its capacity, whatever postulation [could be made], he negates that. // 13 //
[he states].

children.text: abhyupagamya cātmana' sadbhāvamidamasmābhiruktam, paramārthena tu dehendriyavyatiriktātmasadbhāvo 'pi pramāṇābhāvād durlabha ityāha--- sadbhāva iti /
children.translated_text: And having granted the existence of the self, this was stated by us; but in ultimate reality, the existence of a self distinct from the body and sense-organs is also hard to establish because of the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> — hence he says 'existence.'

children.text: prapañcayiṣyate caitadātmavāda itīha na pratanyata iti ||10||
children.translated_text: And this will be elaborated in the <s>Ātmavāda</s> (chapter on the self) — so it is not expanded upon here. // 10 //

children.text:
aparaṃ ca--- 'na caiṣa yātīti vidhiśabda''iti bhāṣyam /
tasyābhiprāyamāha--- yadīti /

children.translated_text: The meaning of this is: if indeed here

children.text: yajñāyudhivākye vidhiśabdo bhavet, tadā citrādīnāmanantaraphalādarśanād bhedena virodhopanyāsārthaṃ yajñāyudhivākyopādānaṃ nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: If the word '<s>vidhi</s>' (injunction) were in the <s>yajñāyudhi</s> sentence, then, since no immediate result is observed for the <s>Citrā</s> and other [sacrifices], citing the <s>yajñāyudhi</s> sentence for the purpose of presenting a contradiction through differentiation would be untenable.
Therefore, the rejection of the word '<s>vidhi</s>' is for the purpose of justifying the citing of differentiation made by oneself. // 11 //
And another [<s>Bhāṣya</s> passage]: 'And this does not go — the optative form' — [this is] the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. He states its intention — 'if.'

children.text: vidhiśabde ko viśeṣa', ata āha--- vidhīti /
children.translated_text: What is the difference when the word '<s>vidhi</s>' is present? Hence he says — '<s>vidhi</s>.'

children.text: vidhiśabde hi kālaviśeṣānupādānād vidhisāmarthyādeva kālāntarabhāvitāṃ phalasya parikalpya syādapi citrādicodanāsvivābhāvavirodhaparihāra' /
children.translated_text: For when the word '<s>vidhi</s>' is present, since no particular time is specified, by the force of the injunction itself, one could postulate the result as occurring at a future time, and thus the contradiction of absence in the <s>Citrā</s> and other injunctions could also be avoided.

children.text: iha tu yātīti vartamānāpadeśānna pratyakṣavirodha' śakyate parihartumityadarśanād viśeṣa iti ||12||
children.translated_text: But here, because the present-tense expression '<s>yāti</s>' (goes) is used, the contradiction with perception cannot be avoided — seeing this, the distinction is stated. // 12 //

children.text:
citrādivākyābhiprāyeṇa cedamasmābhiruktam--- vidhiśabde bhaviṣyattvaṃ phalasya parikalpya virodha' śakyate parihartumiti /
iha tu pratyakṣeṇa bhasmībhāvopalambhānna kālālantaraphalabhāvitayā svargagamanaṃ phalamiti śakyate kalpayitum /
na hi vidhisahasreṇāpyāśaṅkanīyor'tha' śakya' pratyāyayitum /
tadetadāha--- phalaṃ ceti /
takiṃ tarhi vidhiśabdatānirākaraṇasya phalamata āha--- tatsāmarthyeneti /
cetanapravartanātmako hi vidhirantareṇa paralokaphalopabhoktāra
children.translated_text: With respect to the <s>Citrā</s> and other sentences, this was stated by us: 'When the word <s>vidhi</s> is present, the contradiction can be avoided by postulating the result as belonging to the future.' But here, the perception of becoming ashes is apprehended by direct perception...
And mostly this kind of character is seen in <s>arthavādas</s> (laudatory passages)

children.text: mantreṣu ceti te sarve pakṣīkāryā' prayatnata' // Msv_5,9.14 //
children.translated_text: and in <s>mantras</s> — therefore all of them should be deliberately made the thesis. // Msv_5,9.14 //
If this is so, then even in the <s>agnihotra</s> and other [ritual] sentences, there would be falsity of meaning,
since they are parts of Vedic sentences, just like the <s>Citrā</s> and other statements. // Msv_5,9.15 //
Thus [ends] the <s>citrākṣepavāda</s> (objection based on conflicting Vedic statements).

children.text: manupapadyamāna' kalpayedapi kāyakaraṇasaṅghātātiriktamātmānam, tasya ca svargalokagamanamupacaryetāpi śarīre, tasya vā pratyakṣatvamātmani bhāktamityevamādikalpanāniṣedhārthaṃ vidhiśabdanirākaraṇamiti ||13||
children.translated_text: Even if something is untenable, one might postulate a self (<s>ātman</s>) distinct from the aggregate of body and instruments, and its going to the heavenly world might be figuratively applied to the body, or its perceptibility might be figuratively [attributed] to the self — and so on, such postulations...

children.text:
bhūyāṃścāyaṃ pramāṇāntaraviruddho mantrārthavādātmako vedabhāga' /
yathā 'aditirdyeraditirantarīkṣaṃ' 'yajamāna ekakapāla'' ityevamādi' /
sa ca sarva evātra prayatnato mukhyatayā mithyātvena aihikākṣepe pakṣīkārya', tanmithyātvena cānuṣaṅgikaṃ peraṣāṃ mithyātvaṃ bhaviṣyatītyabhiprāyeṇāha---prāyaiti /
'tatsāmānyādagnihotrādicodanāsvapyanāśvāsa' iti bhāṣyam, tasyābhiprāyamāha--- evaṃ satīti /
yadā hi citrādivākyādiṣvaprāmāṇyaṃ samarthitaṃ bhavati, tadā vedavākyaikadeśatayāgnihotrādivākyeṣvapi mṛṣārthatā śakyate 'numātum, ata' kṛtsnasyaiva vedasyāprāmāṇyānna cojanālakṣaṇārtho dharma ityākṣepa'||
children.translated_text: And this portion of the <s>Veda</s> consisting of <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s>, which contradicts other <s>pramāṇas</s>, is greater in extent. As for example: '<s>Aditi</s> is the sky, <s>Aditi</s> is the atmosphere,' 'The sacrificer is a single-dish [offering]' — and such. And all of this is the thesis here...
Thus, in the <s>Kāśikā</s> commentary composed by the teacher <s>Sucaritamiśra</s>, the <s>citrākṣepavāda</s> is concluded.
Now [begins] the <s>sambandhākṣepavāda</s> (objection based on the word-meaning relation).
First, the establishment of one's own position: Vedic speech is non-false,
because it does not depend on a speaker for [conveying] its own meaning, like the cognition of a word from its phonemes. // 1 //

children.text:
atrānantaram"autpattikastu śabdasyārthena sambandhastasya jñānam"iti bhāṣyakāreṇa
sambandhanityatādvāreṇākṣepaparihāro 'vatārita', so 'yukta', paroktākṣepahetvanantaraṃ hi tasyaiva viruddhāsiddhyādidoṣodbhāvanamucitam /
yattu tamadūṣayitvaivānyaducyate tadasaṅgatamevāta āha--- svapakṣa iti /
ayamabhiprāya'--- yāvaddhi sambandhautpattikatvenānapekṣālakṣaṇaṃ codanāyā' svata' prāmāṇyaṃ na pratipādyate tāvad dūṣite 'pi sādhane na 'canodanālakṣaṇo dharma' iti pratijñā sidhyati /
bhūyāṃścānena krameṇārtho vaktumabhipreta' śabdārthasambandhanirūpaṇādi' /
anyathā kriyamāmaṃ (?) tadākāśapatitamivāpadyeta /
taccaitat śabdasvarūpanirūpaṇāvasare vakṣyate /
na cedamākṣepeṇa na saṅgacchate, dvedhāpi pratyavasthānadarśanāt /
yathoktam---
'dvedhāpi pratyavasthānaṃ parahetvavabādhanāt /
ātmīyasādhanoktyā vā tatrātmīyamihotacyate' iti /
na cātra parasādhanadūṣaṇaṃ na kariṣyate 'tatra hetorasiddhatvam' iti citrāparihāre vakṣyate /
anena tu krameṇa tat kartavyamiti tāvadityuktamiti /
tacca svapakṣasādhanaṃ tārkikāṇāṃ cittamanurañja yituṃ prayogadvāreṇāha---amṛṣeti /
vaidikavaco dharmī, svārthe satyamiti sādhyo (?) dharma', svārthe vaktranapekṣatvāt, yat svārthe vaktāraṃ nāpekṣate tat satyam, yathā padāt padārthagatā buddhi' /
padaṃ hi svabhāvādeva svārthena sambaddhaṃ tatpratipādanāya vaktāraṃ nāpekṣata iti sambandhaparihāre vakṣyate /
svārtha iti tantremobhayaviśeṣaṇatayā yojanīyam /
yadi hyamṛṣa vaidikaṃ vacanamityetāvaducyate pūrvapakṣārthasamyaktvāpātādanikaṣṭārthatāprasādhanaprasaṅga' /
na hi svargakāmo yāgaṃ kuryādityādyarthe svargakāmo yajeteti vākyaṃ samyagiṣyate, ṣaṣṭhādyasiddhāntavirodhāt /
yāgena svargaṃ kuryāditi hi tatra sthāsyati /
vaktranapekṣatvāditi cāviśiṣṭo heturupātto 'siddha eva syāt /

children.translated_text: For even Vedic sentences have their own form...
The cognition produced by that is correct, because it arises from eternal sentences;
and for the cognition from sentences — here in the <s>Veda</s> too, the previously stated reasons [apply]. // 2 //

After this, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> has introduced the refutation of the objection through the eternality of the relation [of word and meaning] with [the <s>sūtra</s>] 'the relation of the word with the meaning is innate (<s>autpattika</s>), and the knowledge of that [is also innate].' This is argued to be improper, [since] the reasons for the objection stated by the opponent...
Relying on the eternal relations of word and meaning, and by the stated reason
— that they do not arise from [any humanly established] relation — the opponent declared their falsity.
That the relation exists and is eternal was stated by [the <s>sūtra</s>] beginning with '<s>autpattika</s>' (innate). // 4 //

children.text: vyaktaye vaktrapekṣā, svārthe tu pratyāyayitavye na vaktāramapekṣante, apauruṣeyatvāt /
children.translated_text: A speaker is required for manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>), but for conveying one's own meaning, [Vedic sentences] do not require a speaker, because they are not of human authorship (<s>apauruṣeya</s>).
And because the relation of word and meaning is eternal.
Even a reliable person's statement (<s>āptavacana</s>), which is of human origin and has as its object what is known by other <s>pramāṇas</s>, requires a <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding the speaker.
As stated: 'In the utterances of a reliable person, [verification of] the person is required.' // 1 //

children.text: vaidikavākyakṛta' pratyaya' samyagiti sādhyam, nityavākyodbhavatvāt, yathā tadvākyasvarūpaviṣayā buddhi' /
children.translated_text: The thesis is: the cognition produced by Vedic sentences is correct — because it arises from eternal sentences, just as the cognition regarding the very form of that sentence [is correct].
For that [cognition] too arises from the sentence, since a cognition without an object does not arise.
And the eternality of Vedic sentences will be established in the <s>Vedādhikaraṇa</s> (section on the <s>Veda</s>).

children.text: atraiva sādhye pūrvoktā'--- 'nānyatvāt' iti bhāṣyavyākhyānāvasara uktā'--- doṣavarjitai' kāraṇai' janyamānatvāt, anāptāpraṇītoktijanyatvāt, deśādibhede 'pi deśādibhede 'pi bādhavarjanāt iti hetavo darśayitavyā ityāha--- atreti ||2||
children.translated_text: For this very thesis, the previously stated [reasons] — stated in the occasion of commenting on the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage 'not because of being different' — [are:] because it is produced by causes free from defects, because it arises from utterances not composed by unreliable persons, because even in difference of region and the like, the region and so forth...
He states another formulation — up to 'the cognition produced by that.'

children.text:
atra bhāṣyam--- 'syādetat, naiva śabdasyārthena sambandha', kuto 'sya pauruṣeyatā apauruṣetā vā'iti /
tasyābhiprāyamāha--- nityānityabravīdantena /
asyārtha'--- śabdārthasambandhānāṃ nityatvamāśrityānapekṣatvāditi sūtrakāreṇa yo hetu' svata' prāmāṇyasidhyarthamukta', tena codanānāmaprāmāṇye nirākṛte 'dhunā sambandhodbhavatvābhāvena paro bauddhādirmithyātvamuktavān /
evaṃ ca tadā vārtikakāreṇa vṛttikāramatenātraiva svata' prāmāṇyaṃ vyutpādyamiti darśitam /
tathā ca 'sūtrakāreṇa cocyata' iti punaruktiparihāre parata' paprāmāṇyoktairevākṣepahetubhi' pūrvapakṣo 'bhihita' /
ihāpi ca bhāṣyakāreṇa 'brūta' ityucyate--- avabodhayati budhyamānasya nimittaṃ bhavati, ityādi codanāsūtroktameva svata' prāmāṇyakāraṇamuktamiti ||3 1/2||
children.translated_text: Here the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [states]: 'It might be said that the word has no relation at all with the meaning — so how can it be of human or non-human authorship?' He states its purport — up to 'the opponent declared.' The meaning of this is...
For the purpose of refuting falsity, two things are not accepted by the proponents of that [position]:

children.text: naiva vāstyatra sambandha' kṛtako veti vakṣyate ||5||
children.translated_text: 'Either there is no relation here at all, or it is created' — this will be stated. // 5 //
By the impossibility of the remaining [relations], physical conjunction (<s>saṃśleṣa</s>) is left over;
and the worldly cognition is firmly established precisely in that relation. // 6 //

children.text:
etadeva vivṛṇoti --- sambandha iti vakṣyate 'ntena /
codanāmithyārthanirāsārthaṃ hi sambamandhasadbhāvo nityatā ca heturukta' /
tacca dvayamapi parairneṣyate /
tatra sambandhābhāvastāvadanenaiva bhāṣyeṇokta' /
kṛtakatvaṃ tu 'yadi prathamamaśruto na pratyāyayati, kṛtakastarhi' ityanena vakṣyate /
tadatra sambandhābhāvenānapekṣatvāditi hetorasiddhiruktā /

children.translated_text: And in the absence of a relation,
it has been shown that the cognition of the meaning expressed by the opponent arises [nonetheless].
For when there is the force of an invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>), the cognition of a different object arises even for one who perceives another object.

children.text: anādṛtapratibandhastu yatkiñcid vidvān sa sarvaṃ jānīyādityatiprasajyata iti ||4,5||
children.translated_text: But one who disregards the invariable connection, knowing anything whatsoever, would know everything — this would over-extend. // 4, 5 //

He elaborates on this — up to 'the relation will be stated.' For the existence and eternality of the relation were stated as the reason for refuting the falsity of injunctions. And both of these are not accepted by the opponents...

children.text:
atra bhāṣyakāreṇa kāryakāraṇabhāvādaya' sambandhā' śabdasyānupapannā ityuktvā saṃśleṣasambandhabhāva eva darśita', tadetadvārtikakāro darśayati--- asambhaveneti /
nimittanaimittikāśrayāśrayibhāvādaya' sambandhā' śabdārthayoratyantāsambhāv itā eva, kāryakāraṇabhāvastu boddhagandhivaiyākaraṇairabhyupagata eva /
te 'pyāhu'----
'arthā' śabdāśca dṛśyante pratyakṣā yadyapi sphuṭam /
abhidhānābhidheyau tu jñānākārau tathāpi na''||
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, having stated that relations such as cause-effect and the like are untenable for words, has shown that the relation of physical conjunction (<s>saṃśleṣa</s>) alone exists. The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> shows this — 'by the impossibility.'

children.text:
iti /
evaṃ hi manyante--- na tāvad varṇā' śabda', pratyekamavacākatvāt /
ayugapadvartināṃ cāvayavisamudāyāsarambhānupapatte' /

ata eva gośabdatvādijātyasambhavāt bhūtādiviśeṣāṇāṃ ca pratiprayogamanyatvenāvācakatvād varṇabuddhismṛtisaṃskārāṇāṃ cākṣaravat pratyākhyānāt pūrvavarṇajanitasaṃskārasahitāntyavarṇasyāpi varṇatvenāpūrvavarṇavadavācakatvāt pūrvapūrvanikhilavarṇapadopasahārakrameṇa caramasya kasyacit sphoṭātmano 'navagrahād yugapadavasthitānekavarṇākārajñānātmaiva śabda' /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, because universals like 'cow-word-ness' are impossible, and because specific [elements] like material substances are non-denotative since they are different at each usage, and because the letter-cognition, memory, and dispositional impressions are rejected like [individual] syllables, the impression generated by the prior letters...

The meaning too, being of indeterminate form because all alternatives such as universal, particular, whole, part, quality, quality-possessor, difference, non-difference, and the like are eliminated, does not exist as external — hence, [it is held that] what arises immediately after the cognition of the word, which is of the nature of knowledge, namely external universals and the like...
Therefore, he states the denial of that — the word has no conjunction (<s>saṅgati</s>) with the meaning;
because of the non-observation of proximity in that place — just as the <s>Vindhya</s> [has no conjunction] with the <s>Himālaya</s>. // 7 //

For they think thus: Letters are not the word, because individually they are non-denotative. And since the formation of a whole or an aggregate from [elements that are] not simultaneously present is untenable.
Thus, whether the meaning alone or both [word and meaning] — what is to be proved is unconnected;
and the [argument] beginning with '<s>kṣura</s>' (razor) was stated by some others for the purpose of establishing the reason. // 8 //
Taking it in the form of capacity (<s>śakti</s>), he says: if physical conjunction is denied,
then the relation [suffers from] the fallacy of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatva</s>), or [it amounts to] a mere relation. // 9 //

children.text:
sa cāyamevambhūtor'tha' śabdena janyata eveti kāryakāraṇabhāvameva śabdārthayo' sambandhamātiṣṭhante /
taccedamatidūramapabhraṣṭam, evaṃ ca satyaviditasvarūpaśaktīnāmapyarthasaṃvidupajāyeta /
dṛṣṭā hi khalu mṛtsalilapracchannā api vrīhayo 'ṅkurādikāryamārabhamāṇā aviditasvarūpaśaktayo 'pīti sūktam--- asambhavena śeṣāṇāmiti /
kathaṃ tu saṃśleṣa' pariśiṣyata iti, pratīterabhyupagamācca /
gaurayamiti hi sāmānādhikaraṇyena śabdopaśliṣṭamarthamavayanto laukikā dṛśyante /
abhyupagataśca kaiścicchabdārthayo' saṃśleṣa eva sambandha' /

children.translated_text: And that theory of superimposition (<s>adhyāsavāda</s>) has been elaborated [elsewhere].

children.text: laukikāśca prāyeṇa saṃśleṣameva saṃbandhaṃ manyante iti sa eva sambandha' prasakko nirākārya ityāha--- tasminniti prāhāyena bhavati sa taddeśa eva dṛśyate rañjuriva ghaṭe, tadanantaradeśe vā pradeśinīvamadhyamāyā' /
children.translated_text: And ordinary people generally consider contact (<s>saṃśleṣa</s>) alone as the relation — therefore, it is precisely this relation that needs to be refuted — hence he says 'therein.' [Contact] is generally either observed in the same locus — as a rope in a pot — or in an immediately adjacent locus — as the ring finger [is adjacent] to the middle finger.
But neither of the two — word and meaning — is observed in the locus of the other.
Therefore, like <s>Himavat</s> and <s>Vindhya</s>, there is no relation between these two. (5.6.7)

And this meaning of such a nature is produced by the word itself — thus they maintain that the relation between word and meaning is precisely that of cause and effect. But this is far gone astray. For if this were so, even for those whose inherent capacities are unknown, the cognition of meaning would arise. For indeed, rice grains concealed by clay and water are seen to commence the effect of sprouting and such even though their inherent capacities are unknown — thus it is well said: 'because of the impossibility of the remaining [alternatives].' But how is contact (<s>saṃśleṣa</s>) the remaining [alternative]? — Because of the acceptance of the cognition [in the form] 'this is a cow' — for ordinary people are seen to apprehend the meaning as conjoined with the word through co-referential usage (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). And contact alone as the relation between word and meaning has been accepted by some.

children.text:
artho vā pakṣīkārya ityāha---evamiti /
dvayaṃ vā parasparamasambaddhamitaretaradeśe tadanantaradeśe vādṛṣṭe' sādhyamityāha--- dvayamiti /
atra bhāṣyakāreṇa 'syāccedarthena sambandha' kṣuramodakaśabdoccāraṇe mukhyasya pāṭanapūraṇe syātām', ityuktam /
tasyābhiprāyamāha--- kṣuretyuktamantena /

asyārtha'--- atra bhāṣyakāreṇa śabdārthayo' sambnadhasiddhyarthaṃ taddeśānantarādṛṣṭeriti heturantarṇīta', taṃ ca gaurayamiti sāmānādhikaraṇyapratītibhramād yo nāmāsiddhaṃ manyate, sa evaṃ pratībodhyate--- yadi śabdārthayorupaśleṣa
children.translated_text: The meaning of this is: Here, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, for the purpose of establishing the relation between word and meaning, has implicitly included the reason 'because of not being seen in the locus or adjacent locus of that [meaning].' And whoever considers this to be unestablished due to the error of the cognition of co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) [in the form] 'this is a cow' — that person is to be awakened thus: if the relation of word and meaning were of the nature of contact (<s>upaśleṣa</s>),
There would be inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntika</s>) through [other] relations such as father-son and the like;
Because of the relation of sharing one ground and the like, the example would lack the property to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>). (5.6.10)

Or the meaning may be made the subject of proof (<s>pakṣīkārya</s>) — he says 'thus.' Or, both being mutually unrelated, since neither is seen in the locus of the other or in an adjacent locus, [non-relation] is to be proved — he says 'both.' Here the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> has said: 'If there were a relation with meaning, then upon the utterance of the words "razor" and "sweetmeat," there would be cutting and filling of the mouth.' He states the purport of that — 'razor' through the end [of the passage].
In the denial of the relation of denoted and denoting (<s>vācya-vācaka</s>), there would be contradiction with common usage (<s>lokabādhana</s>);
And there would be self-contradiction with one's own statement — for [things] devoid of relation cannot (5.6.11)

children.text:
lakṣaṇa' sambandho bhavet, artho 'pi śabdadeśa eva syāt, mukhaṃ ca tasya deśa iti kṣuramodakaśabdoccāraṇe mukhasya pāṭanapūraṇe syātām, na ca te sta'ṣa tasmānmodakādyarthakriyānupalambhācchabdadeśe taddeśānantarādṛṣṭeriti siddho hetu' /
sāmānādhikaraṇyabuddhistu śabdārthayornāstyeva /
na hi nīlimnevānuraktamutpalaṃ śabdānuraktamarthamupalabhāmahe /
gādisāsnādimadrūpā hi tayorbuddharudeti /
atra siddhāntabhāṣyaṃ 'yo 'tra vyapadeśya' sambandha' tadeta(tamekaṃ)nna vyapadiśati bhavān' ityādi /
tasyābhiprāyamāha--- atheti hīnatāntena /
atrāyamabhiprāya'---- pratyāyyapratyāyakaśaktirūpo hi na' śabdārthayo' sambandho 'bhipreta', tad yadi
children.translated_text: The purport here is as follows: The relation between word and meaning intended by us is indeed of the nature of the capacity of the conveyed and the conveyor (<s>pratyāyya-pratyāyaka</s>). Therefore, if
what is being proved is the absence of a relation characterized by contact, then the fault is that of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>);
but if the absence of relation in general [is being proved], then there is inconclusiveness through relations such as genetic relation (<s>yauna</s>) and the like;
and even for <s>Himavat</s> and <s>Vindhya</s>, because of their relation of sharing one ground and the like, the example lacks the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proved). (5.6.8, 10)

[have contact as] their defining relation. If [contact were the relation], the meaning too would have to be in the very locus of the word, and since the mouth is its locus, upon the utterance of the words 'razor' and 'sweetmeat,' there would be cutting and filling of the mouth — but these do not occur. Therefore, because of not observing the activity of sweetmeats and such in the locus of the word, and because of not being seen in the locus or adjacent locus of that [meaning] — the reason is established. But the cognition of co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) does not exist between word and meaning. For we do not apprehend the meaning as conjoined with the word in the way that a lotus is conjoined with blue color. For the cognition of those two arises as 'cow' and 'the word cow' [separately, each with its own form]. Here is the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'That relation which is the designable — you do not designate that one [thing]' and so forth. He states the purport of that — 'now' through the end [of the passage].

children.text:
yadi tu vācyavācakasambandhamevābhipretya na śabdār'thena saṅgata iti sādhyate tato laukikavirodha ityāha---vācyeti /
dūṣaṇāntaramāha--- virodha iti /
atra kāraṇamāha--- na hīti parāntena /
ayamabhiprāya'--- caturvidho hi puruṣa', pratipanno 'pratipanna' sandigdho viparyastaśceti /
tatra pratipanna' pratipādayitā, itare sāpekṣā' pratipādyā', tatpratipādanārthā ca pratijñā, tadya eva teṣāmanyatama' para' pratipādayitumabhipreto bhavati sa eva vācyavācakasambandhavarjitai' pratijñārthagaucarai' padai' pratipādayitumaśakya', ata' pratijñāṃ prayuñjānairāśrita' śabādarthayorvācyavācakalakṣaṇasambandha iti tanninirākaraṇe svavāgvirodha iti /
sa cāyamabhidhayā svavāgvirodha' /
pañcadhā hi tadvirodha' /
uccāraṇābhidhādharmadharmyubhayoktibhiriti ||11 1/2||
children.translated_text: But if, having intended precisely the relation of denoted and denoting (<s>vācya-vācaka</s>), the thesis is established that 'the word is not connected with meaning,' then there would be contradiction with common usage — he says 'denoted' etc. He states another fault — 'contradiction.' Here he states the reason — 'for' through the end [of the passage]. The purport is as follows: For a person is of four kinds — one who has understood, one who has not understood, one who is in doubt, and one who has a wrong understanding. Among them, one who has understood is the instructor; the others, being in need [of instruction], are to be instructed. And the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) is for the purpose of instructing them. Now, whichever of these other [three types] one intends to instruct — that very person cannot be instructed by words that are the objects of the thesis yet devoid of the relation of denoted and denoting. Therefore, those who employ a thesis have [implicitly] relied upon the relation of denoted and denoting between word and meaning — hence in denying it, there is self-contradiction. And this self-contradiction is specifically with respect to designation (<s>abhidhā</s>). For the contradiction [with one's own statement] is five-fold: through utterance, designation, property, property-possessor, and the statement of both. (5.6.11½)
One is able to instruct another through words regarding the object of a thesis;
for in the activity of designation (<s>abhidhāna</s>), object-hood (<s>karmatva</s>) belongs to the denoted [meaning]. (5.6.12)

children.text: śabdānāṃ karaṇatvaṃ vā kartṛtvaṃ vā nirūpita' /
children.translated_text: And the instrument-hood (<s>karaṇatva</s>) or agent-hood (<s>kartṛtva</s>) of words has been established,
because of [their] employment in [producing] cognition, and because the togetherness [of word and meaning] is intended. (5.6.13)

children.text:
vācyavācakasambandhasvarūpamidānīmabhidyotayati---abhidhāneti /
asyārtha'--- ekasyāmabhidhānakriyāyāṃ śabda' karaṇaṃ kartā vā, vivakṣāta' kārakapravṛtte' /
arthastu karmaiva /
ato(yad?a) nayo' karmakaraṇatvaṃ (karma) kartṛtvaṃ vā /
nirūpita'--- sambandha iti vakṣyamāṇena sambandha iti /
yadvā--- ekasyāṃ gavādyarthapratipattau sādhyamānāyāmekena vaktropādīyamānāvaruṇaikahānīvadvivakṣitasāhityau śabdārtho yanniyamyete so 'nayo' sambandha ityāha--- pratipattāviti /
upādānādityupādīyamānatayā viśeṣaṇavivakṣāṃ darśayati /
upādeyasya hi viśeṣaṇaṃ vivakṣitaṃ bhavati śorivaikatvaṃ--- paśunā yajeteti /
uddeśyaviśeṣaṇaṃ tvavivakṣitaṃ bhavati, yathā grahaviśeṣaṇamekatvam, uddeśyā hi grahā', teṣu saṃmārjanavidhānāt /
iha cārthapratipattāvekasyāmupādeyau śabdārthau, paśuriva yoge /
ato vivakṣitatamanayo' sāhityaṃ viśeṣaṇamityaruṇaikahāyanyorivānayorniyama' sambandha iti /
(natve?nve)vamaruṇaikahāyanyo' śrūyamāṇayo' sāhityavivakṣā yuktā /
samudāye hi tatra vākyaṃ samāpyate /
(śabdārthau tu) naiva pratītikriyā(yāṃ viśeṣa)ṇatayāśrutau, kathamanayo' sāhityavivakṣā /
na śrūyamāṇatā viśeṣaṇavivakṣāhetu' /
api tu arthasaṃvyavahāro 'pi hi /
pākādau yadaudanādisthālyādi...(kriyā) vyavahāradarśanāt anabhihitamapyarthaṃ jānāti tadā sthālyādīnāṃ vivakṣitaṃ sāhityaṃ manyate, katathā manvāna' svayamapi paktukāmastatsarvamāharati /
evamihāpi bāla' prayojyavṛddhasya viviṣṭārthavyavahāradarśanena tadviṣayāṃ buddhimanumāya śabdānantarabhāvitayā śabdakāraṇatāṃ tādavavadhārayati /
vaktuścāsyāṃ prayojyavṛddhapratipattau darśanapārārthyāt pradhānabhūtāyā(mupā)dīyamānayo' śabdārtayo' sāhityaṃ vivakṣitamiti /
evaṃ ca viditvā svayamapi parārthaprayoge sahitau śabdārthau hṛdayamāveśitāvupādāya śabdaṃ coccārya parapratipattiṃ bhāvayatīti sūktaṃ sāhityavivakṣā varṇasāhityavivakṣāvaditi ||12-13 1/2||
children.translated_text: He now illuminates the essential nature of the relation of denoted and denoting — 'designation' etc. The meaning of this is: In one activity of designation, the word is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) or the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>), since the operation of the <s>kārakas</s> (grammatical factors) is based on the speaker's intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>). But the meaning is invariably the object (<s>karman</s>). Therefore, between these two, it is the object-instrument relationship or the object-agent relationship. 'Established' — [means] the relation, by what will be stated [next], is the relation. Alternatively: in one [act of] cognition of the meaning such as cow and the like, which is being brought about, the word and meaning — being employed by one speaker, like <s>Aruṇa</s> and a one-year-old [cow] — are restricted together when their togetherness is intended; that restriction of the two is the relation — he says 'in cognition.' 'Because of employment' — by [adding] 'being employed,' he shows the intention of a qualifying [restriction]. For the qualification of what is to be employed is intended, like the oneness of a [sacrificial] animal — 'one should sacrifice with an animal.' But the qualification of the topic (<s>uddeśya</s>) is not intended, as [in the case of] the oneness qualifying the cups — for the cups are the topics, since the sweeping-rite is enjoined with regard to them. And here, in one [act of] cognition of meaning, the word and meaning are what is to be employed, like the animal in the sacrifice. Therefore, the togetherness of these two is the intended qualification — thus, like the restriction of <s>Aruṇa</s> and a one-year-old [cow], the restriction of these two is the relation. But indeed, only for <s>Aruṇa</s> and a one-year-old [cow], which are heard [in the Vedic text], is the intention of togetherness proper. For the sentence is completed there in the aggregate. But word and meaning are not heard as qualifiers in the activity of cognition — so how can togetherness be intended for them? [Reply:] It is not that being-heard is the cause of intending the qualification. Rather, practical usage regarding meaning is also [a cause]. For in cooking and such, when one sees the practical usage of [things like] a pot and the like for rice and the like... from observing the activity, even meaning that is not explicitly stated is known, and then one considers the togetherness of the pot and the like to be intended — just as one who intends to cook himself gathers all of those [implements]. Similarly here too, a child, by observing the meaningful activity of the elder who is prompting him, infers the cognition directed at that [meaning], and through [the meaning] being presented immediately after the word, ascertains the word as the cause [of that cognition]. And for the speaker, in this cognition of the prompted elder — which is the primary [result] because speech aims at it — the togetherness of word and meaning, which are being employed, is intended. And having understood this, [the child] himself too, in communicating for the benefit of others, having taken to heart the togethered word and meaning, utters the word and produces cognition in the other — thus it is well said that the intention of togetherness is like the intention of togetherness of phonemes. (5.6.12-13½)
The two [word and meaning] are restricted to that one [activity of cognition] — that is the relation of the meaning and the word.
Therein, although the <s>kārakas</s> (grammatical factors) have no [direct] relation with each other, (5.6.14)
nevertheless, whatever action [they serve] — because of their mutual helpfulness and being-helped in that [action],
afterwards, from the connection in that action, the relation of those two is declared. (5.6.15)

children.text:
nanvevaṃ vadatā śabdārthayo' kriyāsambandha eva darśita', na parasparam, guṇapradhānabhāvamantareṇa sambandhāyogāt /
vakṣyati hi--- 'guṇānāṃ ca parārthatvādasambandha' samatvāt' iti /
syādetat /
kriyākārakasambandhapūrvakatvāt sarvasambandhānāṃ kriyākārakasambandha eva darśita iti /
astu tāvat, taduttarakālabhāvī tu ko 'nayo' sambandha iti vācyameva /
tadetat sarvamanubhāṣya pariharati---tatreti tayārentane /
asyārtha'---- yadyapi kārakāṇāṃ pradhānārthatvānna parasparasambandha' /
tathāpi pratipattyabhidhānayoryā kācit kriyā gṛhyate, tasyāṃ ca kriyākārakasambandhottarakālabhāvī parasparopakāryopakārakalakṣaṇa' śabdārthayorasti sambandha'||
children.translated_text: Objection: But in speaking thus, you have shown only the relation of word and meaning through action, not with each other — since without the relationship of subordinate and principal (<s>guṇa-pradhāna</s>), a relation is impossible. For it will be said: 'And because of the other-directedness of subordinates, the relation [is impossible] because of equality.' One might say: since all relations are preceded by the action-<s>kāraka</s> relation, only the action-<s>kāraka</s> relation has been shown. Let that be so — but what relation of these two arises subsequent to that [action-kāraka relation]? — this must indeed be stated. Having restated all of this, he resolves [the difficulty] — 'therein' through the end [of the passage]. The meaning of this is: although the <s>kārakas</s>, because of being directed toward the principal [action], have no mutual relation, nevertheless, whatever action is apprehended — whether of cognition or of designation — the relation between word and meaning that arises subsequent to the action-<s>kāraka</s> relation and is characterized by mutual helpfulness and being-helped [exists] in that action.

children.text:
tatpunaridaṃ pūrvāparaviruddhaṃ pradeśāntaraviruddhaṃ ca /
tathāhi --- atra tāvadekasyāṃ kriyāyāmupakāryopakārakatvaṃ śabdārthayo' sambandha ityuktam, 'pratipattāvupādānāt' iti kriyānumānāṅgatvameva parasparaniyamātmako sambandha ityuktam /
pradeśāntare śaktireva sambandha iti vakṣyati /
kvacicca śabdaśaktiniyamameva sambandhamāha---
'vācyavācakaśaktyośca niyama' phalalakṣaṇa'' iti bruvāṇa' /
anyatrāpyuktam---
'ekābhidhānimittvaṃ karmakartṛtvayośca yat /
yo vā karaṇakramatvaniyamo 'bhidhayaikayā||
children.translated_text: But this is self-contradictory and contradicts other passages. For here it has been said that the mutual helpfulness and being-helped of word and meaning in one action is the relation — 'because of employment in cognition' — [meaning] that the relation is in the form of mutual restriction as a component of inference regarding action. In another passage, it will be said that capacity (<s>śakti</s>) alone is the relation. And somewhere else, he declares the restriction of the capacity of words alone to be the relation, saying: 'The restriction of the capacity of the denoted and the denoting is characterized by the result.' And elsewhere too it has been said: 'That which is the being-the-single-cause-of-designation, and the object-hood and agent-hood, or the restriction of instrument-hood and sequence-hood through one [act of] designation'

vastutastūpakāryopakārakatvameva sambandha' /
kathaṃ punastadrūpamanayorniyatamityucyate /
