na ca sadānīṃ tau na sta', nityatvāt /
tasmādasadetat /
tanna /
śaktyātmanā vidyamānatvāt
children.translated_text: [continuing] "that is not the relation of meaning and word" — thus. Therefore this must be discriminated: what is the relation of word and meaning accepted by the author of the <s>Vārttika</s>? To this we reply: Just as of substance and quality that are accepted through a single act of purchase, the relation characterized by mutual assistance (<s>upākāryopakāra</s>) through the fulfillment of each other’s expectancy — for neither one alone, without being supported [by the other], accomplishes the act of purchase. Substance, not delimited by specific qualities, is not able to accomplish the act of purchase. And quality, even though the mere substrate-substance is accepted through its own power, is not grasped in a purchase, because of being confined to its own cow-[substance]. When only quality is accepted in the substance to the exclusion of the [full] quality, the act of purchase does not accept it either, because of being confined to its own quality of redness. This is the restriction regarding the meaning that obtains. Similarly here too, of word and meaning that are employed for the accomplishment of the communicative activity of apprehending one meaning, being intended to cooperate — the relation of being mutually helpful (<s>upākāryopakārakabhāva</s>) that arises subsequent to the relation of action and instrument — that itself is the relation. What then is the mutual assistance between these two? Listen: meaning cannot be communicated without a communicating [instrument], and a word is not a communicator without something to be communicated. Therefore, standing as communicand and communicator, they become mutually helpful to each other. And this form of theirs is fixed — so merely through the closest connection, the fixed [relationship] is called "relation," but the fixedness itself is not the relation. The doctrine of capacity (<s>śakti</s>) as relation is also from this [perspective]. For only when the capacities of expressible and expresser exist does the relation of being mutually helpful obtain. But capacity itself is not the relation; rather, here, because of close proximity, through the figurative usage of non-difference, [one says] "capacity is the relation," "fixedness is the relation," "agenthood or instrumentality is the relation" — such are the various expressions. But in reality, the mutual helpfulness alone is the relation. But how is it said that this form of theirs is fixed? For when a word has not been uttered, the mutual helpfulness of word and meaning does not exist. And it is not that they do not exist at that time, because of their eternality. Therefore this is not so. No — because [the relation] exists in the form of capacity.
And it has not been established here that invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) is useful;

children.text: saṃjñeti gamakatvaṃ cenna tadaṅgamiyaṃ bhavet // Msv_5,9.16 //
children.translated_text: if [it is said that] the status of a conventional sign (<s>saṃjñā</s>) [constitutes] indicative capacity — then this would not be a component [of knowledge]. // 16 //
Observing that the utterance (<s>śruti</s>) indicates [meaning], [the convention] is postulated from ordinary usage;
and this [convention] does not convey meaning when the relation has not been ascertained. // 17 //

children.text:
anuccarite 'pi hi śabde 'sti pratipādakaśakti',arthe ca pratipādyaśakti' ata eva sambandho nitya ityucyate /
nanvemapi karahastādibhiranekai' śabdairekatrārthe pratipādye anekārthavacane caikasmin gavādiśabde kathamavyabhicāra' śakyate 'vagantum /
ata' prakaraṇādīnāmapi padārthāvadhāraṇāpoyatvād vṛddhavyavahāre hi bālena kevalapadāprayogādāvāpoddhārabhedenaitadavadhāritam--- yadā yadarthavivakṣayā śabda' prayujyate sa tasyārtha iti /
vivakṣā cārthaprakaraṇādivaśonneyā /
gāmānayadogdhumityukte arthādetadavagamyate sāsnādimatyasya vivakṣeti /
yotsyāmītyukte arthādi(mu?) ṣau pratītirudeti /
tadevamarthaprakaraṇādibhedabhinnamanyayānyayā ca śaktyopahitamanyadanyacca padamanyasyānyasya vācakamiti na padavyabhicāra' /
artho 'pi codbhūtatatpadābhidhānayogyāvasthābhedabhinno hastādiranyo 'nyaśac karādipadānāṃ vācya iti na padaṃ vyabhicarati /
children.translated_text: The meaning too, differentiated by the distinctions of states qualified by the capacity of being expressed by the respective word, such as "hand" (<s>hasta</s>) and the like — is different, and is the expressible of words like "hand" (<s>kara</s>) and the like — so [the meaning] does not deviate from the word.
Moreover, this fixedness has been stated with respect to a single activity.
And of word and meaning employed in a single act of cognition or expression, there is no mutual deviation.
This is what was said: "they are fixed with respect to one" [activity]. // 14, 15 //

For even when a word has not been uttered, there exists the capacity to communicate in the word, and the capacity to be communicated in the meaning — therefore the relation is said to be eternal. Objection: Even so, when many words such as "hand" (<s>kara</s>), "hand" (<s>hasta</s>), and the like refer to one and the same meaning, and when a single word like "cow" (<s>go</s>) has multiple meanings, how can non-deviation be understood? Therefore, since contextual factors and the like have the function of determining the meaning of words — for in the usage of the learned (<s>vṛddha</s>), through the process of inclusion and exclusion (<s>āpoddhāra</s>) when merely the word is employed without [context], the child ascertains this: "When a word is employed with the intention of [expressing] a particular meaning, that is its meaning." And the intention of the speaker is to be inferred from the context of the meaning, situation, and the like. When it is said "Bring the cow for milking," from the context of the meaning it is understood: "The intention is [to refer to] something possessing a dewlap and the like." When it is said "I shall fight," from the context of the meaning, the cognition of the bull arises. Thus, each word, differentiated by the distinctions of meaning-context and the like, and endowed with one capacity or another, being the expresser of one meaning or another — so there is no deviation of words.

children.text:
nanvevamekriyānimittako niyama' śabdārthayo' sambandha ityucyamāne 'numānāṅgamavinābhāva evāśrito bhavet, atastadabalena dhūmādivāgnijñānaṃ śabdādarthajñānamupajāyamānamanumānaṃ syādata āha---na cāpīti /
idaṃ ca śābde prasādhitamityāha--- sādhitamiti /
nanu yadyavinābhāvo nopayujyate, kastarhyupayujyate /

children.translated_text: The <s>Bhāṣyakara</s> has stated: "the relation of conventional sign and signified" (<s>saṃjñā-saṃjñi-sambandha</s>).
But this relation too is not useful.
He raises this doubt — "conventional sign."
"Its component" means "a component of indicative capacity." // 16 //

Objection: When it is said in this way that the fixedness grounded in a single activity is the relation of word and meaning, [the relation] would become dependent on invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>), which is a component of inference. Therefore, by its force, the cognition of meaning from a word, arising like the cognition of fire from smoke and the like, would be inference — hence he says "and not." And this has been established in [the chapter on] <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) — hence he says "established." Objection: If invariable concomitance is not useful, then what is useful?
How is it not a component? Hence he says "observing that it indicates." Through the observation of usage, the indicative
Therefore, the indicative capacity arises afterwards, like that of smoke and the like;

children.text: sānaṅgaṃ tadvadeva syānneyaṃ dhūmādibhi' samā // Msv_5,9.18 //
children.translated_text: that [capacity], being a non-component, would be just like that — this [word-meaning relation] should not be equated with smoke and the like. // 18 //
When the invariable concomitance has been ascertained there, the causation there is indeed by that;

children.text: gamakatvena pūrvaṃ ca tatra notpadyate mati' // Msv_5,9.19 //
children.translated_text: and the cognition does not arise there first through indicative capacity. // 19 //
Here [in the case of words], however, the cognition of invariable concomitance is not prior to denotative capacity;

children.text: yadaiva ceha sambandhaṃ vṛddhebhya' pratipādyate // Msv_5,9.20 //
children.translated_text: and at the very time when the relation is communicated here from the learned (<s>vṛddha</s>), // 20 //
at that very time, "this is an indicator of this" — not from some other nature.
Somewhere they say "this is to be understood from this"; // 21 //
somewhere [they say] "this is the expresser" and "this is the expressible";
somewhere, having seen the activity directed toward the meaning from the uttered word, // 22 //
this convention is postulated.
What follows from this? Hence he says "and this does not."
What is meant is this:
indicative capacity itself is convention-status — not without another relation. // 17 //
And since it is so, therefore the indicative capacity has arrived afterwards, preceded by another relation, just like that of smoke and the like — hence he says "therefore."
He states the fault of that equivalence — "being a non-component."

children.text: yathaivāvinanābhāva eva dhūmādau pratītyaṅgaṃ na taduttarakālabhāvi gamakatvam, evaṃ tatrāpi syāditi /
children.translated_text: Just as for smoke and the like, the component of cognition is the invariable concomitance alone, not the indicative capacity that arises subsequent to it — so it would be in that [case of words] too.
He now states the resolution through the dissimilarity with smoke and the like — "this should not [be equated]." // 18 //
He shows the very dissimilarity — "when ascertained."

children.text: tatra hi dhūmādau mahānasādideśe 'gnyavinābhāvanirūpaṇottarakālaṃ tatkṛtaivāsau gamakateti /
children.translated_text: For there, in the case of smoke and the like, after the ascertainment of the invariable concomitance of fire in the kitchen and similar places, the indicative capacity is indeed caused by that.

children.text: api ca dhūme prathamaṃ gamakatvaṃ nāvagamyata ityāha -- gamakatveneti ||19||
children.translated_text: Moreover, in the case of smoke, the indicative capacity is not cognized first — hence he says "through indicative capacity." // 19 //
But in the case of words, it is the reverse — hence he says "here" with a half-verse. // 20½ //

children.text:
gamakatvenaiva śabde prathamaṃ vyutpattirityuktaṃ tad vivṛṇoti---kathayantītitrayeṇa /
ayamartha'--- tredhā hi śabde vyutpatti', vṛddhopadeśāt tadavyavahārāt padāntarasamabhivyāhārādvā /
sarvatra cātra gamakataivādāvavagamyate /
tathāha--- vṛddhopadeśe tāvadayamasya vācya' ayamasya vācaka
children.translated_text: It was stated that in the case of words, linguistic competence (<s>vyutpatti</s>) is first through indicative capacity — he elaborates this — "they say" with three [verses]. The meaning is this: for linguistic competence in words is threefold — from the instruction of the learned (<s>vṛddhopadesa</s>), from their usage, or from co-occurrence with other known words. And in all cases here, it is the indicative capacity that is cognized first. He states this: In the instruction of the learned — "this is the expressible of this, this is the expresser of this"
for some, the status of the knower is cognized through inference there;
by means of "from this word, this meaning has been ascertained." // 23 //
Therefore, surely these two are established in the world as possessing the capacity of expresser [and expressible];

children.text: itthaṃ vācakatā siddhā saṅkīrṇāpi tata' param // Msv_5,9.24 //
children.translated_text: thus, the denotative capacity is established — and mixed [denotation] thereafter. // 24 //
When the meaning has been ascertained as extracted through <s>anvaya</s> (co-presence) and <s>vyatireka</s> (co-absence),
resting upon the distinctions of many <s>jātis</s> (universals), <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), <s>dravyas</s> (substances), and <s>karmas</s> (actions), // 25 //
the cognitions that arise suddenly, having the character of literal and figurative [meanings],
the world does not wish to discriminate, because of the absence of a reason [to do so]. // 26 //

children.text:
iti gamyagamakabhāva evāvagamyate /
yatrāpi kvaciduccaritād vākyāt prayojyavṛddhasyārthāviṣayāṃ kriyāṃ dṛṣṭvā ceṣṭānumānena gavādyarthaboddhṛtvamupakalpyate tatrāpi yasmādata' śabdādanenāyamartho 'vagata', tasmādayamasyārtha iti gamakataiva śabdasyādāvavagamyate /
prasiddhapadāntarasamabhivyāhāre 'pi iha sahakāratarau madhuraṃ piko rautītyevamādau viditasahākarādādyartho 'viditapikādyarthaśca yo 'yaṃ sahakāratarau rauti tasya pikaśabdo gamaka iti gamakatvamevāvagacchatīti siddhaṃ sarvatra gamakatvaṃ na vyutpattiriti ||21-23 1/2||
children.translated_text: thus, it is the relation of signified and signifier (<s>gamya-gamaka-bhāva</s>) alone that is cognized. Where too, somewhere, the status of the knower of the meaning of [words like] "cow" and the like is postulated through the inference from action, having seen the activity directed toward the meaning by a learned person prompted by an utterance — even there, "because from this word this meaning has been cognized by him, therefore this is its meaning" — it is the indicative capacity of the word that is cognized first. Even in the co-occurrence with known words — in cases like "on the <s>sahakāra</s> tree the sweet <s>pika</s> (cuckoo) sings" and the like — from the known meaning of the associate [words], the unknown meaning of "<s>pika</s>" and the like is [inferred as] "the one who sings on the <s>sahakāra</s> tree — the word <s>pika</s> is an indicator of that" — so one cognizes the indicative capacity alone. Thus it is established that everywhere [the primary cognition is of] indicative capacity, not of invariable concomitance (<s>vyutpatti</s>). // 21–23½ //

children.text:
nanvākṛti' śabdārtha iti va' siddhānta' /
na ca tadvācyatvamanvayavyatirekāvantareṇa śakyate 'vagantum /
atastatpradhānaiva śabdapratītirāpadyeta /
ata āha---itthamiti /
ayamartha'--- anvayavyatirekayoratra niṣkṛṣṭārthaniyamamātre vyāpāra', vācakatā tu nānājātyādisaṅkīrṇārthaviṣayā siddhaiveti ||24 1/2||
children.translated_text: Objection: Your established doctrine is that <s>ākṛti</s> (universal form) is the meaning of a word. And that [universal] cannot be cognized as the expressible without [the process of] <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>. Therefore, the cognition from words would become predominantly dependent on that [process]. Hence he says "thus." The meaning is: the function of <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> here is merely the restriction of the extracted meaning; but the denotative capacity is already established with respect to the meaning mixed with various <s>jātis</s> (universals) and the like. // 24½ //

children.text:
nanvāgopālaṃ śabdārthavyavahāro dṛśyate /
na ca te 'nvayavyatirekābhyāmarthaniṣkarṣaṃ kurvanti /
na ca tān pratyavacākā' śabdā iti yuktaṃ vaktum /
tulyavat pratīte' /
pikādyarthanirṇayasya ca mlecchādinibandhanasya
children.translated_text: Objection: Linguistic usage regarding word and meaning is seen all the way down to cowherds. And they do not perform the extraction of meaning through <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>. And it is not proper to say that words are not expressers for them, because their cognition is equal [to that of the learned]. And the determination of the meaning of "<s>pika</s>" and the like, which depends on barbarians and others,
those who know sentences discriminate for the purpose of establishing relative strengths and weaknesses;
for [a word] is weak regarding the universals and particulars that are separated by gradations. // 27 //
A word that denotes the universal arises by the force of secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>);
therefore, what is denoted by the word must necessarily be discriminated — to what extent does it [directly] express? // 28 //
He says "many universals" with a half-verse, because this will be stated [later].

children.text: ayamabhiprāya'--- laukikā hi hānopādānādivyavahāramātrārthina', na ca teṣāṃ vyavahāra' śabdauccāraṇakṣaṇopajātasaṅkīrṇārthabodhasādhya eveti, śrautalākṣaṇikādivivekaṃ pratyanādṛtā iti ||25,26||
children.translated_text: The intention is this: worldly people desire merely the practical activity of acceptance, rejection, and the like; and their practical activity is not accomplished only by the mixed cognition of meaning arising at the moment of uttering a word — so they are indifferent to the discrimination of literal, figurative, and other [meanings]. // 25, 26 //

children.text:
tena tarhi kimarthaṃ vivañcate ata āha--balābalādīti /
śāstrasthā hyanirūpitaśaktayo na śāstrārthamanuṣṭhātuṃ śaknuvantīti teṣāṃ hānopādānopayogī śabdaśaktiviveka iti te viviñcata iti ||26 1/2||
children.translated_text: Then for what purpose do they discriminate? Hence he says "strengths and weaknesses." For those who are engaged in <s>śāstra</s> (systematic treatise), without ascertaining the capacities [of words], are unable to perform the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s> — so for them, the discrimination of word-capacity is useful for [the purposes of] acceptance and rejection — thus they discriminate. // 26½ //

children.text:
etadeva prapañcayatikakṣyāntaritetidvayena /
asyārtha'-- dvividhaṃ sāmānyaṃ paramaparaṃ ca /
paraṃ sattākhyam, aparāṇi
dravyatvādīni /
tāni sāmānyānyapi santi /
vyāvṛttibuddherapi hetutvāt viśeṣasaṃjñāmapi labhanta iti, tāni sāmānyaviśeṣaśabdenāpadiśanti, tatra ca sāmānyaviśeṣā' sāmānyaśabdasya svārthena kakṣyayāntaritā bhavanti /
yathā sacchabdasya sattāmācakṣāṇasya tadantaritā dravyatvādaya' sāmānyaviśeṣā', teṣu cāsau lakṣaṇābalena pravartamāno durbalo jāyate /
svarthe tu śrutyā vartate iti sa tatra balavān /
kā punariyaṃ lakṣaṇā nāma--- abhidheyavinābhāvena pratīti' /
yathoktam----
"abhidheyāvinābhāvapratītirlakṣaṇeṣyate" iti /
kriyā kiyadvābhidheyāvinābhāvena lakṣyate kiyat svamahimnā śabdenocyata iti śāstrasthānāmanuṣṭhānaviśeṣārthaṃ viveko yukta' /
sā ca lakṣaṇā prāyeṇa nityasambandhād bhavatīti nityasambandhādityuktam /
sambandhamātrameva tu lakṣaṇāyā bījam /
āha--- ka' punaranuṣṭhāne śrautalākṣaṇikavivekasyopayoga' /
śrūyatām--- loke tāvad brāhma
children.translated_text: He elaborates this very point — 'kakṣyāntarita' etc. with two [verses]. Its meaning is: The universal is of two kinds — higher (<s>para</s>) and lower (<s>apara</s>). The higher is called <s>sattā</s> (being/existence). The lower ones are <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-ness) and the like. Those too are universals, [but] since they also cause the cognition of exclusion, they also receive the designation of <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular) — hence they are referred to by the compound '<s>sāmānya-viśeṣa</s>.' There, the <s>sāmānya-viśeṣas</s> are separated by a degree (<s>kakṣyā</s>) from the primary meaning of the word '<s>sāmānya</s>' (universal). Just as <s>dravyatva</s> and the like, which are <s>sāmānya-viśeṣas</s>, are separated by a degree from the word '<s>sat</s>' (being) when it denotes <s>sattā</s>. And when that [word] operates with respect to them through the force of secondary usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), it becomes weak. But in its primary meaning, it operates through <s>śruti</s> (direct denotation) — hence it is strong there. What then is this <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary usage)? It is the cognition through the inseparability from the denoted [object]. As stated: 'The cognition through the inseparability from what is denoted is accepted as <s>lakṣaṇā</s>.' How much is denoted through the inseparability from the denoted, and how much is expressed by the word through its own power — distinguishing this is proper for the purpose of specific practice by those [engaged] in <s>śāstra</s> (scriptural science). And that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> generally arises from an eternal relation — hence it was said 'from the eternal relation.' But the relation alone is the seed of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. He says: What then is the use of the distinction between direct and secondary [usage] in practice? Listen: In worldly [usage], to begin with, for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>—
or to some extent, through the eternal relation, [the word] secondarily denotes the denoted [object];
there, because of the abundance of usage in that [universal], even when those particulars are absent. // Msv_5,9.29 //

children.text:
ṇebhyo dadhi dīyatāṃ takraṃ kauṇḍinyāyeti brāhmaṇasāmānyasthā brāhmaṇaśrutirlakṣamayā tadviśeṣaṃ kauṇḍinyamavatarantī durbalā bhavati ityavyavahitaviśeṣasthayā kauṇḍinyaśrutyā bādhyate /
vede 'pyemeva /
yaju' sāmānyasthā 'upāṃśuyajuṣā'iti śrutistadviśeṣasthayā 'uccairnigadena' iti śrutyā bādhyata ityevamādi darśayitavyamiti /
sāmānyaśabdenātra viśeṣān viśiṃṣanna sāmānyatiriktā' kecana viśeṣā vidyanta iti darśayati /
asati hi keṣāñcid darśanaṃ-- nityadravyavṛttayo 'ntyā viśeṣā' /
te ca vyāvṛttibuddhereva hetutvād viśeṣā eveti /
paramāṇukārayamakaṃ hi kāṇādā dvyaṇukādikrameṇa jagato nirmāṇamātiṣṭhante /
na cāṇutvena parasparamanatiśayānairaṇubhirasaṅkīrṇākārajagadutpādayituṃ śakyate /
ata' santi kecanāṇusamavāyino viśeṣā nāma ye tānitaretarato vyāvartayantīti saṅgirante /
te ca nirdhūtanikhilakāluṣyairaparokṣamīkṣanta eveti /
tān pratyucyate /
na tāvadakṣādhīneṣu bhāveṣvavāntarasāmānyātiriktān viśeṣānīkṣāmahe /
dravyatvena hi pṛthivyādayo guṇakarmabhyo viśiṣyante(dravya?pṛthivī)tvena pṛthivī abādibhyo dravyāntarebhya', vṛkṣatvena vṛkṣā' pārthivāntarebhya', śiṃśapātvena śiṃśapā vṛkṣāntarebhya ityevamaṇūn yāvadiya viśeṣakathā vartayitavyā /
kimatra viśeṣāntareṇa /
aṇuṣu tvekajātīyeṣvapi kāryavibhāgād rūpameva vibhaktamanumāsyāmahe /
no khalvavibhaktākāraṃ pūrvavsatu vibhaktākārakāryaghaṭanāyotsahata iti /
pṛthaktvākhyo vā guṇasteṣāmanyonyasya viśeṣakatvād viśeṣo bhaviṣyati /
sa evānapekṣitaviśeṣāntaro na sidhyatīti cet /
viśeṣā vā kathamanapekṣitaviśeṣāntarā' setsyanti /
akṣaṇe vā tadānantyam, ato manda evāyaṃ viśeṣāntarābhyupagama' /
yoginastu tān paśyantīti śraddhadhānā budhyante vayamaśraddhadhānā' sma',ye yuktiṃ prārthayāmaha iti sūktaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣeṣviti ||27-28 1/2||
children.translated_text: 'Give yogurt to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, buttermilk to <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>' — the word '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' standing in the universal '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,' when it descends through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> to the particular <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, becomes weak — and so it is overridden by the word '<s>Kauṇḍinya</s>' standing in the immediate particular. In the <s>Veda</s> too, it is the same: the <s>śruti</s> standing in the universal <s>yajus</s> — '<s>upāṃśuyajuṣā</s>' (with a quiet <s>yajus</s>) — is overridden by the <s>śruti</s> standing in the particular — '<s>uccairnigadena</s>' (with loud recitation) — and so on is to be shown. By qualifying the particulars with the word '<s>sāmānya</s>' (universal), he shows that there are no particulars apart from universals. For the view of some is: there are ultimate <s>viśeṣas</s> (particularities) that permanently reside in substances. And they are called <s>viśeṣas</s> because they cause the cognition of exclusion alone. For the <s>Kaṇādas</s> (Vaiśeṣikas) maintain the creation of the world from atoms, proceeding through the sequence of dyads and the like. And since atoms that do not surpass each other in their atomic nature cannot produce a world of distinct forms, they therefore assert that there exist certain <s>viśeṣas</s> (particularities) inherent in atoms that distinguish them from one another. And these are said to be directly seen by those who have purged all impurities. In reply to them: To begin with, among things accessible to the senses, we do not see any particulars beyond the lower universals. For earth and the like are distinguished from qualities and actions by <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-ness); earth from water and other substances by <s>pṛthivītva</s> (earth-ness); trees from other earthly things by <s>vṛkṣatva</s> (tree-ness); <s>Śiṃśapā</s> trees from other trees by <s>śiṃśapātva</s> (Śiṃśapā-ness) — thus this account of particularity is to be extended down to atoms. What need is there of another kind of particular? But even among atoms of the same kind, from the diversity of their effects, we shall infer that form alone is differentiated. For surely an undifferentiated prior entity cannot produce effects of differentiated form. Or, the quality called <s>pṛthaktva</s> (separateness) will be the <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinguisher) for them, since it distinguishes each from the other. If [you say] that very [separateness] cannot be established without depending on another <s>viśeṣa</s> — then how will the [postulated] <s>viśeṣas</s> be established without depending on yet another <s>viśeṣa</s>? Or, there would be an infinity of them in a single atom. Therefore, this acceptance of further particularities is pointless. As for the [claim that] yogins see them — those who have faith believe it; we who are without faith and seek reasoning [do not]. Thus the [discussion of] <s>sāmānya-viśeṣas</s> is well stated. // 27-28½ //
from usage in a higher universal, and even when present, from non-usage—
the word 'cow' is a denoter of <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness) alone, which is connected with a single object having a dewlap and the like. // Msv_5,9.30 //
the cognition 'this is the word for cow' arises from <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance);
therefore, indicative capacity (<s>gamakatā</s>) [is known] first, and denotative capacity (<s>abhidhāyakatā</s>) afterward. // Msv_5,9.31 //
'Because of being caused by that' — the relation is characterized as that of <s>saṃjñā</s> (name) and <s>saṃjñin</s> (named);
but this restriction of the relation is stated as <s>avinābhāvitā</s> (inseparable connection). // Msv_5,9.32 //
Because [the word] does not convey [meaning] before the relation is grasped, therefore
the word 'cow' and the like does not have denotative capacity (<s>abhidhāśakti</s>), just like the word '<s>Devadatta</s>.' // Msv_5,9.33 //

children.text:
'anvayavyatirekābhāyaṃ vākyajñāstu viviñcate' ityuktam /
tāvanvayavyatirekau darśayati--- tatreti dvayena /
tatra sāmānye gavādau
gośabdasya bahulaṃ prayogāt tadviśeṣeṣu ca śābaleyādiṣu asatsvapi bāhuleyādiṣu proya(gā?ga)darśanāt parasāmānye ca sattādau satyapi bhāvāntare 'prayogāt sāsnādibhi' sahaikāvayavirūpārthasamnabdhigotvamātrasya gośabdo vācaka ityanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ jñānaṃ janyate sāsnādyekārthasambandhīti cāvinābhāvinā cihnena gotvamupalakṣayatīti /
ata' siddhaṃ gamyagamakabhāva eva śabdārthayo' sambandha' prathamamavagamyate na punaravinābhāva iti ||29-30 1/2||
children.translated_text: It was said: 'those learned in sentences discriminate through <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance).' He shows those <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> — 'tatra' etc. with two [verses]. There, from the abundant usage of the word 'cow' in the universal [category of] cow and the like, and from the non-observation of usage in the particulars — <s>Śābalya</s> and the like — even when <s>Bāhuleya</s> and the like are absent, and from the non-usage when a higher universal like <s>sattā</s> (being) is present — i.e., in another entity — the word 'cow' is a denoter of <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness) alone, which is connected with a single object having a dewlap and the like — thus the cognition is generated through <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>. 'Connected with a single object having a dewlap and the like' — by this inseparable sign, <s>gotva</s> is characterized. Therefore it is established that the relation of word and meaning is first cognized as merely the relation of indicator and indicated, not as <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance). // 29-30½ //

children.text:
upasaṃharati---tasmāditi /
nanu--- saṃjñāsaṃjñisambandho bhāṣyakāreṇokta', na ca gamakaṃ saṃjñeti laukikā manyante, na hyagnerdhūma' saṃjñetyucyate, ata āha--- abhidhāyakateti /
ayamabhiprāya'--- asyārthaṃsyāyaṃ gamaka iti jñāte
nāvyāpriyamāṇasyāvagatau kāraṇatvamupapadyata iti tadvyāpāro 'vasīyate, śabdavyāpāraścābhidhetyucyate /
ato 'trābhidhānakriyāsambandhād gamakatvasyaiva viśeṣo 'bhidhāyakatā śabde jñāyate /
abhidhāyakataiva saṃjñātvamityupapanna' saṃjñāsaṃjñisambandha iti /
avinābhāvitā tu sambandhaniyama', na sambandha ityāha--- sambandheti /
idaṃ ca 'niṣkṛṣṭer'the niyamyate' ityatroktamasmābhi' /
tasmāditi padānuṣaṅgeṇopasaṃhṛtamiti vedi
children.translated_text: He concludes — 'tasmāt' etc. Objection: The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> stated the relation as that of <s>saṃjñā</s> (name) and <s>saṃjñin</s> (named). But ordinary people do not consider an indicator to be a name — for smoke is not called a 'name' of fire. Therefore he says — '<s>abhidhāyakatā</s>' (denotative capacity). The purport is: When it is known that 'this is the indicator of that meaning,' since the capacity for cognition is not justified for what does not operate [on the meaning], its operation is settled. And the operation of a word is called '<s>abhidhā</s>' (denotation). Therefore, from the relation of the activity of denotation, the specific form of indicative capacity known as denotative capacity is cognized in the word. And denotative capacity itself is name-ness — hence the relation of <s>saṃjñā</s> and <s>saṃjñin</s> is justified. But the <s>avinābhāvitā</s> (inseparable connection) is the restriction of the relation, not the relation itself — thus he says — 'sambandha' etc. And this was stated by us in the [discussion of] 'it is restricted with respect to the elicited meaning.' 'Tasmāt' — [this] is concluded by the continuation of the word — this is to be known.
Just as the word is understood as an indicator from worldly usage,
so too the knowledge of its capacity is understood as the means [of knowing it]. // Msv_5,9.34 //
And the grasping of its own nature — just as it operates on the result,
so too the knowledge of the relation — it would not be [determined] by non-capacity. // Msv_5,9.35 //
[this is] to be known.
The words '<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>' and '<s>abhāva</s>' (absence) are synonyms — hence no difference of meaning should be suspected. // 31, 32 //

children.text: devadattādayo hi yadṛcchāśabdā yatraiva saṅketyate tameva pratīpādayanti /
children.translated_text: For <s>Devadatta</s> and the like, being conventional words (<s>yādṛcchāśabda</s>), convey only that with which they are conventionally associated.
And these have no natural capacity anywhere.

children.text: tadayaṃ prayogārtha'--- gavādiśabdo dharmī, nābhidhāśakta iti sādhyam, upāyāntarāpekṣatvāditi hetu' /
children.translated_text: Hence the formal argument is: the word 'cow' and the like is the <s>dharmin</s> (subject); [that it] does not have denotative capacity is the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved); because it depends on another means [for conveying meaning] is the <s>hetu</s> (reason).

children.text: yadupāyāntarāpekṣaṃ tanna svarūpata' śaktam, devadattādipadamiva saṅketagrahaṇāpekṣamiti ||33||
children.translated_text: Whatever depends on another means is not inherently capable — like the word '<s>Devadatta</s>,' which depends on the grasping of convention. // 33 //
'If it is an indicator' — this usage was subsumed by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>. He states that — 'sambandha' etc.

children.text: atra bhāṣyakāreṇa 'yadi pratyāyaka' śabda' prathamaśruta' kiṃ na pratyāyayati' iti paricodya 'sarvatra no darśanaṃ pramāṇam' ityādinā darśanabalena gṛhītaśaktika' pratyāyayatīti parihāra ukta', taddarśayati---yathaiveti /
children.translated_text: Here the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, having raised the question 'If the word is an indicator, why does it not convey [meaning] when first heard?' and having given the resolution 'everywhere, observation is our <s>pramāṇa</s>' — namely that it conveys [meaning] when its capacity has been grasped through the force of observation — he shows this — 'yathaiva' etc.

children.text: asārtha'--- gamakatvameva tāvat śabdasya kimabhyupagamyate, vyavahāradarśanabaleneti cet, samānamidaṃ śkatisaṃvedane 'pi /
children.translated_text: Its meaning is: Is it first accepted that the word is merely an indicator? If so, [only] through the force of observing usage — then the same applies to the cognition of capacity as well.
For one does not observe people understanding meaning from a word whose capacity is unknown. // 34 //

children.text:
syādetat--- prakāśakā' pradīpādayo 'viditasambandhā api svārthaṃ prakāśayanto dṛśyante, tadvidharmā ca śabda', ato na prakāśaka iti /
tacca naivam, śaktivailakṣaṇyāt /
vicitraśaktayo 'pi hi bhāvā' /
tatpradīpa' pratyakṣapirakaratayāgṛhītasambandho 'pi prakāśayatu nāma /
naitāvatā śabdenāpi taddharmeṇa bhavitavyam /
ato 'yamaparyanuyoga' /
api ca vrīhyādayo 'gṛgītasvarūpā api kāryamārabhanta eveti śabde taddharma' kiṃ nāropyate /
kārakahetavo hi vrīhyādaya', śabdastu jñāpakahetu' /
ato 'pekṣate svarūpagrahaṇamiti cet /
kena vedamājñāpitaṃ jñāpakena svarūpagrahaṇamapekṣitavyaṃ na sambandhagrahaṇamiti, darśanabaleneti cet, samānamidaṃ sambandhagrahaṇāpe
children.translated_text: One might say: Illuminators such as a lamp, even without the relation being known, are seen to illuminate their own object — and the word is dissimilar to them; therefore it is not an illuminator. But that is not so, because of the difference of capacities. For entities have diverse capacities. So let the lamp, being of the nature of a direct producer of perception, illuminate even without the relation being grasped. It does not follow from this alone that the word too must share that property. Hence this is an invalid objection. Moreover, rice-grains and the like, even without their nature being grasped, do produce their effect — so why is that property not superimposed on words? Because rice-grains and the like are causes in the mode of producers (<s>kāraka</s>), while the word is a cause in the mode of an informer (<s>jñāpaka</s>). If [you say] therefore it requires the grasping of its nature — by what decree is it determined that an informer must require the grasping of its nature and not the grasping of its relation? If [you say] by the force of observation — then the same applies to the requirement of grasping the relation as well.
When something is said to be the most effective instrument for something,
its dependence on a facilitator does not destroy its own capacity. // Msv_5,9.36 //

children.text: na hi tatkāṇaṃ loke vede vā kiñcidīdṛśam /
children.translated_text: For there is nothing in the world or in the <s>Veda</s> of this kind—
in accomplishing what requires the procedure of 'how it is to be done,' that has no need for facilitation. // Msv_5,9.37 //
And because of being determined individually, just as an instrument would be,

children.text: bāhyāntaravibhāgena kvacit syād vā vivakṣayā // Msv_5,9.38 //
children.translated_text: in some cases, by the distinction of external and internal, or by intention, [it might be so]. // Msv_5,9.38 //
For someone distressed by darkness speaks thus:

children.text: kiṃ cakṣuṣā mamaitena dṛṣṭaṃ dīpena yanmayā // Msv_5,9.39 //
children.translated_text: 'What use is this eye of mine? What I saw was [seen] by the lamp.' // Msv_5,9.39 //

children.text: kṣāyāmapi, darśanabalādeva hi liṅgaśabdādayo jñāpakaviśeṣā' sambandhagrahaṇamapekṣante /
children.translated_text: even in the [capacity's] diminution — for through the force of observation, specific informers such as the inferential mark, word, and the like do require the grasping of the relation,
but not the eye and other [sense organs].
For everywhere, observation is our <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: kārakāścakṣurādaya iti nānumanyāmahe, jñānakāraṇasyaiva jñāpakatvāt, tadetadāha---svarūpeti ||35||
children.translated_text: We do not concede that the eye and the like are [mere] producers (<s>kāraka</s>), since whatever is a cause of knowledge is an informer (<s>jñāpaka</s>). He states this — 'svarūpa' etc. // 35 //

children.text:
nanu ca sambandhagrahaṇāt prāgapyabhidhāne śabda' śakto na vā /
yadi śakta' kiṃ sambandhagrahaṇāpekṣayā /

children.translated_text: If not—
then the grasping of the relation alone would turn out to be the cause, by the principle of 'the good scripture' — therefore he says — 'yat sādhakatama' etc.
To begin with, we do not understand the word as entirely incapable before the grasping of the relation.
Nor does the dependence on a facilitator destroy the capacity of what is capable. // 36 //
Objection: But even before the grasping of the relation, is the word capable of denotation or not? If it is capable, what is the need for dependence on grasping the relation?
Why does it not destroy [it]? Therefore he says — 'na hi' etc.

children.text: yadi hyanugrāhakāpekṣā svaśaktiṃ vihanyāt sarvameva laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ karaṇaṃ karaṇatāṃ jahyāt /
children.translated_text: For if the dependence on a facilitator were to destroy the capacity, then every instrument — both worldly and Vedic — would lose its instrumentality.
For every instrument requires the facilitation generated by the procedure of 'how it is to be done.' // 37 //

children.text: kiñca--- astu tāvaditikartavyatāpekṣā karaṇabhāvaṃ na vihantīti, pratyuta tayāpi naiva karaṇatvaṃ nāsti, pratikaraṇasvarūpaṃ tadapekṣāniyamādityāha---pratyātmeti /
children.translated_text: Moreover: Granted that the dependence on the procedure of 'how it is to be done' does not destroy instrumentality. But rather, because the requirement of that [facilitation] is restricted to the specific nature of each instrument, there is no instrumentality at all — hence he says — 'pratyātma' etc.

children.text: nanvevamubhayasamavadhānamevāntareṇa kāryāniṣpatte' kathaṃ karaṇetikartavyatāvibhāgo darśayitavya', ata āha--- bāhyāntareti bāhyamapi kvacid vivakṣāta' kārakapravṛtte' karaṇatayā vivakṣyata ityāha--- kvacitsyādveti ||38||
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, since the effect is not accomplished without the convergence of both, how is the distinction between instrument and procedure to be shown? Therefore he says — 'bāhya-antara' etc. Even an external [factor], in some cases, by the intention of describing the source of the productive activity, is described as the instrument — thus he says — 'kvacit syāt' etc. // 38 //
But in the case of permanent defect, even with a hundred lamps, there is no sight for the blind;
therefore, since it is [the cause] of seeing form and the like, the eye is the illuminator. // Msv_5,9.40 //
Because of the conjunction of body, self, and mind, because of the force of being non-common [to others],
and because of the presence of the capacity for cognition, the eye is accepted as the instrument. // Msv_5,9.41 //
Just so here too, the knowledge of the relation is a subsidiary, from common understanding.

children.text: gauravāt karaṇatvena mataṃ cet kena vāryate // Msv_5,9.42 //
children.translated_text: If, due to [its] importance, it is held to be the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) — by what is this prevented? // Msv_5,9.42 //
And the [statement] 'just as the eye' — this is said to be a deviating [example];
and even in the case of <s>Devadatta</s>, they accept an unmanifest capacity on rational grounds. // Msv_5,9.43 //
He shows this very point — 'agitated.'

children.text: jñānotpattāvantaraṅgamapi cakṣurna karaṇatayā manyate, kintu kitaścittāratamyaviśeṣād bāhyameva pradīpaṃ karaṇatayā vivakṣatīti ||39||
children.translated_text: Even the eye, which is proximate to the production of cognition, is not considered as the instrument; rather, due to some particular gradation, he intends the external lamp alone as the instrument. // 39 //
And this instrumentality, which depends on the speaker's intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>), is occasional.

children.text: nityavṛttau nityaṃ tu kāryasiddhau āntarasya takṣuṣa' karaṇatvamavagamyata ityāha---nityavṛttāviti /
children.translated_text: But in a permanent operation, the instrumentality of the internal eye for permanently accomplishing the result is understood — he says 'in permanent operation.'
The meaning is: the blind have no vision, i.e., no seeing. // 40 //

children.text: nanvastu vijñānakāryāsattiviśeṣaṇāt pradīpādyapekṣayā cakṣuṣa' karaṇabhāva', ātmamana' saṃyogastu jñānotpattāvatyantamāsanna', ata' kathaṃ tadapekṣayā cakṣuṣa' karaṇatvaṃ bhaviṣyatītyata āha---śarīreti /
children.translated_text: But [objection:] let the instrumentality of the eye be due to its proximity to the effect, namely the particular cognition, in comparison with the lamp and the like; but the conjunction of the self (<s>ātman</s>) and mind (<s>manas</s>) is extremely proximate to the production of cognition — so how is the instrumentality of the eye in comparison with that...

children.text: ayamabhiprāya'-- nāsattiviśeṣa eva karaṇatve kāraṇam, api tarhi bāhyapradīpādyapekṣayāsatti', ābhyantarātmamana' saṃyogāpekṣayā tvasādhāraṇyam, ātmamana' saṃyogo hi rasādijñānasādhāraṇo nāvyabhicāritayā rūpadarśanakāraṇamiti śakyate 'vagantumṣa cakṣuṣa' punarasādharaṇatayaiva rūpajñāne kāraṇatvamiti 'cakṣūrūpādibhedastu' ityatroktamiti ||41||
children.translated_text: The intended meaning is: mere proximity is not the cause of instrumentality; rather, [what matters is] proximity in comparison with the external lamp and the like, and uncommonness in comparison with the internal conjunction of the self and mind — for the conjunction of the self and mind...

Thus, having shown in the example that the division of instrument and subsidiary procedure depends on the speaker's intention, proximity, and particular distinction, he applies it to the topic at hand — 'similarly.'

children.text: anena yattadāgamanyāyena sambandhagrahaṇameva kāraṇamāpadyetetyuktaṃ tadapi vivakṣāviśeṣavaśenāstviti darśitamiti ||42||
children.translated_text: By this, what was said — that by the logic of scripture, the apprehension of the relation itself becomes the cause — that too is shown to be dependent on a particular speaker's intention. // 42 //

children.text:
aparamapi--- 'yathā cakṣurdraṣṭṭana bāhyena prakāśena vinā' ityādi parihārabhāṣyaṃ, tasyābhiprāyamāha---yatheti /
cakṣurhi pradīpādyupāyāntarā
children.translated_text: Another point too — the refutational <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage beginning with 'just as the eye does not [see] without external illumination' — he states its purport — 'just as.' For the eye, without some other means such as a lamp...
When external illumination is not present, form is not cognized by the blind;
and because of the immediacy of the result, the eye is accepted as the instrument. // Msv_5,9.44 //
The cognition that depends on a person — prior to them [i.e., the persons], it was not determined;

children.text: ya' saṃjñāsaṃjñisambandha' sa ceṣṭaśced dhruvaṃ kṛta' // Msv_5,9.45 //
children.translated_text: and if that relation between the sign (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and the signified (<s>saṃjñin</s>) is desired [to be eternal], then it is certainly created [instead]. // Msv_5,9.45 //
Since they have different substrata in place and the like, as in the case of a rope and a pot,

children.text: samaṃ nāstyanayo' kiñcit tenāsaṅgatatā svata' // Msv_5,9.46 //
children.translated_text: there is nothing common between these two — hence there is inherent disconnection. // Msv_5,9.46 //
Even [assuming the eye is] capable of illuminating form by its very nature — [this is] an inconclusive reason.
And the example too lacks the property to be proved — he says '<s>Devadatta</s>.' // 43 //

children.text: yadṛcchāśabdānāmapi jñānasāmarthyaṃ vidyamānameva niyogenābhivyajyata ityadhyāsavāde varṇitam /
children.translated_text: It was described in the <s>adhyāsavāda</s> (section on superimposition) that even for conventional words (<s>yadṛcchāśabda</s>), the capacity for producing cognition, being already existent, is merely manifested by convention.

children.text: atra ca yathā cakṣuriti bhāṣye cakṣuṣa' karaṇatvamityatropapattimāha---prakāśaiti /
children.translated_text: And here, for the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [passage] 'just as the eye,' he states the rationale for the instrumentality of the eye — 'illumination.'
And although this was already said in the [passage] 'in permanent operation,' it is stated again now for the purpose of supporting the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — hence there is no repetition. // 44 //

children.text: tadevamupapādita' saṃjñāsaṃjñisambandha' kṛtakatvena bhāṣyakṛtākṣipta'--- 'yadi prathamaśruto na pratyāyayati kṛtakastarhi' iti,
children.translated_text: The relation between the sign (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and the signified (<s>saṃjñin</s>), thus established, is objected to by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> as being created: 'If [the word] does not convey [the meaning] when heard for the first time, then it is created.'
The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> shows this — 'person.'

children.text: evaṃ cātra prayoga'--- ya' saṃjñāsaṃjñisambandha' sa kṛtaka', puruṣāpekṣatvāt, rajjughaṭasaṃyogavaditi ||45||
children.translated_text: And thus the formulation here is: the relation between sign and signified is created, because it depends on a person, like the conjunction of a rope and a pot. // 45 //

children.text: aparamapi 'svabhāvato hyasbandhāvetau śabdārthau' ityādi bhāṣyaṃ, tasyābhiprāyamāha---bhinneti /
ayamartha'--- yathā rajjusarpādiṣu bhinnadeśakālādhiṣṭhāneṣu kiñcid deśādi samaṃ nāsti, evaṃ tayo' śabdārthayo' /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: just as in the case of a rope, a serpent, and the like, which have different substrata in place, time, and so forth, there is nothing in common regarding place and the like — so too with word and meaning.
Therefore, just like those, these two [word and meaning] are also by nature unconnected.

children.text: īdṛśī cātra prayogaracanāśabdārthau svabhāvato 'saṅgatau, asamadeśakālatvāt, rajjvādivat /
children.translated_text: And the formulation of the argument here is: Word and meaning are inherently disconnected, because they do not share the same place and time, like a rope and the like.
Those two [word and meaning] are indeed not of the same place and time, because their substrata in different places and the like are observed — just like those [rope and the like]. // 46 //
Another [point] too — the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage beginning with 'for word and meaning are by nature unconnected' — he states its purport — 'different.'
Thus, in [the <s>Kāśikā</s> commentary] composed by the teacher <s>Sucaritamiśra</s>, the <s>sambandhākṣepa</s> (objection concerning the [word-meaning] relation) is concluded.
